comment: Loved the Lahuna Strawberry smoothie! Portions are quite large and the service is lovely here. There is one indoor table for two and plenty of outdoor seating. There's also a great burrito shop right next door that was popular. Will definitely come again!

I'm sorry, not sorry that i have to write this review but this has happened a countless of times. We order ahead 15-30mins early just to arrive and be notified that they haven't done our 2 drinks yet just to waste another 5-10mins of my time? I will mention that the drinks are good but whats not good is taking my valuable time when i'm already ordering way ahead of time to just arrive and have to wait more time? The place is not busy, the person is just chilling and on a phone call with their AirPods like, hello? Please check your orders ahead, there's never parking outside so having to hold my car on the street with the hazard lights is bad enough.
Great açaí bowl, price isn't terrible, service is a bit slow tho. Luckily I wasn't in a rush but there weren't many guests ahead of me and it still took 15 mins to order and get food...
Vegetarian food was excellent, portions were generous, staff very accommodating. Don't usually seek vegetarian meals, still a meat eater, but this was noteworthy; satisfied a carnivore like me.

Great spot for lighter and healthier food options :) I've tried their toast and smoothies which were great. They have an extensive menu of kefir, smoothies, and other healthy foods!

They put time and attention into making the food! There's outdoor seating and one small table inside.

Great spot! I love supporting these two store fronts.

Good food. Loved the Lahuna Strawberry smoothie! Portions are quite large and the service is lovely here. There is one indoor table for two and plenty of outdoor seating. There's also a great burrito shop right next door that was popular. Will definitely come again!

Delightful new cafe next to Isabella's, opened by her sister. Fresh and tasty menu choices, both sweet smoothies and delicious salad and sandwich choices. There is a bistro table inside and on the sidewalk but takeout is easy and Huntington Park is just a short walk. Or hop on the cable car to take your food to the waterfront. Service is friendly and quick.
They have a wide selection of healthy food. Very kind workers with good customer service :) thanks ladies.

Such a nice complimentary spot to Cafe Isabella next door! BTS (also good acronym) has a huge menu full of fresh healthy juices, smoothies and food.

It's tucked away up on the hill, and parrots tend to hang out in the trees across the street. There are a few small shared tables outside, take a break in the nice weather and enjoy some healthy options!

Keto, protein, and milk based options too. Happy to see this menu in the neighborhood.

This place is run very poorly. We had to wait 30 minutes for their protein smoothie. They forgot, and when they did finally make it, they continually left things out of the smoothie and kept having to reblend it. There was no line, no one else in front of us. They ran back and forth from cafe Isabella, to get lids or espresso. The smoothie was absolutely disgusting and very thin, just tasted like protein powder and milk. The latte from next door at cafe Isabella was also disappointing. Very confused how this place has such good reviews.

This is one of those places where everything is good. Great, actually. Delicious no bs smoothies with interesting flavors (I've tried a lot of them). Get the persimmon! And the rainbow dragon fruit strawberry thing. And also, wonderful crunchy morning sandwiches with avocado, kimchi, and other things. Every bite and sip I've had here has not only been pleasurable but makes me feel healthier. Do yourself a favor and go. And, why do I sound like I'm writing an ad? Because when I find a place I love, I want it to succeed. Right next its sister (literally - the owners are sisters) coffee and burrito shop. A wonderful addition to the neighborhood.
Great place to get a healthier version of food. The service was good. I enjoyed the avocado toast. It hit the spot. Great place to visit.

A lovely place to hang out with friends. Cozy and comfortable. Foods are very delicious Especially the signature ramen. Very rich and the portion is huge. The store manager Eric is very friendly and helpful. I do recommend this place and I will come back for sure.
I agree that this restaurant is one of the best restaurants in San Francisco. Food Arabic‍

A must-try overlooked spot in Nob Hill, does not pop-up on maps when searching but is an excellent option in the area. Tried this spot for the first time this week, large menu with various breakfast and lunch options, all on par with other restaurant pricing in the area if not cheaper. Small, clean interior - limited seating, would recommend to-go options.

This Awesome Cafe is a New found place that offers so many Healthy options to choose from! Truly the very best and I am not kidding, Avocado Toast in the Bay if not Ever! The way they prepare this Toast is nothing you tried anywhere else! ~ TARA's Tours!

It's a bit pricey but a nice spot in SF to grab a healthy brunch. I ordered the avocado toast and "la vie en rose" kefir and both were great. The ingredients were very clean and my drink was only sweetened with a bit of honey which is exactly what I was looking for. Will definitely come back :-)
We found this place just walking down the street 0MG. From their smoothies to their açai bowls to sandwiches everything was amazing. So delicious.

This is our first time here and the staff was attentive to us. It's right next door to a great breakfast place.

We ordered:
"back to the future" and added pineapple to it - 10/10

"Anti-flu" juice, it was refreshing but could be colder. We would recommend asking for ice with your drink, but it comes down to preference.

It's a small shop that has 3 small tables to sit at outside.

had a super good smoothie from here 10/10. it tasted like a healthy milkshake
if you're looking for something filling but not too heavy this is the spot!
Awesome delicious and healthy options for the neighborhood. I particular like the different green juices. The staff is super nice.

I thought this place was great. Fantastic food, friendly service, happening vibe. We ordered a lot:

Eggplant Tofu - excellent
Shrimp Fresh Rolls
Hot Wings & Garlic Fries
Saigon Steak
Strawberry Fizz
Limeade Fizz
Garlic Noodle Bowl w/ Steak
Orange Passion Fruit Breeze
Thai Tea French Toast Combo
Pink Dalgana Coffee - the winner
Fried Chicken Sandwich

Went here for brunch on new year's day and it was packed. We were seated in about 25 minutes which wasn't too bad. They took our order really fast but the kitchen was backed up and it took awhile to get our food. Understandable as it was new year's day that the food would take awhile but some of the food that came out was lukewarm. Extremely disappointed that this was the case.

Pad See Ew: This dish came out lukewarm. Flavors weren't and just temperature threw off the dish.

Garlic Fries: Classic appetizer, fresh and hot and the sriracha mayo sauce was good.

Thai Tea French Toast: A little too dry for a french toast. The sauce was kind of bland and was straight up tea without any sweetness to balance it out. Fruits were fresh and sweet though.

Tom Yum Soup: Broth was a little bland and missed the iconic tartness of tom yum soup.

Server also forgot one of our food orders on top of the long wait and lukewarm food. I would like to think it was due to the new year day rush but I do not see myself coming back.

Food good
Small place so service can be a little slow
Signature drinks are a very nice looking. Try the rainbow.

Came back here again & brought a coworker. We got there at the right time as it hit packed. I ordered the dalgona coffee again & ordered the crispy chicken salad w/sunny side up egg. Everything was good. My coworker ordered the pho. Unfortunately, she didn't like. She said it was bland. I noticed they put the white flat thicker noodles. I felt bad that she barely touched her soup; but my salad was good.

My coworkers chose this place for lunch; otherwise, I would not have ever known about this restaurant. We were a party of 4. We came on a Wednesday around noon & were seated right away. The place wasn't too small or big; in essence, you could hold an audible conversation. Our waitress was great.
The food was great and I thought the portions were huge. We started off sharing the shrimp spring rolls. The white wrap was good and not chewy or hard. The peanut sauce was good. For drinks, I got the Dalgona coffee. It was rich and tasty.
I love breakfast/brunch and this place serves it until 3pm! I had the Eggs Florentine Benedict. Came with a side salad and potatoes. The toasted potatoes were cut really small, which is what I like; I'm not a fan of big wedge style potatoes. All of it was good. Couldn't clean my plate off because I was so full. I took a picture of it but later found out my phone didn't save it for some reason, so apologies for not including a pic.
Other items my coworkers got were: some type of noodles, stir fried eggplant/chicken w/sunny side egg on top of rice. This looked good and they finished it.
Overall, food, service, and place were great. The price is about $16+. Typical rates for the area; however, the quantity and quality is worth it. I would definitely come back here!

The staff here are the nicest people ever! I've came here multiple times with friends and it always never disappoints! The Saigon steak is very juicy and tender, I also really like how the hoisin sauce adds that wow factor to the steak. I love how the place may seem small on the outside but there are plenty of tables and space when you walk in!

This place was really great! The customer service was amazing and the staff had a great sense of humor. They gave recommendations and they did not disappoint. Hint.. the Thai milk tea pink drink! Super good! The restaurant is kinda set up like a diner but very modern and seems very open because of the windows. Nice. Clean. Great atmosphere! The food was delicious and cooked well. We enjoyed everything. I will say my eggs were a little on the lighter scrambled side than I like but that won't bring the stars down! They were good! I'd definitely eat here again and try some more of the other food menu items! Great place for breakfast, brunch or just because.

YES YES YES! Great vibes, awesome service, creative drinks & food. We ate here two days in a row...and we probably could go back over & over. The flavors are all so different, can't imagine my tastebuds getting tired. I LOVE chicken & waffles but usually you get disappointed by the chicken or the waffle...this dish was PERFECT! Lightly crispy, juicy, and a mouth of yum! So many options with different flavor profiles. A must when you are SF. Best meal for sure!

Lively brunch atmosphere. Reasonable pricing and nice variety of options between comfort food and brunch food. Warm service and large portions.

Seated on short notice, 10-20m wait.

Love coming here every time I'm in the city! The lychee mimosas are the best mimosas I've ever had, and let's appreciate how pretty it looks too?! I love how their menu has a lot of options and their dishes always taste super yummy! Service is extremely nice and attentive.

This spot is a bit out of the way if you don't drive but it's not too bad of a walk from Powell Bart station.

The Saigon steak is delicious, the meat was easy to eat and came with plenty of yummy sauce and nicely cooked onions.

The tom yum soup was good. If you don't think you can finish a whole plate, this is a good choice. It was also loaded with chicken!

The Thai lime tea was refreshing, not too sour and not too sweet.

The staff were friendly and didn't rush us.
Consider this spot for your next casual hangout with friends or family

Make sure to make a reservation because this spot is definitely on the smaller side and always packed!

The Tom Yum omelette definitely stole the show here! The soup inside the omelette was so so good. Paired with the rice it tasted fantastic.

The Thai tea French toast was pretty underwhelming. The sauce was good but the toast was very average.

Would definitely come back in the future!

This place is amazing for its asian fusion brunch! We loved the thai tea french toast, the drunken noodles, the eggs benedict etc. The waiter was very enthusiastic and friendly. The place is pretty casual and good vibes.

We went there on a Saturday morning. The place wad fairly busy, and we got a table because reservation. The inside seating was pretty nice.

They have awesome ice coffees, and you have to try it. I forgot to take pictures, but it was awesome. I got Thai tea french toast which was tasty. My wife got omelette which she was pretty happy.

The only reason I gave them four star is because we wanted to sit longer but they kicked us out because they were short on tables. Other than that no complaints really.

Will go there again if I am in the area.
Would come back only if I were in the area. The chicken fried rice had good flavor but the chicken was more breading than chicken. It was a good value, fast meal

I was recommended this place a while back, and it did not disappoint! Came here at noon on a Tuesday and was seated right away. We decided to do family style so we could try a little bit of everything. We got the Pandan Waffles, Crispy Chicken Fried Rice and the Garlic Noodle Bowl with Tofu

The Pandan Waffles were AMAZING!!! Perectly crispy, and the inside was almost mochi like. Even with syrup, it wasn't too sweet, and the whipped butter helped balance everything out. The bananas were also a great touch, but our berries were a bit sour. This was my favorite of the three.

The crispy chicken fried rice was also super delicious! I love the pickled veggies and the sauce that it came with paired well with the chicken and fried rice.

The garlic noodle bowl was just okay, and I'd skip this on my next visit. The tofu was more like a fish cake than actual tofu. Still not too bad, just didn't stand out like the other two dishes we had.

This is a great spot for brunch, and there's so much variety to suit everyone's appetite! The workers are also super kind and friendly. I will definitely be back!

I'm a bit disappointed during my last visit! Got an order of Chicken and Waffle. The waffles were DiVINE but the chickens aren't . Chicken has outer crispness yet inside felt like reheated chicken than freshly fried ones.

Services remains good as ever but also quite slow with to go orders. Dine-in dinners got their orders faster than to gos. Plus, the taxes and whatnot make it pricey to eat here regularly

Ambiance: it's a cool sit down brunch spot and also good for cute first dates. It's a casual dress code and they do have good music

My friends and I decided to take the Caltrain to city for a food adventure.This is a 10min walk from Caltrain station. SUPER CONVENIENT! If you want to eat right off of the Caltrain.We did make reservations for 1pm. It was quite busy so I'm glad we did. Around 2pm all the hustle and bustle died down. I believe you could just walk in to eat.

On this particular day after doing two workout classes. I was rather ravished with hunger . Haha! I wanted something carby & something filled with protein. I went with the fried rice omelette. A well balance of fried rice and omelette that underneath is covered with mixture of veggies and shrimp. It was mouth watering good. I like how they fusionized it by adding Tom yum flavor to both fried rice and omelette. It gives it off a nice sour goodness like your eating tom yum soup. For my drink I got dalgona Vietnamese coffee. It's like a fluffy coffee like cloud filled with coffee concentrate that you twirl into milky ice for nice blend of coffee richness.

What's savory without sweet?
Friends and I decided to also share banana caramelized French toast. The soft pillowy like bite mixed with berries and glazed brown sugar banana was chef kiss. I would come back just for this. I'm drooling just thinking about it.

Amazing! The food was great for portion size, absolutely delicious, and the presentation was so well done. The service was fast, and it's simple inside, a little tight, but the food was definitely worth it

So many great options to chose from. Our server was so friendly! Would recommend reserving a table.
The Thai tea French toast and the crispy chicken fried rice stood out the most!

Walked in for brunch on Labor Day. Cute Thai fusion brunch spot. Waited about 10-15 minutes for a table which wasn't bad for no reservations. Tight spot but also offers outdoor seating.

We were seated inside and our server came to take our drink order. My bf got the iced lychee tea which was delicious and refreshing. I got the coffee - standard. But service was lacking so I never got a refill lol.

We ordered the banana French toast and steak & eggs specialty. Both dishes were tasty but pretty small portion for the price. We also waited over 45 minutes for our order... And they never gave us water or utensils either... I ended up just grabbing for myself at the front.

Probably understaffed bc of Labor Day but wasn't stand out enough on any fronts to return... I'd recommend Sisterita over this place.

Dropped by since we were in the neighborhood. It was a weekday past noon and luckily there was no wait, so we grabbed a table. It's a cute, modern cafe with kiosk in the front.

***OUR PICKS***

STRAWBERRY MATCHA LATTE ~ this was lightly sweetened from the macerated strawberries on the bottom. Matcha flavor was prominent and the strawberries were sweet enough to balance this drink. You just have to mix it up to get the sweetness all around. I enjoyed it! 5/5

STEAK BENEDICT ~ the eggs were perfectly cooked and runny inside! Steak was tender and juicy. Potatoes were crunchy outside and soft inside. Thoroughly enjoyed this dish! 5/5

FRIED CHICKEN SANDWICH ~ this sandwich was juicy and delicious, but the patty was thinner than a pancake and barely any meat. So that was disappointing. If only it was thicker, it would have been great. The fries were crispy and good. 3.5/5

I'd recommend their benedict dishes if you're looking for a breakfast dish. It was pretty scrumptious! Their other drinks looked good too! We're rarely in this part of town, but I'd come back if I was in the mood for brunch.

Very solid breakfast spot in SF. It is a Vietnamese fusion with limited seating inside and outside but honestly it felt pretty cozy. Our fav definitely was the saigon steak, super recommend that. For traditional breakfast lovers, I would definitely recommend the crunch berry french toast- it's not too dense but slightly refreshing. The garlic noodles were decent, just okay in my opinion. Just felt like it was missing some sort of kick... The salmon benedict was also just ok, nothing very special.

I loved our server, he was amazing. He was very friendly and transparent with us and told our group not to order certain dishes that he didn't recommend, which I greatly appreciated. They've got a diverse menu and outdoor seating as well. The food and vibes were immaculate!
Great Fusion breakfast foods. Good customer service . The Garlic noodles with spicy chicken and the spicy chicken sandwich was delicious.

Had a huge brunch here with a few friends; we were able to try a good chunk of items, most of which we enjoyed. To preface, I'm not a huge breakfast fan so I never think any breakfast spot is amazing, although I do think Mr. East Kitchen offers some really unique fusion items. I enjoyed the thai tea french toast which was not overly sweet, and the garlic fries that come with the sriracha hot wings were so addicting to eat. The garlic pork noodle was tasty along with the chicken and waffle, but the saigon steak was too sweet for me. Potatoes on the side were delish though. Drinks here are gorgeous and yummy!

The place itself isn't the biggest but still has a good amount of seating. Parking is on the street so it's not the most convenient. Service was decent but they were quite busy when we came. Overall, solid option for asian fusion breakfast!

There seems to be an abundance of Thai fusion brunch spots in SF, but very few of them take reservations for the ultra-popular weekend brunch. I'd heard about Mr. East through word-of-mouth and was able to score a Saturday morning reservation a few weeks out.

Mr. East's menu is quite large with a full range of brunch and Thai food classics (eggs benedict, pad Thai), along with some unique twists (pandan waffles, tom yum omelette). We also found it amusing how the "specials" menu was holiday-themed, since our visit took place in the middle of summer. My friends and I decided that the best strategy would be to order a variety of dishes and share everything family-style, and our servers were accommodating and brought us additional plates. This turned out to be the right call because portions are HUGE, and we were glad that we got to try a little bit of everything. We ordered the pandan waffle (my choice), tom yum omelette, Hainan chicken, and berry French toast. Everything came out of the kitchen less than ten minutes after we placed our order.

If I were to choose a favorite "brunch" dish, it would be the pandan waffle - the texture of the waffle was light and fluffy, and the pandan lent the waffle a sweet, mild flavor and cool green color. Plus, the whipped butter provided a salty contrast to the sweet waffle and syrup. The tom yum omelette was unique - the filling had a tangy, fishy flavor that tasted just like its namesake soup. While typically a fan of the sweet brunch dishes, my favorite dish overall was the Hainan chicken. I really enjoyed the tender chicken and savory yet subtle flavors of the rice and garlic dipping sauce; so simple yet so delicious. The berry French toast, while impressive-looking, was my least favorite dish - it was as sweet as a churro filled with strawberry creme and topped with more syrupy-sweet strawberries.

While Mr. East is a solid brunch spot, I'd be just as happy to return for lunch or dinner to try some of their other Thai dishes.

So, it's rare that I update a review this soon especially since I only dined here a couple months ago.

When a friend invited me for a weekday lunch, I chose this spot since it was close to my office and not far from hers. I remember the menu being large and having a difficult time deciding what to try on my 1st visit.

We were seated in the dining area to the right as you enter. We studied the menu before deciding on picking an entree each and sharing them besides getting one of their often-mentioned breakfast item for dessert. We ate family style, starting with a Thai iced tea (https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=saJuyv784apZzH--psHZ3Q&start=144&select=NP3m621knPE6X8afR3Iezw) which we shared; I asked for an extra glass and tested my magician skills in pouring about half ... not bad, maybe four drops lost in the transition. We both enjoyed this as it was a typical version but, with these warm summer days, it hit the spot in quenching our thirst. The 1st entree to arrive was the Saigon steak, eggs sunny side (https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=saJuyv784apZzH--psHZ3Q&start=120&select=njBcgYNy3aj83yCzHFHuwA); Angus tenderloin dice-cut, onions, stir-fried in hoisin sauce, egg sunny side up, served with fried potatoes, garlic toast, house salad. Here is a picture of the apportioned and slightly eaten portion of this as the original photo doesn't show the steak (https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=saJuyv784apZzH--psHZ3Q&start=144&select=6DMhNZXuKs2LxdeWzlShkg). The sauce paired very well with the tender chunks of beef with the onions adding a crunch element to it without being too acidic. Next came the Shaking beef (https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=saJuyv784apZzH--psHZ3Q&start=120&select=I_idSNvjlxI9vCmGYiU9Dw), Angus tenderloin, dice-cut, yellow onion, red onion, green onions. fried shallot, stir-fry in hoisin sauce, which came with baby bok choy and a large scoop of rice. You could say that this is the lunch version of the Saigon steak as the protein and its preparation are the same. Lastly, we tried the Thai French toast with bananas combo with bacon and eggs, sunny side (https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=saJuyv784apZzH--psHZ3Q&start=120&select=_IdV99ZZa4ySmiyl65Cfrw); this was a nice dessert though we were both full and could only take a few bites of the French toast. The eggs were perfect since we were able to put the eggs on both steak dishes. The item of discussion was the Sriracha bacon which had that spiciness and a little sweetness likely from a maple glaze. We finished most of the savory items but my generous host for this meal took more than half of the French toast home. The bacon didn't leave there, trust me.

Service was great as the waitress Amy who I also believe is the owner knew that we ordered too much food and would be bringing some home. The other gentleman observantly made sure our water carafe stayed filled and removed empty plates. They also gave us plenty of takeout boxes to pack our unfinished food. The dining room was about half full at 11:30 am but all tables were occupied when we left around 12:15 pm. I mentioned to Amy that I had not dined here prior to my visit a couple of months ago since shortly after they opened over seven years ago. She explained that they were the new owners and previously had a business closer to Chinatown. I immediately guessed correctly that she ran the popular brunch spot on Broadway named Spork, having dined there a couple years ago before they closed. So if you're looking to try Thai and Vietnamese inspired fusion brunch food, look no further.

It's been a long while, enough to categorize this as a new business for me. I believe I wrote one when they first open many years ago but I don't see one listed.

My memory is that it was a 3 to 4 star one, only complimenting their boldness in opening in this budding neighborhood at that time. Fast forward ten or more years and I finally revisited for a business lunch on a Wednesday late morning.

Thx dining room was fairly full with only two open tables when I walked in. A lady pointed to a two-seater to the right and gave me menus. Being early, I studied the expansive menu which was a stark contrast to what I remembered (pho, banh mi, Vietnamese wraps, salads, etc.). The menu ranges from those to many Thai dishes, many fusion takes of the cuisine. Two particular sections caught my eyes, the breakfast and brunch page ( and the Mr. East specialties (

After my lunch partner arrived, we quickly ordered. I started with the lychee jasmine tea ( it was moderately sweet, probably at a 50% level if you ordered from a typical tea or boba store. I tried the omelette fried rice ( the description reads omelet, shrimp, spinach, onion, bell pepper, mushroom, tom yum paste, sriracha bacon, served with egg fried rice and house salad. My lunch partner commented that it reminded him of the Japanese omurice, which I enjoyed at a place in J Town. This compared favorably to that though this is definitely a fusion version and a non-traditional dish. I enjoyed the many aspects and sections of this dish and the shrimp size was impressive ( I especially liked the bacon which I rationed in alternating bites with the other elements on my plate (salad, rice, and omelet). Yes, I would order this again. The portions are generous as I took about 1/3rd of it home as part of my dinner. My lunch companion did the same with his meal.

There was a steady flow of dine-in customers as well as people picking up takeout orders. Our waitress was quick and efficient in giving us takeout boxes and bring the tablet to me to clear the bill. Big thanks to the gal (no name on the receipt) on taking our order and serving our meals. I hope to try the fried chicken and waffles or the Thai Tea French Toast on my next visit.

We went here around 6pm on a Saturday and there was no wait. The restaurant was actually quite empty at the time I went which I was surprised about since most restaurants are usually busy at that time. This restaurant is located in a bad neighborhood, so maybe that's why it wasn't busy.

Anyways, we ordered the Drunken Noodle Beef, Crispy Chicken Fried Rice, Garlic Noodle Bowl w/ Salmon, Fried Chicken Sandwich w/ Garlic Fries, Pink Dalgona Coffee, Iced Butterfly Lychee Fizz, Hawaiian Rainbow, and Strawberry Fizz. All of the food we ordered was good, but my favorite food item would be the Garlic Noodle bowl and also the Strawberry Fizz drink. I liked how thick and chewy the garlic noodles were and also liked how refreshing the Strawberry Fizz drink is.

I'd still recommend this place since the food and drinks tasted good. I wouldn't recommend going here for a late dinner though because I felt the neighborhood it's in is a bit dangerous because people easily walked into the restaurant and asked my group if they can have some of our food.

We came here for lunch and got seating really quickly for a party of 8 with no reservations. The service was quick, restaurant was clean.

I had the saigon steak and replaced the salad for rice. The portion was huge, steak was well seasoned and tender. My bf had the beef noodles and he was a big fan. The dalgona coffee was good but I likely wouldn't get again.

Ordered the eggplant tofu! Sauce was chef kiss good. A very good portion size, left feeling full. Their vegetarian steak is just the tofu fyi in case you're deciding between veg proteins. Staff super friendly and lots of fun drink options!

Came here with my friend for dinner on a Friday and there was no wait! We took an Uber here, so we didn't have to deal with parking but if you are driving then I would recommend finding a nearby parking garage. Street parking looks difficult. The ambiance is standard, it's pretty casual. We ordered the crispy chicken fried rice, shrimp tom yum noodle soup, and mango sticky rice. Everything was delicious, I can't wait to try their brunch menu!

Mr East Kitchen is such a cute and unique brunch spot! The dishes on the menu consists of Asian inspired flavors which makes for a nice switch-up from a typical American brunch. Loved the dishes we ordered here! We ordered the Tom Yum Omelette, Omelette Fried Rice, and the Lychee Mimosa Pitcher! Both dishes had just the right amount of sauce to food ratio so we got flavor with each bite! The Lychee Mimosa was also bomb and had actual lychee and blueberries in it :) It was my friend's birthday and the staff were kind enough to give us a free dessert item! Overall, staff were super attentive and friendly. Definitely recommend stopping by and making a ressie beforehand :) I will probably try their Thai Iced Tea French Toast next time!

SO GOOD!!! I'm glad my friend took me here for dinner.

Tom yum noodle soup with prawns - The soup is tangy, flavorful, and delicious. Their noodles is a great texture and the prawns are big, which I love.

Tom yum omelette fried rice - This wasn't on the dinner menu, but the chef was able ot make it for us. Also very delicious.

The service was great and friendly.

I would for sure be back to try more dishes!

15/10 -- Mr. East Kitchen Delivers Big Flavor and Fast Service

I was in San Francisco this week for Dreamforce and needed a solid meal after a long day of sessions. I turned to Yelp to find a spot with great reviews, and that's how I landed at Mr. East Kitchen. I'm so glad I did -- they absolutely delivered.

My colleague ordered the Banh Mi sandwich, and I went with the Angus steak dish. He paired his meal with a Vietnamese coffee, while I opted for the Lychee fizzy drink, which was light, refreshing, and the perfect contrast to the richness of the steak.

The food came out impressively fast -- no long wait, just straight to the good part. Every bite was flavorful, balanced, and clearly made with care. The service was friendly and attentive without being overbearing, and the overall experience felt effortless in the best way.

If I could give this place a 15 out of 10, I would. Excellent food, great service, and quick turnaround -- exactly what you want whether you're in town for a conference or just craving a quality meal.

Highly recommend Mr. East Kitchen -- it's the kind of spot that quietly surprises you and makes you want to come back.

Went to Mr.East today for brunch and it was delicious! I haven't had a good brunch in so long, and this hit the spot! My friend and I went around 10:30 Sat morning, parking was easy to find on the street, and the restaurant had some people in it but still some open tables. As we sat there longer, the place got busier, constant flow of people! The place is super casual, but nice comfortable interior with the friendliest staff. Service was so fast too, so even if it's busy, people are in and out because quick service. Ok now on to the food....

The pad see ew (with bbq pork on the side for my veggie friend) was incredible. So fresh, not oily, just fresh veggies and good chewy noodles in a delish sauce! The bbq pork was amazing as well with it.

Berry crunch French toast served on the weekends only is a must get!!! So crunchy on the outside filled with berry cream filling on the inside, omg it was so so good.

Egg & avocado sandwich was standard and delish, the hashbrowns on the side were soo crispy and good especially with that mango mayo!!

Tom yum omelette was packed with shrimp and veggies that were so flavorful and I've never had more perfect crispy breakfast potatoes on the side.

Everything came out so hot and perfect. The drinks were incredible. Pink dalgona, Hawaiian rainbow, lychee jasmine tea, Jasmine butterfly, strawberry matcha latte , would get them all again!

This is my boyfriend and I's favorite brunch spot in SF! The food is always so flavorful and creative- I love all the Asian flavors they add into the traditional breakfast dishes. I always get the omelette fried rice, which comes with a tom yum shrimp omelette, fried rice, and sriracha glazed bacon. I can't even describe how good it is!! I've also had the strawberry matcha and the dalgona coffee, both delicious but the matcha is my favorite. My boyfriend got the banana french toast which he absolutely loved- they were so fluffy and came with a caramelized banana and this delicious cream. You can make it a combo and add eggs and bacon which is nice too.

The space is very modern and clean, but it's pretty small so some tables are right next to the door or squeezed pretty closely together. It still feels very homey and casual. The front area is pretty hectic when there are lots of people waiting and getting takeout. I've had to wait around 10-15 minutes every time I go but it's so worth it. One of the employees told me we can join the Yelp waitlist ahead of time, so will definitely be doing that next time. So excited to go back and try some of the noodles and other dishes!

This place has never disappointed us from the service down to the taste of the food and how fast it comes out. We always have one meal here whenever we are in SF. My son's favorite is the Saigon steak which comes with salad, potatoes, and bread- a real feast. My husband got the salmon curry bowl which is the healthier option and I enjoyed the chicken and waffles. Everything is beautifully presented down to the drinks. Would highly recommend and one of the places I would rate 5/5.

Have you been to a restaurant a second time and find the food it not as good? Well this did not happen here. The food is still excellent! Tried the Tom yum omelette which was unique and tasty. The portion is generous and will fill you up. My son had the Saigon steak and the meat was tender and juicy. We were en route to the airport so got the crispy chicken salad to go (very generous portions and tasted great even when cold)- definitely better than any airport food we would have purchased. I would recommend skipping the chicken satay- it's grilled chicken with side of peanut sauce so did not have the traditional marinated chicken taste. We will be back!

I am super excited to have found this restaurant. It's within walking distance of the Children Creativity Museum and such a gem. We got here for Sunday brunch and was able to get on the Yelp waitlist where they put a table on reserve for us. The restaurant is bright and modern- the servers are very efficient and hard working. Business seem really good and they still ran a promotion where you order 3 entrees and get a 4th free. We tried the shrimp pad Thai (large shrimps, nicely cooked noodles, tofu, and large portion of bean sprouts), Thai tea French toast (delicious but pricey for what it was), chicken and waffles (chicken piping hot and battered perfectly paired with a honey mustard sauce, pandan waffle was not too sweet but could have used some syrup), Thai steak egg Benedict (eggs perfectly cooked and a huge plate of food), and chicken garlic noodles (didn't eat this fresh but still tasted great). The menu was very extensive. We saw people ordering pho which looked great too. Wide selection of drinks including flavored jasmine green tea. We will be back next time we are in SF.

We tried their drunken noodles, Thai tea French toast, Saigon steak, and spicy salmon. Every dish was flavorful and perfectly done. The drinks were just as good: pink dalgona coffee, orange passion fruit breeze, plus lychee and pomegranate mimosas. Bright vibes, hospitable service, and amazing food make this a spot I'd definitely visit again! Thank you for having us

We really enjoyed Mr East Kitchen for the variety of options they offered. They had traditional brunch options, thai fusion brunch options, and also standard thai dishes. The dalgona coffees were sweet at first but when mixed well together, were pretty good.

highlights:
- The tom yum omelette really stood out for its flavors and the sriracha bacon on top was a nice bonus.
- For sweets, we preferred the pandan waffles (which had a nice strong pandan flavor) over the thai tea french toast.

We also ordered a few standard thai dishes. Tom yum noodles were good while the drunken noodles were a bit bland.

This area normally isn't the most ideal for parking and traffic but ended up being fine on a Sunday.

Had a great brunch here! Went on a Saturday around noon, and it wasn't crowded at all, so my group was seated right away. We ordered a mix of dishes: Tom Yum Omelette, Saigon Steak, Pink Dalgona Coffee, Iced Butterfly Lychee Fizz, Thai Milk Tea, Thai Tea French Toast Combo, and Vietnamese Dalgona Coffee.

Everything came out beautifully presented and tasted amazing. The Tom Yum Omelette was a standout with shrimp inside, and the side salad was super fresh. Portions were generous too! I loved my Pink Dalgona Coffee, super cute and flavorful, with a nice strong coffee taste. The server was also really attentive, which was a nice touch. Will definitely be back!

The Tom Yum Omelette was super unique, basically your classic omelette but packed with that unmistakable tom yum flavor. The potatoes and bacon on the side were good too. It's definitely one of the more memorable dishes. The Spicy Salmon didn't live up to its name, no heat at all and kinda underwhelming. I'd probably skip it. The Pad See Ew could have been a bit drier. I felt it was too wet for this dish. The Berry Toast was a hit! Really good and not overly sweet. The Lychee Mimosa was good, though the alcohol flavor was stronger than the lychee.

Loved Mr East Kitchen!! The food was very good and there were so many options! The service was amazing as well with good attentiveness to all the guests.

We got the drunken noodles, which was very unique due to the different type of noodles but tasted so good, will definitely get it again!

We also got the Thai tea French toast which was so yum! The spring rolls were also very flavorful. I got the dalgona coffee which was also very good, I want to try some of their other drinks as well.

You may have to wait for a seat since it gets busy, but that's very typical of any brunch place so not unusual. Will definitely be coming back!!

This is the perfect brunch spot in SoMa! The prices are so fair & they give you SO much food. We went on a Saturday during brunch hours and it was packed. Definitely recommend getting a reservation ahead of time.

Our favorites:
- Tom yum omelette: this is spiced to perfection & the millionaires bacon cuts through the sweet/sour taste
- Hainan chicken: chicken is very tender
- garlic noodles w honey pork: yum the garlic noodles are delicious here
-Thai tea: aesthetics sweet bite for dessert

Also would definitely have to recommend their drinks. Our favorite was the Vietnamese Dalgona coffee & the lychee martini! Highly recommend coming here. The ambiance is casual and cute and the service is so kind they make you feel like family.

I came for a weekend brunch, and would definitely recommend making a reservation as it gets very busy. I've been here for dinner before as well but brunch was a highlight.

The menu items seemed quite unique and the amazing smell from the pandan waffles at the table over kept wafting over. My table got the Thai tea French toast and chicken waffle. The chicken was definitely my favorite, so juicy and tasty!

We arrived a little over 30 mins before they closed for their midday break and the team there welcomed us in! Our server was friendly and attentive. The restaurant has a diner vibe. I had the Garlic Noodles w/Crispy Chicken because they were all out if the five spice chicken. The meal was tasty and fresh. Great place for a quick lunch.

Great food with fast and friendly service. I found myself struggling to decide what to order because everything looked so good
- we just walked in without reservations at noon (although we saw a big line a few minutes after we went in)
- the interior was popping, lots of nice decor and filled with people
- the garlic noodles were great and the waiter recommended the honey pork

I come here OFTEN. Very very very often. Their fried rice is the best, but i'm trying to eat everything on the menu so maybe i'll change my mind later

here are some food ratings:

garlic noodle bowl with steak, 8/10 - so yummy but i think i should try a different protein bc the steak is just ok! however so yum for the price
crispy chicken fried rice, 9/10 - i think i ate this in 5 min ngl
omelette fried rice, 10/10 - pls tell me how you make this i gotta know

the service here is always great! i've had small issues with my food before but i think the service makes up for it.

the restaurant itself is pretty small so the ambiance is just okay but it's a go to spot for my lunch break!
Device was quick and nice and the food is delicious! Portion is really big, would come back again! Love it

Mr. East is one of my favorite brunch spots in SF! The outside is a little unassuming but the inside is welcoming & has a modern decor vibe. After taking the Caltrain up to the city we walked over from the station since it's only about 10 minutes away.

We were immediately sat & started with some of their specialty drinks (pink dalgona & strawberry matcha) which were really tasty & super cute! The dalgona even came with strawberry hearts which is perfect since Valentine's is right around the corner.

The food was also great - our favorites were the Thai Tea French Toast & Pandan Waffles w Fried Chicken. I was a little skeptical of the chicken & waffles tbh because a lot of places are good but not great. However I was so pleasantly surprised, literally crunch asmr as I bit into it lol.

Was looking for anything new to me nearby a meeting I had and this place came up and there was a great parking place right there so...
The place was jammed so I ordered at the kiosk to go but then the place cleared out (classic SF) so I asked for a table. All smiles no problem! I had the fried rice omelette- look up the ingredients!! - it was stunningly good! A bit of spice a bit of sweet and a bit of savory. Top 3 egg dishes I've ever had!
The room is b-fast lunch efficient clean and brisk while always friendly.

I'll be back soon to try more dishes but if the vibe of other diners is any indication, I will love these dishes too.

Not only was the food incredible, but the service was phenomenal! Our server repeatedly checked on us and upon overhearing that we were celebrating two birthdays, he told us that he would bring us some dessert after our meal to celebrate. My friend had also mentioned wanting to make rice at home to eat her leftovers later that night. Our server overheard and brought her a scoop of rice to go!

The food we ate was so delicious. I had the Tom yum omelette fried rice and I would order it again if I could. The filling had large shrimp, sautéed peppers and onions, and tom yum paste. The omelette was topped with their sriracha bacon (sweet/mild heat and you can order a side of it if your meal doesn't come with it). Our table also shared their special French toast which had a delicious strawberry compote on top. To drink, I had the lychee refresher - not too sweet and came with two pieces of lychee fruit. The dessert that the server gave us was fried bananas with ice cream.

I seriously cannot express how great of an experience we had here on a Sunday for brunch. I am already planning my next trip back (they are near Bart for anyone who doesn't like driving in the city as an FYI).

Mr. East Kitchen in SoMa is such a gem. Tried it for brunch for the first time and everything we tried was killer. The bánh mì, the tom yum soup, and the Vietnamese iced coffee were all super well-executed, and damn, that coffee is basically dessert. Service was 10/10. Highly recommend.

Cute brunch/cafe spot. Highly recommended! Service was on top of refilling water. Portions were very filling and satisfying.

Thai Tea French Toast - Plated beautifully, only wish the toast was soaked in Thai Tea.

Pad Thai - Can't complain, always a staple.

Hai Nan Chicken - Chicken cooked to perfection. Rice was very savory and yummy.

Saigon Steak - Cooked tenderly, highly recommend and very filling.

Iced Butterfly Lychee Fizz and Orange Passion Fruit Breeze - Refreshing asian fusion drinks.

I usually never write reviews however the service here was horrible. First I joined the waitlist on yelp and it said the wait would be 14-28 minutes. Yelp said we were still 15th in line however we had been waiting for about 30 minutes at this point so we decided to go wait outside the restaurant. After waiting outside for another 15 minutes a server finally came to ask if we were on the waitlist. I showed her we were on the yelp waitlist and she said okay and had us wait for a bit longer. After waiting outside I realized they were completely disregarding the Yelp waitlist and seating whoever was waiting outside first. If we had never made the decision to go wait outside the restaurant we would have still been waiting 2.5 hours later since they don't update the Yelp waitlist. Once we finally got seated our food took about an hour to come out and once again, tables who were seated after us were getting their food first. At the very last moment, she had told me one of the items in my dish were sold out, which would have been fine if she had told me at the time I ordered, like she was doing for the rest of the tables. Finally, once my food came out I found a hair under my fried chicken, which I should've taken a picture of however I was too hungry to care at that point.

My wife and I came in here on a Saturday. We made reservations the day before. Walked in, and was immediately seated. Restaurant was full, and a long line started to form after we were seated. Noise level is on the loud side, but nothing too bad. We ordered:

Saigon Steak 4/5 - Plated beautifully. Came with a salad, crispy potatoes, garlic bread, steak and over easy egg on top. The steak was tender with a strong Hoisin flavored sauce. Garlic bread was really good for sopping up the tasty sauce around the steak. Crispy potatoes were excellent. I ended up finishing up the entire plate.

Thai Tea French Toast 3.5/5 - This was also beautifully plated. Was cooked well, crispy on the outside while soft on the inside. The Thai Tea syrup was provided in a cup on the plate. We prefer our syrup to be a bit more sweeter than it actually was, but was good nonetheless. Most likely would try the Berry Crunch French Toast next time.

Overall, service is good and attentive. The fusion of Thai, Vietnamese and American brunch was intriguing. I would come back. One suggestion, avoid parking in the lot one block up the street, that states $20. That is cash only price. I paid via SpotHero, which ended up costing $31.75 to park for about 1 hour.

Food was good. Although I was quite upset because I ordered the strawberry milk and it was $7... my complaint is that the strawberry milk was just the nesquik strawberry powder mixed with whole milk. When I eat brunch I expect the restaurants to make their fruit drinks housemade..

We came here for Labor Day weekend and got seated really fast. The food portions were generous. Really recommend the banana French toast and the omelette. Omelette was stuffed with veggies and shrimp which was delicious.

The Thai tea was really strong and good. Overall had a really good time here! Only downside was there was no AC inside so it was quite hot on a warm day.
BOMB. Been a couple times to the bay but the presentation and taste 10/10. Will be back fosho

First time at Mr East Kitchen for brunch with a friend. They have dishes from different Asian cultures, primarily Southeast Asian food like Thai and Vietnamese. On top of that, they have classic American breakfast dishes as well, including eggs benedict. My friend and I ordered the Saigon Steak, spring rolls, and Tom Yum soup. The soup comes with your choice of meat and was heavier on the meat and veggies, though it would have been ideal if there were more actual soup added. The Saigon Steak was saucy and flavorful - if I ordered this another time I would ask for fewer or no potatoes on the side. Payment was convenient for our party of three as we were able to split each of our portions and each tap our own cards. This is definitely a smaller and more casual brunch spot, so keep that in mind if you have larger parties. I would come back to try their Thai Tea French toast and other dishes when I'm in the area.

We came on a Saturday morning for brunch. We got seated right away. The food was tasty. We got the Tom Yom Omelette, banh mi, pandan waffle and chicken, steak Benedict, and crispy berry French toast.

I recommend the crispy berry French toast. It had cream on the inside, crispy on the outside, and not too sweet. It had just the right amount of tang from the strawberry sauce.

The waffle and chicken was also nice. Chicken was not dry and the waffle was crispy on the outside and had a light taste of pandan. Something different from the typical American brunch place.

The tom yom omelette was a bit spicy so need to be aware. The bacon and garlic bread that came with the omelette were very tasty. The potatoes were nice and crispy.

All the dishes looked aesthetically pleasing and would look great on insta stories.

Overall food was yummy and the menu had a good selection of brunch/asian food. Portions were huge.

I would recommend going early because the line was getting long as we were leaving at around 1pm.

Mr. East Kitchen | San Francisco

1. Pandan Waffles -- pandas waffles, seasonal fruit, served with maple syrup and whipped butter
2. Tom Yum Omelette -- omelet, shrimp, spinach, bell pepper, mushroom, onion tom lump paste, sriracha bacon, served with fried potatoes, garlic toast
3. Chicken Curry -- Thai style red curry, bell pepper, basil, botchy, jasmine rice

Mr. East Kitchen, located at 276 5th St in San Francisco's SOMA neighborhood, specializes in Thai and Vietnamese fusion cuisine. Their menu features a variety of dishes, including brunch options like the Tom Yum Omelette and Pandan Waffles, as well as savory items such as chicken curry.

The Tom Yum Omelette is noted for its unique and fragrant flavor, bursting with taste. The Pandan Waffles are a popular choice, often enjoyed with fried chicken and served with apple mustard and syrup.
Definitely a good place for weekend brunch. Lots of options and good for vegetarians too (my guest recommended it for this reason). Staff is super friendly and chill.

spicy fried chicken sandwich was great, not too much of a crowd on wednesday afternoon. food came out very fast

sandwich did have a little bit of oil but i imagine if you got the plain one there would be less oil. fries were good and the aioli it came with was so good

My friend and I came in at around 1 for brunch and it wasn't too busy. Our server was really attentive and funny and the food came out fast.

We ordered the pandan chicken and waffles and also the garlic noodle bowl with pork. Both portions were really big, especially the garlic noodles. The pork was really flavorful and cooked well with that sweet and salty profile I love.

The chicken and waffles were also delicious and I liked how they cooked the chicken with a thick batter. It comes with mustard as the sauce which I love because it's not that common and I'm a mustard lover but if you don't I would ask if you can swap it for another sauce. The pandan flavor wasn't super strong but it was still yummy.

Cute fusion spot and I would come again!

THE BEST French toast we've ever had

@mreastkitchen is a hidden gem serving Vietnamese-Thai fusion dishes and they are definitely a must try. Service was so nice and it's the cutest spot for brunch and very lively , but they're also open for dinner! They're trying to pick back up again after the pandemic so please check them out, you won't regret it! They have such a variety and everything looked and sounded so good we had a hard time choosing our dishes. Was very happy with what we ordered and everything was delicious! Can't wait to come back and try the other items we were eyeing


- -- -- -
Dalonga Vietnamese Coffee
Butterfly Lychee Fizz
Garlic Fries
Chicken w/ Pandan Waffles
Crispy Chicken Fried Rice
Spicy Fried Chicken Sandwich
Tom Yum Omlette
NEW Crunch Berry French Toast (literally so good, please order this lol) - only available on weekends.

Tried this place out today and it's worthy of the hype I've seen it get. The service is great and the food is even better.

We got the dalgona coffee and matcha latte.
For food we loved the Saigon steak (best steak plate I've ever had from a brunch spot), Thai French toast, crispy chicken fried rice and garlic noodle bowl.

Everything was perfect to us, we will def be back!

Everyone's so nice and the food is delicious!

My husband had his birthday this past weekend and let me choose where we'd go for brunch. I had Mr East Kitchen in my bookmarks since last year? Year before last? I'm not sure, but I've had this place bookmarked and so an opportunity came around and I took it.

It was around 11am-ish on a Saturday morning and we were able to find parking easily across the restaurant. I was worried it'd be too busy because SF and brunch together is a busy combination, but they had bar seats open and we got seated promptly. The menu isn't super extensive which I appreciated and I read someone else's review prior that they had really good fries here so I opted for their garlic fries, hai nan chicken, Christmas matcha drink, and my husband got their salmon benedict.

The atmosphere of the restaurant is nice - all the servers we've spoke with were friendly and engaging, not a quick hello and walk away. It was great being in the environment that was as welcoming as this.

The food was also very good especially the fries. The sauce that came with the hai nan chicken isn't the usual sauce you'd see it paired with, but it was still tasty and slather a bit of it on the rice and it was good to go.

Overall, I'd highly recommend Mr East Kitchen if you're in the area and want brunch!

Wow, this brunch was amazing! Huge portions and delicious flavors. Not a single miss. We tried the saigon steak, spicy sole fish, salmon benedict, and crunch berry french toast (available on weekends only). My favorite was the saigon steak. It was perfectly cooked and so flavorful. The benedict is a classic brunch option and super hearty. The sole fish was perfectly crispy and I loved the eggplants and curry with it. The crunch berry french toast was not too sweet!

Their strawberry matcha was solid (very strawberry forward) and I loved their pink dalgona coffee. The whipped coffee on top was strong and so good (took me back to 2020 when i'd make it everyday at home)! Highly recommend this spot for an asian fusion brunch.

Such a gem in San Francisco -- everything was wonderful!

I came to Mr. East Kitchen for lunch with two dear mom friends, and we were so impressed by how flavorful, thoughtful, and comforting every dish was. You can just feel the care in the food.

We ordered the Thai Tea French Toast, Spicy Bacon Benedict, and the Mr. East Salad -- and truly, not a single bite disappointed. The French toast had this rich, Thai tea flavor that was warm and unique -- unlike anything I've had before. They have a special sauce. The Benedict came with a slightly spicy house-made sauce that totally elevated the dish. And the salad? So fresh, crisp, and well balanced. Oh! Their Saigon steak was amazing too!

The staff were so kind and welcoming, and the vibe of the place just felt like a warm hug. I left feeling full, happy, and already excited to come back.

Whether you're a local or visiting from out of town, this is a place worth making time for.

I checked out Mr. East for a quick dinner and ordered the Hainan Chicken and Taro Milk. The Taro Milk was great and not too sweet which I enjoyed. I do wish they had actual taro pieces in the drink. The Hainan Chicken came with a large portion of chicken on a bed of kale and bok choy with chicken rice, cucumbers and a poached egg. It's definitely a large plate of food and the chicken rice was good but the chicken itself was a bit tough.

The menu is pretty big so I'll be back to try the brunch items and the other fusion dishes!

The service was incredible! The owner went above and beyond to give us a good experience and also brought out thai chilis when I mentioned I like food on the spicier side. The food itself was amazing and we absolutely cleaned out our plates. The ambiance was that of a home-y restaurant. There was a great feeling of community here and I really enjoyed it.

I came here with a few friends after running a 5k and I was so glad that we had reservations because it was packed! I can see why it would be because everything that we tried were delicious! I myself got the

Spicy Fried Chicken sandwich - HUGE! I was barely able to fit my mouth over it to take a bite. The chicken was extra crispy and the fried chicken had a sweet glaze on it. It wasn't spicy at all in my opinion but it was still delicious! The sauce on the side tasted like a mild thousand island but wasn't quite as sweet and more savory. Drizzle that on the sandwich and it was near perfection. The hashbrown on the side was good too. It reminded me of a McDonald's hashbrown and those are fire.

Thai-tea French toast - The Thai tea aspect came from the sauce on the side. It genuinely did taste like Thai tea, aromatic, and not too sweet. The toast itself was nice and soft and each bite felt like I was biting into a pillow. Solid spot for brunch!

Love to see how popular they have become since the Yelp top brunch spot article came out. We live very close to this place and had never seen many folks eating here, so we were quite surprised walking in on a sat to see all tables had been taken. Friendly staff, great service. Food took about 20-25 min to arrive but understand given how busy they were. We ordered:

- Shrimp Benedict (5/5): Juicy plump shrimp with curry hollandaise sauce, potatoes and side salad were a nice touch. Poached eggs were quite runny - watch out for the jalapeños, those were quite the spicy varietal.
- House salad with salmon (5/5): Asked for sauce on the side, which we only need to use a little bit of because the salad itself was packed with delicious flavors - the blueberries were some of the largest I had ever seen. Salmon was cooked perfectly.

One feedback I'd like to give to management is to maybe ask staff to switch gloves between putting away dirty dishes to serving fresh food to customers. We sat by the kitchen area so unfortunately witnessed this - I applaud workers for wearing gloves, but saw them touching their faces and dirty and new dishes with.

Anyways, we would definitely be coming back given how delicious and fresh tasting the foods were. Can't wait to try many other dishes next time! Will be rooting for this place to thrive!

I'm very pleased with my experience here! The portions were very impressive and prices were quite reasonable. The food was flavorful and the options were diverse. The service was friendly and timely, and quite accommodating! Ambiance was simple, nothing particularly memorable. Ultimately I would recommend!

A piece of green plastic or paint came out in the food, but they kept insisting it was stir-fried green onion. I wasn't even asking for a refund or anything -- I just wanted to hear something like, "We'll be more careful next time" or "Sorry about that." But they kept insisting it was green onion until the end, and it left me feeling really upset.

Let me say it again -- it was not green onion or any kind of vegetable. It was 100 % plastic.

We ended our SF anniversary weekend with breakfast at Mr. East Kitchen.
This small diner has a fusion menu with a tasty twist on American classics, like pandan waffles with a side of Thai tea syrup and the Saigon Steak breakfast. Of course, I had to have a Thai tea latte to accompany my waffles. Yum!
Our waiter was friendly and attentive and took great care to make sure we had everything we needed for a satisfying meal from start to finish.
If you find yourself in San Francisco, I definitely recommend this place for a great breakfast with a twist.

I love Asian fusion brunch spots and was so excited to try this spot! I got the chicken waffle which was a pandan waffle with fried chicken on top. It came with syrup and cream on the side, and a huge serving of butter on top, which I had to remove. The chicken fried very nicely and was still juicy inside, but could have been a bit more unique flavor wise in my opinion, and I wish that the pandan taste in the waffle had been a bit stronger.

I'd definitely make a reservation if you're planning on coming here on a weekend- I made a reservation for 2 at noon on a Saturday, and we still had to wait ~10 min for our table. Restaurant is quite noisy and bustling inside and isn't as peaceful of a brunch ambiance as other spots, but had an enjoyable meal here nonetheless!

I came here for a brunch on Saturday and it was packed! Luckily my friend made a reservation so we were seated immediately.

We shared 2 items:
Chicken Waffle ($17.00)
+Fried chicken was crispy and juicy
+Homemade Pandan Waffle had a crisp exterior and fluffy interior with a hint of pandan flavor
+Huge portion: We received a drumstick and a thigh, and they were quite large.
+Orchid was a nice touch
-Fried chicken didn't have a lot of flavor.
-Apple Mustard tasted like honey mustard: Couldn't taste any notes of apple.
-Homemade Syrup tasted like maple syrup.
-The scoop of butter was placed directly on the waffle instead of in a dish on the side like the other condiments.

Spicy Bacon Benedict w/fried potatoes & salad ($19.00)
+Bacon was crispy, savory, and sweet: My friend said it reminded her of Millionaire Bacon, and I agreed.
+Eggs were perfectly poached.
+Fried potatoes were crispy.
+Salad was fresh and a great palate cleanser: It came with kale, spinach, and sliced grape tomatoes, radishes, and radicchio.
+Edible floral petals were a nice touch.
+Huge portion
+Not too spicy (however, if you prefer spicy food you may be disappointed)

*Verdict: We were satisfied with the food and it's definitely one of the more inexpensive brunch options in the city.

However, I'm not sure if I'd come back because the tables were very close to each other, so it felt cramped. In addition, it was very noisy inside so it was hard to catch up with my friend. There was a couple sitting next to me and it seemed like they had to shout across the table.

If I were to come back, I would probably come on a weekday.

Absolutely love this place. The staff is incredibly friendly and the food is extremely delicious.

I highly recommend making a reservation and ensuring your party is on.

They have street parking available.

The restaurant overall is relatively clean with interesting decor.

This place is a hidden gem. We ate here for breakfast . Highly recommend that you order the Spicey Bacon Benedict and the French Toast with fruit. The food was tasteful and well prepared! Also, kudos to the server Ben who was so kind and friendly.
Mr. East has found a way to have the explosion of a variety of food taste into breakfast. Maybe one of the best breakfast I have ever eaten.

Made a reservation for Sunday lunch but still had to wait for 10 minutes before I got seated. They have a relatively small indoor dining space but there are a few outdoor tables and chairs. Very casual ambiance. Garlic noodles were good. I followed the recommendation of my server - that honey pork was the best option for the meat. It was great! Hawaiian Rainbow is a nonalcoholic drink. It was refreshing but a little sweet for me. Giving it a 4/5.

Came to Mr. East for a late brunch and left more than impressed. The food, ambiance, and service were great. Amazing options ranging from soups to pad thai to breakfast. We loved this Asian fusion take on brunch. The fried chicken served on the chicken and waffles is cooked perfectly and falls off the bone while the pandan flavor in the waffle adds to an already bold flavor profile. Their prices are very fair as well! Will definitely come back soon!

Went a few months ago with cousins for brunch. Thai tea French toast was unique! I e never seen that on a menu before. Also ordered Viet coffee which was nice and strong. In all honesty, the toast itself could have been stronger flavored, most of the Thai tea flavoring was just from the sauce it came with. Plating is cute and colorful. Would love to come back and try their other foods like the Tom yum omelette.

Make sure to grab reservations if you go for weekend brunch! Or else be stuck waiting out in the cold/heat.

Make sure to make a reservation, as we didn't and ended up waiting around 40 minutes. The servers were nice though and did their best to get us seated. The Tom yum omelette could've use a bit more flavor, but I won't dock a star for that as the amount of food that we were served was well worth the price. Very lively atmosphere with lots of groups and couples.

Came here for brunch on Saturday with my bf. We originally had a 12:15 reservation but there was a parade on market street that delayed us 20-30 minutes to get to the other side of market street + time it took to find parking. We were going to opt for the 5th street & mission garage like other reviews said but luckily found parking on the street right around the corner on Folsom. We called ahead to tell them we'd be late and they were very understanding.

The tables are small so very cozy inside/close to other tables. I got the Tom Yum Omelette and my bf got the Saigon Steak.

Tom Yum Omelette 4/5- the flavors of the Tom yum were very fragrant and present, very much so that it was a bit overbearing/almost too salty as you ate more and more. It was delicious but I found myself looking for a carb item to balance it out. It did come with two small baguettes with garlic butter on top which was nice and the potatoes were bite sized. The salad helped to balance out the saltiness a bit.

Saigon Steak 4/5 - this one also packed a punch but was really delicious. The meat was tender although some pieces were hard to swallow down. The grilled onions were good to offset the texture and added some crunch to it.

Overall, this is def a very savory/heart Thai fusion brunch place. We'd come again but maybe with friends to share other items as they have so many other options we wanted to try

This unassuming little cafe delivers exceptional brunch with a fusion flare! The dishes are very unique and all are delicious. The shrimp Benedict was amazing -- shrimp cooked perfectly, not chewy or overdone and the hollandaise was perfect. The crispy chicken fried rice was fantastic. The chicken was perfectly light and crispy on the outside and juicy and tender on the inside. The dipping sauce was sweet and savory and the rice was perfect Thai fried rice. Service was prompt and friendly, too. It is small inside and perfect for a couple or small group (3-4) for brunch.

I arrived for lunch, dining-in as a solo diner. They feel very understaffed. It's just a huge crowd of Doordashers (all clad in motorcycle helmets, swarming by the order counter) and people doing takeout. I was the only dine-in. There's plenty of tables and interior seating, but most of the tables weren't cleared out at all while I was there, and table service was non-existent. They did eventually start clearing out the tables, but close to the end of when I had finished eating (1pm).

With the complete lack of service, I made a mistake dining in. It's probably why everyone does takeout.

The atmosphere isn't great. Dirty dishes everywhere and it's a lot of yelling to the delivery drivers on which orders are ready.

The food has good portion sizes. I got the shaking beef and it was good. The beef was tender and flavorful. I would order from here again, but next time via delivery instead of dining in.
Beautiful ambiance we got sat down right away and the food didn't take long at all. And service was A+

**DOORDASH/TAKE OUT ONLY**

Mr. East Kitchen offers modern Asian-fusion cuisine. I tend to order from here when my team asks me last minute because it's one of their favorite places to eat. The menu seems to be a mix of Thai & Vietnamese. There isn't any curry option except for the Pumpkin curry, and there seems to be more noodle-like dishes.

The Pad Thai is rice noodle, eggs, dry shrimp, dry daikon, bean sprouts, chive, tofu, and fried shallots stir fried in tamarind sauce. I got it with shrimp (+$2) and it was good - small and plump. The pad thai's flavor was rich and probably had too much tamarind sauce.

The Pad See Ew is rice noodle, egg, broccoli, carrot, and fried shallots stir fried in sweet soy sauce. I've never heard of pad see ew having carrots, but it was interesting. I think the sweet soy sauce overpowers this dish and the flavor is strong.

Though it's not my first place to normally order from, my team enjoys it. I'm open to trying out their fried rice dishes next!

I came here for the first time and it was good! For drinks, I tried their Thai Milk Tea and the Vietnamese Dalgona Coffee. The Thai milk tea was pretty standard and definitely satisfied my craving for it. Their Vietnamese dalgona coffee could've been stronger, it tasted more like an average dalgona iced coffee.

For food, I got the Tom Yum Omelette and it was tasty! The omelette had some spiciness to it, which I enjoyed. I loved the bite sized potatoes on the side and the salad to balance the meal.

I made reservations since I came with a party of 5 on a Sunday morning. Reservations were easy to get. This place did seem to get quite busy when we left around noon.

Mr. East Kitchen is a gem flavorful food and fun drinks all around!

I had the Banana French Toast with eggs and Sriracha bacon. The French toast was fluffy and perfectly sweet, the eggs were cooked just right, and the bacon had the perfect spicy kick. I also tried the Saigon Steak with Chicken Satay, which was tender and packed with bold flavor.

For drinks, the Matcha Strawberry Latte was smooth and refreshing, and the Pink Dalgona Coffee was both beautiful and delicious.

Impressed with the selection of vegetarian options but they do use the same tofu for all of them it seems. It has the texture of fish tofu without being fishy. Still, more interesting than regular tofu. Tried the vegetarian steak, bahn mi sandwich, and the special tom yum soup (no noodles). They all had the same tofu but with different other spices and ingredients.

Bahn mi - 3/5 kinda disappointing in flavor but the ciabatta bun was novel and tasty. The side of hash browns were great.

Tom yum soup - 5/5 really warming on a cold rainy day and was loaded with tofu and veggies. So good!

Vegetarian steak - 4/5 was really a tofu stir fry with salad, and breakfast potatoes, a fried egg, and two small slices of garlicky toast. All pretty delicious but kind of heavy on the onions.

Thai Tea french toast - 5/5 delicious french toast with fresh fruits on the side. Served with a yummy thai tea sauce too!

If you order tea it's free refills! The jasmine green tea is quite nice. Service is wonderful!

I had the Banana French Toast and I was great!! The dipping sauce was a great contrast to the French Toast and the bananas had a caramelized layer on them which was a great surprise. Fyi, the cokes are sold as a 12oz cans. I will come back and try other dishes.

A friend and I checked out Mr East Kitchen for brunch on the recommendation of another friend and didn't regret it. The flavors are a unique fusion of Thai and Vietnamese cuisines. I loved the creative ingredients in my Omelette Fried Rice. We were blown away by the service. If you happened to glance around the room, someone immediately came to see if you needed anything. The dining room isn't fancy but it's energetic with a diverse clientele. Friends who have gone on my recommendation have come back to thank me. I will be back again soon.

This spot was so busy on the weekend! I was surprised because most spots in SOMA are pretty quiet on weekends and even closed but maybe that was why they were busy. It is somewhat small and given the business, I'd suggest making a reservation. Parking nearby is not great most days but you can find some options on Sundays since most street cleaning restrictions are lifted (read the signs of course).

Overall the food was quite good and so was the service although we felt a little rushed as upon arrival for our 11:45 am reservation, they immediately told us we needed to leave by 1 pm due to a large party. The service felt like it had lulls at times and then there was a bit of rush at the end - would have loved them to offer a to-go container or something. But they did offer refills of water and coffee and generally no major complaints.

My friend liked the Crunchy Brioche french toast and found it to be not too eggy like she found most french toast. It did sound like it was somewhat on the sweet side and maybe one note. The spicy bacon benedict was quite tasty but the bacon is not the least spicy despite it being "sriracha bacon" and I don't have a huge spicy tolerance. All the flavors went together well and it was a solid portion between the benedict, the potatoes, and the side of fruit ($1 extra or you can get salad for no charge). It did fall apart a bit when eating but was definitely a dish I'd get again. The eggs were perfectly poached, the portion of bacon was nicely distributed throughout the entire english muffin, and the curry hollandaise was great though it didn't seem that different than a regular hollandaise.

The regular coffee (with oat milk) was a lot better than I expected and quite good. My friend didn't like the matcha strawberry drink she got though and said it had little matcha flavor and was a bit too sweet.

Overall, 4 stars from me. Personally I would prefer a slightly more relaxed, non-rushed brunch but if you are going to be in the area or looking for something somewhat fast (assuming there's no wait or you have a reservation) I think it's a good option.

Great Southeast Asian food. The concept is slightly fusion-y, but it doesn't dilute the quality or intensity of the dishes. For example I had Cha Siu pad thai. The pork was tender and it was perfect for this dish. Also had som tum and shrimp tom yum soup. Lots more menu to explore, so return visits to come...

Space is small and stripped down (which is a good thing, IMHO). The name of the place captures it all, and they live up to the billing.

What an amazing brunch/lunch spot. This is an Asian fusion restaurant. They serve brunch all day, but they also have some amazing Thai dishes for lunch. We came in at around 12 thirtyish and I was kind of feeling more lunch food so I opted to get the salmon stirfry that came with Jasmine rice. It was super delicious and flavorful. A decent portion of salmon came with it. I also ordered the pink dalgona coffee drink, which was so good and definitely picture worthy. It was super cute to be honest. All their drinks look amazing and I can't wait to go back here and try their strawberry Matcha and also probably one of their brunch dishes this time. We didn't have to wait in line surprisingly but I do hear this place can get pretty busy so would suggest coming early.

Came here just for a quick coffee stop -- and honestly, I found it to be quite impressive given the amount of food they offered. (This is in hopes that I will come back again and actually try their food forreals next time).

Service was welcome to the public especially to us. The latte I got had a good balance of whole milk and coffee, and sweetness was exactly what I had ordered -- less sweet for the win!

Love the ambiance too. Though it is next to abandoned buildings, I think that this restaurant has a potential to expand and encourage other businesses to open similar kinds of businesses too.
Go to take out place. Live their crispy chicken fried rice and Hainan Chicken rice. Fast and healthy. Hands down best Thai food in soma.

Came here for brunch with a friend on a Sunday noon and didn't have to wait too long to be seated. The interior is small, but there's plenty of seating inside and the decor is very classy with the plants and greenery.

It took a few tries to get someone to come take our order. I ordered the Fried Chicken and Pandan Waffle and Ice Butterfly Lychee Fizz. My friend got the Vegan Sandwich. Our food took a while to get to us (around 20 minutes).

Fried Chicken and Pandan Waffle: 5/5, I really liked the apple mustard for my chicken, and the homemade syrup was great too. The chicken was crispy yet tender, and the waffle was nice and fluffy. Good portions!

Ice Butterfly Lychee Fizz: 5/5, love the touch of the two lychee fruits as a topping. The drink was a beautiful purple color. Definitely a drink on the sweeter side.

Vegan Sandwich: 2/5, it was fairly flavorless and didn't really come together as a "sandwich." The hash browns felt like they were heated up from frozen patties, and it felt like it needed a sauce or something to add moisture and flavor to it. The side fruit was good quality.

Overall, had a good time catching up with my friend but would order other things on the menu instead of the Vegan Sandwich, which is unfortunate since there are only so many vegan things on the menu in the first place. I would be interested in trying more of the savory things on the menu next time like the Tom Yum Omelette!
Absolutely excellent! Great service, terrific food and so timely. I love the young vibe it has. If they ever upgrade the place it will be an easy 10/10

First time here today and here's my review broken down:
