Interior - cute, simple decor, well lit, small but cozy. Bathroom was clean, which is important to me as well.

Food - the fried chicken was lightly battered, crispy, not greasy, enough flavor to my liking. Thai French toast is something I've never had before but it was good, not great but good! Not overly sweet at all.

Drinks - peppermint mocha not too sweet and matcha latte was perfectly presented! I'm not a fan of the strawberries added at the bottom but I'd have it again next time, just without the strawberries.

Service - friendly and fast!

Overall, not bad for a first visit. I would come back and give them another try but order other items on the menu. When our food came out, it got cold quick; hopefully next time that's not the case.

I had an amazing experience here! The banana flavor french toast was soft and tasted natural. I'm not a big fan of banana flavor but I would order this again! The syrup had less banana flavor in my opinion, but still good and sweet. I'd highly recommend the bacon Benedict too. Very filling too.

We enjoyed service with the waiters. They were extra polite and friendly. They created a friendly environment for us!

Great service, great location, great food. When going to SF it's always scary to park and find a safe location but this place is in a location. The service was great and the server was so honest. They are QUICK bringing your food and drinks. We got seated right away and got our food and finished all within less than an hour. The drunken noodles were our fav. Everything tastes great though.

One of the best restaurants in SF! The service was amazing, and the food was so good my whole family left almost too full
I love how the food is pretty healthy while also being delicious. The drinks are fantastic as well, and I highly recommend the waffles which were even better than I was expecting. My family will definitely be eating at Mr East every time we visit San Francisco.

GET THE HONEY PORK GARLIC NOODLES!!! You won't regret it. The pork is incredibly flavorful and they give you SOOO much meat. You can't really see the size of the bowl but it was huge. There was so much food I stuffed my stomach and still had half left. Will definitely come back since I'm very interested in trying their other items!!

Came here last weekend for brunch with some friends. We made a reservation but were able to be seated earlier, which was nice of the hosts! We were a party of 5. Parking is street and/or structure parking (we parked by the YB parking lot across from Bloomingdale's for $5/hr). Easily accessible by public transit (steps away from Powell Street station).

I ordered a Lychee mimosa as my main beverage for brunch. It was a tad sweet, mostly from the sugar syrup from canned lychees. Still tasty and refreshing though.

For my main, I had the shrimp benedict, which was very delicious. Eggs were perfectly poached, sufficient amount of shrimps, accompanied by a nice curry sauce instead of your typical hollandaise sauce. Portions were very big! I had it accompanied with a side of seasonal fruit (which the host joked around saying that the seasonal fruit selection hasn't changed in years... haha). I enjoyed the fruits, specifically the blueberries which were super sweet! Our group also shared the Thai tea French toast, which was a nice little sweet treat to share for everyone.

Overall, a solid Asian-inspired brunch option in SF. Hope to be back again!

Excited to come here as Mr. East lists at No. 10 on Yelp's best brunch in the country, we made reservations and were seated right away on a Sunday morning.

Service was exceptionally friendly in this lively well lit restaurant with simple diner seating and wall decorations. (The waiter's worth the 25% suggested tip when it's time to tap out.)

We ordered Thai Tea French Toast 4/5, Steak Benedict 4/5, Pandan waffle with Fried Chicken 3/5, and Hot Wings with Garlic Fries 4/5. The portions are generous, fruit on the side were fresh.

The stars were the pandan waffles and garlic fries. The fried chicken meat did not taste juicy fresh; it had a bit of funky taste. The spicy chicken wings were neither crispy nor spicy.

The drinks we ordered, Orange Passionfruit Breeze and Thai Lime Tea were both refreshingly good.

Price here is reasonable for SF.

It's a cute, small restaurant, but it also gives very much a Pho restaurant type of feel at the same time. I came here to have breakfast, so it wasn't too busy thankfully. However, the service was a bit slow and took a while for them to take my order and give waters.

I will say though, that the food was delicious and the portions were very generous!

server was really fun and attentive! food was decent; i ordered the chicken and waffle which was really tasty. hash brown patties were good but a little bit too oily. my friend got the thai tea french toast and actually found the toast
to be a little tough; she said she wouldn't order it again. the breakfast sandwiches are a little small-- they come on a single english muffin. all in all, a decent brunch spot at a good price point with good service.

I see why it is so popular. Great service. Thank you Tran. Inside joke "you know what the doctor say?" I had the salmon Benedict with curry hollandaise sauce. Add$1 for fruit. I got the salad instead and they have the nicer greens. Dressing was just right. Not too much and just enough over the greens. Curry sauce had a tiny kick. The potatoes were done perfectly, cubed, crunchy outside and soft inside. None were burnt and not greasy. Perfect runny eggs. The muffin was soggy. Loved the spinach, cooked. Salmon had skin which is the best part. Good portion of salmon. Was a tad overcooked. My eating mates loved their food too. Salmon curry with brown rice. Morning crispy chicken salad. Limeade fizz. Lychee jasmine tea. We love their food. Yes, it is pretty tight space but everyone was enjoying their food and conversation.

This was bookmarked for awhile and had a weekday off so decided to check it out. I also found out this place is the listed #10 as the top 100 brunch places by Yelp in the country.

Parking can be a bit tough since it is close to downtown but we got lucky and parked 1/2 a block away. This place is located outside of a new building and oddly situated. I made reservations ahead of time just in case but they weren't busy so we would have gotten seated with or without a reservation but I like to make reservations just in case.

We get seated and there was alot we wanted to try. I ordered the garlic noodle bowl with shrimp and my friend got a Hai Nan chicken and we shared the Thai tea waffles. When our food came out, it looked great and the taste amazing. Everything tasted so fresh. I would order the same things again, but I would like to try their other dishes.

I also order the lychee fizz drink and that was good too.

Overall a good brunch place.. Location not best due to parking but I would come back.

Got the Tom yum omelette. It was very interesting. It had the strong spicy, salty and sour flavors of Tom yum soup. It ended up being a bit too salty for me, so I couldn't quite finish it, but otherwise I really enjoyed the unique experience. I want to try their other items next time.

I recently switched co-working spaces nearby and wanted something good and quick! I had been to Mr. East Kitchen awhile back, but I am so glad I went for lunch! I got the Bo Kho, a Vietnamese beef stew, and I was taken back to my childhood. You know when you eat some comfort food and you're like, everything is alright with the world? Anyways, that's what I felt. The service actually took a minute because they were busy, but when I asked where my food was, they offered me a free drink to apologize for the wait! I got the Butterfly Lychee Fizzy drink and it was super yummy! The ambiance was a bit noisy bc of the number of people there for lunch (on a Tuesday!) and all the hard surfaces, but places like this remind me that small businesses are pretty amazing here in SF. Anyways, hope you try it!

Been to a lot of Asian fusion brunch places in sf. The other places have better ambiance and decor than Mr. East but I had the best food and boba here. Loved this shrimp Tom yum omelette so much with the millionaire bacon on top. The fruit tea was really refreshing too. Other people at my table were not as satisfied with their food items. My tip would be to avoid the non brunch items (ie. Soup, pho etc) which were not as good.

Absolutely loved and enjoyed this place so much for brunch! The only thing is their yelp waitlist didn't really work or they weren't updating it, but we got seated decently quickly after coming in. We got the crispy veggie roles for apps which was soo good, loved the crunch texture and soft fillings inside. We shared the Thai tea French toast which was so so yummy and I'm not even super into Thai tea but this flavor pairing was so delicious and also loved the fruit on the side. We also got the drunken noodle which wasn't really the typical thick pad kee mao that you get at a Thai spot - it was chow mein noodles, but we actually ended up loving the flavors since it felt more like a sweet/savory brunch vibe! So yummy and we finished everything. I was disappointed though that none of the coffees could be made decaf. My friend got the dalgona coffee which was really yummy too. I'd love to come back and try more! Service was also fantastic, they brought everything out super fast and all the waiters were friendly and sweet (one was particularly humorous and really made the experience even more great)!!

Interesting food options that accommodate someone wanting fries as well as a rice dish. My 6-year old and I had lunch here before visiting the Children's Creativity Museum a few blocks away. We were promptly seated along the windows and had impeccable timing because shortly after, there was a small line waiting for seating.

I ordered fries and chicken wings and basil chicken. My 6-year old was happy to eat both dishes, and I ended up packing up leftover fries and chicken wings while we finished the basil chicken and rice. The fries were tasty and crispy, but could have used more garlic. The basil chicken was flavorful and the rice and egg were perfect. The serving sizes seemed appropriate as I wasn't hungry or overstuffed.

The service was friendly and but also gave me time to enjoy my meal and checked in just enough without making me feel like I was being monitored. The interior of the restaurant is clean and well decorated. The large windows let in a lot of light. There are multiple tables that can be moved together to accommodate a larger group, and there was a party of maybe 8-10 congregating in one area. Overall the sitting area is pretty small, so I imagine that a larger party would probably have to call in advance. Lastly, the bathroom was also clean.

I would love to eat here again and try more items from the menu.

There's a lot to choose from, we just by what we thought looked good on the video menu on the wall screens.

Easy to get seated, customer service is nice. Food was okay, nothing I think about in my head after.

If I could have gotten something, it would have been the fried chicken dishes. It looked real good.

Our dishes were "okay", nothing I would come back for again.

Honestly every time I come here I am impressed. Their service is fast. The food is amazing and they keep the menu fresh with new ideas and specials all the time while preserving the staples. They have fancy dishes that you can pay a lot for (which are totally worth it) and dishes at very affordable prices which they could raise a bit and I'd still say they are amazing. Can't recommend this place enough. They even decorate for the season!

The food and service are amazing. I wasn't feeling too well one morning and the staff recommended the Tom yum soup. It was incredible. Definitely the best thing to have when you're not feeling well. Their other meals are perfect for brunch. Very convincing location and reasonable prices.

Saw a video about this Asian brunch spot, and as an avid fusion and brunch enthusiast, I had to try this place out. Came here with a friend on a Friday at 12:00 PM and we were immediately seated at a small table sandwiched between two others. The atmosphere inside the restaurant is a bit cramped and loud, with one glance to the left making for awkward eye contact with the tables next to you, but overall good enough to catch a quick and casual bite with friends.

I had such a hard time deciding to get, from the Thai tea french toast to the hainan chicken to the garlic noodles, the options are endless. I settled for the Tom yum omelette that's filled with perfectly cooked shrimp, a tom yum paste, and sautéed mushrooms and bell peppers. The dish is supposed to come with bacon on top, but I opted for extra shrimp instead

Honestly, the flavor didn't really stand out to me. Kind of felt like I was just eating two separate things--egg and a shrimp stir fry. Good omelette but I wish I tried something else for $21. They give generous portions, with hefty sides of crispy breakfast potatoes, a tangy house salad, and two slices of a baguette (they got a little soggy and stale from the sauce dripping out from the omelette).

Service is amazing! They gave my friend and I ample time for us to finalize what we wanted to order. They also waited patiently for my friend and I to finish catching up, which was long after we had finished our food, before coming up to us with boxes and the bill.

A must try brunch spot in San Francisco!

Food: I ordered the Tom Yum omelette and I enjoyed it overall. It definitely tasted like Tom Yum. The portion of shrimp in it was generous. There was soup in the omelette, but not too much where the egg was soggy. The "Sriracha" bacon was rich, but did not taste like Sriracha. The potatoes, toast, and salad on the side were pretty standard. The lychee jasmine tea tasted like canned lychee tea.

Service: Servers were friendly and even offered a free bag when leaving with leftovers.

Ambiance: Seating inside the restaurant is not too extensive, so I recommend making a reservation in advance, especially for brunch on the weekends or large parties. The restaurant and bathroom itself was clean.

Stopped in here for lunch. I started with the garlic fries which were so tasty and crispy. I got the thai French toast which was just okay to me, I usually like my French toast to be sweeter. The eggs were just okay as well. The sirarcha bacon was SOOOO GOOD!! all in all there were a few hidden gems in my meal and the food came out pretty quick which was most important to me at the time!

Delicious brunch! A group of friends went with me for my birthday and we were all not disappointed. I ordered a Hainanese chicken for brunch. I'm used to having broth with my hainanese chicken but the restaurant doesn't make soup during breakfast hours.

The staff was so nice to make me a single broth anyway!

10/10 must visit place

The owner was super personable! He talked with my table and several others while we waited for our food. His suggestions for what to order were spot on! I will absolutely come back next time I visit SF!

Side note: the Back to the Future Musical was fun. Not a remake of the movie!

I've had this spot saved on my list for a while now and I'm so glad I finally got to try it! I made a reservation easily and my friends and I got seated right away. We ordered the lychee mimosa to share and there was actually a lot in the pitcher for $30, very worth it! Also got the Thai tea french toast and it was a crowd favorite because it might've been the best french toast we've ever had. I got the garlic noodle bowl with pork and the portion was huge but also very flavorful. My friends all enjoyed their dishes as well and we definitely plan on coming back.

Parking: 2/5
As it is with most parts of SF, it definitely takes a hot minute to find nearby parking, especially free street ones. But it is possible! We were able to find one for our compact car about a 5 min walk from the restaurant.

Service: 5/5
Our waiter was super friendly and helpful, even obliged to help us snap a quick photo despite the busy atmosphere.

Food: 4.7/5
The Saigon Steak was absolutely delicious! Cooked to the perfect degree of softness yet still chewy, and don't get me started on the sauce it was in! Just chef's kiss! The thai tea french toast was also amazing! The toast was soft to bite, yet still had a slight crunchy exterior. Combined with the thai tea sauce, the toast was so good. Finally, the pumpkin curry was yummy in taste, but a bit disappointing; I personally enjoy my kabocha squashes on the softer side and this one was quite hard to bite.

Drinks: 4/5
We got the Thai tea, lychee jasmine tea, and black milk tea float. All were quite good, albeit a bit on the pricier side. Wasn't a huge fan of the thai milk tea as they use soy milk, which I just personally don't like. The black milk tea float wasn't too sweet (at 75% sweetness) which I liked. And the lychee jasmine tea was fragrant and sweet, as expected, and I would consider getting it again.

TLDR; Great, quick service despite the rush. Food is overall great, would recommend getting the Saigon Steak and lychee green tea!
Fast service, casual dining with good food. The Tom yum omelette was unique with a little kick to it and the fried rice chicken was breaded just right.
The best Thai fusion brunch place in SOMA. I'm usually not a fan of fusion cuisine. This place tool me away. The service is unmatched as well as pricing.

This has been my go to brunch spot lately. The food never disappoints and I've tried a good half of their menu. The dalgona coffee and other fun drinks are always a hit as well. One of my favorites is their crispy chicken. (If you're reading this please make a crispy chicken Benedict ) The servers are always super nice and friendly. We've been going here often because they almost always have day of reservations available. Also don't sleep on their tom yum!

My cousin took me here when I was visiting the city and it blew my expectations. It was strange seeing the lone restaurant among multiple closed businesses but i could see why. From the drinks to the food everything was so good, quick and fresh.

New Year's Day, hungover me couldn't wait for some food and this hit the spot. The only thing was the mango sticky rice mango wasn't too ripe but guess that's what happens when you get it in winter time.

I had the lychee mimosa and coconut cream coffee and both gave me the morning boost I needed.

Definitely a good mom and pop spot to hit up.

Came here over the weekend (Sunday) to celebrate a birthday, and we had a group of 6 so it was hard to find a reservation in the area. We decided to drive over to Mr. East and the parking situation was not bad at all. They also had plenty of reservation times so definitely brownie points for that!

The restaurant has a good amount of seating and we were able to comfortably sit at a table for 8.

We ordered:
Thai French Toast
Crispy Chicken Fried Rice
Tom Yum Omlette
Mr. East Salad
Chicken Waffle

My favorite was the Crispy Chicken Fried Rice - the chicken was super crispy but wasn't dry! The Tom Yum omlette was a close second for me too - good flavor, some of the larger chunks of shrimp were a little dry but still good.

The Thai French Toast was good, fluffy..not a ton of Thai tea flavor except for in the sauce, but still a solid choice for those who can't have brunch without carbssss!!

Service was SO AMAZING! they switched the music to happy birthday for the entire restaurant so they could surprise my friend with fried banana and ice cream. Seriously...so frickin nice of them. 10/10 would recommend!!

Service was excellent. The pink dalgona coffee was perfectly sweet and light but not overly sugary. It paired well with the dalgona coffee when mixed in. The pink drink itself had a light strawberry and coconutty type of flavor, kind of like the Starbucks pink drink but less artificial flavors. The strawberries were cut perfectly into cute little hearts!

The caramelized banana French toast was amazing! Albeit the French toast could've had more of a "crunch" to the toast, the way the banana was caramelized was like a crème brûlée! It was perfectly hot so eat that banana quick because after 20 minutes the caramelized part will melt (still good though).

A very nice and simple brunch. Very busy at 2pm on a Sunday but enough seating for a walk in.

This little, casual Thai fusion place really hit the spot. The omelette fried rice was super flavorful with a nice bit of heat. I also tried the spicy bacon benedict--really tasty, though the spicy bacon kind of overpowered the curry hollandaise. The fried potatoes were awesome--crispy outside, soft inside. And the Vietnamese dalgona coffee was a great way to wrap things up. Service was quick! Would definitely come back for brunch again.

This was a great find on my San Fran trip. We actually unintentionally showed up slightly before opening hours and they were nice enough to seat us. Service was very attentive with great recs from the staff. Its spacious and very clean.

We ordered the Tom Yum omelette and waffle. The omelette was bangin. One of the best I've had in a while! The mix of shrimp and veggies came together so well and the siracha bacon alone tasted great.

Menu is quite extensive with various options for everyone. If I were a local Id definitely make this a staple in my rotation.

I got together with friends for lunch/brunch here and we made reservations for our party of 7. The place is small located on 5th Street near Folsom. It is best if you park in the Mission Street parking garage as parking can be difficult. The food and service are great. We ordered the Saigon Steak, Tom Yum Soup Noodles, Chicken Fried Rice, Combo Waffle with fruit and eggs, Chicken and Waffle, and I order the Chicken and Waffle with siracha bacon and eggs. The food came out piping hot and we enjoyed our meals! Chicken was moist and tender. My friends also ordered the two of the lychee drinks and enjoyed every sip.

From the moment I walked into Mr. East, I knew I was in for a treat. The Thai twist had me intrigued. The food left me utterly speechless. Every bite was a delightful surprise. Let's start with the Vietnamese coffee--it was simply to die for. I found myself almost ordering another, but knew it would keep me up all night :( The highlight of my meal was the spicy bacon Benedict. It struck the perfect balance between sweet and spicy, leaving my taste buds singing. The presentation was nothing short of beautiful, each dish looking like a work of art!! We had to sample the Thai tea French toast which was perfect!!! Not too sweet, but far from bland. Adding to the delightful experience was the fast and friendly service. Despite the amazing food and service, I was shocked there wasn't a line wrapped around the building. A hidden gem!! Would recommend to everyone and anyone!!

A great addition to the brunch scene here in San Francisco. Located in SOMA, Mr. East offers a wide selection of delicious milk tea and coffee, Asian-fusion brunch items, and traditional Thai dishes.

Walked in on a Saturday around 11AM, place was busy but we were seated immediately. Staff are welcoming and accommodating. Space is bright and clean. Been here a few times and food quality remains consistent. Portions are huge too so come hungry.

Everyone come dine at Mr. East, you won't be disappointed!

Mr. East Kitchen is a fusion between Thai and Vietnamese cuisine. Not only is their food aesthetically pleasing, it's also very tasty!

Portions & pricing here is great. Lovely staff & delicious food! The owner (Amy) is so nice and takes great pride in ensuring their customers are happy and enjoy the food.

My friend and I ordered:

sriracha bacon fried chicken & pandan waffle -- best combo!

thai tea french toast -- I thought it was ok. Not for me!

salmon benedict with fried potato & seasonal fruit -- love how much salmon there was! So flakey and soft. Poached eggs cooked nicely.

shrimp tom yum soup -- nice balance of sweet and savory. Beautiful arrangement of shrimp.

iced butterfly lychee fizz
thai tea with boba (w/ oat milk)

I would come back if I was in the area! I would love to check out more of their menu! Everything sounded so good!!

Got the hainan chicken and it was the worst hainan chicken I have ever had. It was overcooked and insanely dry, and the sauce was really weird. Pretty insulting to Asian cultural food.

Would probably come back to try other dishes, but I highly do not recommend Hainan chicken!!

A casual eatery with eclectic Asian-inspired dishes.
EATS:
I had the shrimp egg benedict which was really tasty. My friends liked their dishes such a simple pumpkin dish with rice but was very good, according to my BFF. Another friend had the Hai nan chicken.

+Portions are generous and the prices are reasonable. I would love to go back for lunch again!

-Order at the counter. Service was friendly but a little slow during lunch time.

Absolutely love this place! Came here for Sunday brunch and it was a little packed but we made reservation on Yelp so we got seated quickly. The ambiance is chill and the restaurant has big clear windows which help brighten the dining space.

I love that they give you the option to make a combo meal of French toast and eggs/bacon, the Saigon beef was very tender and flavorful, and everything was well plated and tasted amazing! Will definitely be back!

Absolutely delectable food. Their bacon is a must-have; it's got a sweet and spicy glaze on it that pairs perfectly with egg. The Thai Tea French Toast was good as expected and the fruit was delightfully fresh. Also got the ice lychee butterfly tea drink, which was a great light refresher I was looking for that morning. Food is both gorgeous and tasty. Would highly recommend.
The bahn mi was a little dry, I wish they had used more sauce. The portions are huge though I was fully stuffed from my meal. The service is quick as well and they had plenty of seating.

Delicious basil chicken. Not oily at all, which I loved. The sunny-side-up egg on top was a nice touch. Loved that it came with complimentary steamed rice (since some places charge extra for that), kale, and bok choy - healthy and tasty. Flavors were on point, and the portion size was satisfying.

Could I eat here almost every day? Yep. Delicious Asian fusion cafe, casual yet clean and nice enough for a ladies celebration brunch - which we had on a weekday. Sweet, helpful staff, their menu is attentive to vegan, vegetarian and meat based peeps.

Breakfast, brunch, lunch and dinner options. I've had the Hainan chicken, salmon curry, Pad see ew, spicy sole. Bok choy, eggplant accompanied some. Nicely presented with an orchid Avocado and egg toast, Thai Tea French Toast are some early options but much more is there including espresso drinks and Jasmine lychee tea.

The food was good, but the restaurant was so incredibly noisy. We had a business lunch and ended up having to move outside. Outside was also noisy because of the cars driving by.

I enjoyed my spring rolls and passion fruit tea. t was a light and refreshing lunch.

We sat outside so the waitress forgot about us and I had to flag her down for the bill.

Walked in and got a seat for 2 right away. The service is pretty slow considering 3 servers and half the restaurant was full. Food was ok, nothing great to take home. The restaurant was clean but slightly crowded. I recommend it if you want something basic with a little presentation. Maybe we got the wrong food to try but even if so, wasn't something to take home.

Went here before a movie at AMC. Service is friendly and fast. We went in on a Sunday and hence no business crowd.

Food had nice diversity and flavor. Had the Kang Pan and spicy basil chicken. Nice tastes and spice to them (we get thai hot), but in this case it was not really hot.

Good place to try, lots of diversity in the menu.
I really enjoyed the service and the food was so good. I ordered a Tom Yum Noodle Soup with grilled chicken and the broth was so flavorful. If you like savory and sour soups, this is perfect.

Surprisingly great - kind of in unassuming area of SoMa, but came here with three friends during a quiet workweek lunch day and we all really enjoyed our food. I was skeptical because this is one of those fusion places that does every type of Asian cuisines, but I got the hainanese chicken rice and it was quite tasty -- not really authentic, but tasty.

Also, the price was really good on the day we came-- there was a deal where we got a whole dish for free. Not sure if they still do that but it sure made me happy. Would come back and try more dishes or the weekend brunch

I was visiting friends in the city for the weekend and somehow ended up at Mr. East Kitchen not once but two times! It was just that good. I dropped in on Friday and Sunday morning for a quick brekkie and was happy with both experiences.

Immediately upon entering the establishment, the staff was friendly and attentive. I was seated right away and brought a menu and asked if I had any questions. I ordered the egg and cheese breakfast sandwich ($8) + added an extra egg ($2) + added sriracha bacon ($2) to make the perfect little breakfast sandwich. Not to mention, the sandwich comes with a huge side of fries (which are addictive.)

Their menu is unique and creative in that it's American Asian fusion so they have items that you wouldn't necessarily find everywhere. Overall, awesome spot and still thinking about Mr. East!

Saw this Asian fusion brunch place on Instagram, and decided to check it out  The place is pretty cute inside, and we were able to make a reservation through Yelp, so we didn't have to wait at all (came for Saturday brunch).

Although I was strongly eyeing the Thai Tea french toast, I'm not a super big fan of a sweet brunch, so I went for the Drunken Noodle Beef instead. Also treated myself to a Vietnamese Dalgona Coffee! My friend got the Tom Yum Omelette and a Coconut Milk Latte. We also shared a Mango Sticky Rice for dessert, which tbh I am always craving

I thought the Drunken Noodle Beef was so delicious, it was very nicely flavored and the portion size was great. I also loved my Vietnamese Dalgona Coffee! Despite being very sensitive to caffeine, it didn't give me a headache or make me feel unwell (although I was up real late that night). Also! Despite it not being mango season, the mangoes in the mango sticky rice were very sweet (albeit a bit crunchy, but love anyway).

Do be warned that it is a bit on the pricier side, the total per person was about $40, including tax and tip.

Came for brunch on a random Sunday with a group of 4 at 12. We did not have a reservation, but they managed to get us seated within 10 minutes inside. Very friendly service throughout. It looks like this is a family-owned business as I saw a couple teenagers working.

I'm a sucker for a thai-fusion menu. I was actually hoping for more fusion items but there was really only two: tom yum omelette and thai tea french toast. To eat, I got the tom yum noodle soup with fried chicken and we also shared the thai tea french toast as a table.

The food came out in weird timing. My dish and my friends came out a good 5 minutes before our other dishes so I was just staring at my food in hunger while waiting. Finally the food all came and it was yummy. I do wish there was a heavier tom yum flavor in the soup but it was still delicious. The fried chicken was perfection. The breading was done very well. The thai tea french toast was not too sweet (the highest compliment!!) and the perfect way to end the meal.

If I was in the neighborhood, I would come back!

This was one of my all time favorite brunch experiences. And it turns out I'm not alone because shortly after I went, it was announced on Yelp's top 100 brunches in the country at number 10! I love everything Asian-fusion so when I heard we were giving brunch food this special treatment I was already in. What I love is that they offer standard brunch items that you really want like omelets and french toast. but they just add an Asian twist. I had the Tom Yum omelet and I can't explain how that Tom Yum flavor made such a unique omelet. I enjoyed it so much that I instantly added Tom Yum paste to my Amazon cart so I can have my own jar and feebly recreate this dish at home. They also have amazing presentation with fresh flowers and sliced fruit perfectly placed on your plate. If you're on the fence about trying this place, just go.

Went around 1 on a weekday and there was no wait despite the smaller space. Was excited to try since so many of the menu items sounded so good. Staff were friendly and attentive but food was fairly average -- would be interested to try something different in case it was an off day

our server was really friendly! I feel like this place is a relatively new and hidden gem, boasting Thai & Vietnamese American fusion brunch.

the vietnamese dalgona latte was interesting because the sweet whipped dalgona balances out the strong vietnamese coffee. soy milk substitute was at no extra charge.

the tom yum omelette was definitely the best dish. although it was less spicy and more sweet than the traditional Thai dish, it possessed adequate spices to encapsulate the bona fide flavor of tom yum.

the chicken & pandan waffle was my second favorite. the waffle's pandan flavor was subtle to cautiously introduce someone new to pandan yet enough to emit the plant's distinctive fragrance. the chicken was juicy and just lightly breaded, creating a thin crispy layer. the apple mustard also gave an extra kick to the traditional southern dish.

the thai tea french toast elevated the typical dessert with espresso in the thai tea syrup, enhancing the flavor of the sauce. it had greater tea to sweetness which I personally liked, but some may find it a bit too "siap" (astringent).

overall, would love to come back again and dive into its extensive menu that spans a variety of dishes and unique flavors.

Found this place with my friend by researching for some new brunch food.
The place was a little hard to find as it was next to all the residential and abandon buildings, but inside was super clean and welcoming.
There are a lot of choices, but we particularly wanted to try their Tom Yum so we got the Tom Yum omelette and the noodle soup.
The Tom yum noodle soup looked super good, but it was too sour for my liking. And the omelette was so salty that my friend and I couldn't even eat more than 2 bites.
We told the waiter about the problem and he immediately called his manager over and they took the dish back and remade a new one which was much better.
Overall if you're looking for some Thai brunchy food I recommend, but just be aware it's mostly on the sour side not the savory side.
The service was brilliant. Would love to come back and try different foods.

Mmmm yummy. We made a reservation, called ahead because we were running late, and were still seated immediately with a smile. The food takes like 15-20 to come out, but it's well worth the wait. The Tom Yum omelette is so nostalgic and yums. French toast wasn't too sweet and was super crispy and delicious. AND PANDAN WAFFLE! Please get pandan chicken waffle the waffle is texturally perfect and the mustard sauce is so yummers. Chicken. Also perfect. The drinks were also yum. Me loves this place

Nice cozy little brunch option. Loved the food. Its very flavourful unlike most brunch places where they give the option of salt. I was very full. The drink was cute but heavy. You really need to come in all hungry to this place. Definitely satisfies with the ambiance and freshness.

Really good Asian fusion brunch spot in the city with solid food and service!

My friend and I made a reservation here for brunch on a Saturday (via Yelp!) and were immediately seated once we arrived. The restaurant gives me airy cafe vibes and I loved the decor and all the cute plants! Our food came out shortly after we ordered, and the staff were also very prompt about giving us the bill when we were done.

My friend got a lychee jasmine tea which she loved, and we chose to split the fresh rolls with shrimp as an appetizer. This was the perfect light and refreshing starter, and the peanut sauce that the rolls came with was fantastic.

For entrees, I got the Thai tea french toast and my friend got the fried chicken & pandan waffle. My french toast was perfectly crisp on the outside and soft on the inside, and I like that they provide the Thai tea sauce on the side. The sauce itself had a strong thai tea flavor and wasn't too sweet which I enjoyed! I got to try some of the fried chicken & pandan waffle as well and thought it was delicious.

The food not only looks good, but tastes good too! We got a variety of dishes to try and my friends and I thoroughly enjoyed each one. The servers were so nice and attentive. They said that the dishes we chose are some of their favorites so highly recommend if trying for the first time. Their drinks were delicious and colorful.

Come through if you have a penchant for Asian twists on classic brunch food. It was fairly empty when I popped in on a weekday, so everything was done quickly here. We ordered and paid at the counter, and then the staff brought the food to our table when it was ready.

The presentation of the food was saliva-inducing. I couldn't wait to dig into the garlic fries, which were plentiful. The pandan waffle and chicken were also amazing, but the pandan flavor wasn't very strong. The thai tea french toast was also great, including the sauce on the side. It was interesting how they separated the toast and the fruits.

We had a great brunch here! We came here with some friends on Memorial Day weekend and we really enjoyed our meal. We had reservations so we only had to wait a few minutes to get our table and our service was good throughout the meal. My wife and I got some nice drinks (my wife's had lychee) and they were very refreshing. She had the garlic noodles and she absolutely loved them. I had the Thai tea French toast with sriracha bacon and it was so delicious; the Thai tea sauce wasn't overly sweet and it was very tasty while the sriracha bacon had a great flavor without being overtly spicy. It was a delicious meal overall and we would definitely come here again!

We came here for dinner and ordered the shrimp fresh rolls, hainan chicken, and salmon curry, as well as a Hawaiian rainbow drink. Every dish tasted amazing! I personally really loved the salmon curry, especially the Thai red curry. Our server was really kind, and the food came out very quickly. I would definitely come back to eat here :)

This place caught our eye because it seemed like a nice brunch place, and indeed it was! We came in on a Saturday early afternoon without a reservation and got seated right away. Honestly we got really lucky because a couple more parties came in right after us and they had to wait a bit. Definitely recommend adding yourself to the waitlist in advanced. I got the Thai French toast and my boyfriend got the chicken and pandan waffles.

The Thai tea French toast was good! The sauce it came with tasted exactly like Thai tea. The toast was soft and fluffy. If you like French toasts, you'll like this! I prefer my French toast to be sweeter but am still glad to try this.

The chicken and pandan waffles was really good too! The chicken was seasoned well and the breading was nice. My boyfriend was a big fan of the apple mustard sauce. I prefer the pandan waffles in other places but it was still good.

The Vietnamese dalgona coffee was all right. I thought it would be sweet like Vietnamese coffee but it's more toned down. Good to try.

Overall def recommend trying this place at least once for their specialty items!
interesting hybrid take out/dine in with a combination of thai and breakfast food. delicious nonetheless

Very nice surprise. Had this place bookmarked but don't know where I was recommended.
Located on 5th between Folsom and a small alley of Clementina St.

Went as soon as the place opened and was greeted as entering. I was given a menu and was given the freedmen to sit anywhere.
Service was nice, water with some hint of lemon is served.

I went with a Thai milk tea and the Tom Yum omelette.
That Tom Yum omelette was one of the best I ever had in terms of variety and flavour. The omelette is packed with veggies and shrimp. Some bacon on top, a nice salad with some sort of vinaigrette, and the yum cubed potatoes were perfect. It comes with shrimp too.
The place is very clean and well decorated. Sunlight hits the place nicely as the surrounded area is not covered in high buildings. Nice little atmosphere. Good place to do some computer work or just relax.

Bathrooms are in the back. You need a key.

Nearest BART station is Powell.
MUNI 12, 30, 8, 8BX, 45 bring you here.

I was looking for a place do study, but was also hungry and this place satisfied all my needs! They have great food, decent drinks, good amount of seating with wifi AND OUTLETS. I can hear twice on the weekday afternoon/night and they were never busy enough to the point where you had to wait for seating. Plus the service was super friendly and attentive, they checked on my a few times especially because they saw I was working there for a while. Definitely a hidden gem in the SOMA district!

My friend and I came here for brunch and shared a Thai lime tea and Thai tea french toast combo. I was really excited to try the Thai tea french toast; it was not bad! Worth a try since this is not commonly offered. The Thai lime tea was yummy; it tasted exactly like you're drinking Thai tea and lime juice simultaneously, in a good way of course. The interior is somewhat small but nice and cozy. Service was quick. They do have a lot of interesting fusion dishes that sound good, and I would like to try another time!

Solid lunch option in Soma. I got the morning crispy chicken salad but replaced it with the five spice chicken. The salad was packed with stuff - there was half an avocado, a fried egg, mozzarella, garlic toast - it's way more food than your typical salad. The salad greens included kale which made it seem even heartier. Five spice chicken was fine (not as memorable as other versions I've had), but with everything else that the salad had, it didn't need to be the star. Super reasonably priced salad considering how much is in it.

I think they're most known for brunch (and their brunch menu looks delicious) so will have to come back and try it another time.

- Cute little spot for brunch in downtown SF
- Mixture of southeast Asian and western food.
- Friendly staff.
- Decent portions.

Visited on a Thursday night for dinner. We were greeted and told that we could sit anywhere. The restaurant is decently spacious and neither too busy nor empty when we arrived. Some people came in and out of the restaurant to pick up orders.

The menu is pretty extensive and featured many items that I wanted to try. I decided on the Shaking Beef dish and my friend tried the Drunken Noodles without meat. The shaking beef was soft and tender. However, I thought that the sauce was a little saltier than I preferred. Still, the rice and veggies helped balance out the flavors. Next time, I would try their brunch menu and coffee/boba drinks since they are on Yelp's Top 10 for brunch in the country!

We came here on New Years Day and they were packed as you would expect. They were very kind and accommodated our 6 person table as quickly as they could.

For such a casual eatery the food is immaculate. Nothing I've eaten here as disappointed on portion or flavor. Their Tom yum noodles with crispy chicken are something I craze frequently. Their Garlic Noodles are so flavorful!

I have been back and will continue coming back here!

This restaurant has been on my list for quite some time and i'm so glad I was finally able to go. The food is amazing and I need to return to try other dishes. Very flavorful and crispy. It's a very small space and can get pretty loud. We were able to make a reservation day of, and had no problems being seated. Service was slightly slow, but in good company it wasn't too impactful. I wish so loved closer so I could return regularly.

Ok let's have a real talk about social media and false expectations. Even reviews sometimes are so subjective that you walk into a place expecting one thing and get something completely different. Not at Mr. East Kitchen.

This place lived up to any and all hype we had:

The stuffed french toast with strawberries, chicken and waffles, steak and eggs, french toast with caramelized banana, and crispy fish with eggplant. Not a single dish disappointed. Everything was delicious!! The mimosas were fresh and delicious with real cranberry and thyme garnish.

The staff there was beyond excellent. Constant attention, but gave us room also to relax and actually close the place. They were so kind and helpful. They even helped us figure out what we wanted and how to get the best price. Really nice people - every single person we met and were helped by, there were six.

They were open for Christmas and they staff members are truly thoughtful and excellent. The food was delicious and my vegetarian friend enjoyed the Florentine Benedict while I got the Tom Yum omelette. I love how you can select salad or fruit on the side of the omelette

Great yummy a breakfast with an asian twist. The staff is very nice and it's a sit down and order kind of place. The price is very reasonable for being in San Francisco and it has a very cute and inspo worthy food and place. They have this pandan and chicken waffle that was amazing and super unique.
That one and the Thai tea French toast was amazing. I DEF RECOMMEND THOSE IF YOU COME!
The mango sticky rice is also amazing and a must.

A friend had recommended to come here for brunch. The wait to get seated wasn't too bad - a few minutes at the most.
I was pleasantly surprised that the menu was Thai fusion and was torn between a handful of dishes. We ended up ordering: Vietnamese Dalgona coffee, Tom Yum Omelette, and Vegetarian Steak.

The Tom Yum omelette had all the delicious notes a tom yum soup would have, including the spice. This does have a kick but accentuates the dish rather than being painfully spicy.
The candied spicy bacon that topped the omelette was sweet and spicy, definitely a delicious treat.

The Vegetarian Steak had umami taste and well balanced, especially with the sunny side egg.

Both dishes had baguette slices topped with minced garlic and cheese shavings, diced potatoes, and a little salad.

The Vietnamese coffee wasn't too sweet, and there are non-dairy options available as well.

Overall, would come back again.

In a sea of ostentatious brunch spots, Mr East stands out as the option that provides it all without breaking the bank. You get yummy food that come in good portions, great service and a beautiful minimalistic setting for far less than any other locale in the city.

I started off with the fruit tea, which was definitely fresh and refreshing. I only took a sip of the coffee, which was standard fare. I'd be curious to try their dalgona Vietnamese coffee!

My friend and I shared two options. The Tom yum omelette was amazing. Super flavorful, juicy, lots of shrimp. I really enjoyed everything in it. We got garlic bread, garlic fries and salad with it and yummyyy. The sriracha bacon was more sweet, like honey bacon, but still very good.

Next, we got the pandan waffle with fried chicken. I personally like a strong pandan flavor, but I figured that it was light so anyone can try it. The fried chicken was crunchy and juicy. I wasn't a huge fan of the mustard but I'm not a huge fan of mustards in general.

Best of all, even after eating all this, I didn't feel disgusting. I truly believe Mr East does take their time to curate healthy foods and that's why we still felt great to tackle the day!

Overall, a great casual spot for affordable fusion eats and generous portions.

A nice Thai food spot that opens early in the morning. I had the Hainan chicken rice which is not actually Thai food, but it's good. The ingredients are not very similar to those I had in Asia countries but the rice and chicken were delicious. The food service was very quick but servers were not around that much. The staff was friendly.

Can we please take a moment to look at this spread. This place is not talked about enough! The food, drink, & service were phenomenal! I came in on a Friday morning for brunch & was seated right away. My group & I came hungry & decided to try both their breakfast & lunch options. We ordered their Thai French toast, Saigon steak, garlic noodle bowl with shrimp, & crispy chicken fried rice. To drink, we ordered the strawberry matcha & dalgona coffee. Not only were the portions big, but each dish had such rich & tasty flavors. The Thai French toast had the perfect balance of sweetness, the Saigon steak is at the top of my list for steak & eggs, the garlic noodle bowl had just enough garlic for me, & the crispy chicken fried rice was both crispy & moist! This place greatly surprised me & just when I thought our meal was over, our server came out with one of their desserts - mango sticky rice, shaped like a heart! On our way out, we got to meet the owner who was so sweet & we thanked them for their good food & service. This restaurant greatly surprised me & I'll definitely be coming back here again! Heads up - parking may be difficult to find
Service was great! Food is decent and ambiance is cute. Menu is unique and I would recommend checking it out.

It was my first time at this cute Thai brunch spot in soma with some classic and some unique menu items. I had the Thai Tea French toast, which was delicious. The Thai tea syrup came on the side and you're meant to pour it on top, which I liked since it's more liquidy than syrup and would make the French toast soggy if it was already poured. It tasted like Thai tea but not as sweet, so it gave a nice balance to the meal. The sriracha bacon it came with didn't taste like sriracha to be honest, it had 0 spice and was more like a sweet glazed bacon. My friend also enjoyed her crispy chicken fried rice and we thought both dishes were pretty generous. I'd come here again!

Very rarely do I emphatically promote a restaurant. However, Mr. East Kitchen provided the perfect opportunity for me to do so. The service was excellent and timely, the food was delicious and very fairly priced for the satisfying portions. The whole restaurant is clean, bright, warm, and welcoming.

The menu is a wonderful fusion of flavors with vegan options. I got the tofu Bahn Mi and the flavor was a little lacking, but I didn't use the mayo it came with. However, the garlic fries were addictive and delicious. In my group of 7, everyone devoured their food.

It is a busy, humming place but I placed a reservation 45 minutes ahead of time and we were seated immediately. Despite how busy it was, the food still came out in a timely manner and we never felt forgotten by staff. Highly reccomend.

Wow, I was really blown away by this place! I admit I came with low expectations, thinking that the fusion menu was a gimmick, but the food was so delicious. I really liked the Tom Yum noodle soup - the flavor was strong how I like it, and surprisingly full of shrimp (you can choose your protein). Another standout was the fried chicken and pandan waffle - the chicken portions were huge, and the chicken was surprisingly tender with a Korean-fried-chicken style batter. The drinks were also so yummy (and pretty)!
Such a bright, cute cafe with great food and efficient service. Would definitely want to come back here! (Plus - when I asked to pack away my leftover noodles, they packed the soup and noodles separately so they wouldn't get soggy! A+ service)

Tl;Dr - Reliably decent lunch, brunch, dinner, or whatever you are craving. Its fairly good for breakfast, but I haven't really had a dinner dish here that hit the mark. To each their own, but they are still wildly popular in SOMA.

I want to preface by saying I love these folks, glad to have them here in SOMA where restaurants typically go to die. We lost the French bakery and these guys have held on and flourished, cheers to them.

It's a Vietnamese extremely fusion-ish spot with lots of different dishes and decent Thai tea. Admittedly I don't eat here often, but that's probably because they've become a victim of their success.

Every weekend people pack this spot for brunch, and they have a decent one, it's just not really my ideal ambiance to relax in. Seating is a little cramped inside and the outside tables are usually for larger parties. Chilling outside in SOMA these days also invites occasional issues.

This is my neighborhood so I usually tend to gravitate away from it when I'm enjoying my weekend, but if you are in the area I highly recommend the breakfast or the Thai teas.

The dinner items I haven't been super into, I regularly order the garlic noodles when I'm walking by and get a craving but then I always eat them and think they are missing something. Not sure what but they just don't hit the spot the way they do elsewhere, might be the oil they are using, can't put my finger on it. Needs more.

If the dinner stuff was craved worthy this would be an easy 4, if the space was more chill a 5, but these folks have a successful business based on their choices and SOMA is a tough neighborhood, truly glad for their success. It's just not my vibe, often.

Finally got a chance to sit down at Mr East and have some breakfast outside. I live around the corner and have since thought most of the places here like a Contraband and Les Gourmand are kind of sterile.

They put all this artificial hipster crap here (especially contraband) so it's nice to see something with some soul shine through.

This place is kind of a play on Vietnamese fusion and breakfast with beer on tap so I instantly perked my ears up when I saw it.

It kind of has everything me and my girl would like. Asian food and drinks like boba for her, and beer and breakfast food for me.

Prices are really reasonable, and the quality of the food was superb. I got fresh fruit and she got a steak and eggs. I'll try some pho another time, but from what I see everything is super on point.

As long as they keep the quality up I'll be coming here often. They should get some speciality bottles of stuff like Tiger/Kirin or Sapporo Black, and then I'd really be sold.

Mr East Kitchen is definitely a spot you should visit when going to SF. They have a great menu filled with Asian and Asian Fusion brunch foods! My group really enjoyed how attentive and kind the servers were too!

Starting with the drinks:
Thai Milk Tea - was a very solid Thai Milk Tea. The drink is everything you expect a Thai Milk Tea to be.
Strawberry Matcha Latte - Very good as well! The matcha is definitely the star of the show with this drink and the hints of strawberry definitely pull through with each sip.
Pink Dalgona Coffee - The coffee was flavor was super strong with this one! Not being the biggest fan coffee this wasn't my favorite, but for those who like a strong coffee taste this is definitely both a great tasting and aesthetically pleasing drink!
Hawaiian Rainbow - This drink was by far the best of the 4 to me. It looked great and tasted as good as it looks. It's definitely a sweeter drink but the sweetness is not overbearing. 10/10 would recommend.

The food:
Tom Yum Omelette - This one was definitely a surprise for me as I am not the biggest fan of Tom Yum soup. With that being said this was my favorite of the four dishes we ordered. The sourness of the soup wasn't super overbearing and the flavors mixed inside the egg were extremely delicious.
Saigon Steak - This one was the majority favorite amongst my table. The beef was extremely tender. The stir fry and Vietnamese flavors really stand out to create a very flavorful and delicious dish! Would 109% recommend this one to anyone who goes.
Thai Tea French Toast - very very good dish! I didn't taste the Thai tea from the French toast alone, but when you dip or pour the syrup onto it. It elevates the dish to a whole new level! If you're feeling adventurous I would definitely recommend putting some of the syrup on other dishes as well.
Pad Thai - a solid dish for a crowd favorite! It's less sweet than most Pad Thais I have tried which is a win to me.

Overall Mr East Kitchen provides delicious food and excellent customer service. If you are going to be in the SF area I would 100% recommend trying this place out. I will definitely be back to try more dishes on the menu.

The food from this place is very unique! I had their Tom Yum burrito and it is honestly the best burrito I've ever had with the most distinct taste. Very filling as well; I mean just look at the picture. They also serve mimosas, which apparently if you buy 2 you get the 3rd for like 50 cents. Service was a bit awkward, but there is table service vs ordering from a counter. The decor is fun and trendy. I only wished it was in a location that does not feel as sketch since I felt that way as someone who is not from SF.

It was delicious! We had the Tom Yum omelet, the crispy chicken omelet, the Vietnamese dalgona coffee, and a regular latte. Everything came out quickly and absolutely delicious. I am so glad we popped into this spot. The staff were friendly and the patrons all seemed to be regulars. It felt festive and cozy and it was a great place to stop before heading out of the city.

Was looking all over Yelp to find a brunch place with some friends and actually noticed a lot of Thai fusion brunch spots. Found Mr. East Kitchen and noticed that the menu items were quite cheap around $15-20 in SOMA. You literally can't find these price anywhere, so we decided to come try it out.

I made a reservation, and once we got there at 12pm on a Sunday, thinking it would be jam packed. The place was decorated pretty modern with a light up sign against the wall. There were still 2-3 tables open, so the waiter found us a table easily. He was super sweet!

I tried the Saigon Steak and instead of the garlic bread, I subbed in fruit. Totally worth it! My friends got the Tom Yum omelette and we more than enjoyed our food. It was so flavorful like Thai foods usually do, and the quantity was quite large. The salad was light. I'm not sure what dressing they used but it was delicious. Totally coming here again. So surprised not more people know about this place!

While staying in SF for the night, we didn't want to walk far for dinner so we searched the surrounding restaurants and settled on Mr East Kitchen. This place was a nice surprise, possibly the best Thai food we've ever had. The drunken noodles with beef was incredible. The wife got the pineapple fried rice with bbq pork which was equally delightful. The staff were very friendly, the dining area was very clean, and service was fast. 10/10 would go out of my way to visit Mr East again.
Good food and service. Will definitely recommend this place. There was a paid parking nearby as well.

Pretty good Vietnamese-Thai-American spot. I visited it a couple of times for brunch and dinner and every time had a great experience. This is not a fancy place but it's light, modern and has good service which brings it good amount of visitors. The menu is large so it's easy to find what to eat either you are in mood for sweet or savory food. I really loved their rich zesty Tom Yum noodle soup with crispy chicken and my husband found Pad Thai Shrimp delicious. Glad that we discovered this spot in our neighborhood and I actually see us becoming commons there.

Pretty good Thai-American brunch spot. I visited it on a Sunday noon and it was busy but still had high stools available. The menu is large so it's easy to find what to eat either you are in mood for sweet or savory food. I really loved their rich Tom Yum soup with crispy chicken and my husband found Pad Thai Shrimp delicious. The service was friendly and fast, and people kept coming till the end of their brunch hours so I can assume that this place is pretty popular among those who know about it. Glad that we discovered this Thai spot in our neighborhood.

The food was amazing. I got the crispy chicken fried rice, veggie rolls, garlic noodles, and Vietnamese coffee. Everything was well seasoned and good.

The service was ok. The guy was nice but moody. I had to wait 20 minutes for my order.

There was no ambiance, but they had just opened for dinner. There were a few homeless people outside of the restaurant doing drugs, but that's everywhere in San Francisco.

4.5 stars, solid Asian fusion brunch. I come often.

Good creativity for brunch options, and different than the plethora of millionaire bacon places you can find. I've tried a good amount of the menu and it's all pretty good-- just depends what you are looking for.

This past weekend the weather was nice and this place was almost completely packed. Very surprised. Even then line wasn't too long, and got seated in under 5 min.

Solid Asian brunch (or Asian lunch) in the area. Recommended!

this thai fusion brunch place has a great variety of dishes for different tastes! sadly, i don't think it stands out from the numerous other fusion spots in the bay.

parking is pretty tough per usual in SF. it's just street parking around the block.

the restaurant is fairly small, and it gets busy fast! i recommend coming early. the service is pretty good though and prices are fairly similar to other brunch spots in SF.

vietnamese iced coffee - this is more of a dalgona style drink, so my lactose intolerant baddies be aware of the amount of milk lol. it is pretty sweet, but i liked it!

thai tea french toast - this is definitely the star of the show. the french toast is fluffy, and the thai tea milk is not too sweet. i like how it comes with quite a bit of fruit as well.

salmon benedict - you can't go wrong with an eggs benedict, so we enjoyed this! the potatoes are so crispy, too.

tom yum omelette - we were honestly so disappointed with this! i think tom yum just did not blend with the omelette, maybe because the filling is just between the eggs rather than being mixed in? the flavors were good, but a bit too tasty.

i love the incorporation of asian flavors, and i appreciate the presentation of the dishes. it's a pretty average place, but i'd still come try it out!
Great flavor and quantity for the price. Went in for dinner. The staff was attentive and quick too.

Came for the thai tea french toast, was blown away by the tom yum omelette. The thai tea french toast wasn't too sweet, which I loved. The fruit tasted great dipped in the thai tea glaze as well. The tom yum omelette was delicious and had 4 shrimps! It tasted exactly like tom yum, I loved the mushrooms inside. The salad had a refreshing in contrast to the rich bacon that had a yummy barbecue flavor. Would definitely recommend coming here! Prices are reasonable as well.

We came here for brunch and luckily they had a same day Sunday reservation for six. We started off with some mimosas, which were fine but nothing amazing. I had the fried chicken & panda waffle - this was also fine but not my favorite chicken and waffle. It was bone-in, which I wish was better notated because I'm not a fan of bone-in chicken. The waffle was fine, but didn't have much flavor.
Overall it was a decent meal, but didn't stand up to some of the other Thai fusion brunch spots in the city.

There are two things you must try at Mr. East Kitchen: the Thai Tea French Toast, and the garlic noodles.

This place is a wonderful addition to the food scene in SOMA. They serve southeast asian food with a little bit of Americanized flare.

The staff here is so cute and friendly and helpful. If you sit down to eat, they will constantly check on you to make sure you have everything you need. My water glass never got below 50%!

I had a vegetarian friend come into town and brought her here because they have a large assortment of veggie options. The top vegetarian item is probably the vegetarian steak.

The bathrooms are clean. This place does get busy on Saturdays and Sundays, so weekdays are my preferred visit times.

Everything from the food, service and welcoming ambiance was nothing short of amazing here! It was so hard to chose an entree because they all looked and sounded so amazing! Finally settled on the Tom Yum omelette and it for sure did not disappoint. So much flavor and perfect portion for me. The boba drinks are perfect too.

My wife and I went for brunch and will definitely go back soon probably with more family or friends! There are many other dishes we really want to try! I will definitely try the Thai Tea French Toast next time.

Egg Benedict with salmon- loved it with the house salad w spinach and kale. The salmon w skin on was done well.
Garlic fries w Sriracha Mayo- mmm, crispy fries and yummy sauce.
Fruit blast tea- OMG, I love the combination of this jasmine tea w berries and lychee!

I always love coming here! It's such a cute aesthetic place and has good coffee shop vibes even though it's more of a food place.

Good:
- The food here is so beautiful and portion sizes are great - I loved the Tom Yum Noodle Soup dish - the soup base was great but also the noodles were so tasty and the right texture.
- I have gotten French toast here too and loved it.

Bad:
- Takes a long time to get food when it's super busy here - not their fault but I was waiting for over 45 minutes one time to get food on a Thursday at lunch.

Overall this place is great - prices are reasonable and it's a super great Asian food place.

The food, service and ambience are exceptional!
The place is rated as one of the best brunch spot in the US apparently. Mr East Kitchen totally deserves the title. We had Saigon steak, steak benedict and spicy salmon. Everything is delicious!
I'll definitely come back :)

Mr East Kitchen went far beyond our expectations. Waitstaff was prompt, helpful and friendly but most importantly, the food was AWESOME. We ordered the pad Thai, drunken noodles, chicken satay and pineapple fried rice with bbq pork. It was ALL delicious. We will definitely be going back!

I came here this weekend and had the opportunity to visit this amazingly place, the food was amazing and size was enough if you want to share with someone else. The service was excellent, very attentive, excellent vibe and very humble. It was so good that I came today again and it was delicious too.

Great casual brunch spot for Thai fusion food! Their brunch menu has lots of variety to choose from, including the super fruit tea and dalgona coffee. I enjoyed the Tom yum noodle soup, which came with a generous portion size of crispy chicken and extra bean sprouts and jalapeños. The broth was flavorful and not too spicy.

From the outside you can easily miss this place based on its simplistic facade. The interior was modern and clean but a bit narrow to accommodate large groups (party of seven). The service was very good!

We were excited to try this fusion meets tradition brunch place but was a bit disappointed. Overall, the food was underwhelming. The Tom Yum omelette was not flavorful. You can barely taste any Tom Yum. The Saigon Steak was alright. The Satay Chicken was very dry and overcooked. As for the Fried Chicken with Pandan Waffle... the chicken was very plain and bland. The pandan waffle saved that dish. Each dish was very nicely plated... for photos, if that's what you're looking for.

Our first time here and me and my friends all loved our meals! We ordered the garlic noodle bowl with honey pork, drunken noodles with tofu, and the vegetarian steak. As most spots in SF, seating is limited but not terrible. I still recommend a reservation just in case. Service was great and I would come back!

Mr. East Kitchen offers a minimalistic dining space. Though we were promptly seated, we waited over 30min for our food. Despite this, the Pandan Waffle was yummy and served with a generous serving of fresh fruits, two eggs, and a sausage, making for a satisfying portion. The Tom Yum Omelet was also very good. The sriracha bacon on the Tom Uim Omelet doesn't taste much like sriracha, instead, it tasted like honey-glazed bacon. We swapped the potatoes and the side for French fries and hash browns, and I'll say everything on the plates are delicious.

They don't assign specific server for each table, the attentive staff regularly checked in on patrons, ensuring a pleasant dining experience. In conclusion, while the wait may test patience, Mr. East Kitchen delivers on taste and attentive service, making it a worthwhile dining destination.

Went here for brunch last Sunday during the Pride Parade and were surprisingly able to get a spot very quickly! There are usually a few tables open, but worth making a quick reservation.

Our Lychee Mimosas and the dipping sauce for the Tofu Rolls were a touch too sweet and could benefit from some lemon or lime for acidity. HOWEVER, the rest of the food was awesome!

My vegan Eggplant Tofu dish had great umami flavors, and I enjoyed the texture of the tofu + eggplant. The sauce packed a punch and was balanced out well by the rice and veg.

My friend got the Thai Tea French Toast - one of the restaurant's staples. He said the sauce was absolutely addictive. He originally requested the chicken sausage for the combo deal, but the dish came out with the sriracha-glazed bacon instead. The waitress later came up to us with the chicken sausage and apologized for the switch-up without us even asking! We were extremely impressed by the outstanding service - while we got our food very quickly, we never felt rushed.

Will definitely be coming back thanks to the convenient location and many dishes I want to try!

I had the garlic noodle bowl. It was absolutely delicious!!! I would order again. I had the wings and fries. The fries were hot, crispy, and fresh. Nothing special about the wings. Just wings! I would come back for the garlic noodles anytime.

This is a hidden gem that was worth multiple visits on my boyfriend and I's trip to San Francisco. You can't go wrong with anything you order on the menu from classic Vietnamese dishes (banh mi, bo kho, Vietnamese coffee, etc.) to fusions on brunch classics. Our server was very attentive and we were able to be seated right away surrounded by beautiful decor. The chicken and pandan waffle combo was to die for and my boyfriend's favorite dish was the spicy chicken sandwich. Honorable mention to the Thai tea French toast because I just love the twists that this restaurant successfully curates.
Another gem in Downtown SF. Service was great . The food was awesome and of course price was alright.

While the drinks were delicious, the food was disappointing. For drinks, my partner and I got the Thai Milk Tea and Pink Dalgona Coffee. I love being able to try something new like the Pink Dalgona. It was expensive, but worth it. I like that there were multiple dairy free options too. For food, my partner and I got the Hai Nan chicken and Tom Yum omelette. I picked the chicken dish off the healthy choice portion of the menu, so I was surprised to see that the chicken was so fatty (and not in a way that contributed to flavor.) The presentation was pretty, but the dish fell short of its promising description. It didn't feel like a cohesive exciting dish either. My partner's omelette had its contents unevenly distributed with the shrimp all in one part of the omelette. There were also many flies near us. The restaurant might be trying its best to fight that already, but it was unpleasant to be around.

5 stars for drinks, but the food was very underwhelming.
Great service and food was delicious. Had the garlic noodles with honey pork and it hit the spot and large portion size.

Heard lots of good things, so had to give it a shot! I made a last minute reservation for a sunday morning breakfast around 10am, but definitely didn't need it. Crowd picked up ~11:30am though, so I would recommend a res if you go around that time.

(+)generous portions at good prices
(+)ample counter + table seating
(+)attentive, timely service
(+)clean

4 stars because:
(-)tom yum omelette was lackluster, and I came here specifically for this. rather than all the flavors being combined/working together, it was really just egg folded over some filling that you'd find in tom yum goong. it wasn't sour like the soup, which imo is an important flavor profile here. it was fine, but not special, and I'd definitely order something else.

misc:
mimosa special: buy 3, get the 4th for 5 cents -- not sure if it's seasonal or if it has restrictions

I haven't checked out many restaurants in SoMa as I usually don't venture out to this area, but we saw that this place had good ratings and so we decided to come here and give it a shot. The interior is very modern and sleek, with lots of cool decorations and it was a warm environment. The staff here were very nice, and we were able to be seated right away. The space isn't the largest, but there are a decent number of tables to sit at here.

For our dishes, we decided to get the Crispy Chicken Rice, mango with sticky rice for dessert, and a Pink Drink that they offered. The crispy chicken rice here was great, as the chicken itself was quite crispy (without being oily) and the rice had a good amount of spice that I enjoyed. There was a lot of flavor there, and it was a decent amount of food for the dish. The dessert was nice and I could tell the mango was fresh, while the Pink drink had a unique flavor to it (thought it was still tasty).

If you are around the Soma district and want some good Vietnamese food, Mr. East Kitchen is a good spot to check out!
I got the matcha latte and it was great. I think it was quite sweet but in a good way. My food was good as well. The table generally liked their meals. The dunked noodles were 8/10.

Found this spot on yelp! The ambiance in here is super nice, staff super welcoming, restaurant very bright. We were seated immediately once walking in, so yelp check in isn't needed. When we ordered, the waiter showed us the iPad screen as he was inputting our order, which was super nice of him. We got the Saigon Steak andTom Yum noodles for our entree, along with the Garlic Fries w mayo for our appetizer.My boyfriend really enjoyed his Saigon steak, the meat was just right, not too raw or too chewy. Salad was great, had the right amount of dressing and the potatoes were perfect. Love this spot!!

Walking past this restaurant, I always see it busy during brunch time. I stopped by on a Sunday to see why it's always bustling!

Location: This shop is right off of 5th and Folsom. There is very limited street parking (like always in Downtown SF) so I would recommend going to Powell and taking a 5 minute walk over. There is limited street parking on Folsom.

Interior: Cute and simple on the inside. There are about 10 tables and a little bar along the window for indoor seating. On the weekend, they put a table outside for limited outdoor dining.

Service: We were sat almost immediately for a Sunday. The party ended up being slightly bigger than expected so they kindly moved us to a larger table. They took our orders quickly and the food came out within 15 minutes. Super nice staff who always took care of our table and made sure our glasses were full.

Food: This restaurant is new Vietnamese style. They spin typical Vietnamese flavors into brunch flavors. While Asian fusion is common in the city, it was my first time going to a Vietnamese fusion restaurant. I would say while its nothing amazing, I enjoyed my food. The pandan waffles were perfectly paired with syrup and the fruits were yummy. I would note the portion size was great for me but maybe a bit lacking for those who can eat a good amount. The portions are, however, reflected in the prices of the dish.

Overall, I would love to come here again for a nice meal with friends.
Great service and food! They are quick and very helpful and I've never been in there when it's not crowded
I will always come back to Mr.East! It's so fast and convenient and the workers are very nice! Food is super good and always hits. Also very cute aesthetic.

Came back here for 2nd tom yum soup and fresh shrimp spring roll and spicy Benedict. Still can't get over the chair sounds scratching on the floor, they need to put something like rubber socks on, quite annoying for people who want to enjoy their meal unless they buzz already, I can see some people have manners some not so can be noisy

It's my first visit and will be my favorite to visit again, place are clean and tall ceilings, so you will not feel cramped, kind a loft style place. We came around 10am Service are fast, presentation were melt my heart, so beautiful and portioned well.
I don't feel egg, so I ordered fresh shrimp roll and Tom yum tofu soup, the way I ate them, I dipped fresh shrimp roll into Tom yum. My husband ordered Benedict with potatoes and fresh fruit. I don't have pictures next time I visit would update the picture

We were welcomed with a smile. Our waitress was prompt in providing iced water and a generous sized Lychee Mimosa which had a full Lychee and flavored ice. My second Mimosa was the Pomegranate Mimosa with a flavored sugar rim. Absolutely spectacular.
Tasty, delicious food AND great service. I have dined here a handful of times already and both have been consistent. The staff is friendly and I felt like a regular from day one.

When you start with a fresh roll that consists of just a quarter pound of lettuce and has ONE shrimp only as decoration, there is little room for getting excited!

Cute little restaurant located in an area where all options are mediocre to not great at all.
Staff is quite young but reasonably professional. They forgot my order and had to wait half an hour to finally get my food, but that was not the biggest complaint.
Their food is ok. It is good in the sense it is quite fresh and different than usual, but it lacks flavor and is made to be cheap. But the charge for it is not.

A good option for the area. I would certainly not drive to it.

Stopped by for a late brunch on a weekend. We were all starving and stumbled here. No wait which was great. Friendly staff!

Overall we thought the food was generally ok. But an interesting fusion menu that's different than the typical brunch offerings. I got the Fried Chicken & Pandan Waffle, good flavors but neither the chicken or waffle were that crispy.
Love their fried chicken noodle soup . Chicken was very fresh and crunchy . Soup was very delicious

Really enjoyed Mr. East side! The food itself was great. The noodle bowl was my personal favorite. It was very fresh and delicious! The jalepenos had a good kick to them in it. The Thai tea French toast was good! It was pretty similar to Thai tea roti if you have ever had. The drinks were good. My personal favorite was the lychee fizz. Came on the hottest day this summer so drinks were refreshing but the place was a little warm lol! Service was good, very kind. This is apparently owned by the same owner as spork which is closed most days, so glad I found this place!

I was looking to do a quick brunch by myself before heading out of San Francisco and found Mr. East to try. Checking these reviews I was a bit concerned about a wait time as I was on a bit of a time crunch, but on a Tuesday morning, I was the only sit-down customer. For brunch and being in San Francisco, Mr. East is very fairly priced!
