Thai Tea French Toast (4/5): The titular thai tea comes in the form of a syrup to pour over rather than maple syrup. The flavor really comes though and the dish isn't too sweet, which I really appreciated.

Fried Chicken & Pandan Waffle (4.25/5): The crunch on the fried chicken was amazing, but the chicken itself was a tad overcooked (still moist though!). For the waffle, I wish that the pandan flavor was a bit stronger. The one thing that was absolutely stellar though is the mustard sauce they serve on the side; super strong, but nicely balanced with some sweetness.

This is long over due review! I have been going here almost once a month May that be for brunch or dinner plus have done take out a few times. The food here is amazing my favorite item on the brunch menu is Tom yum omelet. It's so flavorful and it has shrimp hidden inside the omelet. And it comes with a side of rice which is so good I never thought omelets can go with rice but yes they can. For lunch/dinner I usually get the Tom yum noodle soup with tofu and extra spicy. It's really spicy gets your nose cleared out. The soup has so much flavor and I'm usually not a huge fan of tofu but there tofu is crispy and has flavor but not overpowering the soup so it's perfect. The vibe in there is amazing and the service is excellent and very helpful. I usually order through Yelp and pick up but they are on delivery apps.
Food amazing, service amazing, ambiance good. Best spot for breakfast, lunch and dinner

Great brunch spot in SOMA!

I came here around noon on a Saturday and was able to get a seat for 2 within 10 minutes, which is pretty good for weekend brunch.

I ordered the Crispy Chicken Fried Rice and it was delicious! The chicken was divine - I don't know how they fry it but the layer of breading is super thin but flaky and crispy. love the addition of the pickled veggies, which helps to add some acidity to the dish. Prices are very reasonable given portion sizes and quality.

Our servers were super friendly and attentive. I would recommend this spot to anyone looking for a modern Asian fusion meal!

Summary:
Okay for the price, but I'd prefer to spend more and eat elsewhere

Details:
* TBH, for the area and the pricing, the food is decent, but every dish we had was a bit lacking
* French toast comes as three small, thin, half toasts with a side of fruit
* Omelette (fried rice) is more thin and tough than soft and fluffy, but had okay flavor
* Drunken beef noodles had good flavor, but were a bit salty
* Overall, not bad in a pinch or if you're craving brunch in the area, but there are better (albeit pricier) options elsewhere

Accessibility:
Large and spacious with plenty of accessible seating, albeit indoors only.

This place is actually crazy good. I ordered the Hai Nan Chicken through DoorDash. When my food arrived, right away I noticed the portion size was on the generous side. For $17.95, I thought my order was a great value. The chicken was juicy, tender and flavorful. The entire plate had all the right sauces. The green veggies, the ginger sauce, plus the poached egg all complimented the chicken well. The ginger rice was such a simple yet nice touch that truly made the difference for me and elevated the dish to 5 stars.

The menu could be a bit overwhelming because there's a bunch of options. You have to be super thorough and read through it but based on pictures and reviews, it seems like most (if not all) of their food look delicious. Needless to say, I will definitely be back and next time I'll dine in!

Ordered this through DoorDash and it came pretty quickly!

Tom yum soup: I was feeling under the weather, so I ordered the Tom yum soup with chicken. It had a lot of meat and vegetables in it. It wasn't that spicy either, which was nice.

Vietnamese Dalgona Coffee: this was my first time having a dalgona coffee and it did not disappoint! I wish I knew to shake it before hand though because I was just drinking the milk until it was gone and then tasted the espresso. It was really good and I felt caffeinated.

I def want to try more things on the menu. My coworkers had the drunken noodles and they said it was good. I love that they have many options.

The place is very clean and modern. The menu has all of your basic brunch items but with an Asian twist to it. I'd try for the Fried Chicken & Pandan Waffle, Saigon Steak, and Thai Tea French Toast. The fried chicken is so crispy and goes really well with the waffle. The Saigon Steak is marinated well and very tender, and the french toast is so flavorful. Overall, a very good brunch spot!

This establishment is very unorganized. We made a reservation for 2 people and arrived 5 minutes before our reservation. A worker came out, asked me if my name was written down yet, and I told him I had a reservation. He asked to see my reservation confirmation, which I showed him and he enthusiastically smiled and quickly jotted my name down with the number "2" next to it, at the very bottom of the waitlist. There was a ton of space between my name and the last person's name that was on the list for some reason. We proceeded to stand outside waiting, while at least 3 parties (of the same size) who arrived later than us get seated. One of the parties was a group of two people who, upon arriving, look confused and ask the group next to us where they can put their name down. They end up going up to the workers who told them they can write them name down on the waitlist. These two people then got seated 5 minutes later, while we still stood there waiting for our table. After waiting for 20 minutes, someone walked up to the restaurant and asked one of the workers how long the wait will be for a party of 2 (like us). The waiter confidently smiled at the person and told him it will be a 4 minute wait only. At this point, we still hadn't gotten seated and no one checked in with us even once.

It seemed like different people were handling the hostess duties, as the person who wrote our names down ended up being at the cashier for the rest of the time we were waiting to be seated. Different workers were seating customers as well.

We ended up leaving and will not be returning.

Came here to eat with friends on a Friday evening around 5:30pm before going to an event. Not too busy when we arrived, menu has a variety of options, prices are a tad on the higher end but for the portions and food quality I can say it's fairly worth. All of our food came out quickly and everything looked fresh, really enjoyed the drinks we got and then crispy veggie rolls + garlic noodles really stood out to me, wanna come back again for other brunch options. Overall great service and quaint restaurant, the food was delicious, will update the next time I go and try brunch.

Made an easy brunch reservation and walked straight from bart over to this place. Different combination of Vietnamese food and breakfast food.

Beef pho 4/5 it was good. nothing super special
Thai tea french toast 5/5 pretty unique. it tastes exactly as it sounds. french toast with thai tea on it lol. I think their take on millionaire's bacon was pretty good. it was more siracha/ketchup based? It was yummy though.

It was very clean and the staff service was good. Next time ill have to try the milk teas when its not so cold.

Visited on a Friday afternoon and luckily, there was no wait. The location is convenient, especially if you are shopping by downtown. Server was very kind and checked in on our meals.

The food was delicious! The tom yum noodle soup was big and very flavorful. The steak in the benedict was very well cooked. The portions are big and very worth the price. I would definitely come again for brunch and recommend to friends! This is a great place for Asian fusion brunch!

Made a res for 9am, we got there a little early and they were nice enough to let us in early to sit and look at the menu first! The service was very friendly and they were amazing! The thai tea french toast was good but a bit tooooo sweet for my taste. But the Saigon Steak was amazing!!! I subbed fries instead of the breakfast potatoes and it was so good. The steak was tender and the flavor was amazing! The fries were nice and crispy. Even better dipped in the sauce! Definitely recommend and would come back just for this dish! There are a lot of options I'd like to try out in the future too!

I am the biggest sucker for a good Asian American fusion brunch spread and this place did not let me down

I tried the
- pandan waffle with fried chicken (HIGHLY RECOMMEND)
- Tom yum omelette (so flavorful)
- Thai tea French toast (get this)
- shaking beef (YES)
- hainan chicken (double yes)

Everything we ordered was a hit ! There were so many other items on the menu I wanted to try as well - but I'll save it for my next visit.

The service was amazing - all the employees were super nice and the decor was modern. I went during October and the whole place was decked out in Halloween !
Delicious food and prompt courteous service! I found the vegetarian steak to be excellent but must return to try the unique French toasts on the menu.

Came here on a Saturday morning around 10a and we were given a table right away. I'd recommend making a reservation online because it got really busy around 10:45! Price per dish here is pretty affordable and fair for its generous serving size.

Ambiance: 10/10. Loud diners as expected of a brunch spot. Modern and simple interior design. Big windows so plenty of natural light. Bathroom is clean and so cute!

Service: 10/10. Our server was quick, attentive, and friendly.

Food: Thai inspired brunch + lunch!

Thai tea French toast - 8/10. Only two small pieces of toast so weren't enough for the two of us :( the thai tea syrup was delicious though! All that with pieces of fruit made it a bit "healthier", and the fruit served was all fresh. We added two eggs + apply sausage-- the eggs were really undercooked and runny, and our server said the kitchen wouldn't recook them for us? 8/10.

Omelette fried rice - 10/10. Shrimps marinated in tom yum paste tucked away in the omelette were delicious! The salad served on the side was all fresh ad well. Rice was cooked perfectly, and mixing it with tom yum paste was *chefs kiss*

Salmon curry bowl - 9/10. Omg the curry was SO good. Pour the curry over rice, mix the salmon with it and voila! Although I must admit the salmon was slightly over cooked and thus, pretty dry. But!!! Mixing it with rice and curry fixed it.

Earl grey milk tea - 10/10. Pretty sweet but delicious-- I could taste earl grey in my drink.

Overall, the prices here are amazing for the quality and serving size you're paying for! Would definitely recommend this cute place, and would come back to try their other items.

Came here on Sat during the blue angel performance weekend in October. Traffic in the city was not too bad, there is no parking around the restaurant. We parked and walk 5 mins to the restaurant. Live their extensive menu including brunch options. They also have another branch by the chase center with limited options on the menu. Ambiance is causal and restaurant is clean. We ordered the viet coffee, fried chicken with waffles and honey pork with garlic noodles. The food takes very good and the drink is creamy and comes with boba. Will definitely be back to try more dishes.

Came here on Sat during the blue angel performance weekend in October. Traffic in the city was not too bad, there is no parking around the restaurant. We parked and walk 5 mins to the restaurant. Live their extensive menu including brunch options. They also have another branch by the chase center with limited options on the menu. Ambiance is causal and restaurant is clean. We ordered the vietanese coffee, fried chicken with pandan waffles and honey pork with garlic noodles. The food takes very good and the drink is creamy and comes with boba. Will definitely be back to try more dishes.

Showed up on a Saturday at around noon and the place was full but I didn't have to wait too long to get seated as the service was super efficient.

The food was also really good - if you're looking for something homey and filling, I recommend the crispy chicken fried rice!

Since the place isn't too big, it can get a little loud but it's a good place to catch up with your friends. Seems like they have an online waiting list and reservations too.

You know, one of the best things about globalization is that we get to experience a harmonious or innovative combination of flavor profiles from all over the world?

This place does that SO well with Thai, Vietnamese, and Brunch combos. I walked over from a conference nearby, and even though the walk through SF can be sketchy sometimes, it was sooo worth it.

I ordered the Chicken Crispy Fried Rice, which honestly doesn't look like much at first, but it turned out to be an amazingly filling lunch of sweet and sour sauces dipped in perfectly fried chicken. The heaviness of the chicken was perfectly balanced with the light sourness of the sauce on a bed of soft, warm rice.

It was so good that I came by the next day and had the Fried Chicken and Pandan waffle, where the chicken was perfectly fried again, with some honey mustard and sweet syrupy sauce for pairings.

Both visits, the waiters were so kind and attentive, and my seat was comfortable and clean, which always elevates the experience. If you're in the area, and you enjoy a good Asian brunch fusion, this is a great place to stop by.
I can't speak for the other dishes, but I loved what I had!

This place deserves 5 stars and above for food and service! I was looking on Yelp to see what brunch places were around and I stumbled upon the Thai tea French toast and the Tom yum omelette- I was sold! Both dishes were definitely right up my alley, the epitome and definition of Asian American.

The tom yum omelette was PHENOMENAL! I loved every bite and there were ample pieces of shrimp. The whole dish just encapsulates the Tom yum flavor. It is definitely a MUST GET. It even included 2 pieces of Siracha bacon and delicious potatoes. I was literally licking the sauce off the plate (embarrassing, I know. It was that good!!!)

The Thai tea French toast was also good. The bread was a little dry but that's what the sauce was for! I thought it was such a creative dish. There was a mishap with the dish and they offered to remake it AND took it off the bill! That is great customer service. You don't see that happen anymore in any of the restaurants. Nowadays it's just a "oh sorry" type of thing, but not here! Service was always attentive. Our server went above and beyond and explained everything to us and was very welcoming (even though we were in town for the dodger game heh)

Overall, I recommend this place to anyone who loves fusion food. I felt like this place really captures the essence of being Asian American. I wish there was something like this down in LA, but there isn't. I guess I'll just have to stop by the next time I'm in town again.

Mr. East Kitchen has quickly become one of my favorite brunch spots in the city! I came here after seeing it recommended online for their Thai tea French toast, and it did not disappoint at all! I've been here twice now, and everything I've ordered has been absolutely delicious! My favorite thing would definitely be the Saigon Steak! So flavorful and the portion size is perfect. If you visit, you definitely have to try the Thai tea French toast (with the sriracha bacon)! Their Thai tea itself is also very delicious.

The service is also great--staff are prompt and super welcoming. Overall, a great bite with a clean, modern feel inside.
The absolute best Pandan chicken and waffles!!! So tasty and they are always nice. It's a great dine in spot too.

Excellent food, even better service from Tran. Wide variety of selections and relatively inexpensive. Definitely recommend! Will be coming back to try more in the future.

Food (8/10) - Loved the variety of food and the taste. The Saigon steak was super flavorful with a hint of sweetness. The beef was a bit tough but still very enjoyable. The Hainan chicken was super tender and the soy ginger dressing was really flavorful. I would honestly take it to go and just mix it in with some white rice. The rice was fragrant and delicious and the whole dish was cohesive. If I had to say one thing, the savory dishes had a slightly excessive amount of salt for my tasting. French toast was also delicious and the sweetness helped balance out the salt of the other dishes. Particularly, the thai tea sauce was stellar. It was basically just thai tea in sauce form. The bread was a bit on the denser side though. All around, amazing food that is a definite try.

Service (10/10) - Tran was extremely friendly and cordial. Provided excellent service and is one of the rare instances where a server talks on a conversational level. Not much more to comment but just great service. It made us feel very welcome and like we were eating at home.

Price (10/10) - For all the variety and the taste of the food and portion size, each dish was only about $15. The portion was filling and the whole meal only cost about $55 (including all that SF tax). Super good price for quality and taste.

Absolutely would recommend. Try it!

Was in search for a local brunch spot near Union Square and came upon Mr East Kitchen - the fusion menu looked unique and made a reservation (easy!) through Yelp (a few days in advance).

Came on a Sunday around noon time and the place was PACKED! Highly suggest making a reservation ahead of time.

The menu was pretty extensive - plenty of good options for a wide variety of diets or restrictions. Some of the items are more "fusion" than others. We got the Tom Yum omelette and garlic noodles bowl. For the Tom Yum Omelette, think Tom Yum soup ingredients packed in an omelette form - super flavorful and unique! Garlic noodles was also delicious and the portions were filling. We didn't try any drinks but a good amount of both coffee and tea drink options.

We thought the prices were relatively reasonable too, by Bay Area standards. Servers and staff were all super friendly and attentive.

YUMM if you love Vietnamese/Thai fusion food, this place is for you. It's not as well known as other brunch restaurants in SF but it definitely deserves more recognition!

My recommendations:

Thai Tea French Toast: 9/10 - delicious and creamy thai tea sauce drizzled over thai tea infused french toast.

Pandan Waffle with Fried Chicken: 9.5/10 - the salty and crispy fried chicken paired perfectly with the coconut pandan waffle. The waffle had a light sweetness to it and did not taste heavy at all. Chicken was crunchy and juicy.

Omelette Fried Rice: 8/10 - they did a great job of infusing the fried rice with the omelette and the egg was nice and fluffy.

Overall solid place and I'll definitely be back.

Breakfast at Mr East Kitchen was fantastic!

Food: We tried the Saigon Steak, and the chicken and pandan waffle which was just sweet enough as to not really need syrup even though it is included.

Drinks: Vietnamese Dalgona ice coffee is super tasty and their unique mimosa flavors were refreshing.

Service: fast and friendly even without reservations

Space: Cute space with clean minimalistic decor and comfortable seating.

This place is such a gem!!! Really a true 5/5 stars

- Ambience: beautiful interior decor, ample seating, and great jazz soundtrack when I was there

- Food: delicious! from pumpkin curry to hainan chinese chicken, they were all authentic and well executed

- Price: actually really reasonable for the city! can't complain

- Service: It's always been friendly, but i HAVE to give a shoutout to whoever is working at 2:30pm 7/7. I ordered to-go because I meant to eat somewhere else but my plans changed and they were so accommodating to let me eat dine in instead and made sure my water was kept full without being intrusive.

I can understand why my friend who lives nearby ate here 5/7 days of the week when he first moved in

Wow, the Tom Yum Noodle Soup was absolutely fabulous. Probably the best noodle soup I've had all year! Definitely going back for that, and the extensive menu has many other yummy things to try!

The garlic noodz coulda been tastier, more garlicky.

It gets packed for brunch and lunch!

My review is for their thai tea french toast. It sounded really unique, so I had to try it. I ordered it as a combo with bacon. The french toast itself is good. It's very well done with a nice custardy center. The thai tea is served on a spoon that you pour over the french toast. The thai tea itself is really good as well. I could literally drink a glass of it. However, as a "syrup" for the french toast, I don't think it worked too well. The thai tea flavor gets lost and just gives a very subtle hint of it with the french toast. Not what I was expecting, but at least the french toast was done well.

The combo came with potatoes and sriracha bacon. I was intrigued by the bacon so I had to try it. At first bite, it was a little confusing like I didn't know what I was eating. As I let the flavors settle in my mouth, it actually became pretty addictive. The sweet, salty, and spicy combo works really nicely! Definitely a must try.

Are you looking for a cute and affordable brunch spot in SF? Mr. East Kitchen is for you!


Thai Tea French Toast 4.5/5
Crispy Chicken Fried Rice 5/5
Sriracha Hot Wings and Garlic Fries 4.5/5
Salmon Curry 4/5
Florentine Benedict 3.5/5

Thai Tea French Toast was good! I love how there was Thai tea and espresso mixed. The French Toast was soft and moist. However, I do wish it was more crispy. Crispy Chicken Fried Rice was so tasty. It had so much flavor and filling. It reminds me of the Vietnamese fried rice Com Chien Ca Man, which translates to salty fish fried rice. One of my favorite dishes growing up. The fried chicken was so crispy and went perfectly with the fried rice. Sriracha hot wings and garlic fries taste like fish sauce chicken wings with a hint of sriracha. Garlic fries had a lot of garlic, were cooked perfectly, and were crispy. Salmon Curry is good. The curry had a perfect amount of coconut and tom curry with a light kick of spice. Florentine Benedict was good, like any other Benedict. The egg was cooked perfectly.

Overall, the star dishes were the Crispy Chicken Fried Rice and the Sriracha Hot wings with garlic fries. Every item was a reasonable price. Good portions. The staff were really friendly!

Came here for a late brunch/lunch on Saturday around 2:30 and didn't have to wait, but they were about to close their kitchen. They have a very full menu so it was hard to choose but I got the hainan chicken and my friend got the Saigon steak. Not the best chicken rice I've had but it was solid. Their other Asian fusion brunch items looked good so I would come back to try. Service was great and didn't feel rushed.

This place was soo good!! Best brunch ever because of the spin/ fusion flavors. Made a reservation night before easily for prime sunday brunch. It was no wait as a result which was amazing and rare fro a sunday brunch

(5/5) The fusion flavors are sooo good. Got the omelette fried rice and really appreciated how flavorful the shrimp and food was under the egg. Paired nicely and mixed well w the rice

(5/5) My friend got the chicken fried rice and the chicken was soo tender

U cant go wrong with either choice. But personally prefer the more breakfasty vibe

Would love to come back to try the other dishes :D and would come back for these two as well

This is a cute, quick breakfast and brunch fusion spot in SOMA. They were pretty busy on a Saturday morning but we made a reso and had no issues getting seated, and the food came out promptly. The service was quick and thoughtful (e.g., bringing shared plates for us to split the dishes). I also appreciate that you can make your meal a "combo" (add eggs and another protein, I opted for the sriracha bacon) if you want to try something sweet but still want a well rounded meal. We had the pandan waffle with fried chicken and Thai tea French toast combo - both were great! The dalgona coffee was also delicious and served in an aesthetic glass with gold spoon coffee stirrer, which is fun for those of us whose phones eat first. :)

Love the asian fusion brunch options! We got the Thai Tea french toast and Pad see ew. Both were really yummy. The french toast was nothing special in my opinion but the pad see ew had great flavor to it. They had a lot of brunch and lunch options it was hard to pick. It was not too busy when we went which was super nice. Definitely recommend if you are looking for a Thai fusion brunch

If you want me to jump out of bed at 8am to go get breakfast you need only whisper four words into my ear: thai tea and pandan. Seriously like, have you heard of anything better than fried chicken and pandan waffles?!?!? Oh, what was that, thai tea French toast?! Yes please, leave me here in heaven, thank you.

Thankfully the food at Mr East Kitchen was as good as it sounded. Even their coffee was particularly great, including their epic-sized latte that was served to me in a cup roughly the width of my head. Gosh I just can't describe how great both of these dishes were, I can only weep for the fact that I no longer live in SF and cannot go here once a week because you bet your ass I would if I could. San Francisco, see what majesty you have here?! Please do not sleep on this perfect brunch option.
Great food, cool, ambience, and excellent service at a reasonable price. Would recommend going here
Love love their noodle soups and rice plates here. Even the breakfast menu. Absolutely amazing people here very friendly and service is quick!

This place has amazing food. Had a delicious brunch with french toast that was amazing. The steak was yommy too. The saff was friendly the owner asked if everything was good and welcomed input. This place was cozy and clean with a touch of upscale class.

Im not sure why this place isnt packed cause the food and service were on point! And the drinks were all so flavorful without being overly sweet!

The place is spotless clean as well. Great spot for brunch
Great place for breakfast with very different and delicious foods. I tried the French toast and loved it. Speciality mimosa that tasted great. Service was excellent and I highly recommend this place.
Food was good, especially the syrup on my french. The service was great, extremely respectful. And the ambiance complimented the clean space for everyone to eat

I've come here for brunch a few times and our group also went to their bottomless brunch for pride. Everyone here is always super sweet and the service is amazing. Some brunch places, especially bottomless, rush you, but the staff here is super kind and always trying to help. It's also really easy to make reservations ahead of time, even for a larger group.

The food is also great. They have some fusion items which are delicious, as well as some typical breakfast items. I also like that they have a full selection of non breakfast, entree items. This is great for the friends who don't like breakfast, like me. There's always something for everyone. Will definitely come again.

We came here for brunch on Sunday and experience no wait time. They have bar seatings as well as tables, and we were quickly able to move to a table. The inside is adorable and the prices are extremely reasonable. I usually feel like brunch is overpriced in SF, but I was really happy with the pricing and portions here. They also have really good service and people kept checking in on us.

We got the tom yum soup to start. One portion was enough to split between two people as a light appetizer. They're known for their fusion items, so my friend got the tom yum omelette which he really enjoyed and said it was one of the best omelettes he's had. I got the egg and avocado sandwich with fries. The fries and dipping sauce were great, and the sandwich was pretty typical. Next time I'll definitely be more adventurous and try one of the fusion items.
Amazing flavorful food. We are from out of town but whenever we are in SF again, we are coming here. If there is a line, believe me, the wait is worth it

Amazing brunch spot! The service was friendly and it was quite easy to walk in and have a great meal. I loved the fusion twist - the tom yum omelet was a favorite! Fresh, fast and tasty. It was a touch loud but not so loud you had to shout to hold a conversation.

We stopped here and grabbed some of their delicious looking items we had seen on Instagram! They were good but lacking some flavor. The garlic noodles could have definitely used more garlic. I loved the texture of the tofu and that they were served with fresh vegetables. The Thai tea french was flavorful too but the Thai tea sauce did not really have a strong Thai tea flavor. I wish the sauce was thicker or better soaked into the french toast. In general, I do think they have a very fun and creative menu with a variety of items for everyone.

Great food, great service!! Highly recommended. We came in approx 11:30am on Memorial Day. They were busy but we were seated right away. Definitely worth the try. I can't wait to go back and try different items.

Came here on the weekend for lunch. It was super convenient being able to make reservations online so I didn't have to wait at all for a table when I arrived.

I got the lychee jasmine tea and the Tom Yum omelette. The tea was refreshing and I like that I could adjust the sweetness level. The omelette was delicious and the portions were just right. The potatoes were so crispy and the toast was nice and garlicky.

Service was friendly and efficient and I appreciate that it was clean inside (including the restrooms). Thumbs up!

Condiments were super clean. Service was great. Food presentation gets a 5/5 for me.

The Thai French Toast was delightful with a sweet and savory combination. I recommend making it as a combo by adding two eggs & sriracha bacon for an additional $5. The Thai sauce was not overly sweet and the sriracha bacon was SO GOOD! Even if your spice tolerance is not up there, you'd still be able to enjoy it.

For drinks, I had their Vietnamese Dalgona Coffee. ($5) Nothing special but I loved the creaminess of the drink. The coffee flavorful was very mild and tasted mostly milk.

I will be back!

I frequent here and I've never been disappointed by my visits! I've tried most things on the menu and have never disliked an item: they're all delicious and come with super generous portions.

My go to is definitely the crispy chicken fried rice. They use SUCH a good frying method that produces such a light airy crispy layer. I also love the garlic fries (ask for cheese!): they're shoestring cut and super crispy, comes in a sharing size.

The only thing I don't love is the banh mi- it was not what I really expected from a banh mi and the pickled veggies were a little thick cut for my liking. The appetizers are also much less cost effective than their entrees (besides the garlic fries).

I also love the service here: they're very attentive and kind people, and I always have a pleasant time. Highly recommend!

Also: you should check in on the tablets with your phone number for points: every 10 pts is a free drink!

I ordered the Beef Pad See Ew and wow what great flavor!!! Huge portions. I was able to eat half and save half for lunch the next day.

Can't wait to try their other dishes.

food was fantastic. The service was excellent I deliver the food and speedy amount of time. The ambience it's OK for this area. What's nice it is now opens seven days a week between 9 and 3 PM. Order two meals that were just as fantastic. also they have fantastic breakfast. I have not tried them out yet but will do soon.
Im from LA area and we always come here when we are in SF and it never disappoints!! FYI.. There have been times where the line is looonnnggg, worth the wait though

This restaurant has so many great aspects and I highly recommend everyone in the area check it out!

Right when I sat down I was impressed by the vibes/ambiance as the servers were all so nice and helpful, and the interior of the restaurant is very clean and has minimalist/aesthetic decorations.

The menu is also very diverse, which included many American brunch options, Thai/American fusion brunch, Thai entrees, desserts, and a variety of drinks.

Fried chicken sandwich with garlic fries: 8/10
Overall a solid dish that I really enjoyed! The sandwich had coleslaw and fried chicken, and the flavors were delicious. The chicken itself was a little dry but the coleslaw made up for it. The coleslaw had larger pieces of vegetable compared to other coleslaws I've had before, which made the texture better and personally improved the taste. The garlic fries also had the perfect texture and was not overwhelmingly garlicky (it wasn't drenched in garlic oil), and was very tasty with the sriracha mayo sauce.

Steak benedict: 7/10
I personally thought this dish was a bit bland but everything on the plate was cooked perfectly. I would have appreciated a little more saltiness/flavor from the hollandaise, but other than that I couldn't really complain. The steak was super juicy, and the jalapeno on top added a lot of flavor. Also, I usually don't like to eat kale but the kale salad was amazing and the dressing made it so tasty! Last, the homestyle potatoes were PERFECT. Like the fries, the texture was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.

Mango sticky rice: 6/10
The sticky rice was very tasty but the mangoes probably were not in season because they were sour. 10/10 presentation though!

I also got a caramel latte which was pretty good!

Overall, super diverse menu and I would definitely come back to try their other food items. I was super impressed at how all of the dishes I tried were cooked well and I wouldn't be surprised if all the other dishes were just as delicious. There's definitely something for everyone to enjoy here!

Loved loved loved it !
Best Tom yum omelette in San Francisco
A must try and not too crowded if you reach by 10:30am :)

This is my second time getting brunch at Mr East Kitchen, and the food and drinks have been consistently delicious and creative! The servers here are also very nice and attentive. My first time a waiter actually gave us a sample of the Thai Pink Milk which was so nice of him!! (You should get it)

Eating family style with friends, I've tried their tom yum soup, garlic noodles, fries, tom yum omelette, and the various other brunch combos. I really liked their tom yum omelette, because it was so innovative, and love their candied bacon with toast that comes with the brunch combos. Their salmon curry is also great if you're looking for a tasty lunch. However, I would only pass on the fried chicken and pandan waffles because the chicken wasn't as flavorful I expected, and there were only remnants of the pandan. The one thing I would absolutely recommend is the Thai tea french toast, or even dipping your pandan waffles into the Thai tea syrup!

Overall 4/5, and while I find general American brunch food a little boring sometimes, Mr East Kitchen creatively reinvents it by bringing elements of Asian culture, and is my new go to on Saturday mornings!

The chicken & waffles were amazing & so was our server!

I'll be back for sure!
I've recommended the by place several friends..

This is a spectacular brunch spot in SF. I've tried a few of their items and wow, I loved every dish! The Thai Tea French Toast and Banana French Toast are delicious sweet dishes that aren't overbearingly sweet. I love the banana syrup that comes with the Banana French Toast; it pairs really well with the magnolia that comes with a bunch of their dishes. The Salmon Curry Bowl is my absolute favorite. I love the way the salmon is cooked -- very moist, and it is not brown. It's seasoned quite well, too. The curry is what brings the dish home, though. I love the heat; it's not too spicy and pairs well with the salmon and rice. The garlic fries are out of this world. They're fried nicely, providing some crispiness and juiciness. I'm a big fan of the sriracha mayo. It adds some light heat to the fries and enhances the flavor. I've only had dinner at Mr. East Kitchen once, though I don't remember what I got. I think brunch is where they really shine! The employees are very kind, and they work quickly. There's usually a 15-20 (sometimes longer) wait for the food to come, which is rather quick considering the sophistication of these dishes. This spot can get busy during lunch time, but I've never had to wait for a table to open up. It's a very bright interior, though a bit cramped. At least the windows are large! I give them props for the clean bathroom! Overall, Mr. East Kitchen has quickly become a favorite of mine, and I can't stop recommending this to friends. This is a spot my friends and I love to visit when our breaks line up; it's become a tradition at this point.

a good amount of seating, we had a big party of 10, so we were seated right by the door and it was pretty cold :\ the menu offered a wide variety of fusion options! every dish was well portioned, packed with flavor, and tasted amazing! the staff was super friendly, and the restaurant itself was clean and with minimal decor! 
- Thai tea French toast
- Saigon steak
- Crispy chicken with egg fried rice
- Tom yum noodle soup 
- Fried chicken & pandan waffles
Amazing Asian fusion brunch. Love the pandan waffle and Tom yum omelet. My friend got the Vietnamese iced coffee with this fluffy dollop of delicious foam on top. Easy to make a res. Cute decor.

If you're looking for the perfect Thai/Vietnamese fusion brunch place then you're at the right spot! This restaurant offers a variety of unique menu options that sets it apart from other brunch spots- for example the pandan waffle and tom yum omelette that we ordered. We came at around 2:30pm on a Sunday so there was no wait. The staff started cleaning up at 3pm which was when they close after lunch, but they were so sweet and told us to take our time with the food and not feel rushed. The interior had quite a lot of seating but you need to get lucky with street parking. Would absolutely come back!!

Someone in the group saw the Thai french toast and so we decided to try this place out. We arrived 2pm and were lucky to find parking one block away.

There was only one other table, we were given menus and told we could sit whichever tables we wanted. All the other brunch places that are insta-worthy with the flowers aesthetic is nice and all but I really enjoy the simplicity here. I really appreciate the variety of food they offer here compared to other brunch places. Their water don't taste good. Lol

Food:
Thai French Toast: Personally, I'm never a fan of sweet dishes. I think most french toast at these sort of brunch restaurant chain is just simply overrated. Thai flavor wasn't really strong enough for us, but we'd recommend adding on the Sriracha bacon, not much of a Sriracha kick, more taste of BBQ and ketchup.

Saigon steak: Exceed our expectations, beef was really soft and tender. But there's a after taste that I did not enjoy. But overall, still a great dish.

Shrimp garlic noodles:
Really good garlic noodles. A lot of garlic but I would ask for extra garlic next time. Comes with kale but I kind of liked it. Fish sauce for you to pour in but I didn't since I like my noodles dry, and fish sauce might take away the flavor of garlic. Shrimp wasn't that flavorful but still done well.

The best breakfast I ever had, it's just soooooo delicious am not exaggerating, this people really know how to cook , the Vietnamese coffee so good!!! And the amazing people working here are so friendly definitely 5+ stars!!!

We got seated right away since me and my cousin walked in a couple minutes after they open and the ambiance was super spacious and nice! We had the pandan waffle combo and the fried chicken sandwich with garlic fries! Our drinks was the pink dalgona and regular dalgona iced coffee! We also ordered the holiday matcha latte for my sister who was too hung over to join us (it was nye)! Overall, the portions were huge and worth the price! Would definitely be coming back & hopefully with my sister next time :))

This place has been on my to try list for a while, and I'm glad I've finally gotten around to eating here for brunch! I first found the restaurant on social media, and I loved the concept of Asian fusion for brunch.

I took some of my friends here after a night out, and the space is cute. I got the Dalgona coffee, Saigon steak, and split the iconic Thai tea French toast and pandan waffles. First, portions are incredibly generous. The coffee was amazing, my steak was good but a little dry at some areas but the flavors were well balanced, and the desserts were wonderful. The menu was super diverse and unique, and I definitely plan on coming back again to try other things in their menu.

Service was pretty good as well.

Excellent food. Breakfast / brunch dishes are cooked to perfection which my wife likes. I like to order the noodle dishes. They display the food very well and they place a flower on it to add to the color. The staff is very nice, friendly, and professional. Food comes out within 5-7 minutes. There usually is a line for lunch so go early or expect to wait for a couple minutes.

Mr east kitchen has a fresh look with delicious food. The servers were extremely hospitable.
The dalgona coffee did not disappoint and was delicious.
The garlic noodle bowl was filling and filled with umami .
The chicken and rice dish came together with a delicious dipping sauce.
Overall highly recommend to have a quick bite or hang out with friends. Would definitely visit again !!

I come here quite often because it's close to where I live and I absolutely love this place! The portions are generous for a reasonable price point and the food quality is always great. The workers here are so nice and accommodating and the interior is very clean.

I've tried A LOT of things on the dinner menu and my three favorites are:
1. Pad see ew
2. Garlic fries
3. Crispy chicken fried rice

The breakfast Tom yum omelette is really amazing too if you go during that time!

Came here on a late Friday and got seated immediately. This spot is relatively small, but has a chill vibe with a great playlist to match while you enjoy your food. The staff was really nice and quick with our orders out in about 15 minutes or so. I went with the Salmon Curry. I will say, the presentation of this dish definitely struck me. I feel like I've been to enough places where something plated this well tends to cost much more, especially for big cuts of salmon like this. It was tender, and topped with plenty of garlic. You won't be disappointed as the meat easily comes apart. I also really enjoyed the curry. I tend to like curries on the thicker side and can't stand it when it's too watered down. For me, this felt just right, and had plenty of flavor. You also get a good amount of rice on the side, important for helping mop up any leftover curry you might have at the end.

Overall, I recommend checking this place out. It's nice, it's casual, and you get a solid value meal. I imagine myself returning to try more from the menu.

a real gem for breakfast or brunch. The siracha bacon eggs benedict was fantastic, eggs cooked just right and beautifully presented plate.service was around 20 minutes for food . Went on a thursday right before lunch hour plenty of seating. Good amount of food for the price.

Food: came here for brunch and ordered the shrimp omelette. Looked good but very tasteless. The sriracha sauce from omelette also soaked the fruit, giving everything that flavor. The Thai tea though was good.

Service: prompt service, with nothing really standing out one way or another.

Ambiance: small diner with a lot of traffic. Lots of stool seating looking into street.

This is such a late review but the food was soo good that I had to. I stopped by here to pick up a quick lunch. I ordered the garlic noodle bowl with beef and a jasmine milk tea. The noodles were sooo good, so much garlic flavor. The beef was also super tender. I also loved the little side of veggies especially the Bok choy. Also huge portions as I felt really really full. The jasmine milk tea was also really good, super chewy and bouncy boba. Highly recommend stopping by.

I wish I got the name of our server; he was super nice! We dined on Sunday, March 24th, around 2 (owners of this account, please give him a shout out for us)! We had 5 with us and 2 friends came in last minute, and they were super accommodating.

I had the salmon benedict. I'm used to a few slices of smoked salmon on benedicts from everywhere else but they serve their salmon benedict with a full filet. Not complaining! Loved it. My girls got their new pink dalgona, it's on the sweeter side. I had the Vietnamese dalgona and it was perfect for me. Since we had a bigger party, we shared the Pandan Waffle and thai tea french toast as dessert. I must say, if you have room, do try the pandan waffle.
Great food and very good quality. It wasn't busy for Sunday brunch which was surprising. Ambiance was good too.

Absolutely delicious. I went in for a weekday brunch and there was no wait to be seated. Order and pay at the counter, then they bring the food to you.

I ordered the garlic fries, pandan waffle and chicken, and thai tea french toast. The garlic fries were amazing. I loved that they had their own spin to the fries. It came with packets of ketchup. The chicken also tasted garlicky which made the chicken breast flavorful. The pandan waffles lacked pandan flavor but I loved the sauce. They gave apple mustard sauce. I absolutely hate mustard but this sauce was truly amazing. I can literally taste the apple flavor and then a savory flavor follows. The thai tea french toast really had the thai tea flavor to it. The fruits it came with made it a fulfilling meal.

I definitely recommend this place if you want brunch but you're tired of the same american menu options. This place puts an asian flavor twist on things
11/10 food presentation, quality and taste! Great service and such a cute spot. We visited back in January '23 and still talk about this place!

The Thai Tea French Toast was perfection!! This was my first time here, and this meal was great. The price point of $14 for the dish was more than reasonable.

I also ordered the lychee mimosa, and it was decent. Would not order again, but this is more of a personal preference.

If you're looking to try something different from a traditional breakfast, I highly recommend this place. Upon entry I was warmly welcomed by the host and promptly seated. The host was attentive to my needs and checked in to make sure everything was still good. I ordered a tom yum omelette and dalgona vietnamese coffee. I cleared the plate! I was so happy to have visited this place and will be coming back.

Food and service was amazing! We had the Thai tea French toast and Tom yum omelette and it was delicious and very unique. Service was great and they even set up a table outside since we came with our dogs. Highly recommend!

Came here today after taking a nap from an early flight and it was busy but we were still seated immediately, service was great, food was delicious. Sriracha bacon was very different and well cooked and flavored, French toast and waffle was great as well as the Vietnamese coffee. Will definitely be back.

Yummy food at very reasonable prices for SF, what more can you ask for?

Mr. East Kitchen has become one of our household go-to for getting a great Asian fusion meals at good price points in Soma. They give out sizable portions with good flavor, and is good for both dinner and brunch. Their banh mi sandwich has juicy pickled vegetables with lots of meat and absolutely love the garlic fries. The Hai Nan Chicken is always a tasty option if you want something healthier. For weekends, definitely recommend trying their French toast. They also have plenty of seating option typically so no need for reservations.

Wow, this place is a sleeper. The food is really great. I looked at the menu and it's pretty much all my favorite foods in one place. Went with a couple friends and we ate family style. We got the garlic noodles with chicken. Loaded with the good stuff and picked vegetables to cut through the fat. Also had a reasonable amount of veggies in the bowl.
We also got the Thai French toast which was a Thai twist on a classic. Lastly we got the Tom yum omelet with hash-browns and fruit.
We all got different coffee drinks and all were good. I like this place and would come back anytime.
The neon stag on the wall was a little weird and I didn't get it.
Also - I felt Bourdain calling in my ear, when I went to the bathroom, it was a tad gross. Like the base along the floor was super dirty, like they just sling around a dirty mop and call it good.

Food was fantastic, service quick and they allowed me to buy their sweet n sour sauce to go. It was packaged for travel and I would buy more if it was listed online. This sauce is some of the best I've ever tasted. Ambiance was outstanding. Highly recommend for a great meal!

Visiting from Indiana. The food was amazing. I had the chicken fried rice with sweet n sour sauce. Bakchoy and shallots were outstanding! The sauce was so good that I ordered it to go! Overall a 5 star experience

Lucky me to find this spot at the perfect time!
Portions are big. My salad with grilled salmon was so big, that I couldn't finish it. Delicious! Definitely coming back
Food tasted good and was fresh but the host was really rude, genuinely killed our meal.

One of the most innovative breakfasts I've had in a while! Mr East Kitchen really delivered on melding traditional Thai and Viet flavours unconventionally with brunch food, which I just love. The Tom yum omelette was so incredibly unique in the best way, the hanger steak Benedict was reminiscent of all the flavours of marinated meat in a banh mi or vermicelli bowl (lemongrass, fish sauce, sugar, etc) and the Thai tea French toast provided the perfect sweet note to end on while not being overly sugary.

All of the portions were huge - I came with an appetite but was not able to make a dent in the sides! The service was extremely attentive and our server was incredibly friendly and kind. Couldn't recommend this place more if you're looking to mix up your usual weekend brunch!

Surprisingly affordable brunch.

I tried the eggs benedict and the pandan waffles with fried chicken. While nothing was mind-blowing, it was all pretty good. The potatoes were crispy, chicken was juicy, eggs were perfectly poached. What really stood out were the prices. Paying less than $15 for a brunch dish in the city is unheard of these days, and yet there were no issues with the food, the atmosphere, the service, or the portion size here.

I definitely want to come back to try some of their lunch items. If you're craving American style brunch with a bit of a twist, it's certainly worth a visit.

We came to this place on a Saturday morning for brunch; it's a quaint place near an apartment complex. The ambiance was very open and lively. We were seated relatively quickly and the owner was very kind and patient while explaining the menu.

There is a promotion currently happening for the rest of the month - if you buy 3 entrees, you get a 4th one for free and in addition the owner was nice enough to give us one order of the dessert of the day for free!

The presentation of all the dishes were super cute and the food was all delicious! We ordered/received:
1. Thai Tea French Toast - The French toast was delicious and the Thai tea "syrup" when poured on top added just the right amount of sweetness.
2. Fried Chicken & Pandan Waffle - The pandan waffles were delicious and a perfect combination with the crispy fried chicken. The sauces it came with added to the flavor.
3. Dessert of the Day (Taro & Corn Tart) - These were delicious and not too sweet!

Overall definitely enjoyed eating here and excited to come back in the future to try the other items on the menu!

Food (3.5/5): We got garlic noodles, crispy chicken fried rice, and thai ice tea. I am writing this Everything tasted alright, but nothing stood out.

Service (5/5): You order at the front, and they deliver the food to your table. Better suited for a more casual meal!

Ambiance (5/5): The restaurant was very well decorated and well-lit.

Overall (3.5/5): Although nothing stood out to me, everything was pretty solid, and I would consider this a good spot for a casual meal.

Was craving a good Asian brunch place in soma, and came upon this place! While we weren't expecting much (the menu seemed kind of white washed) the food was pretty good but nothing spectacular. They do have a few unique items on the menu like Thai Tea French toast but the menu overall gave me conflicting feelings on what to order when I saw pho and banh mi on the menu next to fried chicken and French toast.

My friend got Pandan waffles and fried chicken which she loved! The chef also was able to tweak it for her and make her chicken spicy, which was very nice of them. I got the Florentine Benedict, and all the food was very filling. Good portion sizes. Like I said, nothing too special about the Benedict compared to other brunch places but I guess there's nothing too much you can do to make a runny egg special.

Service was very kind. Food was reasonably priced for downtown SF! Interior was modern and clean. Might revisit at a later time and try their other menu items just because the owner was very kind to us.

We came for dinner but their brunch looks really tasty! We got:
- Shaken Beef (5/5): Really tender beef smothered in a delicious sauce! Really homey dish when combined with rice and veggies. Sadly we had to pay $1 for rice when the dish was already $18, my only complaint.
- Hainan Chicken Rice (3/5): Hainan Chicken is normally very tender since it's boiled, but this chicken was very dry and tough on the bottom :( Perhaps they cooked it ahead of time and merely chopped it for the plate. It wasn't worth the $17 imo so I'd recommend passing!
- Thai Iced Tea boba (4/5): Tea was good, boba was a bit old. Tasty overall!

The interior is actually really nice, and it's hard to tell from the outside. Very clean and spacious indoor seating.

Decided to make a stop here on a Sunday morning. The restaurant was busy but my boyfriend and I were seated immediately. Service was on point, greeted my boyfriend and I promptly. I ordered the Tom Yum soup, which I've never heard before but the ingredients enticed me enough to order it, with fried chicken as the protein. My boyfriend ordered the chicken pho. The Tom Yum was oh so incredibly delicious! Then the fried chicken was a perfect flavorful crisp, with crunchy garlic taste, very freshly made. Even the waiter was like "you ate all of that?! That was a lot." I actually did finish the food because the flavor was phenomenal. You have bit of that sour taste, which wasn't overpowering, fish sauce for that hint of saltiness, and a slight kick of spiciness, which was just a perfect blend of flavor! I didn't have a taste of my the chow one pho but my boyfriend's bowl was just as empty as mine.

We decided on Mr. East Kitchen because 1 of us wanted brunch food and 2 of us wanted lunch food. And this place offers both! We got a Benedict, Pad Thai Shrimp & Drunken Noodle Beef. I must say they did a better job on the noodle dishes than the benedict as the egg came overcooked. Both noodle dish we got was good, and the portion was generous.

This place has a casual setting, you would order at the counter first and then get a table number assigned to have your brought over. I would love to try more items on their menu next time when I am in town, this is the perfect spot if your group is deciding between a brunch/breakfast or lunch place!

After meeting up with my parents, we decided to try this highly recommended restaurant. Each dish was not only delicious but also a feast for the eyes. The warm hospitality from the staff made the experience even better.
Probably our favorite restaurant in SOMA! When we go in the service is great and when we order out the food is hot and plentiful! Do yourself a favor and check out Mr. East!

I had gone here not long after Mr East Kitchen opened and I was not impressed. I'm glad I gave them a second chance and I'm sorry it took a few Years and Covid. The food was excellent! I really enjoy the Tom Yum soup with noodles. It's great. I'm glad they're still going strong and I'll definitely be a regular.

First time trying this place and I loved it. Came here for my gf's bday dinner. The pineapple fried rice was very interesting and no pineapple but was still good. I actually enjoyed everything. I definitely want to try their breakfast brunch menu. Service is also very good. The beef stew with bread and chicken and pandan waffle is a must get. Overall we enjoyed our meal and will be back.

Fresh and delicious. I'm always calorie conscious and they had a lot for me to choose from and a nice clean place with nice ambience! I really like their entire menu. I've never had a bad meal there that's for certain.

I just have to say this the food is delicious. I go there to get a quick bite now and again and it never fails to impress me simple good fresh food. That's what I like about them and the service is fast.

I looked up some recommendations when I came to visit SF last month and was so glad this place popped up. I liked it so much that I visited twice in the one week I was here.

For my first visit, I got the Saigon Steak and the Americano. The steak was done perfectly and the sauce is to die for! The coffee was smooth and was just overall a great experience.

The second time, I went for the Salmon Benedict and again, everything was cooked perfectly. I also got the Vietnamese Dalgona Coffee and the coffee was creamy and not overly sweet (but make sure to give it a good mix).

The service was amazing and everyone was so attentive and kind. They even remembered my face when I came back the second time. I highly recommend and cannot wait to return myself to try the other stuff on the menu!
The food was delicious and there were good vegan options. This will definitely be one of my go-to brunch brunch spots.

Mr. East is a must try. Not only is the food amazing but the service is sensational. One thing that makes Mr. East stand out is the staff. The staff are the most friendly hardworking conversational people. The vibes and ambiance are top tier. Special shout out to Emmy and Tran! May god bless them.

Wanted to try something new today and Mr.East Kitchen did not disappoint! The favors, presentation, and service were amazing! Would def recommend coming here if you want to try some good viet/thai fusion!

HOLY AMAZING BREAKFAST!!! This place is wonderful. Just drag your tired self here in the morning and eat this:

Thai Tea French Toast: Oh my God. Seriously. I could eat this every day.
Florentine Benedict: YESSS!
Siracha bacon. I can't even. Yes, just eat it.

Lovely hidden gem, casual, delicious food. Highly recommend.

Seriously one of the best breakfast I have ever had and one of the nicest dining experiences I have had in a while.

The gentleman who sat us and took our order was so kind and patient and warm with my two special-needs sons, one of whom is diabetic. We just felt completely at home in this beautiful space

And the food? I cannot tell you how amazing the food was. Unique takes on traditional breakfast items like French toast, were just out of this world.

Location is also very convenient to anybody visiting Moscone Center, Yerba Buena, MOMA or, if you like a bit of a walk, Union Square.

I would recommend this place to anybody!

NOT TOO SHABBBY. AN AVERAGE JOE. but there's nothing wrong with that!

Food has been reliable and great. I have had the Garlic Noodle Bowl, Florentine Benedict, Thai Tea French Toast, and Mr. East Pandan Waffle. Service has been generally fast, except the coffees do take a while to make. BUT did i note, the portion size is quite worth!

DEFINITELY WORTH A VISIT on a NORMAL day =D

This place is my FAVORITE breakfast place now the food is so yummy I would give 6 stars if I could. The waiter we had was so fun and nice. This place should definitely have a Michelin star. Very good place would definitely go to it again many times.
Food is DELICIOUS! We ordered the chicken pandan waffle combo, saigon steak, and spring rolls. Just wow. So much flavor in everything. Must try place.

My friend and I were looking for a brunch place on a Saturday morning before a visit to the museum and came across this place which wasn't too far. When we arrived, I think it might've been around 11am and the place had quite a bit of people dining in. The seating situation is you either sit at a table or they have you sit at the window. We both ended up getting a window seat together which wasn't too bad. We ordered, sat down, and when we got our food I was really really impressed with the plates.

My friend and I got the same exact thing, the Classic Two Eggs with Sriracha bacon and a side of Thai Tea french toast that we shared. I gotta say, the french toast was pretty dope, and I really liked the bacon cause the sriracha sauce they used for it, made the bacon taste almost like how a Western from Carl's Jr. tastes. I also like that there was fresh fruit included as well. The staff here is really friendly, which is a huge plus, especially for a busy spot like this. Next time I'm heading to SF with someone, and it's around brunch time, I'm definitely taking them here!

one of my top breakfast spots in SF!!! Foreal tho we went to sweet maple the following day and we weren't as impressed as this restaurant. Service is fast and friendly. Food was soooo good. Honestly I don't even like bacon but this place cooks it so heavenly. This was near our hotel and easy to walk to. Definitely coming back here!!
I loved my Saigon Steak. It was very tender and super flavorful. Would highly recommended!

I had such a hard time picking what to have for brunch because everything looked so good! Came here with some lovely friends and it was a pretty good time. I got the classic 2 eggs breakfast and it was solid, definitely did the job. The sriracha bacon was really cool, wasn't too spicy, and was the perfect tenderness.

Came here for brunch and found that the food looks better than it tastes. The Thai Tea French Toast was a cool twist on the classic dish, but it was disappointingly dry and flavorless, even with the Thai Tea sauce. The eggs were also not great (overcooked and generally just not good). The real standout were the breakfast potatoes -- they were so crispy and flavorful that I would come back just for them.

The vibe is pretty casual and service is good. The one annoying thing was that there were a lot of flies in the restaurant that I had to swat away from my food.

It's located in the financial district and therefore isn't very busy or packed. It was definitely a nice spot to come to lunch in between work. The restaurant itself is on the smaller side and I think it would feel crowded very fast if it was in a different location.
The staff however is very friendly and the food is A M A Z I N G. 10/10

This place has Asian fusion brunch and a solid selection of Thai food. Staff were super friendly and was very accommodating. Whether you want some fried chicken & pandan waffles, Tom yum omelette, bánh mì they got a lil bit of everything. Their mimosas were super tasty too. It gets a little crowded and luckily we were able to get a table, but you can make reservations too.
Delicious food, warm service, and a big menu with plenty of options. We'll definitely be back to explore more of the menu.
Such a great find! This place was so good! great food and coffee and the staff were excellent, highly recommend. The restaurant was so cute inside and I loved the vibe!

Ordered vegetarian pho and sticky mango rice to go last week and they delivered on all flavors, and so much more! I always ask for spicy pho but all I get at other stores in an extra pack of chilli oil, which is fine, but Mr east kitchen? They put habanero pepper slices or something in my pho making it just the perfect hot! And the vegetarian pho broth flavor is incredible!!! The sticky mango rice was brilliant as well - desserts always seem like they get over too quickly. If there's anyone to blame for it it is my greed for sweets.

The service too was quick and friendly. Quick temporary parking is available in front of the store for easy pickup, but because it is on main street, if you have to dine in you might have to find parking lots nearby.

The only thing I am bummed out, not just about this place, but most of them - is that they use a lot of plastic containers and it hurts my semi-San Franciscan heart to see so much plastic. Sometimes I don't order food from outside to prevent wastage of plastic. I wish there were options to bring our own container!! It would make us even more loyal and regular customers!

As for Mr East Kitchen, I am going to be your regular - and for anyone looking for tasty, optionally spicy, vegetarian pho, look no further!

First time trying their crispy chicken sandwich. Very crunchy and flavorful. The actual chicken breast was a bit thin but it made up for it in flavor. The fries are garlicky and well seasoned.

I had the Thai pink tea and it was not my favorite. I would give it a 3 stars. I asked for very little sweetener and it was VERY SWEET! I don't plan on ever ordering that but overall in the past their drinks have been good.

Garlic noodles are FIRE!! So delicious!! They always season the noodles to perfection. The veggies on the side are cooked perfectly with a nice crunch. Chicken is tender, moist and flavorful. Atmosphere is laidback, clean and welcoming. Staff is friendly and always go above and beyond.

Example: There was a couple sitting next to us.They got up and left and forgot their jacket. I didn't notice immediately. I ran outside to try to catch them but they were across the street. (I was so full from those noddles to run) I told the cashier and he jolted out after them and ran a whole block. (San Francisco length blocks) Poor thing came back to work huffing and puffing from the run but managed to get the jacket back to the custom. If I could give them 100 stars for customer service, I would.

I would highly recommend Mr. East Kitchen as a great spot to eat!

A cute brunch spot in SOMA with fun thai/vietnamese fusion brunch! There are a toooon of different options on the menu, and it was super hard choosing exactly what to get. Unfortunately, I think the dish I chose fell a little bit short of my expectations.

I ended up ordering the Omelette Fried Rice (replaced bacon with potatoes) - and I was SUPER excited about the Tom Yum flavor included. However, I was let down - there didn't seem to be much tom yum flavor at all & this dish was kinda expensive for a lackluster omelette. The fried rice wasn't anything extraordinary either. I think this was definitely the case of me ordering the wrong thing.

I will say that I would potentially come back & try other dishes though! there were some great Yelp reviews, so I'll rely on those next time when choosing what to order :)

My go-to brunch spot. I always take my family and friends to Mr East when they visit me.

I've been to Mr East over 5 times in the past few months and it always hits. Everything I've tried on the menu has been phenomenal.

Our go to is the delicious Tom Yum Noodle soup. We're obsessed.

The interior is also very cute and clean with lots of plant decor. The service has also been great each service has been very nice and attentive, even when they get really busy at peak brunch time.

Ordered delivery on DoorDash. The basil chicken and shaking beef was really flavorful. The pad see ew was good but chicken, although plenty was too dry. The portions are large and price for SF is decent.

4.5 stars! Very creative brunch fusion spot with tasty food. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because the portions are smaller than average so I'm not full. I do recommend getting the Chicken + pandan waffles, and Thai tea french toast!

I'm catsitting at my friend's place at Mosso this week and noticed Mr East was right around the corner. I noticed they had great reviews so decided to give it a try. My standard for Thai restaurants is the pad Thai. I got the shrimp pad Thai and was really impressed by the portion size and amount of shrimp given. The flavoring was a bit light for me but it's still one of the better pad thais I've had in the city and prob my favorite south of market now.

I've been here once in person pre-Covid and have ordered delivery twice during Covid.

The location is bright and clean, and the menu is a creative, modern take on classic, pan-Asian dishes and ingredients. The prices are very reasonable for the quality and quantity. The proprietor is also super nice and welcoming!

Last time I ordered via caviar I got...
Garlic noodles with five spice chicken ($15) - large serving of flavorful chicken on garlicky noodles served with fresh, crispy veggies
Pandan waffles ($12) - light waffles that are not too sweet. The syrup was quite unique, and a little reminiscent of Chinese cough honey and loquat syrup. Also really loved the fresh, sweet fruit
Taro Fresh Milk - the drink was just ok and the taro flavor was unfortunately rather diluted

Definitely looking forward to coming back

So I was quite surprised by the taste here. Their food is basically their take on the originals. If you come here for original food such as pho and hai nan chicken, you may want to rethink it. But if you're adventurous and is willing to taste a different take, they're great for brunch!

The pho has skirt steak instead of original Viet meats. The flavor is not pho but still delicious with bean sprouts and basil. There's plenty of hoisin sauce and sriracha to dip in.

The hai nan chicken isn't served cold but hot and the sauce isn't onion ginger but some weird sauce.

Both dishes are definitely worth trying. Top it off, they have 4 mimosas with the 4th one only $.05. Check them out!

Note: they also have basic bitch brunches options too so that's a plus.

So yummy!! I'm usually pretty skeptical about places that are more modern but serve "authentic" dishes. But this place definitely blew me away. We got pad Thai, papaya salad, Tom yum noodle soup, and pad see eww. All very top choices, papaya salad could've been a bit spicier but it is ok. Everything was well seasoned and very similar to the authentic taste. I took my Mom and Aunt here and they both approved of it. I would recommend the Tom yum noodle soup with crispy chicken which is so different! The servers are also very nice, and it is a fair price!

Banh mi hit or miss
Sometimes pickled
Sometimes not
Sometimes good amount of meat
Sometimes not

Today ordered salad as the side to the banh mi.
Got fries instead making whole box greasy and oily.

This place is cute, has some fun American brunch options with Thai flavors and some typical Thai dishes. No menu items that Thai people actually eat for breakfast though so don't expect that. It's American brunch with a Thai spin. Got the fried chicken with a pandan waffle and pad see ew. The pandan waffle was really good, but the fried chicken was forgettable. The pad see ew was fine but it had broccoli instead of the traditional Chinese broccoli so again this is catered to Americans. Food took a while to come out (about 30 minutes) and I can tell the wait staff felt a bit frantic so seems like they still need to work out their systems. Rooting for them tho! I'll probably come back b/c it's close to work but wouldn't necessarily go out of my way to come here.

Really good taste, have never had something like the thai iced tea sauce before. I'd give this place 3.5 stars if possible - their location in SF is not the best, but I'm grateful for their seating us immediately. My friend and I got mimosas here as well, but I wouldn't say this is the place to drink, especially if you order soup like I did

Amazing! Stumbled upon this gem, and we are sooo glad we did! Absolutely delicious! We have a fam of five, so we go to try a variety of items!
Salmon eggs Benedict- delish- eggs cooked perfectly
Bo kho- so flavorful! Perfect!
Chicken And waffles- the best of all items!
Chicken Pho - sooooo good ( our youngest fav)
Avocado Sandwich- crispy and light

The house potatoes are a must, Vietnamese coffee as well. The kids got black tea with boba to go and they loved it!

Mr. East kitchen exceeded my expectations. I got the Saigon steak as a breakfast dish and it was such a treat. The flavors were out of this world. Not only did I enjoy the breakfast choices, I enjoyed the team working as well. They were fast and friendly. I was greeted at the door as soon as I walked in. Such a cute little place to stop and have breakfast or lunch!! I will be back for sure

Can't believe I haven't written a review for Mr. East Kitchen yet. I remember coming here for brunch before COVID-19 days and appreciating the format - high-quality Thai, Vietnamese, and classic brunch dishes like egg bennies and French toast. The space is small, like most in SF, but cute and brightly decorated.

It's really incredible how every dish I've tried from Mr East is utterly delicious. The Thai and Viet dishes compare favorably with just about any restaurant in SF that focuses solely on those cuisines. Better yet, Mr. East Kitchen sources premium steak, chicken, and shrimp for its dishes, and you really can taste the difference. I've tried the following dishes so far:

- Drunken Noodle Beef
- Lava Beef
- Garlic Noodles with Shrimp
- Shaking Beef
- Thai Tea French Toast

all of which are 4/5 or 5/5 star dishes! Most of the lunch dishes come with super-fresh steamed bok choy or kale so there's some healthiness there too.

I was pretty worried about these guys once COVID-19 hit, since the brunch crowd is pretty much 100% dead, but now they're working hard to keep this place alive and offering all kinds of discounts for takeout, especially if you order directly from their website or on-site! I'm really not sure how they continue to keep working magic in their kitchen to turn out such high quality dishes with these discounts when their original prices are already super reasonable by SF standards (~$15 for any of the lunch entrees which come with a pretty big portion).

I almost forgot: they also have boba! Maybe not quite as good as some of the best standalone boba shops, but quite honestly as good as a mid-tier boba place like a Sharetea and surprisingly great quality for a restaurant that's already serving multiple other kinds of cuisines. I would even go so far as to say the best boba that I've ever had from a restaurant that's mostly focused on food (I've tried the matcha and Earl Grey and both were great).

Oh and the people who run this place and work here are lovely people too!

Come try this place if you haven't! Come get lunch here every week or every day!

Woke up hungover and craving something soupy. The only place open at 9am was this place!! So glad I found it because the service was excellent, food was great and the restaurant was super clean and cute.

The tomyum noodle soup was delicious, very lemon grassy and I was surprised that it tasted pretty authentic. Lots of veggies, flavor and I got mine with tofu.

Also ordered the beef pho. The chunks of beef was of really great quality meat. The omelette fried rice was also delicious and it came with bacon on top. There were mushrooms and shrimp inside the omelette.

The lychee fruit tea came a little sweet for my liking but overall this place exceeded my expectations :)

I went here for brunch, and it was absolutely delicious. The Vietnamese coffee was so good; recommend the iced version. I got the salmon benedict and ate the whole thing; the side salad was even amazing. The inside was clean and good lighting along with friendly staff. If I am ever in the SOMA area, I would definitely stop by here again; it's a must.

Soooo delicious! Love the Florentine Benedict, as well as the veggie soup. Eggplant and tofu is also the bomb. Everyone there is so unbelievably nice and friendly, just a very welcoming vibe. It's my go-to brunch spot!

OK, so I am obsessed with this place. While it's always great to stumble on something that you feel is new, these days it's better to share a find like this than to keep it to yourself. I've been there a few times now, and cannot say enough about the food, the service and the drinks. Think brunch menu with a Thai and Vietnamese twist. I dream about the Saigon Steak, as well as the Tom Yum omelette. The Spicy Sole Fish gives me my elevated fix for my east coast Fish & Chips. Food is fresh and portions are healthy. The Thai Lime boba tea directly hits my sweet-tart needs. Highly recommend!

Such a lovely spot!!

I love the variety of dishes offered here. They range from chicken pho, to eggs scrambles to salads.

I ordered the mr East salad and oh my gosh so so so good. It's a great balance of savory and sweet. The blueberry dressing isn't too strong and truly blends well with the flavor. To top it off the salmon is very well cooked.

They also have an extensive list of drinks : boba, coffee, mimosas. Drop by!

Salmon curry salad was good

Thai tea French toast was unique! I have e never seen that on a menu before. Also ordered Viet coffee which was nice and strong.

I came across this place on DoorDash and ordered the spicy salmon with rice. It was so good! The salmon was cooked perfectly and it was so flavorful. Salmon was cooked with green beans and red bell peppers. I liked that it came with steamed bok choy as well for when you want to balance out the flavorful-ness

I def want to try the other items on the menu!
The siracha bacon was so delicious and their Thai French toast was the perfect blend of sweet and savory!

Our brunch at Mr East Kitchen was AMAZING! We were so impressed with every single thing. The server was so nice and made sure we had absolutely everything we needed. The restaurant was cute and really close to our hotel. The mango mayo is everything I have ever needed.
Ordered the banh mi for pickup and it was incredibly disappointing. Bread was soggy and there was barely any filling in the sandwich.

After reading some reviews and looking through photos on Yelp, my wife and I decided to go here for brunch. And it did not disappoint! Staff was very attentive and helpful, not to mention funny! Must try the pandan waffles & chicken or the steak!
Very small, but cute interior. I was lucky to get a seat when I came with friends. The garlic noodles were really good, and the chicken was tender. The fries were also crispy and tasted good.

Excellent food and service! The plating was beautiful and our server (Tran) was super delightful to interact with. Service was quick and the food was tasty. We got the Tom Yum omelette, chicken bahn mi and fried chicken sandwich and each dish was amazing

Tried this one to try something new! Everything from breakfast to lunch and then some! We had the crispy fried rice and beef dishes. Steak Benedict was also great. Can't go wrong with just about anything in order here. Great customer service even though a little slow to start, but will come back again.
