This was a local restaurant for me and they offered reasonably priced items that were delicious. However the proportions for some dishes aren't great. For stir fries, I got too much rice and too little stir fry.

Pros: reasonably priced and taste
Cons: proportion size

Mr East Kitchen is an establishment built for "instagram-able" pictures with a large selection of Asian brunch cuisines.

Vietnamese dalgona Coffee 4.5/5
- Not too sweet but creamy with the right texture.

Garlic Noodle Bowl 4/5
- The noodles were rich in flavor but the steak was slightly over cooked and lacked flavor.

Thai Tea French Toast 3/5
Portion size was lacking but that explains why the price was cheaper. The thai tea sauce was good but the toast was dry.

They also had a promotion at the time where if you order four items you can get the fourth one (cheapest item) for free!

[Pre-Covid review]
It's been awhile since I came to Mr East Kitchen. I remember seeing all the hype on Instagram and decided to try it out with a couple of friends. The interior is nicely decorated and definitely an opportunity for a quick photoshoot with your food if you're feeling it.

I ordered the Thai tea French toast - an interesting twist on the classic French toast. It's definitely an IG-worthy dish - with lots of fruit, Thai tea sauce, and powdered sugar. I found the Thai tea flavor to be a bit weak, but overall it was good!

They have other options on their menu, like more traditional Vietnamese dishes and drinks that I didn't try. I think it's a great place for not just brunch but also lunch or dinner as well.

I do think the dishes err on the expensive side, but not too bad, especially since this is San Francisco, and I almost couldn't finish my food (I was pretty full), which is a good thing - so don't be deterred by the price.

One of our most frequented places while in SF. The food is incredible, portions are large, and the prices are some of the lowest we've found in the city.

Banh mi sandwich: 9.5/10, best we've had yet. The meat was so, so good. It was juicy and just the right combination of sweet and salty. The bread was soft and didn't hurt our mouths like most other banh mi's. Close to perfection

Drunken noodles: 9/10, so flavorful but a tiny bit too spicy for personal taste. A spot on drunken noodle dish though

Salmon curry bowl: 8.5/10 so creamy, salmon was well cooked

Crispy chicken fried rice: 8/10, chicken was juicy and well cooked

Vietnamese Dalgona coffee: 8/10, very strong flavor, a little too sweet, but still a very refreshing drink that we get each time

Was hungry for some lunch and wanted to get some Chicken Pho. I ordered that and a side of garlic fries. The soup was light but flavorful. I loved that it was northern Vietnamese style with the flatter, wider noodles. There was a good amount of chicken with the pho too. The garlic fries weren't overly garlicky either. Just enough garlic and salt seasoning.
Great customer service and didn't take too long to get our order. Eggplant tofu with rice was AMAZINGGG

great place for a carby asian inspired brunch!! the food's a little heavy so wouldn't come all the time but definitely when you need some asian comfort food.

for food i liked the tom yum omelette! it was a cool take on tom yum soup and comes with lots of salad and potatoes to complete the meal. the thai tea french toast is also great for sharing. pad see ew was pretty standard but tasty.

for drinks i recommend the lychee jasmine tea, very fruity. the drinks tend to be on the less sweet side and they let you customize sugar level. i would order one level above whatever you normally get at a boba shop. the passionfruit tea ended up being a bit too tart since we ordered low sugar.

Really good and fresh. Didn't expect toasty but soft ciabatta to work so well in a bahn mi. Wish the chicken had a little more flavor but the tenderness was perfect- I think they poached the chicken which makes it pretty easy to bite into. They also give a good portion of fries which is nice.
Excellent service, great food! Lychee Mimosa is a game changer. Really recommend the crispy chicken fried rice!!
Great twist on some classic breakfast/brunch items. Highly recommend Tom yum omelette and the Thai tea French toast. Fruit was actually fresh! Very friendly staff. Definitely recommend
So good! Decent portion sizes and I love the fusion dishes. I've come here twice now with separate people and never fails to hit the spot. Make sure you get the Lychee Mimosa too!
Wow ! Just wow. The food was flavorful, ambience great . The customer service was also really good and attentive ! I definitely want to come back and try everything on the menu !

A rather busy restaurant for its location. The food was very good. We ordered the garlic fries and chicken pho. The garlic fries were great. The pho was fine, but not the best I've ever had. I was jealous of some other people's food that came out. I'd like to come again to try other food.

It's just okay, I wouldn't come back.

Yelp says I need to type more. Try it if you want, the plating is very pretty, but the flavors were too subtle for me.
Food and service was great I will def be back for that Thai tea French toast it's amazingggg!

Mr. East Kitchen offers some pretty interesting and unique Asian fusion dishes on their brunch menu, such as the pandan chicken & waffles or the Thai tea french toast. They also have a good variety of "normal" dishes, like pho or fried rice.

The dishes that I tried this time around were the chicken pho, the Tom Yum omelette, and the mango sticky rice. The broth for the chicken pho was pretty mild in flavor, but it was honestly really refreshing and just what I was craving at the time. I only snagged a small bite of the Tom Yum omelette, but it seemed flavorful and was packed with ingredients. The mango sticky rice was probably my favorite of the three, the rice has a great consistency and paired beautifully with the sweet mango.

The price for each dish is a little steep, though they do generally give you a good amount of food. Also note that there is currently a "buy 4 items, get 1 free" discount, which is great if you're dining with a larger party. There were a couple of items on the brunch menu that piqued my interest, so I'd return to give those dishes a try.

Listen... When I tell you I dreamt of the Thai Tea French Toast two days after trying it... I just knew I had to write this review.

Mr East Kitchen exceeded my expectations and more. I cannot stop raving about it! I've been looking for more brunch spots to try in the area, and I saw that this place had East Asian inspired brunch so I knew I had to stop by. The restaurant itself is not too big, however the windows, lighting and greenery gave a nice feeling of openness I really enjoyed. We were seated quickly without a reservation. We got the Shrimp Benedict, Saigon Steak, Thai Tea French Toast and two Vietnamese Dalgona Coffees.

Our food came out so quick, which is something that rarely happens when getting brunch in my experience LOL. Our drinks were out first; it was a really interesting take on Viet coffee as it made the drink a lot creamier. I really enjoyed the curry hollandaise sauce from my benedict! The shrimp was tasty, however just a wee bit overcooked.. I think this dish would be perfect if it was a crab benedict. Fried potatoes were perfect!! From the size of the taters to the slight crunch you get in every bite... I inhaled my plate. You also have the option between salad and fruit, which I opted for a salad because I knew our french toast would have fruits. Even the greens were scrumptious n flavorful. The Saigon Steak was soo yummy as well!! I couldn't help but steal some bites from my bf's plate.

I gotta say, the star of this meal was definitely the Thai Tea French Toast. Despite having a major sweet tooth, I don't normally opt for sweet breakfast food items because I can barely finish my own entree, but for some reason this toast was calling my name and BOYYY I am so glad I got it we should've ordered one plate each. You get 3 pieces of toast, thai tea sauce and some fruits on the side to enjoy it. I loved the presentation and I had a blast drenching my toast with the sauce. Now you'd think it'd be a sugary flavor bomb explosion but everything was so perfectly balanced yall. The toast stayed firm yet fluffy despite being covered in the sauce and the thai tea flavoring wasn't overwhelming at all. The fruits complimented the sauce so well. I wanted to lick my plate so badly after our meal I kid you not. I loved how we left not feeling over bloated, which is something that always happens post brunch for me. Can you believe that we finished brunch and I jogged home for the last two blocks.... Who does that after eating dessert. This treat is a MUST try and I will for sure come back for more.

Another highlight of our meal was our server. We didn't catch his name but I believe he is the owner's relative. We were so surprised he wasn't the owner of the restaurant because he was so friendly and attentive with all the guests! He kept on checking on us throughout our meal and provided great recommendations. I thought it was hilarious how I asked him about a drink recommendation before ordering the Viet Dalgona Coffee, and he followed up with me at the end of our meal to tell me that he tried the one I originally wanted and saved me from making the wrong choice. Gotta love the honestly! Can't wait to try the Tom Yum Omelette and Pandan Waffles next time!! :D

Very neat and modern interior. The lighting was a bit green, which was an interesting choice. The dishes were creative and tasty. I got Tom yum omelette, which I never thought would be a thing but enjoyed it. The waiter that helped us was friendly and passionate.
Great brunch menu with lots of options for every kind of diner. Loved their breakfast food!

I ordered the Garlic noodles with chicken.

One of the best garlic noodz I've ever had, MUST TRY! So glad to have discovered this gem!

The chicken was super yummy too!

I really need to go back and try their brunch! They have Thai Tea French Toast, Pandan Waffles, and a Tom Yum Omelette! Some of my favorite flavors!!
Amazing everything! Food, service and ambience. The owner chatted with us and took our order. Personal touch was pleasant. Service was great. Ambience perfect

Great little diner place with nice vibes
This is a bit of asian fusion mix to it, the food was good and great presentation , bit too sweet for my taste though
Very good chicken pho. Will be back to try other dishes. Clean interior, and quick service.

Ordered take out from Mr East Kitchen today!
Highly reviewed and raved about by my friends so I decided to give it a go!

The food was really good and the portion sizes were pretty big! The garlic noodles were not basic at all, the noodles even without the grilled pork on top were deliciously seasoned and would have been really good on their own. The grilled pork was my favorite part! The pork was juicy and not dry at all, it was sliced into good bite sized pieces to either eat alone or to eat with the noodles. The vegetables on the side were nice and refreshing to cut through the heaviness of the noodles and meat! I particularly liked the pickled carrot and radishes!

If you want good Thai food that would probably last you for lunch and dinner then this is the place to go!!
Also the sticker on their packaging was super cute!!

This place never disappoints for breakfast/lunch/brunch. There is truly something on the menu for everyone, and the prices are quite affordable--especially for being in the city. The crispy chicken fried rice is their most popular item, and the chicken is juicy, crunchy, and tender! When I am craving soup, I like both the Tom Yum Noodle soup (not too spicy which I personally like), and the Chicken Pho. I got shrimp in my Tom Yum Noodle soup and the shrimp was perfectly cooked and so sweet! There is also a variety of yummy sweet items. My favorite is the Pandan waffles. They are not too sweet and have a yummy, airy texture. It is also nice that you can get a drink here and take it to go with you!

TIP: Do make a reservation online or call in in advance though! You will be seated much faster because people with reservations have first priority.

Food was delicious! Service was amazing! Very friendly and welcoming. Glad we stopped here.
Highly recommend!

This restaurant is in a great location less than a block from the Intercontinental on Howard and 5th. The menu is creative but accessible to even the most conservative palates. It's a very open, clean space where conversation is easy and private. The wait staff is attentive and charming. The food is prepared from fresh ingredients in a style that highlights the natural flavors. The price point is perfect! We enjoyed the Sriracha bacon and Eggplant vegan stir fry.

Came here for a Sunday Brunch and I have to say this might be my new favorite brunch spot in the city! The service was impeccable, as the servers were extremely polite and on top of everything (our water glasses were constantly full and we were waited on so quickly). As you can tell from the photos, the food was not only delicious but aesthetically beautiful. I've had many chicken and waffles, but the chicken and pandan waffles may have been the best I've had since the chicken was extremely juicy and the waffle was delicious. The ambiance was very picturesque and peaceful, and I would 100% recommend this place for a weekend brunch

An absolute gem of a restaurant! I was visiting a friend in San Francisco, and the only time that worked out for us to meet was around brunch...which I have to admit is not my favorite meal of the day nor my expertise. Thank goodness we stumbled upon Mr. East Kitchen! This delightful Asian fusion restaurant has a beautiful array of breakfast, brunch, and lunch dishes, as well as a delightful selection of drinks (and more traditional dishes if you come here during non-brunch hours). I tried out their Mr. East Salad, which is a delicious fillet of grilled salmon, diced avocado, sliced shallots, blueberries, and strawberries on top of a bed of kale and spinach. The salmon was perfectly crispy and delightful, and the natural fattiness of the salmon was a great contrast against the fresh greens, subtly sweet fruit, peppery cut of the raw shallots, and slightly sweet and sour blueberry vinaigrette. It admittedly felt a bit strange to be eating a whole fillet of salmon at 9 AM but it was delicious and, hey, that's what brunch is for. My friend tried out one of their other exciting fusion menu items -- their thai tea french toast. The thai tea sauce was the iconic vibrant orange color, and her plate looked absolutely gorgeous with the beautiful slices of texas toast and fresh fruit. She also tried out their Vietnamese dalgona coffee, which was AMAZING. Whether you're looking for a sweet or savory brunch option, Mr. East Kitchen will definitely have you covered!

Beyond their food, the overall atmosphere of the restaurant is absolutely delightful. The staff is incredibly kind, helpful, and attentive, and the entire restaurant is clean and modern. The storefront is entirely glass, so there's an abundance of natural lighting, accented by their cute blue walls and lovely decor. I'm honestly so sad that I was only in San Francisco long enough to try this place once -- I can't wait for the day when I can visit again and try out the other incredible items on their menu.

I had a wonderful brunch with a friend here a few days ago. The venue is clean and the staff is quite nice. I had a delicious chicken and waffle (pictured). Well many people might be put off by the sight of green waffles, they bring back memories of childhood for me. I would absolutely go again, I love the idea of breakfast and Asian fusion.

I came with a friend on a Sunday for lunch. We made a reservation and ran ~15-20 minutes late, but our reservation was still honored, which we were so grateful for. We got the Thai Tea French Toast combo and the Pumpkin Curry to share. The french toast combo was so tasty, with the most delicious thai tea drizzle. It was nice that the sauce came in a separate little container, so you could control the amount on the toast. The pumpkin curry was also great and had the right balance between savoriness and sweetness. Both dishes had beautiful presentation. The service was great, and the staff were so friendly! The restaurant itself also feels bright and airy. Will be making another visit in the future!

Drove to the city to try this place out cuz we wanted something new, asian and looked healthy.
Upon arrival, this place was very unexpected. There's a counter you can walk up and order to go, with limited space to wait.
Don't let that steer you away. You can choose to dine in. There's lots of great natural lighting for this instagrammers and presentation of food is superb.

We were quickly seated and the server was very attentive with great suggestions of local fav items. We orders the Tom yum omelette and a steak Benedict.
The flavors were new, interesting and refreshing that all worked out well. Potatoes were perfectly crisped and side salad was super tasty with wonderful power greens!! Every bite was quite orgasmic. We couldn't shut up about how great everything was.
I got the lychee sparkler as well and that was very delish.
On top of that, they were offering a 20% discount to customers if at review was done. First time I got to flash my elite status and show them that I didn't have time to leave a review, but for sure would be when I got home and had more time. Ahahahah
The team was delightful and my bf and I both agreed that we would be going back to try lunch items!
Great job Mr East!! Thanks for a fabulous brunch.

Came in on a sun and lucked up as the waitlist was only 15min. Stayed in a hotel close by so was able to walk a few blocks as I'm glad I did as there was street parking only.

The location is small. They had two tables outside but for the most part it's indoor dining.

I was greeted & seated quickly which was nice. I ordered the Thai Tea French toast w/ siracha bacon, fruit and scrambled eggs (what the majority of folks come in for lol)

The French toast was fluffy but the Thai tea syrup was OK. I personally would've enjoyed it better w/ reg syrup. They douse the bacon in this sweet si racha sauce that made it hard to enjoy as well. I'd order that on the side

Fruit was fresh & eggs were good.

I would come back to try other things

Randomly found this place on Yelp near union square and now is going to become my new fav place. My bf and I got the Tom yum omelette and the Thai tea French toast and wow the flavors are amazing!!

Tom yum omelette: so flavorful with tons of shrimp. They didn't skimp out. Paired with crispy potatoes and salad or fruit. We got the fruit.

Thai Tea French toast: my new favorite French toast. It was chewy almost like mochi. Eating it alone had some Thai tea flavor but it was all in the sauce. Light and not heavy Thai tea flavors that' def enhanced the French toast. Paired with fruit.

Would highly recommend and def coming back. Parking was a challenge but we were able to snag a 1 hour spot in the one way street on the side.
The food was amazing. The best bacon I've ever had. The service was great and it's such a chill spot. Fruit was very fresh!

I found this spot last minute before my gf and I were preparing to head back home after visiting San Fran for a few days. Based on Yelp reviews, we decided to give it a try. Although reservations aren't required, I made one for 12:30. We arrived at 12:15 and were immediately greeted and sat at two top. The restaurant is cute and quaint. I will say that the tablea are close but we didn't feel crowded at all. The waiter was nice and provided us with water as soon as we sat down. A few minutes later he came back and asked if we were ready to order. We weren't quite ready yet but did want to start with an espresso, lychee martini and salmon bites. Once he returned, we ordered Fried Chicken & Pandan Waffle and the Tom Yum Noodle Soup with chicken. There was only one waiter who appeared to be handling everyone's table so it took a good 15 minutes into our meal before we received drinks. But I will say the Lychee mimosa was well worth the wait! The salmon bites came with broccoli and sweet potatoes which were all lightly tempura battered. The dipping sauce paired with it accompanied it well. The Tom Yum soup was flavorful and a great portion. However, I would probably opt out of the chicken next time because it seemed to be a mixture of white and dark meat and I prefer white. The waffles were great and had a unique taste and green hue. Perhaps they were made with green tea. Nonetheless they were rich and delish! All in all, I'd try Mr East again when back in the area.

Very good value given the serving portion!! The omelette captures the Tom Yum flavor really well with generous portion of shrimp. The satay and veggie spring rolls are pretty standard. I personally would like the chicken to be more roasted. Overall, it's a solid brunch place. The service and ambiance are ok although being a little crowded and loud. Would come back again to try more things!

Ordered catering from here last week and everybody was pleased with their order. Each order came with a label of what the food was and the persons name which came in handy when we were trying to see whose was whose. Their portions are also great and you really can't beat the price for what you get. I would definitely consider using this place for all your catering needs.
Good food and good service. Will be coming back when I visit SF again. Also, very clean restaurant.

10/10 would recommend.

If you're not sure if you're craving Thai, Chinese, or Viet this place is probably right for you. We ordered Thai food, Pho (Northern style), Hainan chicken, and all of the dishes were relatively good. Mr East Kitchen usually has a lot of promos so out of the 5 dishes we ordered one was for free. My friend got a Coconut mango as a dessert and that was delicious.

This place is amazing. The staff were great and they knew exactly what to recommend. All the meals we had were beautifully presented and were super delicious. You honestly cannot go wrong with any selection you make. Obviously if you do not like waffles do not order waffles. The desert was good but not as good as the food. We are definitely going to go back when we get back!

Came here for Mother's Day Brunch and made a reservation on open table. When we got there our table was already ready. They brought out our drinks within 5 min of ordering and our food 10 minutes later. Service is amazing

Food:
Thai tea French toast is the reason I come here. The sauce is perfect and taste like Thai tea but not overpowering sweet.

Tom yum omelette was also delicious and love the Tom yum flavors.

Pandan waffles was just alright. Wish it was crispy.

Overall would highly recommend this place. Street parking can be difficult to find but luckily we found one a block away.

I saw they won top 10 brunch on Yelp recently. so I gave them a try. The food was pretty good. I'll definitely stop in when I'm in the area. I ordered the fried fish substitute garlic noodle instead of rice. The fruit tea was wonderful too.

Stumbled across this place while killing time before our movie at Metreon. Wow! It's not often I give 5 stars, but looooved this place!

We were first attracted by the cute ambience. The service was prompt and we got seated right away.

Excellent Asian-fusion brunch food. My partner really enjoyed the omelette-rice. My Saigon Steak was what I will remember for a long time. The beef was so tender, and the sauce so flavorful. Combined with the crispy potatoes, garlic toast, and a side of rice - it was perfect!

My only slight note is that the service could have been around more frequently to check-up, but I know they were super busy. I had to get up twice to ask for stuff, but to their credit, they took care of my requests instantly.

I think we now have our new go-to place for pre- or post-movie meals!

This is a great cute brunch spot! I went here for a double date on a sunday morning and made a reservation just in case it was busy. The reservation process was extremely easy and were seated immediately. The location is a little on the small side but the big windows make the space feel a lot more open.

As for the food the coffee was a bit too sweet for me but that just comes with ordering dalgona coffee. The salmon eggs Benedict was delicious but slightly on the water side with lots of hollandaise sauce. The pandan waffles were fluffier than traditional vietnamese pandan waffles but it had a decent pandan flavor. The fried chicken was crispy and juicy. Overall a great brunch meal and considerably not too expensive for SF.
Never disappoints. Still one of my fave brunch places in the city. Yummy food... best service.
I love brunch and exploring new brunch places. This is a new find for us. No waiting, good service, good food & very reasonable prices. Will surely be back.
Food was great!! Tran & M gave us recommendations & they were perfect tum yum soup & shaking beef (I think it was called)
Food was so good - I had the chicken and waffles and a yummy drink which I can't remember the name of but it was creamy like coffee like - amazing - staff was so helpful - I can't wait to go back

I'm always a fan of unique food creations and Mr East Kitchen was the spot for that!

O R D E R E D
- Thai Tea French Toast
- Steak and Eggs
- Chicken Pho
- Garlic Noodle Bowl
- Lychee Jasmine Tea

V E R D I C T
Believe it or not, this was the first time I ever tried chicken pho and it was amazing [at least from Mr East Kitchen it was]. They even had a promo happening where you order 3 dishes and get 1 free. Of course I hopped on that and got 4 dishes, cause WHY WOULDN'T I?! The lychee jasmine tea is so refreshing and doesn't taste like its water and syrup, so I appreciate that.

I will be back to try their super fruit jasmine tea, fried chicken & pandan waffles, and mango sticky rice.

Mr. East Kitchen was my first meal after a long move to SF, and I'm so, so happy that it was!

I'm usually a skeptic about fusion flavors, but this restaurant completely changed my mind. The menu is testament alone to how thoughtful the restaurant owners & staff are. Besides the cute handwritten sign outside featuring new dishes, their menu had so many unique items I wanted to try - like Thai tea French toast, garlic noodles, shrimp benedict, and Saigon steak (among other traditional dishes as well)!

We decided to go all-in on fusion flavors and had the tom yum omelette and fried chicken & pandan waffles, and they were as stunning and delicious as they sound!

Tom yum omelette: I loved the lemongrass flavors and real seafood in the omelette, and the salad was surprisingly well-dressed and had a lot of variety. The garlic toast was crisp and fragrant - a perfect complement!

Fried chicken & pandan waffles: The chicken was hot, juicy, and well-seasoned, and the pandan waffles had their subtle but signature sweet flavor. Both great by themselves, even better together and with the accompanying sauces!

Besides the food, the ambience was modern with bright natural lighting, and the service was friendly and attentive! The prices are reasonable for brunch, and honestly worth every penny.

I've passed this place a few times and it looked cute so I was looking forward to trying it. I came at about 11:30am on a Sunday morning with a friend. There is mostly communal seating, and you order at the counter and they bring it to you.

I got the Morning Green Salad ($10+ $3 chicken), and when I was ordering the man didn't seem to understand what was in the salad when I was asking questions about the type of proteins offered. It was a bit frustrating, but I finally was able to order. It was definitely a good portion size for the price and it wasn't bad, but I felt the chicken was a bit too salty.

My friend got the Omurice ($15)- which came with fried rice, egg, and bacon. It looked like a pretty big portion, except while eating it he discovered a lady bug! They brought him a new one pretty quickly.

We waited over 30 minutes to get our food and overall, I was not super impressed with this place.

I came here with my mom and we ordered the thai tea french toast and tom yum omelette, both of which were tasty. The thai tea french toast was good and the thai tea syrup had a strong and yummy thai tea flavor, although I wish it came with more! The tom yum omelette was quite yummy as well. Our server was extremely sweet and made us feel at home.

Mr East Kitchen

I'm so happy! I can walk to an affordable breakfast spot steps away from my home. Everything on the menu sounds amazing... pandan, thai tea, and more! Usually if I wanted something like this, I'd need to drive at least 20 minutes out and a little more for parking troubles elsewhere. I don't think this is a place you should come out of your way across town for, but definitely a "I'll try it!" spot. :)

The Food
My expectations weren't high nor did I come in starving. I ordered a Thai Tea French Toast Combo which was less than $20 and he got a Vegan breakfast sandwich, which was two hash browns and a salad in between. I wiped my entire plate clean and probably just left the orange ring that was served. For a cheap breakfast, I was pretty happy with my order. As for him, his meal was light and was able to continue to breathe and walk once we left. Our orders were good and we were satisfyingly full afterwards.

The Drinks
We ordered a Thai Tea boba and Vanilla Latte, both subbed with Oat milk. We don't have any complaints.

The service
We came in at 10 am without a line or wait time. There were more people picking up other peoples' or their own food rather than sitting down. We were immediately seated, given water, and our drinks came in no less than 3 minutes after having ordered them.

Alternatives
You can totally opt to pick up your food and order online. Right now they offer 20% off your purchase which I think might be more worth it than to dine in.

I'll happily come back to try more things. Can't wait.

Came here for lunch with a friend originally excited to try their brunch items but those are only available on weekends :((

Instead we opted for the shrimp pad thai and garlic noodles with grilled pork. Portions are generous but taste was barely there. The grilled pork was also dry and on the tougher side.

Interior was spacious and has the typical rustic modern chic vibe you see with a lot of new restaurants. Service is good as well.
Amazing breakfast spot. Unique flavors and such good salad with breakfast! Service was quick even though they were busy. Thai tea comes without sugar so you can sweeten to your likeness. Yum!

In San Francisco for Memorial Day weekend and came across this gem
Food was delicious and service on point
Great place!!

I have been here multiple times and my go to is the pad Thai! It is so he best that I have tried in the Bay Area. Their coffee drinks are delicious. The service is always wonderful. All the hosts are attentive and kind. Prices are reasonable and portions are great! Highly recommend.

This restaurant is on par for what you expect in SF. The waiters were very nice and the space was relaxing.

Eggplant tofu was amazing, the sauce kept me eating! Tofu was firm and a bit chewy, I really enjoyed it. The pad Thai shrimp was good, shrimp seemed a bit over cooked but there was some nice flavor. The garlic fries were super garlicky and well fried. If you like the garlic fries that are dripping in oil flavor this will be perfect for you.

I'd say overall a good spot to eat, one I would eat at again. A solid spot.

Mr East Kitchen filled my cravings of some good eggs benedict, and I took the chance to get it on a Saturday morning. Ice heard that only appears on the menu for weekends and I have to say that it was worth the walk from the hotel to get to.

I ordered the eggs benedict with steak (comes by default medium rare but you can adjust it) and garlic fries because I can.

The fries were quite garlic-flavored and crispy, which I enjoyed quite a bit. The garlic is quite strong so it's mainly for those who really like the sensation of medium-heavy garlic. It wasn't oily which was nice and I thought it was a nice side to the main course.

The steak eggs with benedict were great. Had a nice oozing egg on top of the steak which had both tenderness and packed a lot of juices which I like.

The portions that I got was really large and filling, but then again I had the Garlic fries to add in addition to the normal single dish meal, but I still think it would be filling even without fries.

The eggs benedict complimenting the hash browns really seal the deal as a very hearty meal. Everything from the lettuce to the steak had a distinct yet had good combinations of flavor with every other ingredient in the dish. Personally, I thoroughly enjoyed the breakfast Benedict here, and would probably come again if I'm in the area.

If you are to in the SF area and have any taste you have a moral obligation to visit this establishment. Great customer service. But what is the selling point is the food itself. You must without any hesitation order the Saigon steak immediately after entering the establishment. You will thank me greatly after your spiritual breakfast journey.

The food was so good and comforting. I'm native Thai and while the curry and soup was VERY very very slightly a bit too sweet for me, I ordered take out so could add a few drops of fish sauce and it was perfect. $18 for perfectly grilled and seasoned salmon, perfectly cooked rice, and a side of deLICIOUS curry?? Yes pleaseeee. The Tom yum noodle soup was one of the best broths I've had so far in the bay, strong flavors and well balanced acid and heat. Inside was nice and sunny, and the people behind the counter were nice to talk to and quick with getting my food to me, which was ready 30 mins before I got there and still piping hot as it was kept in an insulated bag. I will DEF be back and am so glad I've found this spot in SOMA.

It may be easy to miss if you are not paying attention. Street parking so you may have to circle around a few times and walk. My first impression was that it was very spacious inside with limited seating, so the best time to come here is on a weekday. You order/pay first at the counter, then sit down.

Their food was okay and it is kind of pricey for what it was, but I feel like it is one of those spots where you want to come for the IG pictures. Honestly, the Thai Tea French Toast was the main reason for my visit and it was decent to try one time. They also have a limited/small boba menu, I was glad that they had the jasmine milk tea. Their milk teas were decent, I think I preferred their earl grey milk tea a little better.

Love finding fusion food brunch places that are unapologetic about their ethnic flavors. That Tom Yum omelette was everything and I were to ever replicate it, it would have to taste like what I had here or I wouldn't stand for it. Loved the refreshing sweetness from the salad and toast to compliment.

The Thai Tea french toast was okay, I wish they incorporated more of the thai tea flavor into the toast and not just the drizzle on the side. It has potential to be really amazing- just not quite there yet.

Overall good place for brunch!

Came here for brunch on Sunday with a few friends and we had such an amazing experience! The servers were all so friendly and kind from the moment we walked in until we left the door, even though they were busy. The place was super clean inside and had a great vibe overall. I ordered the Tom yum noodle soup w/ shrimp ($14), and it was the perfect balance of sour and spicy. I appreciated that the shrimp was also not just some frozen shrimp that they added in - the pieces were big and flavorful! The only thing is that it wasn't spicy enough for my liking, so I asked for some Thai chili to add to it. I ordered the Vietnamese Dalgona Coffee ($6) to get my morning coffee fix, and it did not disappoint! Overall - 9.5/10 (only tiny complaint is that street parking is so tough to get around here) will definitely be coming back!!

Mr. East is defintely worth a visit. I wasn't impressed with the Thai Tea French Toast ( I think I assumed it would have abundant flavors of Thai Tea and be unique, but it's just French toast ). I wish I would have tried something else. Next time I will try the Waffles and Chicken or Benedict. We will defintely be back to try something else when we are in town again.

Covid Restriction:
Must show Vaccination card to eat inside.

There are a lot of ~asian fusion~ brunch places in the city, but I was actually really pleased with the little twists that Mr East Kitchen added to your typical brunch items. I shared the thai tea french toast and the shrimp benedict with a friend, and I was a big fan of the thai tea sauce on the french toast and even more so a fan of the curry hollandaise sauce on the benedict. How have I not had this before? Genius. I mean sure, the shrimp and the toast were slightly limp, but wow, the sauces were really special.

It's a small, more casual spot, so it hasn't been taken over by brunch crowds yet. The one nit I have is that it was really cold since the doors are so close, and our food got cold almost immediately. Otherwise, it's a great spot to go to if you don't feel like waiting in line.
We order from here for our Friday work lunch! We all get something different and everything is delicious!! Especially the fresh spring rolls!!
Great food ..... had the Thai French Toast ..... Delicious and brought home the drunken beef noodle also delicious
Food was delicious, and came to the table looking exactly as vibrant as in their photos. Service was great and everyone in our family loved the meal they got. Really enjoyed our meal here!

One of my favorite take out places. So delicious! And they give you plenty of food. I usually get the Pad Thai or Thai Tea French Toast.

Top of pic is their new patatas bravas - it's finger lickin' good

If you have not been to Mr. East for brunch yet wyd?? This Vietnamese restaurant offers fusion brunch items that are affordable, beautiful, and most importantly, delicious. I came here for a girls' brunch with my family and we were all satisfied at the end of the meal, even my picky Asian grandma. The great thing about the menu is you can order brunch items or go right into lunch with a noodle soup or rice plate. We ended up getting the banana french toast ($12), thai tea french toast ($12), fried chicken and pandan waffle ($13), and the tom yum noodle soup with shrimp ($14). We also got their iced jasmine milk tea and a hot vanilla latte with almond milk. I really liked the jasmine milk tea as the tea flavor was super strong, but the vanilla latte was a bit disappointing. There could have been a stronger coffee flavor, it felt a bit too milky. I liked their french toast, the bread was soft on the inside but crisped up on the outside to a perfect golden brown. The banana and thai tea flavoring were in their icing that came with the toast, but the banana one was pretty mild it just tasted like normal icing. The fresh fruit that came with each french toast was a welcome addition to each plate. I couldn't believe that the french toast was only $12...not sure if I'm too used to SF brunch prices but this was totally worth it to me. The pandan waffle was also good, great pandan flavor and crisped up enough on the outside. The chicken was really good with the mustard, though it was a bit dry. It was crisped on the outside and had a good flavor to make up slightly for the dryness. The tom yum noodle soup was really good in flavor! I loved how tart and creamy it was. The rice noodles were wider, which soaked up the delicious broth better than thin noodles. There were also a lot of shrimp and sides of bean sprouts and jalapenos if you wanted it spicier. Overall, really good experience - clean and bright, great service, and dishes that are definitely worth it for the price!

Service was fast and the food was really good and the prices are pretty cheap given that it's sf. I'd definitely come here again and try other items on the menu. I wish the chicken was crispier and the waffle had a more pronounced pandan flavor though.

So glad my fiancé came across this spot on YELP and chose this for our lunch, especially after coming back to SFO hungry from a flight! Hidden gem in SOMA forsure :)

*WAIT TIME- our party of 3 was seated right away and we did not wait long for our orders to be served.

*AMBIANCE- casual vibes, Perfect place to catch up with friends/fam while enjoying delicious food. It also looked and smelled clean in there.

*QUALITY- To be honest, I was a bit nervous after seeing that there wasn't a super big menu but I was surely surprised in a good way! Quality over quantity forsure :) their food tasted fresh and far from greasy. Drinks didn't taste inauthentic and powdery as well.

*CUSTOMER SERVICE- good! Greeted upon arrival and patient when answering questions.

*OUTDOOR SEATING- n/a, NOT dog friendly

*PARKING- no private lot and barely any street parking available. Best bet would be to get dropped off there or park somewhere further and take a walk.

Food is very tasty though it can seem like the price point is a ever so slightly on the higher side (maybe)
The service is very quick and the ambiance is quiet with street views.
Dishes are amazing! Thai food as it should be. Service also great, our orders came out quickly. Definitely recommend!
Nice staff, tasteless food. Salmon curry had no flavor, pineapple fried rice with unseasoned Shrimp. Jasmin lychee tea was amazing. Banana french toast was good. Wouldn't go here again.

opens 9am and popular...not packed, but few waiting outside before opening...some tables already reserved...location 5th near folsom...clean and modern asian fusion restaurant open for breakfast, brunch, lunch and dinner...clean, airy and tidy...seated with menu and taking a dalgona vietnamese coffee $5, but substituting oat milk for $1 more...an americano $4...browsing the various asian inspired menu...trying a tom yum omelette $19...chicken pho $14...pandan waffle with fried chicken $13...prices are quite reasonable for the city...tom yum omelette was quite tasty with the thai flavors of light, tart, salty and citrusy...very good and a bonus for the sweet savory glazed bacon...fried chicken was crispy good and cooked to perfection...not overly salty and good with the green waffles..chicken pho was clean and simple...nothing to get excited about, but not bad...$73 total after tax and tip for everything mentioned...

so good and returning for a 2nd day...trying the saigon steak & eggs $18 and was excellent...cubed steaks were a burst of flavor and becoming the favorite choice so far...tom yum noodle soup with choice of meat $14...selecting crispy chicken and served chicken katsu...the soup was mild, but tasty....this noodle soup had a better and bold flavors and would pick over the chicken pho...taking the fried chicken with waffles again for the child...overall, the flavors are milder, sweeter and more americanized, but the asian influence to the dishes do shine...for the price and some of the dishes that shined, thought mr east kitchen did a great job...

What can I say about this place? Well if you're not eating here, you're frankly missing out! Seriously, I dream about eating here. If I wasn't over an hour away-I swear I'd eat here everyday if I could. I ate with a party of 4 and everything was phenomenal. Even the drinks, man they were delicious!!!

Don't take my word for it...just find yourself pleasing your taste buds to this glorious gem!

Love the Thai French toast. So tasty and unique.
The portion of food is great! Will revisit for sure.

What I learned the past year is to never get THAI'd down by someone not worth your time. And I'd much rather spend my time on this Thai Tea French Toast. This Vietnamese brunch place caught my attention with the aesthetics (and the first Vietnamese bougie brunch place I've heard of).

.:: FOOD ::.
Thai Tea French Toast $11: texas bread, thai tea sauce, seasonal fruits. It looked better in the pictures. I wish they used better quality bread. The sauce was too liquidy. If it was thicker, it would DEFINITELY hit the spot because the flavor itself had the subtle thai tea taste where you can actually taste the tea balanced with sweetness.

Garlic Noodle Bowl $13: served with Vietnamese Egg Noodle, Butter, Garlic, Parmesan Cheese, Parsley, Kale, Bok Choy, Served with Fish Sauce. We chose five spice chicken with the dish. Other meats cost extra. It was just ok to me. Flavors were not quite there yet. Could use more umami and more seasoning to the chicken.

Overall, not bad, could use some improvements to perfect.

.:: Service / Ambiance/ Parking ::.
You order at the counter, pay, and seat yourself at any available table. Came on a Saturday around 10:30am and found a seat for a party of 2. They bring the food out to you. Our waitress was pretty nice and friendly. Food took about 10-15 min to come out.

The place is hipster-y with a hint of minimalistic touch. Tables were wooden. Looks like a chill place to study or catch up with friends.

Parking sucks as always in SF. We parked in a garage 1 block away, paid about $8 for 1-2 hrs? I forgot.

.:: COVID PROTOCOLS ::.
As of 7/3
-staff wears masks
-staff wears gloves
-full capacity
-does not do temp checks
-electronic menus on wall behind counter/paper menus avail as well
-plexi glass in place at the counter
-contactless payment

Cutest Asian fusion brunch spot in San Francisco! Must gets are the Florentine Benedict and the Thai tea French toast The mimosas are delicious and my favorite was definitely the lychee flavor! The chicken Pad see ew was also deliciousss! Definitely one of my fav breakfast spots in the city with the friendliest staff. Can't wait to visit again

I've only tried Mr. East Kitchen's milk tea, so that's all I can comment on for now! I tried their Thai Milk Tea with boba and it was $5.50 with tax. The Thai tea was very tasty and had the perfect amount of sweetness. A nice, classic milk tea. The only reason I'm giving 4 stars instead of 5 is that the boba was rather firm and chewy, as though it wasn't made fresh. Otherwise, the drink was wonderful. The staff were very friendly and kind! The drink came out extremely quickly in less than 2 minutes! Finally, the inside was very aesthetic and cute. I recommend checking them out!

Brunch is amazing here. Was able to get a reservation on Yelp the night before. Pandan Waffle with Fried Chicken and Tom Yum omelette were both amazing, and the Earl Grey Milk Tea with Oat Milk was delicious. Highly recommend!

We came here for a Sunday breakfast and ordered the Thai Tea French Toast, Taro Milk Tea, Veggie Roll, Lychee Jasmine Tea and the crispy chicken fried rice. Everything tasted as good as it looked. Personally, I wasn't a big fan of the Lychee Jasmine Tea (tasted a little soapy imho), but other than that we left very happy :)

Ordered food for pickup at the restaurant. Wanted the drunken noodles but realized they only have it available during brunch hours (9 am to 3 pm) but decided to go with the Pineapple Fried Rice. The food came out hot, ready and on time. Decided to eat the food once I got back home in San Jose (about an hour commute) and my food was still hot without me warming it up. You cannot go wrong with ordering anything at the restaurant! Would recommend if you're looking for good food in the city!

We came in with a table of 7 and they were luckily easy to accommodate us for a Friday brunch time! My friend got us the mimosa as it was an early pit stop, but I won't let that judge me for the garlic nooodles! Overall I thought it was tasty, the overall noddle texture was well and the sauce blended well together to remind me of my childhood! The grilled chicken has the flavor I expected it be so I would get it for sure.

The food tastes good and there are variety of dishes you can try. The restaurant is a decent size and enough tables. The food came out very quickly and the staff is very friendly. The price is reasonable compared to places in the same area. We ordered garlic noodle with shrimp and it was great. The shrimp was cooked perfectly. The fried chicken with egg fried rice was also good. The chicken was not overcooked and it was very crispy on the outside. I really recommend trying their pink milk as well.

Made plans to go eat here. Didn't end up eating there because it was so cramped. It's a small restaurant with not much room. We were offered a table outside but it's not like a legit outside dinning area. It was literally just a plastic table with two plastic chairs on the sidewalk. I'm normally not picky about things like this but it literally look like someone randomly put chairs and 1 table on the sidewalk. It didn't look intentionally at all. Decided to go somewhere else.

The service was great! Very attentive and personable. Walked in for lunch after 1pm for a table of 4 & was seated immediately.

So many options on their menu- I wanted everything!

I ultimately ordered the chicken pad see ew and asked for it to be spicy with fresh bean sprouts on the side.

They delivered!!! I wish they had ground chili flakes but I was satisfied with the fresh Thai Chili's to add onto my plate. The dish was super flavorful!!!

Will be back- often!

upon arrival they were busy but were still attentive to us as we just walked in during peak brunch hours. the atmosphere was very lively and friendly, automatically we felt welcomed and the service was amazing through out our whole dine in experience. I don't remember word for word what we ordered but they were all delicious. The fresh fruits complimented the waffles and the savory dishes were outstanding. If I were to nitpick I just personally prefer longer noodles but every restaurant is different and I respect that. Another thing I loved were the bokchoy! Perfectly cooked and had the most satisfying crunch. Portions of the food were also big and for two we ended up having to pack some to go! Definitely will be coming back if I'm ever in the area :)
Service was great and the food was even better! The place also looks beautiful from the inside

It's rare that I eat at Vietnamese fusion restaurants that are both authentic, creative, AND well-executed. Usually food is either fresh and aesthetic, or traditional and delicious... well Mr. East Kitchen is all that and then some!

We came here early in the morning after our flight not expecting much, but wow, every dish is crazy good. Everyone talks about the Garlic Noodle Bowl which is crazy good, but my favorite was the fresh tofu on it. The bouncy texture of the tofu made it the best tofu I've ever had... so unexpected! The Tom yum omelette came with this honey sriracha bacon that's just TO DIE FOR. And the Thai tea French toast was a fun twist on a classic. The sweetness reminds me of Hong Kong toast. This Southeast Asian inspired brunch spot is a hit in my book and I look forward to coming back!
Love this restaurant, the food is always so good here. Got a lot of boba and food here and the quality was consistent every time. The interior is really clean and pretty and the staff is nice :)

Vegan Delight was very flavorful & delicious
The dish is hearty & healthy. It was a good portion size. I ordered it with brown rice.
Food tastes good. A bit hectic in there on weekends during brunch hours. They were able to accommodate our party of 6 without reservations pretty quickly. Would make a reservation next time.

Came here for lunch yesterday! One of the more worth it places in SF. We got the tom yum noodle soup. The portions were HUGE and so tasty. They also gave crispy chicken on the side, which were super tender on the inside. Service was nice as well. Will be back!

I recently visited this brunch restaurant and was absolutely blown away by the food. The positive reviews are absolutely deserved -- this place is top-notch. I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a fantastic brunch experience.

So I came here because one of my friend picked this place to meet up. I didn't have many expectations, but I had hopes that this place would surprise me. However, I will say that the food was alright. I would say the food was on the blander side. I'm glad they have various sauces to dip food in, because that's what I did often.

The food I had was garlic fries, garlic noodles, Thai tea, and the fried chicken sandwich. I was a fan of the fried chicken sandwich, but that was it. I was very displeased with the Thai Tea. It barely had any flavor.

As for the service, the staff were very kind. I really appreciated the service of bring the food out and cleaning up afterwards.

The venue is small and that is most likely due to covid. The place is fairly boarded up as well; which I assume is from all the hate and violence that has occurred in the past year.

It was an okay experience. I may revisit and try something else as other folx have had better experiences.
Tasty food and quick service. Smaller place for seating inside than I thought but worth coming in for brunch. The thai tea french toast is a must try

Absolutely spot on phenomenal and authentic flavors. We had the sriracha bacon, the fried spring rolls, the hai Nan chicken and the Tom yum noodle soup with shrimp. We gorged!! Ahh so so delicious.

Don't skip the lychee mimosa and if you haven't tried it, get the HOT Thai tea- you can thank me later
This is one of the best meals I have ever had, highly recommend! The service was amazing too!

Great quality Asian fusion brunch, see food pictures for enticement. Came here with a big group and got seated close to when they opened. Can fill up in a hurry as you get into the later brunch hours. Hope to be back soon!

The food and atmosphere is absolutely beautiful. Tran was our hostess and he was amazing, provided great service, very knowledgeable of the dishes and gave perfect recommendations. We had the Thai tea French toast, fresh rolls, Tom yum omelette, bottomless mimosas and matcha latte and everything was beyond what I expected. The Siracha bacon was sensational with both dishes. We were so stuffed we had to take a shopping break and return in the afternoon for the mango dessert and pad Thai. Highly recommend this restaurant, I cannot wait to come back. Thank you, Mr East Kitchen. Wonderful experience.

Bland food :/ we ordered the garlic noodles with chicken + spinach & bacon omelette. Omelette lacked simple salt or pepper seasoning. The garlic noodles were bland - Laksa & Perilla garlic noodles are way better. I guess this is why they have a whole station full of seasoning & sauces? The garlic noodles, veggies, and chicken were also lukewarm. I like hot foods so this wasn't as enjoyable. Maybe their pho is better? It seems popular. Their portions are large and the price was fair.

The ambiance is nice though! Cute furniture and good music!

I really like the food here.
Tea was awesome.
Service is also good and a comfortable environment.
I appreciate this.

I have to admit I was kinda turned off by the rather stereotypical name which sounds like a Chinese takeout place somewhere in a rural red state where they make General Tso's chicken in a deep fryer that smells of rancid tater tots. Unless of course that's actually the owner's name. If so, my apologies, Mr. East. At first glance, I thought this was a bubble tea shop with semi-edible snacks where the customers have a median age somewhere south of puberty. However, I was pleasantly surprised that they offer a more robust menu of Vietnamese dishes. On my virginal visit last month, I actually did order the Large $6.50 Bubble Milk Tea (photo: http://bit.ly/2TxshP4).

In a diva mood, I asked for oat meal for no particular reason. By the way, I'm well north of puberty, like polar ice cap north. I also ordered the $14 Chicken Curry to go. It turned out to be quite a hearty portion with lots of chicken and plenty of velvety sauce (photo: http://bit.ly/2Bo2xxv). It just didn't have much of a kick, so I grabbed the sriracha from the fridge and did a major splooge on it. It for delicious quickly. I came back weeks later out of a whim one evening. You know what a whim is, right? It's when you're feeling peckish and too impatient to go home and actually cook. This time, I ordered the $6 Tofu Fresh Roll (photo: http://bit.ly/2BmBToL) and the $10 Eggplant Salad (photo: http://bit.ly/2REzECx).

I was impressed. Instead of the standard salad roll cut into six identical bite-size pieces, the fresh roll was actually one mini-burrito-size roll full of fresh ingredients including slightly grilled tofu pieces. The eggplant slices were actually warmed up, an unexpected but welcome touch, and they were placed on a pile of nicely massaged kale and sprinkled with shaved Parmesan cheese. I was happy my whim turned into such a happy, healthy meal with a minimum of calorific guilt. Regardless of the food, I have to say I was even more impressed by the exceptional service on both visits. A very conscientious staff. Good job, Mr. East...whoever you are.

FOOD - 4 stars...it improved between visits and I liked that
AMBIANCE - 4 stars...clean and open, well maintained
SERVICE - 5 stars...their sweet spot if you ask me
TOTAL - 4 stars...has Mr. East met Mr. West and imposed trade tariffs yet?

RELATED - Looking for other Vietnamese options? Here's a collection of places I've tried and reviewed: http://bit.ly/2O3Qaeo

Our Sunday School leader brings us here every couple weeks and I always look forward to it. The food is great. The service is great! The hospitality is great! We get our food really quick.This place is well-deserving of 5 stars!

Surprisingly better than I expected. They're offering 10% off all menu items during SIP as well! (However, I am listing out the regular prices because I'm too lazy to do the math.) I was in the city and was in the mood for some soup noodles as the weather was a bit gloomy. I also decided to pick up food for the entire fam.

I got Tom Yum noodle soup ($15) with tofu - good flavor but not as sour as the Tom Yum you'd get at a normal Thai restaurant. I was happy with the portions for the price and ended up sharing it with my sister. The tofu was good and soaked up the flavor. The consistency of the tofu was like what you'd expect from a fish cake, but it's vegetarian. Also came with some veggies like kale and bok choy. I would have liked a few more veggies in my soup, but over was pretty content with my dish.

Thai tea french toast ($12) for the sister because she is a sucker for all things Thai tea flavored and has a soft spot for french toast. This dish was supposed to come with eggs...but WE DID NOT GET ANY. It wasn't really missed, but still... I'd like to get what I paid for. It did come with a nice side of fruit and two little sides of the Thai tea sauce.

Other dishes we got included the eggplant tofu ($15), garlic noodle bowl with tofu ($15), and drunken noodle beef ($16). This place really likes to serve kale and boy choy with all their entrees. It was a common theme noted across all the dishes. I was able to try a bit of the garlic noodles and while the noodles have good springy texture, the garlic taste is a bit faint.

Staff was good at wearing masks and gloves. However, the patrons that I saw when I visited the restaurant weren't very good at wearing their masks. Half the people I saw only had masks that covered their mouths and left their noses exposed. I would feel a bit more comfortable if the staff was more strict with enforcing proper mask wearing. I get that these aren't the safest times for everyone involved, but I just wanted to get in and out of the place as soon as I could when I saw that.

Came here randomly since I was in the area with my gal friend. I ordered the waffles and she had the pad Thai. My waffles were amaaaaaaazing. They were so soft but still toasty. Loved. My friend ate all her pad Thai in three bites, she said it was so good. My cappuccino was as equally well made. I would love to try more of their menu since they had a lot of vegetarian and vegan options.

The place is very cute and they offer limited indoor dining. The staff was incredibly nice! I did see that the chef in the back was walking around the kitchen with his mask hanging on his chin and to be honest that did rub me the wrong way... but everything seemed clean otherwise and again, the food and service was great.

I am obsessed with Mr East Kitchen. I was only in town for a couple months but think I ate at and ordered from here at least 5x, if not more. I dream about the crispy chicken fried rice dish - the chicken is perfectly crispy and basically just melts in your mouth. I unfortunately never got to try brunch here, but would absolutely come back the next time I'm in SF.

Omg. So good. I'm eating the spicy sole right now...it's a really good amount of food for the cost & it's DELICIOUS. The women who took my order were super nice, decor is cute, food was ready in about 15 minutes. Zero complaints. So yummy.

Food: the hai nan chicken was yum. The chicken breast was ridiculously moist and soft. I was questioning whether it was dark meat. The rice has flavor that i expect in this dish. The sauce is a little different than I am used to. I am more used to grated ginger sauce and maybe a spiced sauce. But regardless. It was so tasty. I am impressed! I have eaten a lot of bad hai nan chicken.
Great customer service!! Food was great as well . Street parking near by . Mimosas were delicious will be back !!!
Pad Thai was so damn good. Cool little spot to go and enjoy tasty food. Kinda weird that they combine classic American breakfast food with Thai food but also kinda cool. 6/5 spot, must try.

@MREastKitchen
_______________
Entree:
Garlic noodle + Steak
Eggs Benedict + Curry Shrimp
Small Plate:
Fresh Roll
Imperial Roll
Drinks:
Thai Milk Tea
Super Fruit Jasmine Tea
________________
I enjoyed both entrees! The breakfast menu runs till 3pm!!!!
Me and my friend thought the fresh roll was tastier than the imperial roll. I like how it was sliced in half like a sushirrito. Thai tea looked good but, I thought my fruit tea was over the top sweet and over packed.
_________
I been here twice, first time had the curry chicken, I think I'd definitely come back and get that again!!!
-Thanks

Addicted to their dalgona coffee!!!
OMG they are DELICIOUS but it's very strong and will make your heart race lol.
I drink coffee every single day but it still makes my heart tachycardic lol.
Also the workers there are so friendly!!
If you order at the restaurant they even give you a discount.
Love this spot!

Live literally next door to this place.

Whenever we want some refreshing brunch, we always come to Mr East Kitchen. Place is pretty cozy, and the food is always great.

One thing that I remember in the past though (a year or two before COVID), was that we tried eating at this place, we got some Pho, and it wasn't great at all.

Haven't tried their Pho again ever since then, so no idea whether things have changed. Been eating all of their other menus, and they're fantastic.

I ordered the 2 eggs scrambled dish. And a side of hash browns. Cappuccino with oat milk and the lemonade. I was Feeling under the weather and just needed some substance. By the time I got there my cappuccino was already kinda cold and they graciously offered to make me a fresh one! Honestly yall between the cappuccino, lemonade and the side salad (did not expect that!) I'm literally feeling way better. Very good Mr. East. Very good

Environment and aesthetic is a 10/10, the food is like a solid B-. Omg I know this is weird to rave about but the bathroom was really really nice.

The service was really nice! They gave my friend mocha drink instead of matcha but when we told them, they fixed the problem almost immediately. It was also funny bc I ordered a side of bacon and they gave it to me on a completely fresh plate.

First time visiting the city and this place was near the hotel. Reviews looked good so I decided to grove it a try for breakfast. Coming from east coast I am used to a little more flavor but the meal was still delicious. The staff is super friendly and judging by the orders that was leaving out first thing in the morning others definitely enjoy their meals. This place will be added to my favorites to hit up when visiting SF

HIDDEN GEM FOR BRUNCH! This brunch place is relatively new so I guess not that many people know about it yet - so enjoy the lack of crowds while you can :) Also a 20% off discount if you check in on yelp!

The interior is SUPER CUTE and a great way to up your instagram game ;) Portion sizes are quite big - my friend and I shared two things and could barely finish.

- Shrimp Benedict - so good! They're pretty generous with their shrimp. Their hollandaise sauce was really nice - there seemed to be a hint of seafood flavor in the sauce which was a good twist, and went really well with the shrimp.

- Thai tea french toast: The french toast had a nice crunch to it and wasn't too sweet which is what I like! The thai tea sauce is really nice too but I wish they had a bit more sauce, since the middle piece of french toast ended up barely having any sauce.

- Lime thai ice tea - I've only ever had thai milk tea, so this was quite unique for me. The thai tea flavor is strong; definitely worth trying!

All the food we had was very tasty. American dishes had a Thai twist. Service was great, especially "M" remembered us from last week, and the staff always checked to see how everything was. Prices are reasonable for San Francisco. The restaurant is clean and well lit. If you like Thai food, this place is a must try.
The food is good, prices are reasonable and the servers were very nice. Garlic Noodles. Mango Sticky Rice

I love this place! It's hard to come by an Asian fusion brunch restaurant that has really decent prices for the city. I've had their tom yum omelette, hainan chicken rice, pandan waffle and fried chicken, garlic noodles, tom yum soup, and mango and sticky rice. They were all good! The service is nice too.

Cute breakfast spot! Im glad we made a reservation though. It's busy and there isn't a lot of seating inside the restaurant so I recommend getting a reservation if you can.

Ordered the steak Benedict. Nice portion and I thought the price was fair for a Benedict like this! Steak was good. Eggs poached perfectly. Big fan of the curry Hollandaise sauce! I've never had anything like it and it added a nice twist of flavor to the dish.

Service was great and pretty quick as well for how busy it was!

This place is definitely IG worthy, and their food and drinks are pretty good!

Their garlic noodles are yummy and decently portioned (can't compete with Perilla's though), and their spring rolls are a nice snack!

Their jasmine milk tea has a really nice balance of milk and tea, and I loved the passion fruit bits in their passion fruit green tea! I would definitely recommend getting less sugar in the drinks, since 100% was too sweet for me, especially for the passion fruit drink. Boba was sweet but could've been a little softer!

Definitely want to come back and try their Thai Tea French Toast one day for brunch.

We loved everything about this place! Easy to get a reservation, wasn't too crowded, and the food was really delicious! I had the Mr. East Kitchen salad that came with grilled salmon, greens, blueberries, strawberries and a blueberry vinaigrette. I love that there are healthier options available. My husband got the fried chicken sandwich which he really enjoyed. We also ordered the pandan waffle and it was really good! We'll definitely come again! Service was great and all the servers were super friendly!

Mr East Kitchen was a great find during my recent stay in San Francisco. If you are tired of the ordinary breakfast food available at most restaurants, give this place a try. I loved the fusion on east meets west. My breakfast included traditional fried eggs and potatoes accompanied by Sriracha thick sliced bacon and garlic toast. My breakfast companion had his meal paired with Thai tea French toast. Yum! And the coffee was good too! Win-win!

One of my absolute favorite brunch spots. Their Saigon Steak is juicy and super flavorful! Their chicken banh mi is very good as well with its strong flavor and soft bread. And of course I can't forget my favorite drink, the lychee mimosa! Can't recommend this place enough!

Quick, casual breakfast/brunch options. I little pricey at $15 for a Vietnamese sandwich but guess that's pretty standard in SF.

Their tofu banh mi was delicious, but it definitely need more veggies and/greens to stand up to the heavy ciabatta bread. Mine was great because I opted for the side salad that I added, but if you go with the standard fries, the sandwich would be lacking because of the limited fillings. Tasty dressings and spreads that bring everything together nicely.

Service is quick and casual. Very scrappy how they made a Saran Wrap shield at their counter to protect their workers from COVID -- stay safe!
Thai tea french toast was delicious, service is fast, and it's super clean inside. Definitely a go-to spot!

Connected to an apartment building and in a decent location. Usually pretty busy at lunch time but service is good and fast. I've had lots of different things but the drunken noodles are my go-to. Their drinks are also really good! Definitely recommend.

I came here for a quick lunch break and glad to find this place. I had the garlic noodle bowl with grilled chicken, It was really good. I hesitate getting garlic noodles initially because it sounded little too heavy for my first meal of the day. However, this noodle bowl feels pretty healthy given the amount of fresh vegetables it has. The noodle is not too oily and just right. I would love to try more stuff here. I am especially curious about the Thai Tea Toast.
This place has a casual vibe and cleanly decorated.

Pretty nice new place, near where I live. On the expensive side, in terms of prices but pretty good none the less.

Came on opening day, there was a pretty long line, and a lot of people eating in. Didnt mind waiting.

garlic noodle with pork. Pretty good! Not greasy, flavorful. Love the seasoning on the meat. Underneath was the stir fry bok choy and kale. Kale was surprisingly not bitter.

Pho and skirt steak: good as well! Broth was flavorful and clean, not greasy. Kale and bok choy underneath bed of noodles too. Pho noodle wasnt normal pho noodle. I prefer the pho noodle.

Hojicha boba: delicious!

Overall, healthier version of vietnamese food. Great if you work/live by. Portions are nice, and you won't have to take half you meal home. I liked how there was greens in the dish, which isnt traditional, but i like that I'm getting a wholesome meal.

Place is self served.

Luckily no wait on a Sunday for brunch! This place was walking distance from our hotel, so thought we would check it out!

You order at the counter and seat yourself. Indoor/outdoor dining available (one table outside). Staff is very friendly.

We had the salmon Benedict and pandan waffles. Food presentation was 10/10! Side salad with the Benedict was amazing as was the entree. It is grilled (not raw) salmon FYI. The pandan waffles were alright, was expecting a bit more pandan flavor. I was told it was 4 pieces, but it's really one waffle cut into 4 pieces.. Probably should've gotten the chicken and waffles combination.

The mocha latte was great! Perfect temperature and taste!

Would come back to try other dishes if I lived here!

Co-worker: "What's for lunch today?"
Me: "I'm going to get Vietnamese."

Co-Worker: "Ohhh in the TL - I wanna go!"
Me: "Naw, I'm going to check out this new Modern Vietnamese fast casual eatery on 5th/Folsom."

Co-worker: "Modern?! It's not legit unless there's a salty thumb in your soup!"
(If you're a fan of actor and comedian David So, then you'll get this reference: https://bit.ly/2MtiM3g)

Ok, I get why many people are apprehensive of modern ethnic cuisine BUT when done one right, it could be great like Liholiho, Kin Khao, and Asian Box...the restaurant, not the happy ending.

Softly opened this week, Mr. East Kitchen is a new fast casual eatery serving Modern/Americanized Vietnamese food. The menu is chipotle style: choose your bowl style - Pho ($12.95), Rice ($12.95), Salad ($11.95), or Banh Mi ($9.95), then choose your protein - Chicken, Pork, Tofu, or Steak (+$1). They also serve Imperial Rolls ($10.95) and Spring Rolls ($9.95).

For drinks, they have Coffee, Juice, and Milk Tea (Earl Grey, Jasmine, and Hochija).

I like that they label menu items dairy-free, gluten-free, soy-free, vegetarian, and vegan. Very thoughtful of people's dietary restrictions.

There's a 4.5% surcharge on all orders.

I ordered the Salad w/ kale, cabbage, cherry tomato, mango, papaya, tamarind vinaigrette ($11.95 + $1 hanger steak upgrade): https://bit.ly/2PfMW8H. Unfortunately, it wasn't my jam. The flavors weren't balanced and the vinaigrette was on the sweeter side. The kale, being the fusion part (?) needed to be cut in more manageable pieces. The hanger steak was flavorful with a nice sear but chewy. Because the salad lacked acid and a textural element (needs a crunchy topping), it got monotonous quick and I could only eat half.

I enjoyed the Hojicha Milk Tea (Medium - $3.95) more: https://bit.ly/2PgA56f. The roasted green milk tea was perfectly creamy with a good roasted, nutty flavor. It's a bummer that you can't adjust the sweetness. I usually order my milk teas 50% or less sweet so the regular sweet was too sweet for me. If you're sensitive to caffeine, I recommend getting the hojicha since it's low in caffeine.

Service was polite and my order was ready in less than five minutes so it's great for a quick lunch.

Clean and minimalist, yet instagrammable ambiance with lots of mini plants. There's table seating and counter window seats for 30+. The lack of sound dampening causes noise to bounce off the walls so it was quite loud when I arrived. But, I arrived at the tail end of the lunch rush as people were leaving so it was fine once my order arrived.

As far as Vietnamese fast casual goes, my preference is Asian Box but I probably ordered the wrong thing at Mr. East Kitchen. The garlic noodles look like a solid option. You can never go wrong with butter AND carbs!

I had a work lunch here and was incredibly surprised by how good the food was. I got the Pad Thai here, which in my opinion is the litmus test on how authentic the food is. It was really good, they used real tamarind instead of tomato sauce. This is one of my new favorite Thai spots in SF
Food was incredible. Service was great. Cool vibes all around. Best breakfast we had while in sf.

What a great surprise! I brought my family into the city for Father's Day and wanted a semi-quiet spot we could relax and have good conversation over tasty food prior to the Giants game and Mr. East Kitchen fit the bill!

The space is extremely clean and minimalistic, very refreshing and inviting. Staff properly wore face coverings as of our 06/20/21 visit and had a plexiglass barrier at the register.

Indoor seating was allowed with the option to order from the counter or via mobile (they have a QR code at the entrance with a '$5 off your first online order' offer.

I paired an ice cold Singha (Thai beer) with the Classic 2 Egg breakfast and thoroughly enjoyed it! The eggs were cooked properly and served hot, the salad was lightly dressed and a great compliment to the hash browns and Sriracha bacon, which I'm convinced is my new favorite food! The bacon was a medium cut and cooked well (not floppy or burnt) coated in the Sriracha sauce which has the consistency of bbq sauce with the kick of Sriracha.

Staff were super friendly and provided complimentary ice water which was much appreciated!
Cool new fusion food, during busy hours you'll have to wait a long time for your food, probably small kitchen or understaffed. Otherwise theyll have nice looking food on a plate!
They have the best lychee ice tea. If ur a lychee fan, then this place maybe the right spot for you

Mr East kitchen has a really nice ambiance. The service was amazing.

I got the pancake plate and the garlic noodle bowl. I also got the iced latte. This was such a good meal after a nice work out. If you are around SOMA, this is a nice spot for a quick bite.

We're fortunate to live across the street from this gem. We typically have their brunch and lunch, trying to taste everything on their menu. I love their Thai tea French toast, Hainan chicken and Vietnamese dalgona coffee.

The staff are friendly but we have yet to dine in.

A cozy casual corner situated along the blocks of SOMA in SF, this Asian fusion brunch eatery takes a mark for its generous portions of feel-good food.

Was promptly seated on a Saturday afternoon, the interior atmosphere was of a calm, simple enclave amidst the busy streets of downtown. Natural lighting provided a spacious tone. Broad selection of dishes of classic brunch items from benedicts to Thai and Vietnamese staples of Pad See Ew and Garlic noodles.

I ordered the garlic noodle bowl with chicken. The noodles were flavorful, seasoned with shavings of garlic uplifted by butter, enhanced by the accents of parmesan cheese and sprinkles of parsley. Not too salty or over dampened by garlic. There was a good chew to the noodles, firm with a flick of softness. Pickled radish and carrots livened up the dish for a side of acidic punch. Bok choy seemed more of a garnish than a component of the dish however vegetables make a good balance to the dense palate of flavors as garlic. Chicken was gladly not dry but retained a moist center with the five-spice rub owing to the choice of chicken thigh over breast meat. Anyone who has had garlic noodles before cannot deny the lure and magic of this delicate combo paired with any protein. The dish hits home with a splatter of flavors. The dish delivered. Would recommend!
So rare to find such excellent service in this city! Everyone was kind and thoughtful and the food was delicious!

The food here is so good, everyone in our group loved their dishes. Went for breakfast and I wish we had time to go back a second time. My favorite was the omelette fried rice (no bacon), hubby devoured his Saigon steak also, Lychee is my new favorite mimosa flavor. The staff was so kind a really competed the experience.

Nice breakfast or lunch place in Soma. Pretty unique Thai inspired breakfast/brunch place. Me and buddy, Dewy, split the omelette fried rice and the Saigon Steak. Both plates were empty by the time our other friend arrived, 25 minutes late.....He went with the Vegan Delight even though he isn't vegan. It looked decent but there were way better choices. The staff was great, engaging and fun to talk with about absolutely nothing at all. I would definitely go back.
The top dishes here -- hainan chicken, Tom yum soup -- were both tasty and were presented well. The chicken that came with the tom yum soup was crispy, would recommend

Mr. East Kitchen has fantastic deals going on right now! 10% off all orders AND if you spend over $40, you get a free chicken sandwich! So worth!

Mr. East Kitchen serves Asian fusion for such an affordable price! I had a chance to speak to the owner, a kind and sweet Asian lady who reminds me of my mom, when I stopped by.
