During these troubling times, it's so important to support Asian-owned businesses like these. The food was yummy and the portion sizes were huge despite the affordable prices. Combined with the sweet service I received, this eatery really feels like home. Whether you're feeling like pho, fries, Thai food, brunch, or milk tea, you can get it all right here.

Highly recommend the garlic fries and the Thai Tea French toast.

Delicious food and friendly staff!
Highly recommend the garlic noodles
Very clean and delightful

I came here 2 weekends ago and wasn't really impressed.

Bahn mi: the sandwich was dry and needed some type of sauce or marinade. There was nothing impressive about it, so definitely won't be going back for it. It came with fries, which did taste good, but this wasn't enough to make the meal worth it as a whole. I'm not sure if this is just an issue with their veggie meal options, the two friends I went with eat meat and seemed satisfied with their meal.

Service: I went on a rainy Saturday afternoon so it was very crowded and unorganized. It took us awhile to get seated as they kept forgetting we were waiting. This doesn't seem like it would be a problem normally, and the staff seemed genuinely sorry about it.

I might try going again for their sweet brunch options as those seem popular, but not sure I want to spend money on trying their other veggie options.

Delighted to have a new Vietnamese fast casual restaurant in the neighborhood. It's similar to Freshroll but less chaotic, much cleaner, friendlier staff, more seating, and better ambience.

Rather than the Subway/Chipotle style of building the dishes in front of you, they are prepared in the back. The downside is it's harder to customize, be but upside is faster service and a less chaotic experience.

Be sure to check in on social media for a free Milk Bubble Tea!

Delicious spot near downtown for asian-inspired brunch!! It's a bit of a little walk away from Market, but highly worth it in my opinion!! We walked in around 2pm on a weekend and were seated straight away. Both dishes we got (Tom Yum Noodle Soup and Pandan Waffle + Fried Chicken) were delicious!! So hearty and flavorful. Service was great, our servers were kind and quick to refill our waters. Prices were good too. There are a few places near downtown that have a similar vibe but are a little pricier. The food is just as good, so I'd pick Mr. East over those any day!!

This was one of the most fun experience that we have. Recently we have celebrate my friend birthday. The employees was very friendly and we enjoy it. Shoutout to one of the employee that have help us put our cake in their fridge and bring it out when we needed later. Will come back to this restaurant again. The food was very delicious and our belly was filled. Thanks for having us!

I got the breakfast which was waffles fresh fruit and bacon and egg. It was pretty good.
My wife got the shrimp pad Thai and that was really good actually better than mine. The boba tea was ok

Mr. East is my favorite restaurant to get brunch at in sf! Everyone here is so nice and friendly. The food is consistent, delicious, and plated so prettily. My fave dish is the Thai tea French toast I highly recommend everyone to try this place.

Amazing food and amazing drinks. Food came out fast and was delicious. They accidentally forgot to give us our garlic fries, but it was still on our bill so I asked for a refund; They gave us a refund and garlic fries to-go which was a very nice suprise. Would definitely go again.

The food is really flavorful here. I got the Tom yum omelette and it is very flavorful and worth it. The garlic bread is also very flavorful. We also ordered the lychee mimosa and the new cranberry holiday mimosa. They were sooo cute. The lychee mimosa was really good and sweet. They have cute holiday decorations in the front. The owner was sooo sweet she came and greeted us and made sure everything was fine and if we enjoyed the new cranberry mimosa. The staff are very friendly and offer great service. I would recommend to you if you want to try a Thai/vietnamese/american brunch style!

Fried chicken with garlic noodles-8/10
Mine was some veggies thing-6/10
Tofu was good everything was good except basil flavour- it was just too much- ruining other things
Patatas were 8/10- good seasoned and flavourful
Ambiance is good- like every other place in apt building
Service was ok
Good food service and ambiance. Except for the French toast, the portions are pretty hearty.

This place is a pretty cute asian fusion brunch place in SOMA! The interior is really clean and aesthetic so it's a great place to just sit and chat while eating. I think I also saw some people working there, so they probably have wifi (although I'm not 100% sure about that).

I went with my friend and we tried the Mr. East sandwich and the thai tea french toast. They also sell coffee and milk tea which is nice.

The food was pretty tasty and the french toast wasn't too sweet either! They definitely have a more fusion/modern take on asian food, so if you're looking for something really authentic I'd probably go somewhere else.

I think the thing that brought this down for me was the portion size, which was pretty small. My friend was still hungry after we ate and I wasn't that full either, and we each ordered one entree. I also don't have a huge appetite so I was a little surprised.

I live in Mosso so this is right next door to me, but I've also been here before the quarantine.

I'm a big fan. Their food is freshly made, well priced, and most of all, the workers are super friendly and sweet (especially Pat, he's a sweetheart!!) Amy is also really nice.

I recommend their DALGONA COFFEE, drunken beef, garlic noodles, salmon bowls, and their brunch items. Honestly you can't really go wrong!

I've been here like 8 times already, about 2-3x a week! I expect to come back again and again.

I come here a lot for brunch by myself and with friends. This place has never missed a beat on food or service quality. My favorites are the steak or shrimp Benedict, and the Tom Yum omelette. Food can arrive a little slower than you might expect during busy periods, but it will be worth the few extra minutes. Staff are super friendly.

Really cute Asian fusion place. We came here for Sunday lunch at around noon and had to wait a little while even though we had reservations because they were really busy, but we did end up getting 10% off the final bill though, so that was nice. The menu is really cool with a lot of different things we wanted to try, but we ultimately went with the popular Thai tea French toast (with a very a nice Thai tea syrup over regular French toast) and the chicken and waffles with a pandan waffle (the flavor is hard to describe but adds kind of a unique almost savory flavor to the waffle). The chicken was crispy but a little on the dry side. I had the lychee Jasmine tea, which was really good, very lychee forward. Overall, the food was good and really caters for those who enjoy sweets that are less sweet, with some unique Asian twists to classic brunch foods. Would recommend giving this place a try!

I'm always grateful for more fast casual options. This is like a slightly more upscale Freshroll with a lot more options. While the restaurant and food is aesthetically more pleasing, the taste could use a little work. Thankfully they're kinda new and have time to tweak the recipes.

Garlic Noodles w/ Steak: The garlic noodles aren't quite as good as An the Go / Crustacean, but they are better than some joints I've tried in Little Saigon. They have that nice al dente chew and a generous amount garlic. But it could probably us more garlic / flavoring. I was hoping the steak would be like the thinly sliced seared beef you sometimes find in a vermicelli bowl or on top of garlic noodles. Instead it was kinda like what you'd get on top of an American salad. Definitely could have used more marinade. Also, there were a ton of veggies; I had mixed feeling about that. On one hand, it makes it a more complete and healthier meal. On the other hand, most garlic noodle places don't load you up with veggies and thus I felt a little shorted on the noodle allotment.

Sriracha Hot Wings: These were horrible. I thought about letting them drag the review down to 2-stars, but figured I'd be cautious since this place is kinda new. The skin was so flappy; not a single crispy bit. There wasn't a single drumette (my favorite wing sub-component). And the wingettes were unnecessarily cut up. There is no need for that plus it makes biting off a tiny bone shard more likely. And the sauce was kinda dull, almost like they only use sriracha and no other flavorings.

I love Mr. East kitchen! This family-owned restaurant is located in Soma, not a far walk from Yerba Buena. My go-to meals here have always been in the evening, but every time I have passed during brunch on the weekends the restaurant is fully packed! I recommend the garlic noodle bowl and basil chicken. I plan to try out brunch there in the near future!

OMG, I was surprisingly surprised the food was really good.

I was confused to how garlic fries fit into a Vietnamese dish. But i had decided to try the Tom Yum with chicken, the Pineapple friend rice with beef and the garlic fries.

The Tom Yum was my favorite out of the the three dishes. the noodles was cooked perfectly for it being steamed in a bowl during delivery. the soup was amazing. it had just the right about of spice and it was spicy if you add the little container of sauce that they give you. they also add fresh lemon grass. it was just amazing and delicious.

The pineapple fried rice was nice and flavorful, maybe it was just the pairing of beef was not the best choice. they had chunks of pineapples, cashew, cherry, raisins. which was nice and refreshing but i personally wished that they had more curry flavor. or whatever they put to make the rice yellow.

I cant wait to try other items on their menu.

I got dumped today and went to get pad Thai when I was hungry for dinner and they made my night. I asked for half tofu and half chicken and it was so delicious! The service was amazing, as it was the first time, and I am so grateful for their flexibility and fast cooking! It only took 20 minutes for it to be ready! Truly made my night!

Some of the most delicious food I've ever had! Their eggs Benedict was TO DIE FOR!! Their only issue is that it's a very small and cozy place and they seem understaffed, the poor waiter was doing his best both times but seemed stretched thin. It also took a while to get our food both times I went there. Regardless the food was certainly worth the wait and the presentation and taste were out of this world!!

I came here with some friends on a Saturday for brunch after hearing they had a Tom Yum Omlette--I had to try it!!

They're an order at the counter and sit down to wait for your food to be delivered kind of place. The wall has a shelf that comes in at eye height when you sit so I'd avoid tables along the wall if you can!

The Omlette was a little underwhelming -- I couldn't really taste the Tom Yum and the shrimp were a bit over done. My friend got the Tom Yum soup though, which was way more flavorful and delicious. I would go for the noodle soup and not the omlette next time.

Super disappointed in the experience today. Came here for brunch on a Sunday. They are not busy at all plenty of seating. You order ahead and grab a number. You serve yourself with napkins forks and stuff. They have a great selection of condiments. Decor is modern. Space is open and clean.

We ordered veggies spring rolls, basically it's fried egg rolls with vegetables stuffing. Came out hot. They are the best thing we had!

Samosa were small and under seasoned. The curry potato were mashed, no other vegetables inside, just plain curry potato. And they needed more salt or cumin. They were super mild and boring.

Honey got the avocado and egg sandwich with cheddar cheese. Specifically asked for cheddar, they said ok. So the first time it came out, it had bacon on it so we sent it back. Second to came out, avocado were not ripe. And the cheese is definitely American slice. Hash browns are the generic frozen ones. They were fried to perfection it's like getting one of those hash browns from McDonald's

We split the Thai Tea French toast. We asked to have egg and steak on the side. And when it came out. They put it on the same plate. My dude is vegetarian so couldn't eat the French toast that was touching the steak. Steak was overcooked. Chewy. And French toast was very very disappointing. Soggy, not flavorful at all. The Thai tea syrup was very bland as well. It's a total miss.


Tea and latte were good. Other than that, nothing on the menu meets expectations. Not friendly vegetarian friendly, lack vegetarian awareness. Will not return.

Paid Mr. East Kitchen a visit on a Saturday for lunch. It wasn't crowded at all - given the area, it's probably more busy on the weekdays. The inside isn't huge, but they have a good mix of smaller 2-4 tables, barstool seating, and a long community table. The interior is very cute and aesthetically pleasing! The greenery on the tables is a nice touch.  Its menu is Asian-fusion. You order at the counter, get a number, and seat yourself.

Food:
* Thai Tea French Toast: An interesting twist on the classic french toast! The thai tea syrup sauce was nice. They give a good amount of fruit.
* Garlic Noodles with Pork (you get your choice of meat!): The construction of the bowl is a bit like a Vietnamese Vermicelli bowl with pickled vegetables, cilantro, and fish sauce on the side. The garlic noodles itself were good.
* Earl Grey Milk Tea: Enjoyed the milky earl grey flavor, and paired nicely with the food.

The food was just okay for me. The quick service and pleasant ambiance are a great plus. Nice place if you don't want to wait a want a mix between breakfast and Asian food.

Review for boba only!
Found this spot on the way back from a movie at the Metreon.
Not a fan of Sharetea, and this wasn't too far from where I was.

Cute little spot that with a modern interior that also serves food (which looked very good and was well priced!) but only came for boba.

I got a matcha boba and he got a milk tea with boba. He's a little pickier about boba balls than I am, I tend to at least eat what i get (unless it's really horrible).
The boba here was not good. The drinks themselves were good. The matcha wasn't powdery or separated, it was very homogenous and tasted good. The milk tea was pretty good as well. It was just the boba balls that neither of us were fans of.
They tasted bland and both of us had clumps of boba inside our cups which made it hard to sip up at all. The texture was good, but they were so clumpy it made the drink literally difficult to enjoy since nothing was coming up.

I will update the review when i return for food which looked really good, but don't think i'll be stopping back here for boba! I am forever on the search for a solid boba spot on the way to the Metreon.

One of my favorite breakfast staples is a good Benedict so I am always looking for great brunch places. This is a cute, casual, order at the counter restaurant with individual and family style seating. I ordered the shrimp and avocado Benedict and wow, no regrets! The shrimp was butterflied and grilled, avocado portion was generous and let me tell you, the Hollandaise sauce was curry style! Unexpected but excellent surprise. Hashbrowns were good with a slight coconut hint but could have been more crispy. Salad had a sweet Asian style vinaigrette which was a lovely contrast to the other flavors, though a bit over dressed. Will definitely be back to try other dishes.

Order was taken quickly and drinks were brought out promptly. Something happened in their system where the order didn't go through so we sat for almost an hour and noticed a bunch of people getting their food before us. They came back out to take our order, but we had already ordered. They checked and found our order. They apologized and offered everything for free to us. The food was really good as were the drinks. We understand issues happen, but they made things right. Will return to explore more of their delicious menu.

Great experience here - tried it out for Sunday lunch and was really impressed.

Service was great. For those dining in, they seated us and then we ordered up front at the chaser when ready. Then, they deliver the food to the number at the table.

Food was excellent. We had garlic noodles with grilled chicken, chicken (not grilled) pho and a fried chicken sandwich and fries. Everything was tasty and I'd reorder any of them!

They checked COVID vaccinations and spaced the seating out. Will come here again!

Thank you for accommodating kids and providing excellent service!!

Their weekend lunch is bomb! I went this past weekend with my friend since I was craving Asian/Asian Fusion food. I don't see what I got on their online menu, but in-store I believe it was sriracha bacon and eggs with fried rice. A bit heavy, but so good! I've also ordered to-go from them a few times for lunch and my experiences those times were meh - the food was a bit cold and so the textures and tastes were a bit off too. That being said, I'm definitely a fan and it's easy enough to get to (BART and MUNI are both close by) that I'm sure I'll be back soon :)

Great experience with pickup at Mr. East! We ordered in store and they were so friendly and helpful with the menu.

We got the Tom Yum noodle soup and also the early grey milk tea. Lots of customizations available for the milk tea and it was pretty good! Tom Yum noodle soup was a good portion and super hot and flavorful.

They're doing a lot of promotions right now like 20% off and also $5 off when you do contactless ordering through an app! Highly recommend
Every time I bring my friends here they love it, their coffee drinks are awesome, highly recommend the breakfast sandwiches, and their matcha pancakes are great according to my friend

Delivery. Everything arrived warm and just right.

A truly beautiful experience!
Fresh, nourishing. delicious.
Wonderful find. Will recommend, and be back.

Had the Tum Yum soup.
Thai tea French toast is so on point was going to this place because i saw an ad so I give it a try and it's worth it!

Good service, modern looking clean interior, and great food, fresh and good portion. I got morning crispy chicken salad and everything came fresh and well made. I also tried the Saigon steak and it was very juicy and delicious.

Great find. Lovely people. Great food. Will go when in town again.

Was treated so well. Not conventional breakfast. Well maybe if your used to Asian cuisine. I am. Ha

Most amazing staff!
The pumpkin curry and vegan delight is amazing!
Don't miss the Patatas brava. And the most amazing dalgona coffee! Highly highly recommend
I've been ordering takeout from MEK over the past 2 years, and they've consistently served tasty, well balanced dishes. Counter help is always friendly. The space is welcoming too! Give them a try.

Really wanted to like this place, but giving it a 3 stars since the food was fine but the restaurant itself is very grimy. They have a variety of asian dishes and everything we ordered was good, however there are flies/gnats in the entire restaurant. They were flying around us while we were eating and some even landed on our food if we were not actively swatting them away. It was very nauseating and honestly makes me question the cleanliness of their kitchen as well.
Best breakfast I've ever had. Fruit was fresh, everything was hot when it came out and the service was even better. Inside was beautiful and clean. Please give this place a try!
This place is legit. I was hoping it would survive the pandemic and so glad it did. Love the garlic noodle dish and padseeew. But everything is bomb.
Slam dunk. Amazing flavors that seem so obvious to be included in every breakfast dish. Highly recommend!
Great place for breakfast or brunch. The waitresses were super friendly and welcoming. The foods were good and they were mixed in Thai and Vietnamese foods

One of my foodie friends asked if I was free on a Saturday morning for brunch and I was like yeah let's do it. He suggested this place and it looked promising and it sure was!

You order at the counter first then find a seat after. I think since the place is fairly new not many people know about it yet and that's a good thing because most brunch spots in the city have at least an hour wait on the weekend. There was no wait so we had ample amount of time to explore the menu options.

My sister and I decided on the Thai Tea French Toast $11 and added eggs + Sriracha bacon +$4. Also got the California Omelette $15. The Thai Tea French Toast is not too sweet and I love that the sauce is on the side by default. That way I can control how much I want and get a nice boomerang shot for the gram. I was a bit skeptical on the Sriracha bacon, but it was surprisingly just the right amount of heat and sweet. I love that they do not skimp on the fruit. I kid you not half of the plate was mixed fruit. The California Omelette was a solid choice as well because they gave a hefty amount of shrimp. I swear I had one in every bite. The salad was so refreshing with yummy citrus notes. They offer homemade raspberry jam which was the perfect match for the toast that came with the omelette.

One of the best brunch spots I've had in awhile and I'm the type who doesn't go out of my way to get breakfast often. For the heavy portions under $20 in SF, my asianess is screaming. New year, new brunch :)

The Banh Mi Sandwich is the best I ever had. The bread is fresh and soft, very easy to bite into. Sometimes grilled pork can be tough and dry but that's not the case here. The grilled pork was juicy and tender. They were very generous with the meat, and there were plenty of vegetables into the sandwich. The garlic fries were also very nice.
Great place for lunch. Variety of food options to pick from. Usually fast service aswell.
The tom-yum omelette and Thai French toast were amazing. Also really good service! Would come back and highly recommend

Mr. East Kitchen is a great Asian fusion restaurant that's a little more on the casual side. The restaurant style is order at the counter, and they will bring you your food. They have such a wide variety of foods, covering Thai, Vietnamese, Chinese cuisines, and more. I ordered my favorite - drunken noodles. It definitely fills a craving!

5 stars for everything + 1 more for good service, should be 6 stars. This is first time here, the Vietnamese lady is very nice and friendly, she suggested about the food and recommended for the Spicy Salmon for us to try. The dishes is so delicious than we thought. The Thai gentlemen invited us to the table and give us a good service and nice smile.
One more thing, this is our first time The Vietnamese lady gave us a 2 free drinks and 20% discount. Amazing..
Wonderful, we will come back and recommend for our friend. We will come back together.
After lunch, The Vietnamese lady introduced us her name is Amy and her coworker name's M . Thanks you for giving us a good service. Will back.

Went to Mr. East Kitchen on a whim and I'm so glad I did. The food was excellent, we ordered the salmon Eggs Benedict and the Thai Tea French toast; 10/10 for both dishes!! We also ordered a plain latte and mocha latte which were much larger than expected and some of the best coffee we've had in SF which was a pleasant surprise. I would highly recommend visiting here when in the area but be sure to make a reservation if possible. Although the place appeared empty almost every table was reserved and they were gracious enough to fit us in.

My sister and I had just dropped my dad off at SFO and we were starving! We found this place and decided to head on over. They made sure we were vaccinated (which we appreciated knowing everyone in the store was vaccinated since we have immunocompromised people in our family.) Our food was so filling and delicious! Just look at the picture. I am not a fan of sausage but I think this was the apple sausage and I loved it!! Definitely recommend
Amazing food!! The pics don't do them justice. Great quality ingredients and friendly customer service. Can't wait to go back!

Solid fast casual brunch and lunch place, fair price and delicious food, would recommend.

This is my go to place for lunch since I live in the area. If you order through Allset with their promo credits, this place costs less than $15 for lunch which is very good.

This place is a very cute little Vietnamese shop, where the interior is lined with plants and cute things, and the whole atmosphere screams TRENDY! It makes me wish I had a girl squad to eat breakfast or brunch here every weekend.

The breakfast sandwich meals (~$8) comes on an English muffin and two sides of perfectly crispy hash browns. I like to stick one hash brown in my sandwich for the ultimate experience but some might find that blasphemous. My recommendation is to add some kind of weekend mimosa experience and you've got yourselves a dedicated girl squad entourage each weekend. ($20 bottomless mimosas and omurice?! It's my ABC dreams come true)!!

The stir fried noodles (pad see __) are a solid choice that will not lead you astray. The pad Thai is not too sweet. But, I am here for the steak pho. It's a $2 up charge but WORTH IT. The soup is deep and flavorful and the noodles are the soft, slightly wide kind that doesn't stick together hopelessly if left unattended for too long. And the steak pieces are perfection.

The Banh Mi will do you no wrong either, so order away!

Ambience: Casual setting, modern design, clean. Nice for brunch or lunch.

Service: Overall, good. Items are ordered at the register. Food was brought out in a reasonable time and was hot. Only possible issue- meals were not brought out at the same time, but, I do appreciate that it was warm (rather than sitting on the counter and growing cold just to be served together).

Food: Delicious! Overall, 5/5 for food. This is based on the Eggs Benedict, with avocado, and Garlic Noodle Bowl, with steak. Flavors were on point. Their house hollandaise sauce has a nice sweetness with coconut; appreciated the asian fusion here. Garlic noodles were well seasoned with a nice thickness- would have preferred if they were just a tad al dente (but they won't stop be from coming back. Steak was also cooked well. All ingredients were fresh.

Price: Appropriate.

If you're looking for a delicious brunch with fresh bold flavors, check out this spot. We would be back to try new items!
This place is excellent and food delicious. Punches way above its weight for a brunch place. Prices really good and excellent service.

Randomly walked into this restaurant the other day.
The food was definitely good I ordered the shaking beef and my friend got five spice chicken noodle bowl.
big portions and tasty food.
The shaking beef was done just right. Very juicy!

We ordered chicken garlic noodles, veggie spring rolls, and chicken pho from here (they don't have a beef option or else I would've probably chosen that)

The chicken garlic noods was my favorite dish out of all of them. Chicken was grilled perfectly and was flavorful. Veggie spring rolls are delicious as well, but I would say they're slightly over fried for my liking. Chicken Pho was a let down because the flavors were not as strong as I would've liked. The portions of the dishes are definitely very generous and were enough to sustain two meals for me :)

A great spot for a quick bite for lunch. the decor here is cute and aesthetic as well.

Update: I had a typo in my previous review stating that the generous portions were a let down (but it was due to an incomplete sentence!) sorry about that. Love the big portions and would love to visit again

The crispy chicken fried rice is great option for dinner or lunch. Come here for brunch and try the omelette fried rice and banana french toast for a combo of sweet and savory! I love the vibes and the plants give it such a warm vibe. Thai tea, thai tea! Overall I don't wanna hype up the place too much but come thru and support this business!
Parking is rough but lyft bikes are right around the corner!

Visiting from Seattle and a lot of my local friends recommended me to go to this place. Garlic noodles were really good, came with pickled carrots, pickled daikon, bok choy , kale, and some Vietnamese sweet fish sauce on the side. I didn't really expect for the garlic butter flavored noodles to go well with fish sauce but I was pleasantly surprised! These noodles were straight gas, no lie. Fresh rolls were good too. They came with a side of peanut sauce. Also very gas.

Ordered pickup through Doordash - pickup was quick and easy!

Overall: large portions and good flavor

Shrimp Pad Thai: great Pad Thai flavor, noodles were a bit overcooked and broke apart easily, but the portion was enough for two meals! Would recommend!

Pork Banh Mi: good overall, large chunks of pork and pickled vegetables which fell out easily but the pickled vegetables were soooo good and the garlic fries that came with the Banh Mi were phenomenal!

This place was a wonderful find! Not in the most busy part of SF. The inside is very clean and the look is so modern. The food was really good. The hash browns are anything special. I would definitely come back to this place again
Delicious & great service. Highly recommend. The atmosphere is not ideal, kind of spare & generic, but the food and drinks are worth your time.

As I was running in the rain in San Francisco getting drenched I walked into a restaurant not knowing what they even serve. As soon I entered I was greeted by all the employees including the chef line they were wearing masks but the welcoming smile was beaming from their eyes. Now let's talk about food, oh my my I can't explain how delicious and flavorful my breakfast was. The bacon was drenched with the Tom yum sauce and it was the best I have ever tasted. My husband ordered the Tom yum noodle shrimp soup and he loved it. The ambiance of the restaurant was very beautiful and environment very friendly and homely. I also ordered the Thai tea French toast which was to die for. I encourage everyone to order that for sure. The coffee latte and its presentation was something I needed that day. The rain pouring outside while I sat there staring at the leaves falling down with the rain and life just happening in slow motion with every sip of my latte. Best experience I could have had in this rainy weather. Please do visit this place and comment and let me know what you think about it. Happy holidays

Guys, the Thai Tea French Toast was amazing and the presentation was very nice. It came with a side of fruit and you can even order bacon and eggs to go with it.
I'm not a breakfast person so I tried to to keep it light. My sister ordered the garlic fries which was quite crispy.

They also serve boba and now I totally regret not ordering any.
There was plenty of seating just because we arrived right when they opened. It did get a little busy right after though.
So glad I stopped by here first because it set the tone for the rest of my day. Cannot wait to stop by here when I visit the Bay Area again.

Best garlic noodle spot around, so flavorful and like that it comes with vegetables!

Thai Tea French Toast - was good, would use both sauces to really soak in the flavor

Would come again just to try everything else :)

Parking - very difficult, closest is a parking lot on mission and 5th I believe

This spot is great if you're in the Financial District/SOMA area and are in need of a low key brunch spot! I went around 1:30PM and there was a ton of space for seating. You first order at the counter, then you seat yourself with your number. It's a very nicely decorated restaurant, and great for catching up with friends! Their closing time is at 3, which I thought was a bit odd and put a tad of a rush on our table.

Overall, I think the star of their weekend brunch is definitely the Thai Tea French Toast. I definitely enjoyed it and thought it was good, but it was just missing the star factor for me. I personally didn't think it tasted that strongly of Thai tea, so I was a bit disappointed with that. I had to add a lot of their Thai tea syrup to taste that flavor. I will say the fruit that came on the side was so fresh and delicious! And the presentation? STUNNING!
The spicy sole fish is amazing. Curry is good and the fish is crispy and flaky. Super nice lady runs the place all by herself but she's super quick. Will definitely be back!

Super cute spot with friendly staff!

I was intrigued by the Thai tea French toast and I was not disappointed. The thick Thai tea sauce, almost pudding like, had just the right amount of sweetness! Not too sweet that you'd get sick of it. Perfectly paired in a combo with sausage and fresh fruit.

Shrimp Benedict: they are generous with the shrimp and avocado so this is a must if you love those two things! This was one of the most unique benedicts I've had and I thought breakfast benedicts are all pretty much the same.

The portions and variety of food we had on our plates left us full and happy!
Great food and friendly service. Very clean. Would definitely come back again! Drunken Beef Noodle was delicious!

Food Review: Mr. East Kitchen - A Fusion Experience

I recently had the opportunity to try out Mr. East Kitchen, a restaurant that offers a mix of Vietnamese and Thai cuisine. I decided to go for the chicken pho, as it's a classic dish that I love. However, my experience with the pho broth at Mr. East Kitchen was a bit different from what I expected.

Typically, pho broth is not spicy, but at Mr. East Kitchen, the chicken pho broth had a noticeable spicy kick to it. While it wasn't necessarily a bad thing, it was unexpected. Additionally, the broth wasn't completely clear as I'm accustomed to with pho. Instead, the presence of Thai basil gave it a green tinge, further enhancing the spiciness. Overall, it was a unique twist on the traditional pho broth, but not necessarily what I was anticipating. The chicken pho was priced reasonably at $14 and came with wide noodles, jalapeños, bean sprouts, lime, chicken bits, and onion shaved skins. The inclusion of these ingredients added a nice variety of flavors and textures to the dish.

Aside from the pho, I also tried the spring rolls priced at $9. They were decent but didn't particularly stand out. They were served with a dipping sauce, which added some tanginess to the rolls. However, compared to other places I've tried, they were just average.

One highlight of my meal was the garlic noodles, which I ordered as a side for an additional $3.50. In fact, I enjoyed them so much that I would have been satisfied if they were the main course instead of the pho. The garlic noodles had a flavorful and rich taste, and they were cooked to perfection. They were definitely the highlight of my dining experience at Mr. East Kitchen.

Lastly, I tried their pad Thai priced at $15. It was decent but didn't particularly stand out compared to other places I've tried. The flavors were good, but there was nothing remarkable about it that would make me choose it over other Thai restaurants.

One positive aspect of my experience at Mr. East Kitchen was that I was able to use an Uber Eats gift card, which made the meal even more enjoyable. However, considering the overall experience, I don't think I would choose Mr. East Kitchen as my go-to place for Thai or Vietnamese cuisine unless I'm specifically craving their garlic noodles. I might consider trying other dishes if I happen to be nearby, but this experience didn't highly motivate me to explore their menu further.

In conclusion, Mr. East Kitchen offers a fusion experience by combining Vietnamese and Thai cuisine. While the chicken pho had a spicy twist and the spring rolls were average, the garlic noodles were outstanding and worth trying. If you're in the mood for Thai or Vietnamese food, there may be other establishments that can better satisfy your cravings. However, if you find yourself nearby and craving those delicious garlic noodles, Mr. East Kitchen is worth a visit.

We stumbled upon this little spot while walking around SoMa and I'm glad we had a yummy breakfast! We tried the Thai tea French toast, the garlic noodles, the Tom yum omelette! We also tried the Vietnamese dalgona coffee which was okay. The Thai tea drizzle for the French toast was not too sweet, which I really like. The omelet had good flavor, not too strong of a tom yum taste, but really, mainly the shrimp inside tasted like Tom yum. The rest was just eggs and vegetables. Overall, I think I'd come back to try the other dishes!

I saw this place on Yelp and I knew I had to come here! The place is really nice and chill, there's loads of space so it doesn't feel cramped at all. It's very casual and simple, which makes it a great place for you and your friends to come for lunch. I got the Tom Yum omelette because I never heard of that before and I was really curious. It was a really yum omelet with a lot of goodies inside. It was less cheese and egg compared to usual American omelettes, and it had really flavorful veggies inside. There was a slight tomatoey taste that was quite special, I think that was the Tom yum addition. Overall I really enjoyed it here (:

I had a nice experience here.

I had the Basil Chicken which seemed to be inspired by Thai flavors of salty/sour/sweet and everything was balanced very well. It arrived with brown rice and steamed vegetables and a perfectly cooked egg - it definitely made for a hearty meal. I also had a bit of the Garlic Noodles with Chicken and that had great Vietnamese flavors in the dish. They have a nice menu since you can order anything from sandwiches to noodles to salads to rice bowls. I also had a Thai iced tea, which was good and not too sweet.

I'd recommend this spot if you're in the area. The setting is modern and comfortable and a nice oasis from the craziness in SoMa.

Hai Nan Chicken is delicious.

Cute little spot. A mix of viet and Thai food. Recommend this spot!

Second time coming to Mr East, last time went the brunch route and had a really tasty Thai tea French toast! This time I went savory and got the drunken beef noodle -- such good flavor! Good blend of spicy and marinated beef the honey pork garlic noodle was also great and the mango sticky rice was killer, the table was fighting over the last bite!

Love this place - Mr East Kitchen is truly the perfect spot to get work done (they have reliable WiFi) or to catch up with friends. While I can't say the food is anything remarkable, the atmosphere definitely deserves 5 stars - cute decor, plenty of seating, sparkling clean, never too crowded, and never too noisy. I'd camp out here all day everyday if I could!

Food-wise, the menu is pretty extensive and there is something for everyone. Portions are also pretty generous.

Want something clean but filling? The Morning Green Salad is pretty bomb (love their tamarind vinaigrette).

Want something heavy and carby? Well heck... they have pho, noodles, rice plates, and banh mi served with your choice of protein. It can't get any better than this!

Want something fried and greasy? Garlic french fries to the rescue. Yumm

Want a warm drink on a cold day? I recommend their matcha latte with oat milk. Yes, they have oat milk!

Want brunch food without having to wait in lines for days? Come on the weekends to try any of their egg dishes or the Thai Tea French Toast. Presentation/plating is always on point, aka very instagramable (:

All in all, don't come here expecting og/authentic Vietnamese food, but you can definitely count on them for good fusion Vietnamese food (at generous portions) and a great atmosphere.

Ordered the chicken Banh Mi which comes with fries and the fresh rolls because I needed something to eat before picking up a friend. This was close by. NEVER AGAIN. Not only was their "banh mi" $12 it was further away from a real Banh Mi as Taco Bell is from Mexican food. Over all scores Food 1 Service 10 Value 2 nothing worse than overpaying for crappy food!

Came here awhile back when they first opened. Their menu was very limited at the time. They only had the signature bowls. So it was exciting to see how much they've expanded. They now serve breakfast foods as well. Considering I'm a huge fan of brunch food, I was really excited when I found out.

The Thai Tea French Toast was delicious and had a nice presentation to it. It came with a generous side of fresh fruits. If that's not enough, you can even make it a combo by adding 2 eggs with your choice of bacon or sausage for $4. The portion size was perfect for me. The Thai tea sauce had a really nice consistency and flavor to it. However, the french toast itself was a bit too soggy for me. They were drenched in too much sauce. Everything else was pretty tasty though. I thought the poached eggs were poached perfectly. The whites were just firm enough to hold the creamy yolks inside.

My friend ordered the Shrimp Benedict which she really enjoyed as well. They're very generous with their shrimp. The curry hollandaise sauce was really nice and pieces of jalapeno gave a really nice kick which went really well with the shrimp. Hash brown on the side was crispy and well seasoned with flavor.

The ambiance was also really nice. Cute interior and super trendy! My friend and I had a great dining experience. Super impressed at how much this place has grown. To my fellow Yelpers, I highly recommend this place for both brunch/lunch. Why wait in line 1+ hour at other brunch spots when you can get efficient service here.
Ordered the lava beef for takeout. It was soo good!!! Definitely coming back to explore more items on the menu.

Came here on a weekday around 2pm for a late lunch with our parents who were in town and were sat right away. The servers were very kind and very efficient.

To drink, my husband and father in law ordered the Vietnamese dalgona coffee which was really good.. strong and also sweet. I ordered an iced vanilla latte, which I didn't love.. I could hardly taste the vanilla or the coffee.

For our food, we ordered the Tom yum soup (small size), chicken pho, pad see ew, garlic noodle bowl with 5 spice chicken and the shaking beef. The shaking beef and pad see ew were full of flavor and my personal favorites, but everything was really good!

My husband and I really enjoyed the food and the service and plan on coming back in the future.

I had a curry bowl with chicken. Such a huge portion size! The chicken was moist and the curry itself was full of flavor. It was very creamy. I'm so glad the dish came with bok choy too.

The space was clean and bright. A good place for lunch with a friend.

They serve American breakfast foods (omelettes, etc.) on the weekends, which I thought was an interesting contrast to the Asian menu. The restaurant caters to a wide audience!

I have lived in the vicinity for over a year and have always walked by Mr East Kitchen but never went in. Today I finally went in and I'm kicking myself for not coming sooner! The food was so amazing and the staff was really friendly. I came in near their closing time and they were nice enough to stay open a little longer to let me finish eating. I will definitely be back! I'm excited to explore their menu they have a lot of items that look unique and tasty

I don't understand how this place has 4 1/2 stars. Everything we ordered was bland and dry. To top it off, the food wasn't even served hot, I felt like asking if they could throw it in the microwave or something. You would be better off eating bag ramen.

The food and Ambience was really good. It's definitely recommended to come early or get a reservation as once we sat down it was full. The fried chicken was really crispy and Panda was really good. I would come back again to try some of the other dishes.

They don't have much room inside but it's always been relatively fast to get the food and there's been seating when I visit in person. I love their tom yum flavor omelet, fried rice, waffles, and sandwiches.

Honestly, this place is super adorable and aesthetically pleasing, but they need to improve on their food. I ordered their garlic noodles with five spice chicken, spicy sriracha wings, garlic fries, and steak pho. Yes, in pictures it looks very appetizing and all, but the food didn't really have much flavor. It was more on the bland side. The steak pho was probably the worst dish I got. The steak in the pho was hard to chew while the broth had no flavor hence the pho wasn't very good. I also got the earl gray milk tea with boba-- this was okay. I would come back in the future if they improve on their menu and work out the flavorings on their dishes.

CORRECTION TO REVIEW + RATING UPGRADE

Owner called yesterday to personally apologize - wow! Being a small biz is not easy and for the owner to call, it significantly deescalates a poor experience. That, and the owner let me know that it's no a "roach" but a bug that's common in bok choy, but said sorry nonetheless and reassured a more thorough washing of veggies. I fact checked him after since the bug looked like a roach to me with its nasty antennas but google quickly corrected me and that it's a "jumping leaf bug" which made me feel a lot.

Net net - we used to be big fans of Mr. East Kitchen and decided to never eat there again after the bug episode. But now with the owner calling and that it's not a roach, we may be back to eat or order delivery again.

Roach in garlic noodle with salmon. Omg! Am reporting to sf heath dept too, unbelievable!

Update 1.5 hours after calling restaurant:

Revised from 1 to 2 stars. Restaurant worked with postmates to issue refund and offered me an entree next visit (not sure we'd ever go back but gesture is nice). Staff apologized and reassured that they are going to look into this with kitchen crew. Overall positive issue resolution but still...

This place is ok. Came here after we landed in San Francisco. We were hoping for a nice breakfast but this wasn't really a breakfast place. The dish I had was actually good. There are a few things on the menu you can get for breakfast. We were just disappointed with the selection. Nothing on the menu when you walk in says they serve breakfast. We were going to walk out but the host said they have breakfast, so we tried it.

Tasty, affordable, and well done food. I love that you can order directly through their website and every time I've done so, the food has been fast, hot, and ready for pick up! I'm grateful that we still have this restaurant as an option to eat from in SoMa - make sure to support this local business!

TLDR: I've had their catering and was excited to see that they offer brunch. It was overall damn great and would love to come back!

Knowing how bad waits are for weekend brunch, I was looking through endless searches on Yelp. Then Mr East Kitchen shows up and I'm like OMG I love love their garlic noodles here!

My friends and I agreed to go after our escape room. When you walk up front, it's similar to a Panera or Corner Bakery but a lot smaller. You would order first then take a number and find your spot.

What we ordered:
- I ordered the garlic noodles with salmon... Girl wanted her noods and would have not been satisfied without it ¯\_(ツ)_/¯. It comes with kale salad and I never appreciated kale until I ate it here. There was no bitterness to it! They also offer a decent portion of salmon, which I could barely finish.

- Tom yum omelette - overall had the tom yum punch, but don't know how I felt knowing it's not a soup. Their Sriracha glazed bacon is delish!

- California omelette - I did not eat this one but my friend finished it all! And she usually brings her food home after.

- steak and eggs - your classic steak and eggs.. and the portions are huge! I've been told that the Thai tea toast doesn't have Thai tea flavor...

- Omurice - looking at it, it doesn't look like omurice at all. BUT, the flavors are there! It felt like I was eating a pad Thai with rice.... Rice Thai??? I would actually want to eat this next time I come back

- earl grey milk tea with light sweetener - oof the earl grey is strong! Loved it and definitely would come back for that again

The only reason why I am rating this one star lower is because:
- their catering is on time and delicious, however the chicken is very bland and needs the sauce with it
- it may just be me, but I did see that they were supposed to offer Thai tea toast with the omelettes, but neither of them had it

Overall, please give this place a try! If not, definitely try their catering out.. it's relatively cheap for 10+ ppl and there's a lot of leftovers!!
Love this place!! tried it with my bestfriend and it was hard picking what to order cause everything looks so good. Also love the place and it's definitely 'instagrammable'

honestly SO GOOD! My friend and I were looking for a nice breakfast spot and this place seemed perfect! Beautiful interior, once you enter you're seated or you can order for take out. My friend got the salmon Benedict and I got the poached eggs with the sriracha bacon and it was all amazing! Spicy but not too spicy, and the eggs were good. Thai milk tea was also yummy! We do recommend :-) staff very friendly also!! Priced about $21-$22 per person with drinks but pretty average for sf brunch! If you're in the area pls check it out!

Mr East Omelette has generous size, comes with bread and hash brown, and test so good. The service is very friendly. Due to wearing a mask, I couldn't hear the person who took my order very well. He came out from behind the counter to confirm my order so we don't have miscommunication. Will defiantly come back to try other items on the menu.

Very cutely decorated interior with great natural light. Street parking only, most of it is metered.

We got the Thai Tea French Toast, Pandan Chicken and Waffles, Hai Nan Chicken, Garlic Fries, and Steak Eggs Benedict. All the prices were really low for San Francisco and the food was decent.
My favorite was the Fried Chicken & Pandan Waffles. The chicken was juicy and the Pandan waffles were flavorful and unique. Plus the entire dish was 11$ only. The Hai Nan Chicken was also good, the chicken was slightly dry but the rice had great chicken flavor.
The Thai Tea French toast was served with the Thai Tea sauce on the side, and didn't have powdered sugar on it like in other Yelp photos. The portion was generous and there was a lot of fresh fruit served with it. The flavor of the Thai Tea sauce was overly sweet though.
The Steak Eggs Benedict was yummy, eggs were poached well and the portions were big.
The garlic fries were tasty, on the crispy side (which I like) and had strong garlic flavor. They have a special Sriracha Mayo dipping sauce with their fries which is a great mix of creamy and spicy.

The food is overall great for the price!
This place was so good! Large portions, as well as discounts and promos of free food. Good Asian fusion. We had the Pho and Benedict Shrimp. Then got a free fried chicken!! Thank you!

Nice ambience, flavorful food, and good service.

Had the Banh Mi and enjoyed it, others in my group also liked the Thai Tea toast and the garlic noodles with shrimp.
Food was so good. Got the Thai tea French toast and hai nan chicken. Yum yum yum yum yum

The fried chicken and rice was really good - had the perfect amount of light crisp. Every dish looks delicious, the ambiance is great, and staff super attentive / kind.

Portions are quite large as well. Will be coming back to try the rest of the menu...

I've come to Mr East Kitchen a few times pre Covid and have started ordering DoorDash from them throughout Covid. Overall, I've had a good experience with the food and the restaurant has good ambience as well.

The restaurant has Asian fusion food, ranging from Thai to Vietnamese to Chinese. There are also more traditional American breakfast foods so there is definitely a variety.

The only reason why my rating is 4 stars and not 5 is because of my DoorDash order yesterday. I ordered a mango sticky rice that was $7. The rice was super hard and the mango was not great either. I would definitely not pay $7 for that dish. Other than that, I've generally had a good experience with this place!

Mr. East is a go-to spot for me whenever I'm in the area. The employees are always super nice whenever I walk in! It's definitely not gourmet food, but the portion size is pretty hefty and will fill you up!

I usually get the crispy chicken rice, pad Thai, or pad see ew and I've always been satisfied. Their banh mi sandwich is on a ciabatta roll instead of French roll, which I am personally not a fan of.

During shelter in place, they have a 20% off all entrees & 15% off all small plates/drinks, which is actually a pretty good deal!
i really like this place. good food, courteous staff. 4 star instead 5, bc they recently raised prices.
Had a variety of dishes at the table, would recommend the Thai tea French toast, omelette fried rice and the patatas! All had great texture and flavor!! drinks were great and super kind service

Service is okay but we kept having to wave the waitress over. The eggs Benedict were really good but the potatoes were really plain. My brother really enjoyed his French toast . Ambiance was kinda depressing it's all sad music played in a acoustic version which kinda turned the mimosa vibe down.

Ordered the five spice chicken, garlic noodle off Club Feast delivery service. The chicken is flavorful and juicy. The garlic noodle is satisfying (not too fatty) and there's a nice amount of kale, bok Choy and pickle to brighten it up!

FINE DINING WITH THE EASTS.

Absolutely divine! Like seriously, how can you go wrong with this place? They have a piece of everything for everyone to enjoy, that's what makes them so great.

What we ordered:
Thai Tea French Toast, Morning Green, Classic 2 eggs (w/ Sriracha Bacon), Avocado Toast, Basil Chicken, & Garlic Noodles

What we loved:
Everything.

What we hated:
N/A

The Thai Tea French Toast was my personal favorite as it wasn't too sweet (which I like!) and had a nice crunch to it on the crusty edges and soaked in Thai tea? I mean......what else could you possibly want. It was different and unique, I don't think you can find this in many restaurants. The Morning Green is something I'd order after a morning yoga session, it's light but contains your healthy omega-6. The Sriracha Bacon though....now that's a thicc piece of bacon alright!!!! The bacon had more of a jerky texture to it rather than bacon (not a lot of fat) and the sriracha made it sweet, savory, & spicy all at once.

Thanks so much to the lovely staff for serving us such an exquisite meal. All of SF needs to hop onto the East's Kitchen train ASAP.

My friends and I came around 11am for a tasting and we were absolutely blown away by the food and presentation! Parking is pretty difficult, and the neighborhood is rather rough. However, we didn't have to look too hard to find a parking spot. The restaurant is more like a cafe, where you order at the front and find a seat. They also offer wifi, which makes this place a good place to get some light work done if you're a solo diner.

We decided on the lava beef, garlic noodle bowl with shrimp, thai tea french toast, passion fruit tea, and the thai milk tea. The thai tea french toast was so aesthetic! It came to the table looking like a mountain of delicious fruit, luxurious thai tea sauce, and powdered sugar. It was a little cold when we finally ate it, since we were taking pictures of it, but it was pretty good! The toast was really soft and spongey and it wasn't too sweet. The lava beef was also great, but be aware that the sauce is very spicy if you have a low spice tolerance! The garlic noodles are also very good, and there was a good portion of shrimp.

The passion fruit drink was the best drink we had that day! It was fruity, and the boba was fresh. We loved the specs of fruit in the drink. The thai milk tea was a little diluted, and we wish the flavor was a bit stronger.

I see this place being a great place for lunch or a quick brunch! I'd recommend a try!

Amy and M behind the counter are the best. Compliments to the cook in the back too. Way yummy Thai tea French toast. Unique twist that really works. Another standout is their mildly spicy salmon rice plate. Rich flavors, lots of salmon pieces, five different veggies. Winner!! I also enjoyed their 2-piece fried chicken with pandan waffle. I even enjoyed cross dipping the waffle in Thai tea sauce. So good. Can't wait to try their various other offerings.

One of the best brunches I've had in a while! Ordered the chicken banh mi with a subbed side salad instead of fries and the pandan chicken and waffles togo. The side salad had a mouth watering dressing and the ciabatta bread was some of the softest bread I've ever had. The banh mi was definitely Americanized but it was still extremely yummy! The fried chicken was perfectly crispy and the mustard dipping sauce was a great addition.

Cute Vietnamese spot in Soma! They also have creative Asian fusion brunch items in weekend! Highly recommend trying their special brunch menu!

Things I've tried so far:
Garlic noodle bowl with grilled chicken 4.5/5
Grilled chicken is super tender!

Morning green salad with steak 3.5/5
A lot of kale... I'll say 80% of it is just kale, which makes this salad a bit hard. But the steak is a 5 star.

Spring roll 4/5

Earl gray milk tea 4.5/5

Nice clean hole in the wall. I stopped by for breakfast. Not a ton of seating, some people turned around. I picked the tom yum because I could have gotten plain eggs at my hotel. Really good choice for a mix of cuisine.
Really fast service and fantastic delicious food. We got takeout during Covid. Great Covid safe practices and take out was delicious!!!

This place is a gem! Simple Vietnamese/Thai inspired dishes that are super delicious. We were able to find street parking relatively easily. The interior is bright and inviting with a nice wood aesthetic. We ordered:

Lychee jasmine tea: super refreshing drink! They have real lychee fruit in the drink too!

Passion fruit jasmine tea: this was ok. The passion fruit aftertaste wasn't that great and there was no sweetness at all.

Sriracha wings: pretty good! It tasted kind of like a mix between barbecue and buffalo sauce. It comes with 6 wings, which is a good amount for an appetizer to share.

Garlic noodles with pork: yuuuum! The noodle texture is so soft and it's super garlicy! I also liked the pickled vegetables but it was a bit strange to me that only some of the vegetables were but the bok Choy wasn't. Be sure to dip the meat in the fish sauce- pouring it all in might make the flavor too salty.

Thai tea French toast: a great brunch choice! I wish the flavor of the French toast was more pronounced but it was still delicious. It also includes a hefty portion of fresh fruit which really balanced each bite.

Curry shrimp eggs Benedict: the star of the meal!! The curry flavor is very evident in the sauce and it was so tasty. The shrimp was also cooked perfectly! The hash browns were crispy and the perfect golden brown & even the side salad was dressed with a delicious vinaigrette! Definitely the dish to get when you come here.

A great place to stop by for lunch/brunch in the city!

Saw the business in Doordash and decided to give Mr. East Kitchen a try. Didn't know what to order so I went with the Garlic Noodle Bowl and Drunken Noodle as suggested on the popular item list.

Garlic Noodle -
The noodle was delicious, infused with the buttery garlic flavor. You can see bits and pieces of garlic on every string of egg noodle. Since oil's the main source of flavor, you definitely want to eat the noodles with the steamed/fresh veggies on the side to not get overwhelmed by the greasiness nature of this dish. Usually I only order Garlic Noodle at other places when there are other dishes on the table so I won't feel sick afterward from the amount of grease. However, I think the bowl had a good balance by itself here. Well done! - minus the chicken... Couldn't really taste the 5 spice chicken. The meat was tender, softer than what I expected from thigh meat. I recommend using the sauce on the side for flavor.

Drunken Noodle -
Same type of egg noodle as the garlic noodle, which was surprising since usually this dish is served with the flat rice noodle. Upon the first bite, I realized what the dish was missing due to the type of noodle used- the wok stir-fry noodle texture/flavor cooked at high heat. Also, the ho fun noodle absorbs the flavor a lot better than egg noodles and relies less on the oil to carry the flavor. I love the generous amount of basil which provided that spice aroma. The addition of small tomatoes was a very nice touch - This was the first time I've had it in a drunken noodle dish and oh my, it made a huge difference. Although it makes no difference to me, but Mr. East Kitchen uses Jalapenos instead of Thai chili peppers. Also, this dish was noticeable more wet compared to Garlic Noodle. I am not sure it's because the noodle was not properly drained or what. Either way, it caused the noodle to pick up less flavor with each bite. Drunken Noodle also came with side veggies.

Even though I might have sounded a bit harsh above, I just want to be clear that I liked the two dishes overall and will definitely come back to try out other items on the menu. Also, I would like to try their Drunken Noodle made with the flat wide rice noodle (Ho Fun) instead of egg noodle.

Our company ordered food from this place so this is based strictly on my experience with the food; it has nothing to do with ambiance or customer service.

When I received my boxed lunch, I was pretty excited! I heard great things about this place. It was lukewarm- not a big deal, I can always reheat it. I poured some of the fish sauce onto my rice and beef steak (I always do this) and took my first bite. Unfortunately, it wasn't so great. There were about 6-7 pieces of beef steak. Took a few more bites with rice. The beef steak was chewy. I wanted to love it to soo bad! But there was no flavor and extremely bland. The veggies were okay but also tasted like they were boiled - not much flavor at all.

Sad to say, will not be returning. I reside in the East Bay where I have access to very good Asian food. I'm so bummed :(
So yummy. I had the Tom yum omelette with fruit. Great flavors + my favorite breakfast foods. The bacon and potatoes were fantastic.

Overall a great spot for brunch with an extensive, creative menu. Service was terrific, the space is incredibly cute, and food was good! Would definitely come back.

AMBIANCE/SPACE
Really cute space with wonderful decor and ultra-high ceilings, but important to note that they DO NOT offer outdoor dining! My friends and I thought they did because of their Yelp page, but I guess it's out of date. The tables are also a little close together. My friends and I didn't mind too much though, and they clean the tables well between customers.

FOOD:
Banh Mi sandwich: the fact that it was on untoasted ciabatta gave it a bit of a strange texture, but flavors were good. Fries were AMAZING and a super generous (perhaps too generous) portion!
Thai Tea French Toast: good french toast, and the dip had a true Thai tea flavor. The dip was a little dense though for repeated use
Eggs Benedict: my friend got this, and I would definitely come back to try this next time! Everything was well cooked, and it came with fruit and salad. The plate was aesthetic, yummy, and priced well.

SERVICE:
Great and friendly service. They were attentive with waters and food. You pay at the cashier up front, but they still come to your table every now and then to check on you.

Super cute decor but food was a huge letdown. I ordered the pho with steak for $13. It was very much fusion style with bok choy and fatter rice noodles than typical Vietnamese pho. The steak slices were thick and there were very few. The bowl looked large but it was mostly soup (like 80%) and very little actual noodles. The soup was too salty and didn't taste authentic at all, so I didn't drink it. Another thing to note is that when they first brought out my order, the soup was lukewarm so I had to send it back to get heated so that the steak could cook properly.

My friend got the surf and turf for $17 and it was also disappointing. He only got 2 pieces of shrimp and 4 tiny pieces of steak. It really wasn't even close to being a filling meal.

Overall food was really 2 stars but I'm going with 3 since the ambience was really nice. Maybe I'll come back to try the boba but definitely not the food.

this place is so random and i would say that the primary issue i have is that they do everything okay, but nothing really excels. they have pho, they have brunch food, they have thai food. but none of the plates are as good as at a restaurant that is specific to that cuisine.

The employees were I credibly kind, got seated right away and the food was DE-LI-CIOUS! It's a small, modern, cute restaurant with so many delicious options. And you must get the mango sticky rice! Also met the owner who was so sweet. Will be going back again when I'm in the city!
Food was ok, not too memorable unfortunately. The menu is quite interesting but flavors are a bit bland. Service was very nice and quick.

Milk tea with boba at Mr.East is my new favorite in SoMa. Comes in 3 simple flavors- black, earl, and hojicha. Tea flavor and sweetness level on point. (I wish they offered milk alternatives like oat/soy milk!) Can't wait to try their Vietnamese igarlic noodle & hot rice bowls. Can we also take a moment to appreciate the beautiful interior design? *heart eyes* Support local businesses

Update:
The chicken with ginger rice was so tender and flavorful but not heavy. Brownie points for the fresh asian bok choy!!

The pho was total comfort food and I felt healthy eating it. Props to not going overboard with the sodium. Good quality bone broth also proven when leftover soup gelatinized from collagen. Can't forget to mention the *fresh* veggies for that fiber intake!

Soft opening deal- free (quality) boba drink with purchase of entree. Get it while you can. Also they have oat milk tea now!! Dairy lovers, I dare you to try.

Milk tea with boba at Mr.East is my new favorite in SoMa. Comes in 3 simple flavors with fancy organic milk- jasmine, earl, and hojicha. Tea flavor and sweetness level on point. (I wish they offered milk alternatives like oat/soy milk!) Can't wait to try their Vietnamese inspired garlic noodle & hot rice bowls. Can we also take a moment to appreciate the beautiful interior design? *heart eyes* Support local businesses

Fantastic, fresh flavors, clean ingredients, really sweet wait staff and just good eating. I'm a huge fan of Mr East's, particularly of Amy, I see her all the time when I go in and she always makes my trip brighter. I think it's important right now to support local businesses, and Mr East's is very deserving of that support. I must have eaten here 50 times in the last six months, having lived next door, and the quality of food and the service is just phenomenal. I wouldn't keep going back if not!

Stop wasting time reading this review and go straight to Mr East Kitchen. This was our 1st visit. We had brunch here. It was fantastic. The combination of styles and flavors are perfect. American dishes you recognize with Eastern flair. I can't think of a healthier appealing meal than the Tom Yum Omelette with side salad of kale & baby spinach. Check this place out when you are in town.
Brunch was amazing! totally recommend if your looking for a hearty brunch.
The food was wonderful especially the pineapple fried rice and basil chicken. The lychee fizz was to die for and it great for sweet craving. We will be back!
One of the best restaurants inSF! We came here every morning for brunch during my vacation. All the dishes are so delicious and elegant in shape. Really enjoy the experience here.

Total hidden gem in SoMa. Not a place where you would expect to find such decadent and well-executed brunch menu items, but this will be my go-to place for brunch going forward.

I ordered the Tom Yum Omelette because it sounds very unique. I was not disappointed. The quality of the ingredients is high, the flavors are interesting/balanced, and the portion is generous! Plus, the place is modern and clean; the staff members are always friendly and courteous.

This place has easily become one of my top go-to COVID takeout spots. Great deals (I recommend ordering directly through their site rather than DoorDash, if you can! You get good discounts) and a nice location.

Staff is always friendly, and food is prepared promptly. I've had their bubble tea, pad thai, drunken beef, wings, fries, etc... Haven't been disappointed with taste, portion, or price.

There's also a severe peanut allergy in my household, and we've had no issues being able to eat foods that normally are untouchable (like Pad Thai). Not too greasy either.

Definitely give it a try!

One of the best breakfasts ever + perfect dalgona coffee! Hands down would come here again when in town.
Siracha bacon
Waffle
Chicken apple sausage
Thai French toast
Wish we could have had the chicken and waffles or the pancakes.

Good service overall- they are very welcoming and they will even say bye to you! I like the place a lot and the atmosphere is great. Super clean and aesthetically looking. Order up front and they will bring the food to your table. Thai milk tea French toast was very food. I don't like syrup because it can get super sweet but this wasn't isn't and it just melted in my mouth. Their chicken was super juicy and crispy. It's not your hard crisps that you have in other restaurants. However I do wish their chicken was well seasoned- which is why I gave 4 stars

The atmosphere and food was super. The restaurant does get busy so there will be a wait time to order food and get seated. Dishes on their menu ranges from the classic staple comfort Vietnamese/Chinese food to modern remixes. I ordered the han nan chicken with ginger rice and let me tell you the rice was delicious. Would definitely eat here again.
Food is delicious! Restaurant is clean & employees are very nice. The mango sticky rice is my fav!
Love this restaurant! The food is always fresh and yummy and the menu selection is amazing. We eat here all the time!

Super delicious garlic noodles. They come with a generous amount of chicken, and their fish sauce is nice and mild. They have vegetarian options as well. My friend got the vegetarian garlic noodles and the tofu that the dish came with was amazing! Also try their boba drink. Their Thai milk tea is super yummy. Not to mention their restaurant is super clean and cutely designed.

Im a fan. Here are some of my favorites:
(1) chicken & pandan waffle. The chicken is fried with a crisp skin, usually its a drumstick and thigh (which I prefer). Love the dark brown sugary syrup for the pandan waffle, the waffle tastes fine without syrup as well
(2) eggplant tofu, sort of a class over rice dish that I really like
(3) shaking beef, flavorful and tender

For drinks I like the thai fruit tea

Hard to find parking, but that's always an issue with San Francisco. This place is an amazing hidden gem. Typical San Francisco prices, but holy cow do you get your money worth. Huge portions.
My partner got the shrimp Benedict. The shrimp were plentiful and the eggs were absolutely perfect. I was happy to have gluten free options, even though they gave me bread anyways. I got Two eggs, over medium with hash browns and added that sriracha bacon which was Devine! We shared a hot thai coffee, not too sweet! Yum. perfect little date spot.
Very tasty banana French toast, especially when you're hungry! Service also quite swift and good. The shop itself is bright and clean. Perfect place to meet a friend.

We stopped by here for brunch before heading over to SFMOMA. The food was delicious. We ordered the Pad Thai, Drunken Beef Noodle, and Garlic Noodle with steak as my meat choice. The kids loved the pad thai and I enjoyed the garlic noodle. My husband said the drunken noodle was good. Not his typical food, but it wasn't bad. He said the meat was too chewy. However, if you like spicy food, the drunken noodle is for you. We will definitely stop here again if we are ever to be in the city.

Came here during their soft opening for breakfast and enjoyed the two egg plate with bacon. The hash browns and scrambled eggs were particularly enjoyable! The staff was attentive and nice.

Overall a great local spot in SOMA with average SF pricing for quality food and an esthetic environment. I will surely be back here soon!
The food was amazing. I came here with a friend that was visiting sf and she loved it as well. This is a great brunch spot and I will definitely come back soon.
The restaurant is decorated very well and is clean. The staff was super friendly and the food was served quickly. The meal was delicious, I loved the garlic noodles with pork!

I'm for sure coming back. The food is so fresh and clean. You can see it in the color of the veggies. Delicious flavor. I'm super picky with food cause I am all about quality, this place succeeded my standard

I don't think there are enough words to describe how amazing this place is! The food is absolutely deliciously delicious!! The quality of their ingredients is impressive and everything is super bright and fresh. My fiancé and I ordered basil chicken, chicken pad Thai, and the shrimp fresh rolls with a matcha latte and a Thai iced tea. Every bite and sip wowed us more than the one before. DEFINITELY RECOMMEND

A hidden gem that me and my friend tried this last weekend and was so pleasantly surprised! The interior was modern and very nicely decorated with very high ceilings and nice interior design/decorations. I ordered the thai tea french toast and my friend ordered the tom yum omelette and thought both were delicious. Normally when I order french toast or pancakes the fruit on the side is so minimal that it's honestly just a few pieces for decoration but my french toast came with so much variety of fruit that it filled up almost half the plate! The french toast was delicious along with the thai tea sauce that came with it. My friends omelette was also delicious - she asked for no bell pepper and onion and in return the waitress offered her more mushrooms in her omelette instead. The customer service was great as they checked up on us every so often and made sure our food was just as we liked it. We also ordered a dalgona vietnamese coffee and jasmine green tea which were both good. The PRICES for this place were also a steal! My entire meal along with my drink was only $18 while my friends meal + drink was $20. At a normal brunch place in San Francisco, an average price of an entree is at LEAST $15 pre tax/tip so these prices were great along with the high quality of food and service they provided.

100% recommend if you're in the mood for some asian fusion brunch without paying the steep prices!

A great place for fast casual Asian fusion brunch. I always get the morning salad which is delicious - fried egg, spinach, avocado, nice sweet/tangy vinaigrette! They add in a slice of brioche toast which has great texture (though they just swapped it with a baguette slice which wasn't as good). Have also tried the boiled chicken which was solid.

Misses for me: banh mi has a ciabatta bun rather than baguette and is dry - you're better off going to Fresh Roll for that. Also a bit pricey for a fast casual place but such is SF

Beautiful space, gorgeous presentation, flavorful food.

I got the Benedict w steak & it was perfect.

The staff was helpful & kind :)

Came on a late Sunday morning. We had the shrimp curry benedict and hanging (beef) benedict; they were like $15 each. I thought it was pretty decent. Shrimp was cooked well but the coconut part of the curry could've been a little less domineering. The meat for the beef benedict surprisingly was not tough. Flavors were pretty good, and the kale salad side was a nice touch.

Americano did the job and passion fruit jasmine tea was good.

I liked the clean, bright space.

We weren't sure if there was service so we didn't tip till the end; there's a cash tip bin by the register. It's not standard service but they did bring the food and clear the plates.

We forgot to use our yelp check in discount that's currently available, but the staff made a onetime exception to apply it by updating our transaction.

Overall I'd come back, likely to try lunch or dinner items.
Highly recommend, especially for brunch! The tom yum soup with noodles is great value!

I had the spicy salmon and substituted garlic noodles instead of rice

It was fantastic

Startrd with the egg rolls which were incredible. You place them in a leaf of lettuce and add mint, carrots, etc wrap and dip. They were great.

The dining mate had the steamed chicken and he loved the sauce it came with

The Vietnamese coffee, which was very different, was so good, we ordered a second one

The cops on the beat were eating here....so you know it's a good place

Order at the counter

We walked here. Very clean and nice. People working here are sweet

Service is great.
Clean.
New.
Fresh.
Friendly.
Very very good coffee.

Always on the lookout out for a fresh new breakfast place, we decided to come here. It's close to home but also a refreshing change from the norm.

#Thai Tea Franch Toast - Great spin on a classic. I don't particularly like french toast and almost never order it but after the amazing experience at Jax (https://bit.ly/2MSBajO) a few weeks ago, I was craving the sweet goodness. This definitely hit the spot and filled my craving.

#Hash Browns - Excellent. Crispy, crunchie, awesomeness. Far above average!

#Chicken Apple Sausage - Great with lots of flavor. I'm getting this every time. Better than most.

#Coffee - is excellent coffee and worth coming in just for a cup. (note to self: I need to take more time in my reviews and talk about how bad coffee is at so many places.

Come back here ASAP.

Really happy this place opened up, it's really good! You can tell there's a lot of thought and effort going into the restaurant from the attention to detail and continuous improvement. I've been here on multiple occasions before writing this review in hopes to see how things progress, and thus far...

Food: I had the pork rice bowl and I was pleasantly surprised by the flavorful rice! The dish as a whole was great for lunch though a bit expensive to be a regular thing for me. It felt healthy and light but also nicely filling. I had the garlic noodles a while ago but it was a bit on the dry side for me, though still pretty good. Kale salad comes underneath with most dishes and was also a bit of a surprise to me, though I definitely didn't mind.

Drink: I waited a few weeks before reviewing and this is where the biggest difference was. On my first visit, the milk tea and boba were mediocre at best, but they've really improved! At this point, it's my favorite stop for Hojicha Milk Tea and perfectly chewy boba! Though I haven't had a chance to try their draft beer, you already know it's good if it's on tap.
