Nice garlic noodle. Not a big fan of their pho though. And the dinner entrees are good too.
The staff are also very nice.

Great Vietnamese food in clean, airy atmosphere!
Well worth the detour!!
Not overly priced compared to less fresh food at tourist traps/mall up the road!

Had the noodles and grilled pork option. The food was quite delicious but the portion felt a bit small. The pork was tasty but also on the drier side. Service was really great and i would happily go back to try one of their other dishes. My coworker had the salad and tofu option and enjoyed it as well.

Beware of the pho... Not really pho imo and bland.

Eggrollsbelow average BUT ice matcha latte was really really good and customer service was awesome.
This is just what this neighborhood needed! Casual but adorable, cheap but quality ingredients, in the middle of a touristy area but very authentic. I would recommend this place 100 times over!

It's only the soft opening right now, but it already caught my attention. It's a nice place to get Vietnamese inspired food. It's not as expensive as I was led on to think since yelp has it at $$, but it's about the same price as a typical meal at other $ restaurants here in SF. There's a great atmosphere and decorations. Would come again and again!

I'm really picky about my pho, but this place has a good take on pho! It's not traditional, but the quality of the broth, noodles and steak is great The cost of the pho is a little pricey (but pretty standard for SF), but the bowl is a large size. I also love the atmosphere of the restaurant - it's nicely decorated and it extremely clean Would recommend trying this place out!

If you're looking for authentic asian food, this is not the place! They have a modern take on asian food which is good though - although what I like the most about them is their portions! I've had lunch here and take out and had positive experiences both times. I've gotten the salad, pho, and boba and thought they were all fine. Not mind blowing, but good enough for me to go back (mainly out of convenience since I live and work nearby).
Delivery was good, I tried the Bahn mi and it was okay, not as authentic as I thought.

Had the banh mi sandwich. Delish! Not your traditional banh mi (they swapped out a toasted baguette for a toasted ciabatta) but it worked! It holds true to some basics and is tasty. Simple and good fast casual Vietnamese dressed up in modern decor. I sense a mild antler theme to the decorations, I must be missing something.

I placed my go to order on Yelp via Grub Hub.. the garlic fries and siracha hot wings were super fresh. Fries were crispy and not over trenched with oil. Wings had just the right amount of kick of spiciness and meat was still moist. Pick up time was earlier than promise as well! Reasonably price.
The food is really good here. The pho and tofu is as good as any I've ever had. My girlfriend loves the garlic noodles

This place is awesome and a solid 4.5 (my ONE 'gripe' at the end;). IMO, I think it would be hard to expect a place that serves several completely different styles of food in a quick-serve setting to have incredible dishes, but the fact that EVERYTHING is above-average is glorious. So much variety to suit nearly any of the many moods of my appetite. Along with very good Vietnamese for this area, you also have options of a pretty deep brunch menu i.e. benedicts, omelets, french toast, etc.. throw in some kinda-random-yet-fantastic side options like garlic fries, SRIRACHA WINGS, as well as surprisingly great beers on tap I could easily eat breakfast lunch or dinner here almost any day. My only problem- it's a tease to have beer, but no mimosas to coincide with the brunch menu‍ lol #basicpplproblems

It took them forever to make my egg and cheese sandwich. And when I opened my box, the sandwich was a big mess. It was practically falling apart. Sure it was cheap, but it's really just half a sandwich, since they only use 1 slice of bread. Also, who puts a wilted piece of lettuce in an egg and cheese sandwich??!!
Loved this place. The service was awesome and the tea was just as great. Cool place to grab a refreshing drink! In love with them food! Highly recommended!

I LOVE this place!!! The food is super fresh and they don't skimp on the vegetables. I just got a free drink because of their rewards program and they gave me the bigger size with all the add-ons (boba, oat milk) without giving me a hard time. The interior is beautiful and clean and it's a nice place to work (WiFi). The praram shrimp is my personal fave and the pad Thai is good too!
The pho was alright. I chose to pay an extra $1.00 for the steak and only got 4 small pieces. The place is cute, though!
Their drunken noodles is superb. I also recommend the shrimp pineapple fried rice. Just about every item on their menu is excellent and exceeds the average quality.

Really like this place. Wish they'd have kept the breakfast menu through the week, because their special eggs benedict with those hash browns... UGH, I miss them so and am rarely ever in town on weekends, when they're still served.

I just recently moved to SoMa and happened to live right next to this restaurant. I was pleasantly surprised to have access to a really good Asian food so close by! Their prices are justified by their large portions. Their chicken banh mi is my personal favorite but other great options include the pad Thai, pad see ew, and the salmon. I come here one to three times a week and have not had a single complaint. Highly recommend!
1 star for the interior. 1 star for the ok price of the portion and the ok taste. But overall it's average. The beef is good. We had pho soup and egg noodles. Both were just ok

Tried the chicken garlic noodles a couple of weeks ago, as well as on official opening day when they were giving it for free for the first 100 customers. The chicken was flavorful and quite a lot in quantity so that's good. But I wish the garlic on the noodles was a little less, because by the end of my lunch I was tired of eating way too much garlic! Also a little more pickled vegetables would have been awesome! Overall great vibe and will come back again to try other things on the menu.

this food was digesting, not to mention it took them 35 minutes to make my mood and my friend ordered the same thing and his came right away. i wouldn't say the entire restaurant is not good, but the group of friends i went with did not like it as well.

My lunch on the go. Their food is really good, vietnamese cuisine with little twist. The chicken basil is my fav, then noodle with shrimp. Come in the morning for quieter vibe to work and a cup of coffee. Excellent!
Hi took a banh-mi to go and it was delicious! Far better than Bun Me or any known places. I saw they have those massive bowls (soup or noodle), I can't wait to go back and try!
I'm from the East Coast and We walked into this place because of its rating on Yelp and let me tell you... this place is amazing! The portions were large and the taste is A-1!
Can you say YUM? Love the quality of the food and options! Very healthy sides and all the food is cooked to perfection. More like "thank u, me next!"

Salad was good, but pretty small for the price. The chicken and kale were tasty, and I always appreciate a kale salad that doesn't have that overly healthy kale salad taste you know?? I partook in the free boba giveaway and opted for no milk (I really wish they offered milk alternatives like almond or oat). The tea itself tasted really bad... I think it had soap in it?? It was really foamed and literally tasted like I got a mouthful of shampoo like every other sip??????? Ambiance is relaxing, lighting is very modern, and people seem nice.

We love their chicken pho, tom yum noodle soup, and dalgona coffee. It's the perfect place to go when you are craving for something light, feels healthy, but super delicious. Everyone there's extremely nice. Whenever we had special requests they've done everything they could to help with what we needed. Hope they survive the pandemic as this is our favorite place in soma.
Jay welcomed me to the restaurant and was very friendly and professional and helped me order. I've never been here before but I would like to come back

I really wanted to like this place! The garlic noodles are great and I wish they would just give you the option to get just Garlic noodles without an option of meat or Tofu. I ordered Garlic noodles with Chicken but the Chicken was fatty and had a strange flavor. I also ordered a Jasmine milk tea with Boba, the Jasmine tea was bitter and tasted over steeped. I went in yesterday to give their milk tea another chance and this time I ordered the Earl Grey milk tea with oat milk and Boba... the Earl Grey was way over steeped and so bitter. It tasted like I was drinking perfume and dried out my mouth. I am a tea drinker and love milk tea so I know it's not my palette. My advice would be to not over steep your tea. I know this place is new and so I'll come back in a month or so when they've worked out the kinks.

The asian lady at the counter is really nice. Since the pandemic they have been very clean about their surroundings and will clean up after u so as soon as youre done with everything you can stand up and just leave and they'll clean the rest for u so that they can clean it thoroughly. The food was also really really good, has a nice representation somewhere in the middle of classy and casual. In addition, the place is really aesthetic and has a good vibe. I would really recommend it to people to come and eat here and help support their business and try their food. Really, its good. Will come again for sure.
Ordered the chicken rice bowl, chicken had way too much fat but good in flavor, they also gave me a free jasmine milk tea for checkin in which was nice and really good in flavor.

Really tasty food, had gone back 3x in the past month to try other items on menu. I wouldn't recommend their imperial rolls. Not worth it for 2 tiny pieces of egg rolls. The salad with chicken is probably my favorite item on menu. The tapioca drinks were really delicious too, which was surprising.

We've been to Mr East Kitchen frequently in the past year (dine-in prior to covid and takeout during covid). Their food is always well-made with generous portions and reasonable prices, in particular their Banh Mi sandwich, pho, garlic noodles, crispy chicken rice have been absolutely delicious! The staff are fantastic and super friendly.
5 stars! Incredibly clean and great procedures during COVID. Friendly and professional staff. Really tasty food at a reasonable price!
Came here to try the steak pho. It had 0 flavor, probably the worst pho we ever had. Still would come back for the brunch but very disappointed
Had the garlic noodles and Thai tea french toast. Might be the best brunch in SF. Definitely going back

We love coming to eat at Mr. East Kitchen, the ambiance is so nice and calm, just the right thing in a busy city. The food is amazing and always comes out super quick, it is not too pricey for this area of town and the portions are big. The staff is always nice and welcoming. I haven't tried their breakfast yet but heard its super good. One thing I absolutely love is that they have a vegetarian option for all of their menu. Its still really hard to find veggie pho or bun me in SF so having this place accommodate vegetarians and vegans is really great.

My friends and I came here for dinner after going to the convention. We enjoyed very much the vegetarian pho, coconut prawns and again the sandwich. Great simple and fresh flavors! Fast and quick nice service. My boys who are pretty picky with their boba teas enjoyed it very much.

We came here after shopping at the Westfield shopping center to grab a quick bite to eat before heading to the movie. We spotted this place on the way to Westfield. It's about 2 blocks down from Westfield. I'm so glad we came here rather than eating at Westfield food court. The food was delicious and fresh. The staff were very nice and the service was quick. The atmosphere was clean, fresh and modern. The Vietnamese sandwich had a little twist from the traditional banh mi. It was served on a nice ciabatta, crunchy and soft at the same time. The flavor was wonderful, the egg spread was very nice. The mixed kale salad that came with the sandwich was nice. The tea was fragrant and flavorful. I will definitely return again.
It's my third time coming here, I enjoyed their food very much. The atmosphere is great and awesome service. The curry is very tasty, spicy and flavorful.
I keep going back to try different things, everything has been great. I don't eat meat and there are several vegetarian options, and they've been very kind and accommodating.
Mr East Kitchen is a hidden gem in SoMa for modern Asian cuisine. Their garlic noodles and stirred fried eggplant are my go-to dishes. Good food and friendly staff.

This place is great, from their food to service. The food was amazing and had a perfect balance of everything you would want in asian food. To match the quality of the meal, even during covid their takeout service was above par. Would definitely recommend and come again.

Today 10.4.2018

I am editing this review, I do apologize for any outburst I had on 10.1.2018. I did accept the apology of this establishment and they did take care of me. Now I will be going back to this place on a regular and many thanks again.
This is my favorite restaurant to go to in Soma! The service is great and the staff are always friendly. I really like the garlic noodle and drunken noodles, it's so tasty!

This might be controversial, but I like the bubble tea more than Boba Guys or Sharetea or iTea. I got the oatmilk earl grey boba with regular sweetness and it was divine

The owners/employees are also super friendly, and one of them came over to specifically ask me how to pronounce my name. That's something that has never happened to me before at any establishment

Not very impressed by the fresh rolls or jasmine milk tea. Rolls were almost all lettuce and noodles with only one shrimp per roll and a strong mint taste. Hopeful that some other items on the menu would be better. Service and ambiance was good.

Order food online and the left me very disappointed. So never had any issue with ordering online before but guess the driver got confused and made the experience worst. I do food delivery also in the past so i can give u a chance if u mess up but jf you going to mess up then at least give me a call and not senting me a message saying the food in front of my porch or lobby area when it wasnt. It was a driver from the restaurant also didnt say anything to me or even apologize. The food was so soggy when i got it. I was like really. Wont ever go back to them or give them another try. Their customer serve sucks. Waste about 80 dollars on food that look like a kid throwing food on the food. Asked food to be spicy wasnt even spicy. They failed me and i dont like giving bad rating but this is some place i wont go to ever.
Wow so you only apologize after getting a review and stuff not before. I worked at restaurant before and let my customers know where i was at and if there was any delay. Cause getting tips and business what made me push myself hard but you want me to tell you how i order the food when your staff didnt even apologize to me. It was one if ur own staff at the restaurant. This is an example of an restaurant trying to save face and not lose customers. So you want me to just be like oh 80 dollars is nothing right. I thought i try some good food but u left me with food that was soggy and unbearable. So how should i respond to you. Then be happy that everything okay with an computer answer.

My boyfriend and I wandered into this place and it's delicious! I had the Mr. East, a breakfast banh mi -like sandwich with a runny egg and thick sriracha bacon and came with a refreshing kale salad. The coffee was also quite good. Good for a casual bite.

I was waiting at the door while the place was supposedly open and three employees repeatedly saw me standing there knocking for ten minutes without coming out to tell me or putting up a sign that the place wasn't opening up until late due to a cash register problem. You guys gotta let customers know what's going on and not ignore them.
I had the garlic noodles and bahn mi here, both with chicken. Their chicken is very good, but the highlight are their fries; so crispy! Service is good and food is prepared quickly.

My friend and I were visiting San Francisco for the day and decided to stop by after skimming a few Yelp reviews and looking at the pictures other reviewers had left. I was very intrigued by the Thai Tea French Toast ($11), so that's what I ended up ordering!! I made the meal a combo by adding two eggs and a side of sriracha bacon ($4, not pictured). The french toast was SO good!! I highly recommend. It was very sweet, but the side of fruit help offset that. The eggs were perfectly cooked and the bacon was alright (not my favorite but I still ate it). It was a lot of food and definitely filled me up until dinner time. I also ordered a matcha milk tea with oat milk (+$1) and pearls. It was very yummy! The place itself is a very Instagram friendly place. I feel like a lot of restaurants in the U.S. don't pay much attention to interior design, but this place does and I really appreciate that!! With that being said, I would definitely come here again!
Nice clean and delicious. It's going to be new place for hanging out. Boba is tasty. Must try garlic noodle with pamesan cheese. Everything is so good.
I've gone a few times and everything ive ordered has been great. The boba tea is super good. Everything tastes clean and healthy. Would recommend.
Garlic noodles were great. Chicken was tender. Service was great. Boba was yummy. And yelp keeps saying this review isnt long enough so i need to fill it up with more words

Chicken garlic noodles are great! Fresh boba and goes great with the noodles. I also had the banh mi pork sandwich which came with a delicious salad and had a sauce/butter on it. Today my boyfriend ordered the pho and really enjoyed it too! Highly recommend. The store is very well decorated and the vibes are great. I'm lucky to live in the apartment building connected to it for a quick food run :)
I couldn't wait until we were finished eating to leave a review! Incredibly quick service and amazing food. Highly recommend the steak pho and garlic noodles. Delicious!!!
Food is crap, prices are pretty high for what you get. Id suggest going to Tin or another Vietnamese joint close by.

I come here a lot because it's close to my work and I like boba teas and egg sandwiches! The garlic noodles are good, and so are the fresh rolls. Nice spot to sit and drink a beer with lunch. Sometimes it gets crowded on weekends. Since I have been coming here I have noticed small improvements and upgrades and the staff works hard and is attentive and efficient.

Food is great but customer service poor. Ordered a curry as they closed. Realized I did not received the curry dish when I got home. Returned next day to explain the situation and that I was not able to bring it back as they were closed. Server did not want to do anything about their wrong, because I did not bring the food back the next day. She was rude and did not apologize. Eventually agreed to make me the correct order again free of charge as compensation. Poor customer service experience.
Lychee Jasmine Tea and Garlic Fries is a must try. The wings are also good, asked for a side of spicy mayo for the wings..

I came here around night time wanting to try the thai toast which they actually don't serve at night :( I tried the beef pho and milk tea. Milk tea was pretty good, good tea flavor and milk blend (3.5 rating) Beef pho was alright (3 rating) Broth was not like authentic Vietnamese taste which could be stronger in flavor. I love their sriracha hot wings and garlic fries (both 3 rating). Place was very clean and good customer service (5 rating). Overall, I definitely wouldn't mind coming back and try other food on the menu.
Good food! But, no more breakfast during the weekThe prices can be lower but it's SF, so it's expected.

Very simple and delicious food. I really like the ban me sandwiches. I brought a lot of my friends come here. All of them like the food in here. I also like the boba tea in here. But one time I order the boba tea without ice. It only come up with half cup. I hope there will be a choice to fill the full cup even it will cost some money.
the garlic noodles are phenomenal. really sweet workers, amazing customer service, and the restaurant itself is super cute. 10/10 would recommend.

I went her for the first time and was pleased more so than I expected to be. What I expected was a trendy breakfast spot full of influencers jockeying for status. What I found instead was a down to earth breakfast spot with great service.
My family and I got the Nova Omelette which had salmon on top. It was delicious but I wish it was inside with cream cheese, the chicken and waffles and the crispy chicken sandwich. My favorite of the bunch was the chickens and waffles. The pieces were nice and crispy with the perfect amount of seasoning and the waffles were soft and buttery. It was the perfect accompaniment to the savory component to the dish. The chicken sandwich was amazing and would be perfect for lunch.
I am happy that I have a new brunch spot, I love in my rotation to keep things fun.

This is my second visit to four chairs. We got there at around 11:30am and it was packed. We put our names on the yelp waitlist inside. We checked to see if we can do it through the yelp app and it was not available. The wait wasnt too bad for 2 people. It was about a 20 min wait. Inside was really loud with music and people talking. We ordered a k-bomb chicken Benny and a loco plato. They were okay and nothing too special. The portions were big. Service was good. They came to refill the house coffee a few times.

We were a bit disappointed since the first time we came, it was really good. We got a salmon benedict and chicken and waffles that time so maybe that's why. Overall, it's 3.5/5 but I wouldn't wait more than 20 minutes, and will have to explore other brunch options.

Yup yup yup! Finally made it to this place and the food was worth the wait! I started with the volcano coffee, which is coffee and your choice of whole milk, almond milk (extra), or oat milk (extra). The coffee at the top was thick, not quite like a milk shake, but stuck to the spoon. It was not too sweet, but like an iced latte. Then I tried the crème brûlée French toast and the K Bomb Benny. Both amazing! The French toast sauce tasted just like crème brûlée. This was just the right amount of sweetness. The sauce was similar in consistency to an evaporated milk. The hard sugar shell topper was also a nice bonus.

The K-Bomb Benny was really tasty. The chicken had a kick. It was crispy and tasted like a buffalo sauce. The eggs were nicely poached. The hollandaise was a little too tangy for my liking. The potatoes were crispy as well, but needed some seasoning.

The place was very cute. There was a good amount of space between tables. I had no wait at 1:45 in the afternoon. The service itself felt very rushed. Maybe because they were closing in 45 minutes, but I did get the hurry up vibe.

All in all I really enjoyed the coffee and food. Nice portion sizes. You won't leave hungry that's for sure.

It was very hard to find where to get in line (on a kiosk) because everybody was blocking it. We ended up getting a time of 35-45 min. When my partner looked at it later, it changed to an hour and 10 min. Very weird haha. They sat us down near next the bar where they prepare drinks. Servers kept bumping into me and tangling my hair, it was very uncomfortable. The food was pretty good but the drinks came late, I'm guessing they forgot about them. They were delicious though, the blood Mary was a little sweet but overall very good. My partner loved his mocha and his chicken. The tomyum Benedict that I got was pretty good. The salad was delicious, the potatoes were very good, and I loved the Benedict sauce. Overall 3.8/5. It was a little hectic inside and crazy so we probably won't be coming back but it was a nice experience still.

This is my second time here and for some reason, the first time that I came, I felt like the food wasn't that amazing. I probably came when it was super packed and the overall experience wasn't too enjoyable for me.

Came back two years later and gave it a second chance because my friend really wanted to try this place and the food surprisingly wasn't too bad! Both times though, I felt like the drinks tasted better than their food. I took a sip of everyone's drinks and none of their drinks disappointed me!

Overall, this is a great place for brunch and the service was excellent!

Get here when they open and get seated immediately :)
Worth the hype! The food is as tasty as it looks. Drinks were fire. Pancakes were our favorite but I'm glad we shared and both got savory egg plates. Don't think you can go wrong.
They're fast and efficient, even as the restaurant filled up.

Four Chairs is one of the new-wave Korean brunch spots in the Bay, in the same lane as Berkeley Social Club, You Deserve Good Things, Breakfast Story, and Giwa. It's super Instagrammable and has a laid-back vibe that sits somewhere in the middle: not as extra as Giwa, but a little more put-together than Berkeley Social Club. Space is tiny and not dog friendly, so join the waitlist early and be ready to hunt for parking on nearby residential streets. Once you're seated, service is consistently sweet and attentive.

Food-wise, my favorite is the fried chicken and waffles -- super delicious and very, very filling. If you want something lighter, the two eggs with toast and potatoes is simple but cooked perfectly, even if the portion feels small for the price. My sister usually goes for the eggs Benedict and likes it. I also always get the strawberry matcha: strawberry syrup on the bottom, matcha on top, super cute and always tasty. Overall, it's a vibe-y spot for Korean-influenced brunch if you don't mind the wait and tighter seating.

After going to Poppy + Rose in LA, I've been on a brunch streak! I decided to check out Four Chairs because the chicken and waffle caught my eye and it did not disappoint.

Putting an Asian twist on brunch with Korean flavors (such as sauces on traditional American brunch), Four Chairs is a BRIGHT , spacious, and cozy decor with wooden aesthetics and an overall perfect place to catch up with folks!

Although the waitlist closed and we got there at 2:30pm, the lady serving us was so sweet and allowed us to sit inside as long as we ordered immediately. I got a strawberry matcha latte (MIX THOROUGHLY else you'll get a mouthful of strawberry), the chicken and waffles (the waffles ARE DIVINE-- soft and they soak up so much flavor / the breading on the chicken wasn't evenly distributed and too thick in my opinion but it was good otherwise) and the egg Benedict for my sister (the eggs themselves were delicious and were perfect with the English muffin-- but sogs up quickly so eat fast, and the avocado absorbed a lot of lemon juice so it was on the tart side). I also ordered two eggs on the side-- overhard, my least favorite part but still good-- get the eggs runny. Also got the okonomiyaki fries to go which was great several hours later. All this food came out to be $70 including tip which is super affordable in this day and age!

Will be coming back whenever I get the chance! Located in a cute neighborhood too with decent walking sights.

The food here was fair, it wasn't something that amazed me too much but I will say it's pretty filling. I wish I tried something different but it's okay! Next time I come back I will make another review.

Service was great! I will say they are the sweetest people ever! The only thing is that there was a bit of a wait but that's normal at popular brunch spots.

The inside of the place had many tables but I will say the tables were pretty close together to other tables. Other than that, it's a pretty cute place, I'll probably get something different next time!

Four Chairs has been my favorite brunch spot in the city for years. The ambiance is very casual and comfortable, with a modern design that still feels warm and well decorated. You can tell it has a lot of regulars. Some of the seating is a little worn at this point, but it honestly adds to the lived in charm.

Service has always been great. The staff is friendly, efficient, and welcoming every time. I usually come before 10:30 am because it gets extremely busy afterward and lines start forming quickly. Joining the wait list is easy thanks to the tablet kiosk at the front. Metered street parking is available, though it can be pretty competitive on weekends.

I almost always order the same thing: the Southwest Scramble with a side of sourdough toast. For a long time, this dish was very consistent and one of my absolute favorites. Recently, though, the flavor has not been quite the same, they don't add cilantro or the microgreens anymore. I am not sure what changed, but I am hoping it is temporary because it used to really stand out.

That said, their house potatoes are still some of the best around. Always crispy on the outside and perfectly cooked inside. Lately, my new favorite addition has been the iced matcha strawberry drink. I usually ask for it in a to go cup so I can finish it at home, and it never disappoints.

Overall, Four Chairs is still a solid brunch spot with great service, a cozy vibe, and reliable comfort food. Even with a few small changes, it remains a place I keep coming back to and would absolutely recommend.

Four Chairs was such a great spot for brunch. The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming, making it perfect for a relaxed weekday meal. The food was flavorful and well plated, with generous portions that definitely hit the spot.

The service was friendly and attentive without feeling rushed. We only waited about 10 minutes to be seated on a weekday, which made it an easy and stress-free brunch stop. It's the kind of place you can easily linger at while catching up with friends over good food and drinks. Overall, Four Chairs is a solid brunch spot that I'd definitely come back to and recommend.

This place is lively and busy at all times. The portions are large and there is a big selection of items. Many items are egg based or chicken based. Good Korean fusion choices and some unique flavors.
Their drinks are delicious and look good too.
Now because it gets busy, it's sometimes hard to get the staff's attention.

Regardless, it's a good spot and one of the more unique brunch options in the city.

The locations of the restaurant is on Mission St, which is very busy. We got to the restaurant about 10:30 AM on a Sunday. There is only street parking and not a lot so it took a bit to find a spot. The front of the restaurant does not catch your attention when driving by.

Maybe we lucked out but there was no wait to get seated. About 11 AM the restaurant filled, but they were quick to seat so no real line outside.

Once inside, the nice clean contemporary decor was very inviting and the staff friendly & attentive. It did not take long for the food to be served.

We ordered drinks, the Volcano Coffee & the Mango/Green tea Latte. Truth we ordered the drinks because of the way they looked in pictures. Unfortunately they were more pretty than flavorful.

Food we ordered the K-Bomb Benny that had poach eggs on a ciabatta bread with Chipotle Hollandaise sauce & the K-Bomb
chicken sandwich. The chicken was definitely the star of the dishes. The chicken was moist & crunchy and the sauce was so well balanced in taste that complimented the chicken. I only wished it was a little spicy. Even the chipotle hollandaise was not spicy, but we ended up eating the whole dish.

We ordered the Creme Brûlée French Toast, which was beautiful, but it was nothing special.

I would come back for the chicken and to try other dishes to see if they are as good as the chicken.

FYI....The meter police were sitting outside, so make sure you find a valid parking space.

Flavor (5/5): Tried their korean fried chicken Benedict and it was super yummy! It's a saucey fried chicken that went well with the potatoes, toast and eggs. Very flavorful!

Instagram Worthy (4/5): Cute restaurant and great presentation on the food.

Service (4/5): Very prompt on ordering and food came out pretty quick despite it being pretty busy for brunch. All the servers were dressed up for Halloween, loved the spirit!

Takeaways: Solid brunch spot in SF. Any party above 7 might be difficult to hear each other across the table as the restaurant is pretty loud. SF parking can be tricky for this place, some free parking spots 5-7 mins walk away but lots of unhoused people along the way.

Perhaps this is an unpopular opinion, but I found this place to be overhyped. It flooded my Instagram feed when it first opened, and I'll admit I was influenced. In reality, the food is no better than any other standard brunch spot, and much of it tasted pretty generic.

I arrived just before noon on a Saturday and was seated immediately for a party of two, which was a nice surprise. However, the Korean Chicken Benny tasted more like it was covered in Mae Ploy sweet chili sauce than anything resembling gochujang. The lychee butterfly pea drink reminded me of Lychee Calpico or canned Chinese lychee drinks.

Aesthetically, everything is beautiful, but the food itself was mid. The only dish I genuinely enjoyed was the Crème Brûlée French Toast but not enough to return for it alone. There are plenty of better brunch options in the city, and that's just my honest opinion.

My family and I were in town for Thanksgiving weekend and finally got to try Four Chairs after having it saved on my list for a while and it did not disappoint! Even without a reservation, we were seated quickly, which was a great start.

We ordered their Volcano Coffee, which instantly reminded me of the Dalgona coffee we used to make: creamy, foamy, and such a fun throwback. I went with the By The Bay Benedict, and it was delicious. The shrimp were perfectly succulent, the potatoes were crispy and flavorful, and the hollandaise sauce tied everything togethe. Even the side salad was refreshing.

My partner ordered the Crème Brûlée French Toast: rich, sweet, and delicious. My mom had the Nova Omelet, and the smoked salmon was fresh and full of flavor.

Service was friendly and quick throughout our meal. The only thing to note is that parking can be a bit tough, but it's worth the effort.

We'll definitely be coming back the next time we're in town!

The pancakes were beautiful and fluffy. It was very creamy and sweet. The Korean fried chicken was slightly crispy and quite salty. I loved the runny eggs. The matcha latte had a jasmine scent.

We (party of 4) waited for an hour for a Wednesday brunch. However, food was served quickly after ordering.

The servers were very friendly and efficient. The food is delicious with unique flavors that are Asian fusion with Tom Yum sauce on eggs Benedict! Go early if you don't want to wait for long to be seated.

My first time here and I just could not get over how I had not been here before! Amazing staff, food, and interior decor overall. Convenient location in the city, although parking could be challenging outside depending on what day/time you go. We met up for brunch and everything on the menu looked mouthwatering. They have a QR code menu and all of their dishes come with a nice visual image of what you shall expect. We ended up getting a few things, but my favorite item on their menu would have to be the mascarpone pancakes! Everything about them was beyond delicious! From the fresh fruit, to the mascarpone creme, to the fluffy pancakes, to the syrup. It all just tied together very nicely. We were also able to share one order of pancakes amongst the three of us, while ordering our own entrees. Everything was very filling and satisfying.
Would definitely return here again on another occasion. Apparently, they don't take reservations and I heard during their peak hours, their line is out the door. I think our party got lucky because of the rainy weather. They also don't seat you unless everyone in your party is present. Just something to consider if you plan on going :)

Finally getting around to writing my review. Unfortunately, I don't remember much other than the food being pretty yummy, and we had no trouble getting a table since we made reservations. The place quickly filled up, and I do remember it being a bit warm inside. Overall, it's a place I'd go back to again.

Stop what you're doing, and add this place
to your must eats list!

Four Chairs was on my top 3 best during our trip to San Francisco. After seeing all the rave on social media & insta worthy meals, I just knew I had to check it out for myself.

We were told there was a 10-15 minute wait, but got seated after just a couple minutes. We were immediately greeted and given water upon seating.

Menu is available via QR code and there lots of fun options! All of the drinks are photo worthy creations where you can choose from a variety of matchas, lemonades, booze & more.

I opted for the butterfly lychee and not only was it so freaking pretty, it tasted SO GOOD.
Incredibly refreshing and the right amount of sweet & tarte. The drink is adorned with a mint leaf & of course lychee.

Our food came out rather quickly and all at the same time!! Everything looked amazing- important as the eyes always eat first.
We ordered 2 kids pancake meals, cheeseburger, traditional breakfast & eggs & Kbomb Benny.

Everything was delicious. The kids plates were
So adorably plated & the pancakes were nice & fluffy! The cheeseburger portion was HUGE & flavorful. Love that they add a delicious spread to the burger itself.

The k bomb Benny was UHHMAZING. This dish comes with a salad, potatoes and eggs Benedict's atop a ciabatta bread. The chicken was juicy, tender, crisp and loaded with flavor.

Everything about our meals, drinks & service was excellent. Definitely must try if you're in the area & we would totally go out of our way again to eat here!!

Oh my! Oh my! So yummy! Perfect spot for breakfast and brunch. Menu is not extensive but has plenty of options you can't go wrong. We had a sweet tooth so we tried their crème brûlée French toast and their mascarpone pancakes. Both were DELISH and not too sweet at all! Paired it with their iced tea volcano coffee. The place inside is neat with a cute atmosphere. Service was excellent. I'll get their savory menu next time.

Love these types of over-the-top fancy brunch places. After a medical appointment nearby on a random Wednesday, decided to go into diabeetus overload with some sweet brunch treats. Sugar overload, but totally worth it!

Crème Brûlée French Toast: This was too luxurious looking to pass up! Very photogenic, it came out covered in a sweet cream with a nice brûléed bit on top. The two toasts were soaked nicely with batter and cooked up custardy. Though the crusts could have benefited from a longer soak, since they seemed a tad dry. The cream was also custard-like in flavor, much more indulgent than maple syrup. The brûlée on top was crunchy and tasty, but unfortunately there wasn't much. Might have been better if they placed the toast side-by-side, to get more surface area crispy.

Mocha Lava: Another photogenic item. The top was this creamy whipped slightly bitter coffee foam. Underneath was a bunch of super sweet and yummy chocolate milk. Mixed together, it was a delicious mocha drink that is way better than anything from Starbucks.

Super quick and nice service. The fries were really tasty, had a lot of umami toppings, and was a big serving. I've never really had fries with kewpie and bonito.

The benny was cooked awesome and the sauce on the chicken was a perfect blend of sweet and heat. The hollandaise was creamy and egg was perfectly runny.

The mascarpone pancake shocked me the most because it had such a light texture. Paired with the fruit and syrup made an overall great brunch

Ambiance:
Modern industrial vibe--stylish, clean, and welcoming.

Service:
Great service overall. Joining the waitlist was super easy, and we only waited about 15 minutes before being seated.

Drinks:
Strawberry & Mango Lemonade -- sweet, fruity, and refreshing. A must-try

Food:
Absolutely delicious!
* French Toast Crème Brûlée (10/10):
Sweet, savory, moist, and served hot with so much crème. Every bite was rich and indulgent--really, really good.
* K-Bomb Chicken Benny:
The chicken was incredibly flavorful, eggs were poached to perfection, and the potatoes were crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.
* Fried Chicken & Waffle:
The fried chicken was perfectly crispy, the waffle soft on the inside and nicely toasted on the outside. The hot chili sauce tied everything together with the perfect balance of heat and flavor.

Overall:
A fantastic brunch spot with great food, drinks, and atmosphere. Definitely worth the visit!

Came here on a Saturday at 10:30 for a party of 2 and we were seated right away. But just be aware the later it gets the line and wait gets longer.

We ordered the Chicken and waffle and this did not dissappoint. The chicken was crispy and very tasty. They serve it with sometype of hot honey and it so good. My husband tried Kbomb chicken benny,the chicken was good and tasty but something about the slaw we were not a fan of. We also got a side order of the mascarpone pancake it was delicious!! Of course I had to try the volcano coffee and it was amazing!!

Def will return with the family

Pick up what I'm putting down- this is my second time going to Four Chairs for brunch because I enjoyed it that much, and wanted to give it a proper second try before I left a review (in case it was a fluke). Fortunately, it wasn't! I love a good brunch spot, especially when it comes with an extensive drink menu. We were lucky to snag a table right away, as this place is generally packed. Seats are pretty cramped, but I'm sure it helps to get the brunch rush moving quicker! Now onto the food:

Mascarpone Pancake 4/5 I adored this presentation, love the layers, colors and how they used the mascarpone to keep the fruit in place at the top. Such a fun-to-look-at, delicious dish!

Pacific Bay 3.5/5 Supposedly the hollandaise is Tom Yum, but we didn't taste any of that iconic sourness. Could've had more salmon, buy maybe i'm being greedy hehe.

Matcha Mango: 3/5 wouldn't order this again, the mango was more tart than sweet and the matcha wasn't my favorite.

Butterfly Lychee: 4/5 I'm a big lychee fan so I make sure to order this drink when I see it. If I could get it less sweet, that'd be an automatic 5 out of 5.

Overall, another enjoyable experience! I wouldn't hesitate to come back and try some other items.

Definitely one of my favorite brunch spots I've tried recently! Really fun and tasty fusion dishes, my favorite being the popular K-bomb chicken benny. The chicken is glazed with a signature sweet and savory korean fried chicken style sauce, and it was really juicy! Also really enjoyed the lightly savory and refreshing nova omelette. The house potaotes were great here too. Drinks weren't my favorite, but I did like the butterfly lychee (however it tasted mostly like calpico). Would skip on the overly sweet mango matcha and mango tango. Okonomiyaki fries weren't bad but a bit too crispy for my taste.

Service was nice and attentive despite it being really busy on a sunday. Parking seems really difficult and dangerous, but my friends and I took the bart here. Place itself is average sized but tables are super close together, so it's cozy but cramped when busy!

Solid brunch spot between Bernal Heights / Mission. Came with a group of 6 friends and the wait was pretty bad on a weekend around 11:30/noon -- over an hour long. We ordered a mix of sweet and savory dishes, and I enjoyed everything I tried. A lot of the dishes remind me of Kitchen Story.

The french toast was probably the standout to me (surpusing since I'm not usually big on french toast). The creme brulee glaze on top was yummy and the sauce and poofy toast was excellent.

I probably wouldn't wait in line here again since you can get the same stuff at other brunch spots in SF but glad I came!

Came to this place on a Friday lunch. There was no wait but we were still surprised that the place was quite packed. We loved the fusion brunch dishes. My fav was the tom yum Benedict! The drinks were also really good! We will be back soon

So my cousin brought me here for my birthday. From the street it didn't look like much, except for the crowd of people standing around outside on a Sunday morning. Yes, you will wait for a table. It only took about 25 minutes. Knowing what I know now, I would wait an hour. Got to see some nice old school cars cruising up and down Mission while we waited.

Our server was so sweet and had excellent timing. He always had a smile on his face. Loved that!

We started with the Velvet Whipped Coffee and the Lava Mocha Coffee. I could just stop here. I think about these drinks everyday. If I didn't live in the East Bay...I would have one of these everyday. I would just rotate between the 2...each day. How have I never had one of these whipped coffees before? Apparently I missed the craze during lockdown. That's fine, cause I'm caught up now. If you haven't had a whipped coffee and you love coffee...go get it!

I had the K Bomb Chicken Benny. Perfectly poached egg. The chicken is crispy, saucy and yummy. When I got a fork full of chicken, egg, a little bread and cabbage and smeared it in yolk and spicy sweet sauce...my eyes rolled back in my head. Think I'm joking? Ask my cousin.

She had the K Bomb Chicken Sandwich with those fries! So good! I've never had those style fries before. They're great.

We shared the Creme Brulee French Toast. It was fantastic! We were so full and we couldn't finish everything, so we got boxes to go.

The restaurant has a nice contemporary look, airy with plants. Its a little noisy but not bad. It can get warm in there so try to sit near the window.

Loved every bite! Will be taking my daughter there for the coffee!

Thank you cousin!

My friend and I met here for brunch over LDW. It'd been on both of our lists of places to check out. My friend arrived right at 10am right as they opened and got us a table, which was fortunate, as the place quickly filled up with patrons. She was already seated when I entered at 10:01am, and it took me a couple minutes to get past a group that was lined up waiting for a table because of how narrow the hallway was. I really didn't like the layout set-up.

We each got an egg benedict dish. I ordered mine on a whim as the waitress came to take our order. Originally, I planned to order a scramble, but she recommended a benedict instead. I thought the food was just okay. The one I ordered, which she recommended, came with toast rather than an English muffin, which I wasn't a fan of. Overall not bad, but also not that impressed.

I was looking forward to coming here for brunch after reading all the positive reviews.

I made a reservation on Yelp for party of four Thursday at 10:30am.

Hubby & I arrived before our friends, and were able to be seated at a table for four in the back.

The menu can be QR'd. My phone couldn't pull up the menu so I got a hard copy.

Drinks:
* hubby got the soju Bloody Mary. If you want a bacon strip it's an extra $3. He passed. He thought the drink was too sweet.
* mango matcha for me - I said easy on the ice but still plenty of ice. I requested oatmilk. Extra $1. My drink was very eye pleasing as many of the drinks are. You've got to be a matcha fan to enjoy this drink. The ice helped to diffuse the matcha.

Ordered -
* hubby got the chicken and waffles. The waffle was great. Was perfectly made. He thought chicken lacked flavor and a little overcooked. Came with a dipping sauce.
* I got the k-bomb chicken benny. At first glance it looked so delicious. But the benny was very lukewarm as was the roasted potatoes. The kfc was a chicken breast coated but the coating fell off. So unless you made an effort to put the topping back on, the chicken itself was very bland.

Our friends ordered the leafy green benny and Mascarpone pancakes.

The food looked more delicious than it ended up tasting.

Total time 90 minutes.

When we left there were at least a dozen people waiting for a table. A few folks had carryon luggage. Just arrived in the City or planning to leave?

I don't think I'll be back.

Parking was also challenging.

Came to Four Chairs in a group of 4 around 10:30am on a Sunday, and put our name on the waitlist at the front. The estimated wait was about an hour, so we took a short walk up to Bernal Heights, which was the perfect activity while we waited for our table. We got a text and checked in and seated were immediately. It's quite busy and crowded - as expected for a Sunday brunch in SF.

We got the mascarpone pancakes, creme brulee french toast, shrimp benedict, and a scramble. Everything was surprisingly good - not too heavy or overwhelming, and portion sizes were quite large. We did wish that the benedict had more of the Tom Yum hollandaise suace, as it did get a little dry, but the sweet items were all excellent.

I'd definitely come back again to four chairs - its a great brunch option :)

This is a great brunch place to come to for catching up with friends. It's busy, but the wait isn't too bad (around 30 min on a weekend around noon). The atmosphere is cozy and the restaurant is surprisingly spacious.

My friend and I ordered the K-bomb chicken benny and the crème brûlée french toast to share. They were both tasty in their own ways. The chicken was juicy and had good flavor and the toast was so fluffy. I do think the toast is a bit much if that's all you're eating, so it was nice to get a balance of sweet and savory between the two dishes we ordered.

I definitely want to try some of the drinks the next time I'm here.

After doing a little Yelp searching, I came across Four Chairs and let me tell you... the pics had me drooling all week! I was literally counting down the days.

First tip...give yourself extra time for parking and wait time. I got lucky and found a spot right across the street and the wait was only about 30 minutes. The only tiny downside, it was an extremely humid day in the city, which caught me by surprise, well it was very muggy inside. They had a little fan behind us trying its best, but it needed backup!

Now on to the good stuff...the food! I already had my heart set on trying something new, so I stepped outside my usual and ordered the K-Bomb Benny and when I tell you they KNOCKED IT OUT THE PARK... they knocked it out the park! I am not an Eggs Benedict girl but Four Chairs converted me. Perfectly poached eggs, soft bread (I didn't even need a knife), and that Korean chicken? OMG...flavorful, absolutely unreal. Even the side salad was amazing.
My daughter ordered the Crème Brûlée French Toast with a side of eggs and said it was a 10/10!
We also ordered Oatmilk Mango Matchas and let me just say... I was speechless.

Bottom line...I'm obsessed. Four Chairs is officially on my must return list. If you haven't been, for sure go.

Line was super long on a weekend for brunch but went by pretty accurately to the estimated wait time which was 30 minutes. Walked into neighboring cafes to pass the time. We got the cream brûlée French toast which was amazing. Creamy with the inne bread being very soft and fluffy. The edges were a bit hard and dry but still yummy. We got the Benedict as well which was pretty average. Overall cute spot and will be coming back to try more of the sweets on their menu.

Food: 7.9/10
Service: 8/10 (busy)
Ambience: 8/10

I was really looking forward to this place after seeing it alot on social media. But the food was not good. We tried the korean and pacific benedict but it was not good. The chicken on the korean benedic was good but the rest was not so much. The drinks were good. We got the matcha latte and it was really good.

Solid pancakes, loved the mascarpone layering. Salmon omelette was pretty good, though it had more cheese mixed in than ideal. The interiors are nice, but almost completely artificially lit, some sunlight wouldn't hurt.

Funny outdoor look, the sign makes it look like this is a decrepit spot for bail bonds. Maybe on purpose?

I came to take my mom for breakfast here and it was a cute breakfast spot. I got the by the bay plate and it so good, the shrimp was delicious. I also came right when they opened so service was very quick. I recommend the whipped coffee SO GOOD.

My first time at Four Chairs. The ambiance was nice, and the restaurant was full. We were seated by the window. I loved the almost floor to ceiling windows. The service was wonderful; fast, friendly and welcoming. On each table, there was a carafe pitcher of water and a pair of small drinking glasses sitting in a cute basket. That was thoughtful.

We ordered the Marscapone pancakes to share , Chicken & Waffles and the Portobello Burger. The food looked great, but it was lacking flavor. The pancakes didn't have any sweetness to it. The chicken was crispy, the drumsticks were huge, but the meat was not seasoned. My daughter's portobello burger was "okay".

All in all, I liked the vibe and the service was great. I may give it another try.

First and only time at Four Chairs. I was recommended this brunch spot by my good friend who has grown up in San Francisco. I arrived around noon and had a hard time finding parking near the spot. Walking into the place, it was very clean and modern but despite having many tables open, there was no host system or someone to guide me to a table. I ended up waiting around 20 minutes just for a server to show me to a table.

The menu itself is very elaborate with many different sweet and savory options. My friend ordered the K-Bomb Chicken sandwich which turned out to be drenched in an overly sweet sauce. The sandwich felt heavy due to the overarching sweetness. I ordered the Mascarpone Pancake 16 Stack of Three Served with Banana Berries Whipped Mascarpone and Maple Syrup. The pancakes had the fluffy soufflé technique and while tasted good didn't feel all too special. This shop seems to be more focused on being instagramable than food focused.
One of the best brunch places I've been to. We all loved our food. Friendly and attentive service. Would love to come back when in the area.

My coworkers and I recently went to four chairs for a breakfast. The main course of Korean fried chicken was delicious and fully of taste. It was filling but the pancakes very much sealed the deal for me, the best pancakes I've had in SF. I've had the other popular breakfast/brunch spots but four chairs should be in that conversation as well.

The crowd was chill, the vibe is very much about the food. The staff were helpful and attentive.

I came here with a couple of friends on a Saturday for brunch. Our group of 4 had to wait around 45 minutes in order to be seated after joining the waitlist.
I ordered a chicken and waffle and the food came out around 10 minutes later. The check was crispy on the outside while still being very moist in the inside. It definitely tasted good with the sweet chili sauce in the side. The waffles were light, crispy, and tasted very good with the butter and maple syrup. This was probably one of my favorite waffles due to the texture as it stayed crispy throughout the entire meal.
Overall, it was a wonderful place to get brunch if you don't mind the wait.

Amazing brunch place! We went on a Saturday afternoon and there was a 25mins wait for a table of 6. The inside is cute and was fully decorated for fall. The place is kept clean.
They have interesting drinks menu from Pima coco mimosa to mango matcha late. My friend got the choco milk and said it was too sweet. The Bloody Mary was a sight and tasted pretty good.
For dishes i got the chipotle Benny, the English muffin wasn't the traditional one, it was thick but I dint mind, my friends did. I just wish it had more hollandaise sauce. Overall still pretty good, unique flavors that you know would come together. My wife got the k bomb chicken benny and honestly it was the best dish. The chicken was juicy, crispy, the sauce on it was insane. I would get that if I were to go again. My friends got the pacific sunrise and lively omelette. Both dishes were relatively healthy and tasted great. I feel like it's one of those places that you can't go wrong. Highly recommend!

Amazing food! Absolutely loved my iced coffee and the fried chicken is to die for. This restaurant quite cozy and worth the wait if there is one. Service was nice and quick. Just make sure that you add yourself to the waitlist on the ipad through yelp

Their food is amazing they give you so much food that you can't even eat it all from beautiful made plates that comes from the heart making it from the heart from love you could tell from the way they serve you the hospitality is top 10 I highly recommend this place to go because it's amazing not only do they serve you they put the tender loving care into their food by the way they serve you the way it looks before you eat it it's so amazing that I'm very impressed we should all try their food because I don't think none of us will regret it they have so much different kind of food to pick out of from breakfast to brunch the breakfast and brunch meal is top 10 because they give you so much that you know you're not coming out of that restaurant without being full they give you so much portion and they make it out of love and the way they serve you the plate looks beautiful take a look at the photos
Great vibes and decor. Solid service. Cool options for Korean fusion dishes; however a little over-valued. Probably would come back if some fam/friends wanted to get together for a lively brunch.

Nice upbeat, cute hidden gem. I went with a big party for brunch on the weekend, so we were able to try and share a bunch of items. This was the first time for me but a few in my party have been here before. Overall, food looked amazing, and taste was ok overall. Staff was very nice. Definitely would go back.

Great brunch spot! I went here on a Sunday with a few friends and had a great time.

Since we came on a Sunday, we waited for a good hour for our table. Once we were seated, the waitress greeted us quickly and got our orders. I got the eggs Benedict and that was really good. We also shared the French toast. The cream on the French toast was super rich and delicious. That was my favorite dish there. The dalgona coffees are also a fun drink to get. Overall taste was on par to how beautiful the dishes look. I wasn't disappointed by the taste at all! Highly recommend going here.

WOW!!! Four Chairs was an absolute hit. This is one of my favorite brunches I've had in a long time.

The K-bomb chicken benny was so delicious. It was an eggs benedict with a delicious pickled cabbage and then a large korean style fried chicken on the side. Chicken was flavorful and moist and filling! And this creme brulee french toast was amazing. I've honestly never had anything like it. The custard was delicious and I was practically licking the plate. I would say the drinks are cute but could be better. I got the Thai iced tea and it could've been a little stronger. I have admittedly become pretty picky about cafe tea drinks but I would personally save my money (and maybe get another dish here instead).

Overall a fantastic experience and worth the wait! Quick service once you order and the inside of the restaurant is so cute. I will definitely be back!

Stopped by here on a Friday mid-afternoon for a party of 2 and even though there were 15 parties in front of us, we only had a 15-20 minute wait. There is quite a bit of seating at Four Chairs and the tables actually turnover quite fast. The staff is quick and efficient. We ordered the Strawberry Matcha latte, Mango Matcha latte, Nova Omelette, K-Bomb Chicken Benny, and the Crème Brûlée French toast. Everything tasted delicious and the food came out impressively fast considering how many other patrons were at the restaurant.

The Nova Omelette had a good amount of smoked salmon and the omelette had parsley embedded in it. The K-Bomb Chicken Benny was huge and the flavors were so tasty! Crème Brûlée was also 10/10.. it was just the right amount of sweetness! Overall, drinks were also so tasty. Would definitely recommend stopping by here!

I visited on a weekday at 12 PM and found that there was available seating. I didn't have to wait, and the service was fast. The restaurant has limited space, so the tables are a bit close to each other.

For drinks, we tried the iced mango matcha and volcano coffee. Both were spectacular, bursting with flavor but not overly sweet. The matcha was light, and the mango added a wonderful fruity touch. The drinks came filled with crushed ice, which was somewhat disappointing, but we were still big fans of them. The volcano coffee is like dalgona coffee and reminded me of the instant coffee drinks we made from the tiktok trends in 2020. It had a strong coffee flavor and added some sugar packets to help even it out.

For our main course, we ordered the k bomb chicken sandwich, K bomb benny, and a grilled chicken avocado salad. The salad was light and refreshing, with juicy pieces of chicken throughout. I wasn't expecting to like it as much as I did, but ended up being one of my favorites! The chicken sandwich and K Bomb benny both contained chicken that seemed to be marinated in gochujang. It had a tangy sweetness with a nice spice. I also ordered house fries with my sandwich, and they were the crispiest fries I've ever had! So so delicious.

Came in on a Monday around 11AM (holiday), and was seated for 2 in less than 10 minutes. My friend had recommended the k-bomb chicken benedict as it's what he gets every time. Also based on reviews seems to be a popular item. Very much worth the hype! Servers were kind, spacious and good brunch spot for friends, family, or even solo! The pancakes were a bit too sweet for our liking but the fruits helped balance it out.

Nice decor, food overall good, service professional. Only real comment, they pack the patrons in... no space left unoccupied. Id prefer a little space between diners.
St the table smoked salmon Benedict , and the chicken waffles. Loved the seasoning of the chicken Waffles sauce... shindig with lite chili's. Chicken looked perfect, but slightly over cooked... chewy. (Pass)... but the Benedict was good. .popular place waited around 45min to be seated.. sometimes they have pre-wait, but was taken off while trying to use. ‍
Wait staff was attentive and worked well together.

It was a challenge to find parking around this restaurant. When we got to the restaurant, there was a wait list. We should have joined the waitlist on Yelp.

This restaurant doesn't have paper menus. You have scan the QR Code to look up the menu. Then, a waitress will stop by to take your order.

We ordered the Okonomiyaki Fries, Creme Brulee French Toast, K-Bomb Chicken Benny, Chicken Apple Scramble, and the By The Bay Benedict. For beverages, we ordered the Mocha Lava, Matcha Mango, and Coffee.

The Okonomiyaki Fries were warm when they got to our table. They had bonito flakes and kewpie mayo. The Creme Brulee French Toast was just ok. We wished they torched the bottom slice of French toast as well. The chicken for the K-Bomb Chicken Benny was tender and juicy. The Chicken Apple Scrabble was nothing special. The By The Bay Benedict came with Tom yum sauce, which added a nice kick to it. All of orders came with salad and potatoes. The potatoes were flavorless and dried. The Mocha Lava had chocolate milk and it wasn't too sweet. The Matcha Mango was refreshing.

Come here early if you don't want to wait long to sit and eat. We came here for breakfast around 10am and there was no line, by the time we left the line was already long. Anyways, food great! I ordered the Salmon Benedict, it was delicious. The service was good, server was busy but attentive enough. Ambiance, welcoming, open and very Bay Area modern vibe.

After a long, 1 hour flight from LA, we got our Turo rental and drove straight to Four Chairs.

Not that it's one of the most popular places for brunch in the city, and not for its delicious amounts of Benedict's, but the amazing service and wonderful ambiance inside.

Highly recommend the K Bomb Benedict and their Bloody Mary, made with Soju :) absolutely floored with the flavors, and the portions kept us full for basically the whole day.

I would also say to make reservations ahead of time - because we were there basically at opening, and boy did it fill up :)

Absolutely everything I tasted here was magnificent.


~FOOD~

We tried the chicken and waffle, chipotle eggs Benedict, and the crème brûlée French toast along with a chocolate milk and iced Volcano coffee.

CHICKEN & WAFFLE
The chicken was not too breaded, just the perfect amount of breading, the meat was not dry one bit and it had good seasoning. The waffle included a nice creamy, ever so slightly sweet butter that paired well with the crispy waffle. It's a good portion if you're hungry too!

CHIPOTLE EGGS BENEDICT
It's not spicy which is a plus so everyone, even those who don't like spicy foods, can enjoy this dish! You can always add chile sauce but you can't take it out! The eggs were soft and the chipotle was very delicious. Also a great portion if you're hungry as it comes with a side salad and fries. You can substitute the fries with fruit for an additional +$3 which I thought was disappointing for those trying to eat healthier.

CRÈME BRÛLÉE FRENCH TOAST
Crème brûlée melted crispy caramelized sugar on top of the vanilla custard sauce made this French toast very elevated. I finished the whole thing! My only complaint is that it doesn't come with enough fruit.

SIDE EGGS
Thankfully this place understands what over hard eggs are supposed to be cooked like, I usually end up with a greasy fried egg with a soft interior when I ask for over hard at other breakfast restaurants. I throughly enjoyed these eggs and the micro greens on top show that even side dishes are given the same effort and attention to detail as entree dishes.


~DRINKS~
Next time I want to try the cocktails here as their specialty mimosas look intriguing.

VOLCANO COFFEE
This is basically a throwback to the dalgona coffee from COVID lockdown times haha. Fluffy whipped sugar and coffee atop iced milk of your choice. Delicate, not overly sweet, refreshingly cold all at once.

CHOCOLATE MILK
GUUUURL this is the fanciest chocolate milk I've ever seen and tasted in my life lol! The glass cup was lined with chocolate syrup and the chocolate milk was topped with two marshmallows. Tasted as good as it looked!


~SERVICE~

Every time I have come here there is a waitlist but it usually goes by quickly. The waitstaff are attentive and kind. Despite an always growing waitlist and line, the waitstaff don't rush you which I absolutely appreciate.


~OVERALL~

I can't wait to come back here for brunch. This is my new favorite brunch place. Four Chairs is a perfect place to take a date or hang with your girlies.

One of my favorite brunch spots in the Bay Area! All the food tastes great and the service is incredible.

The menu changes frequently enough that it stays interesting. But the changes don't deviate from their overall vibes.

Food- the food was excellent. I enjoyed the thick cut bacon on my benedict and appreciated all the greens that came with it. I was stuffed, but I kept eating because it was really that good!

Service- it is a casual spot. The service was also casual. When you walk in, there's a spot to wait and also a screen to add yourself onto the Yelp waitlist. There were a couple large parties that day, but I didn't notice them calling anyone out from the list. People kind of just showed up and stayed by the screen--then were seated right away. There were parties who were waiting outside for their name to be called (or wait for their whole party). Either way, the waitlist to getting seated was a little confusing.

Ambiance- so many couples on dates! It's a cute spot.

Cute and modern brunch spot with delicious food! I came by on a Saturday around noon and it was packed. You can put yourself on the waitlist on their ipad in store and check your status in line on their yelp app. Estimated time was 30-45mins but we ended up waiting 1 hour. I would say be prepared to wait on the weekends as they were definitely busy!

Matcha latte: 3/5, it was just okay quality

Pacific Sunrise: 4/5
2 poached eggs with smoke salmon + Tom Yum hollandaise served on Brioche toast, side salad, and potatoes. The potatoes were the best I've had, super crispy!

K-Bomb chicken Benny: 5/5
2 poached eggs with Tom Yum hollandaise served on Ciabatta bread, side salad, potatoes, and a piece of Korean fried chicken. This one was a bang for your buck and my favorite! The Korean fried chicken had good flavors and the tom yum hollandaise was very unique, something I've never tasted before.

Overall, great brunch experience! I would definitely come back with friends to try their other items!

Side note: This is not the place to sit and chat after finishing the meal as they do need the tables for the next guests so guest should respect/keep that in mind when coming.

We went here to this cute, little breakfast place for Mother's Day, so the place was crowded, but thankfully the line moved fast. We were 16th in line when I put us on the wait-list, and not even 20min later we were 4th.

We got the By the Bay, K-Bomb Chicken Sandwich, Creme Brulee French Toast, as well as the Mocha Lava and Pina Coco with Soju, which we got pretty fast.

The By the Bay was a different sort of Benedict with Tom Yum Hollandaise Sauce with Grilled Shrimp, Cherry Tomato, and Mushrooms on Brioche Toast including Potatoes and Salad. The Egg and Shrimp were cooked perfectly and went well with the Tom Yum Hollandaise Sauce, but there wasn't enough Sauce. Wished there was enough Hollandaise Sauce for the Bread to soak up instead of just being on top. Also, they need to seriously work on their Potatoes. It just came with Potatoes that were in some dire need of seasoning. Even with the Pepper, Salt, and Ketchup we added to the Potatoes, we could still taste that they were lackluster.

The Chicken in the K-Bomb Chicken Sandwich had good flavor that went well with the Sriracha Mayo Coldslaw. Also, the Fries were thankfully seasoned unlike the Potatoes.

As for the Creme Brulee French Toast, this thankfully had more sauce than the Benedict, but this was just okay. It didn't taste bad, but it was meh especially for the price I paid. I would not get that again especially when I have tried better French Toast.

As for the drinks, the Pina Coco with Soju was asthetically pleasing especially in the cute cup, but it was just okay. It was thankfully not too sweet, but I could not for the life of me taste any Soju in the drink.

The Mocha Lava also looked nice and had good Chocolate flavor, but could have used more Coffee flavor.

Overall, the service and ambiance was great, but need some work on some of their food and drinks, but liked it enough to come here again to give them another chance.

my friends and i came here at 10:30am on a saturday and there wasn't a wait for a table of 3. we were seated as soon as everyone arrived.

the food was just good. i ordered the pacific sunrise and this dish didn't particularly stand out to me or feel special. the k-bomb benny was a bit more unique -- the korean fried chicken was cooked well and juicy inside. i also liked the salad it came with, mostly because of the dressing and fresh greens.

the interior and the food and drinks are very aesthetic and i'd recommend coming here with friends or on a cute date.

when we left around noon, there were a lot more parties waiting outside for a table, so definitely come early if you don't want to wait.

Came here around 10:30 am for a party of 2 and was able to be seated immediately.

The inside definitely gives off aesthetic brunch vibes, and the food is super picturesque! The portion size was pretty decent, as each plate came with potatoes and salad.

However, I think I still give 4 stars instead of 5 cause the food was good, but it wasn't particularly amazing to the point I would really come back. Overall, enjoyed the food and experience but I think there are more bang for buck brunch places out there. Definitely still worth a try though if you haven't been

Nice brunch spot.
They've got all your classics on the menu and some fun "instagrammable" drinks.

The food was nice and had great flavor. The salmon Benedict was yummy and the eggs were cooked perfectly.

I also had the volcano coffee and had the perfect amount of caffeine to wake me up and enjoy with my food.

The inside is nice and not too loud. The servers were very kind and attentive.

Nice brunch spot in the mission. I'll be back to take some friends

I give this a 7/10. The pancake was good, maybe a little bit fluffier would've been really good. French toast was good too. The matcha was great, however the straw was small and the ice was small so it kept getting caught. Would prefer a bigger straw or bigger ice. The menu scanner needs to be changed. Super hard to scan, ended up just googling it. The ham on the Benedict wasn't too salty which was good. Wish there was more hollandaise sauce. The breading on eggs benny was sooo hard to cut. Service was okay, never came back to check if we needed anything after getting food. 4/5 for the vibe of the restaurant.

Overhyped and always busy.

Dishes (ranked from best)
1) K-bomb chicken Bennie: chicken was excellent in flavor, texture, and portion. The chipotle hollandaise sauce missed the mark. Best dish I had there though.
2) Whipped coffee: good but sweet
3) Strawberry Matcha: way too sweet with the condense milk and strawberry syrup. The topped strawberry was also old.
4) Crème Brûlée French Toast: nothing special but the bottom toast was burnt.

Logistics:
-super hard to find street parking, no parking lot
-accepts cc
-takes yelp reservation

Came in today with my family. The food was really good. The inside was nice and friendly staff. A special shoutout to Oscar. I'm assuming he is a busser. He was so so kind and very helpful. Very hardworking.

Wait time was about an hour. The food makes up for it. The French fries are amazing.

Only con is them only having 2 toilets. lol there was a constant line of people waiting.

I would definitely come again.

We got ti restaurant at 10:30 on Sunday, and we got table within 20 min. It's a busy area, so plan to arrive early, because it's very hard to find a parking. . We ordered their signature mocha coffee and Velvet whipped coffee, and mango green tea latte, pancakes, chipotle Benedict and French toast. Overall food is great, but restaurant is busy and you have to wait for each order for 20-25 min. The place is also super cute, great decor, but service overall felt very rushed. Good experience, but because of parking situation and wait I gave 4 stars.

Came on a Sunday around 11:30 for brunch and put our name down on the Yelp waitlist inside the store. We were seated at 12:30. They turned off their online waitlist for Sunday. Sunday brunch is very busy and loud inside, with long waits for food and the check. I would recommend coming here on a weekday to avoid the wait and for a nicer ambiance inside.

I would give the chicken and waffle a 3.5/5. The waffles are the best, very fluffy and airy. However, the chicken is not seasoned at all, even the breading. This may be a hit or miss depending if you like the sweet chili syrup with fish sauce that is paired with this dish. The bland chicken makes it customizable with the syrups provided or the condiments at your table.

I got the Loco Plato and my gf got the Chicken and Waffles.

Loco Plato: $23. it's alright. It'sjust a spinach egg scramble with shrimp on top. Needed some pepper and hot sauce.

Chicken and Waffle: $18. Waffles are fluffy and good. The fried chicken needed a bit more seasoning as it was bland. I did not like the sweet chili sauce that was provided. Wish it was closer to fish sauce. The breading for the chicken was too doughy. I could taste the flour.

The service is really good but there is a really long line! The check in for the waitlist at the time could not be done over the app and was only person.

The inside is pretty spacious and loud since it was packed.

Came here with a reservation at 10:30 AM on President's Day and it was packed. You have to check in on the kiosk even if you have a reservation to let them know you're there. The decor inside was nice, I liked the wood paneling of the walls and there was plenty of sunlight coming through the front windows despite those being the only ones. It's a bit noisy inside due to how many people were there, so conversation was hard to hear at times.

I got the Lively Omelette, and it was good! Loved the chunks of avocado, and it was plenty cheesy. I got ciabatta as my toast, which felt a little dry. I liked the potatoes, though I found them a bit bland. Servers did a good job taking care of us despite the busy restaurant and us being in the back corner. Dishes and drinks here are very Instagram-able, and I would love to come back and get one of their benedicts sometime because my friends really liked theirs.

We stopped in on a weekend and the place was absolutely packed. The wait felt much longer than expected, with a lot of standing around before being seated. We ended up at a communal table, which was fine, just not something we were anticipating.

I ordered the K Bomb sandwich along with the volcano coffee. The coffee was definitely the highlight--sweet, strong, and genuinely tasty. While the presentation leans heavily into the Instagram-worthy gimmick, it was still fun and enjoyable.

The sandwich, however, was a bit too much. The fried chicken was overly sweet and sticky, with a marinade that made everything soggy and hard to eat. It quickly became messy and overwhelming, which says a lot considering I almost never leave a crispy chicken sandwich unfinished. The fries were excellent, though--easily the best part of the plate.

Others at the table enjoyed their benedicts, so that may be the safer choice. Overall, it didn't quite live up to the social media hype or justify the long line.

Four Chairs has been on our radar for a while; the first time we tried to come was a Sunday around 11am and that was a mistake because the wait was about 60-90 minutes long. We returned on a Monday around 11:30am and luckily it wasn't as crowded. For a party of 2, we were seated in around 5 minutes. (Once we left around 12:30 though, there were people waiting outside.) They don't have a physical menu and so you scan a QR code that's shown at the table to see the menu on your phone.

For food, we ordered Okonomiyaki fries, k-bomb chicken benny, mascarpone pancakes and a butterfly lychee drink. The drink and fries came out first within 10ish minutes. Fries were solid!! To be honest they were the main reason I wanted to try to this spot and they at least met my expectations. I like the thin shredded bonito flakes over the typical thick appearance.
