Also the fries weren't drowning in the sauce, which allowed the texture to not be completely soggy. I'm usually skeptical about aesthetic/instagram drinks, but the butterfly lychee was actually really good!! I would totally get it again -- tastes like a typical lychee fizz.

K-bomb benny was also alright. The chicken was good, the eggs and bread were fine. I wasn't a fan of the home potatoes, they didn't really have any flavor aside from tasting a bit burnt. Probably wouldn't get it again and instead try the k-bomb chicken sandwich. Mascarpone pancakes were probably one of the best breakfast pancake dishes I've had! It was perfectly sweet (not overly sweet) and I enjoyed the fluffy consistency.

Overall had an enjoyable time here and the food met my expectations. With that said, I personally wouldn't wait an hour for brunch here.

Service, brunch, ambiance, and presentation 10/10. Upon walking in we were greeted right away even though they were super busy! We were seated promptly as we made a reservation and were quickly greeted by our server. Everyone that worked there was very friendly and we were checked in on the perfect amount of times. The food was delicious, I got the pacific sunrise benedict and my partner got the mascarpone pancakes. We always share a sweet and savory plate to get a good feel of what the restaurant has to offer and this place exceded my already high expectations. The benedict was so yummy and vibrant, I loved the Tom yum hollandaise and felt that it brought out all of the other flavors on the plate as well. The salmon was super fresh and the eggs were poached to perfection (super yolky). Now for the mascarpone pancakes...WOW. I didn't know if I was going to like all of the soft textures together but boy was I wrong. The pancakes were so fluffy, fruit was fresh & sweet, and the mascarpone cream added the perfect touch. The presentation of both plates was also awesome, it's always neat when the great presentation matches the great taste. Next time I'm in the city I will be coming back to try another one of their specials. Wonderful experience!

Fast service for a brunch spot!
Went around 2 and there was a ~30min wait but staff is certainly efficient.

The mascarpone pancakes were yummy! Not too sweet - the whipped mascarpone was a good balance to give moisture to the pancakes. A detail I appreciated was the maple syrup side was warmed up.

The pacific sunrise (smoked salmon benedict over a french toast) was good ~ the sauce was not a traditional hollandaise but had a tang. Potato side was crispy!

Soooooo freaking good! Truly one of the best brunches I've had! We arrived at 10:45 AM on a Sunday morning and we're hit with a 30 to 45 minute wait. We signed up on the waitlist and took a walk outside. We only ended up waiting about 23 minutes, which was a glorious surprise.

We ordered the mascarpone pancakes, Korean chicken Benny, omelette, and loco Plato. And let me tell youuuuu. AMAZING! The pancakes were a hit for the whole table. They weren't too sweet and were perfectly balanced with the fruit on top. Additionally the pancakes themselves were incredibly fluffy. All of the savory dishes were so satisfying and yummy. The flavors were creative, but not too over-the-top and enough to be the perfect brunch craving food.

The atmosphere is nice. Even though they were busy, the service was very quick and efficient. I will definitely come back the next time I'm in San Francisco!

We visited on a Saturday morning and waited about 10 minutes. The restaurant was bustling with people, and the tables felt a bit close together.
You can view the menu by scanning the QR code on the table. There's also a menu posted outside, so you can decide what to order while you wait--which is helpful since it includes pictures!
The dishes were beautifully presented, and the service was quick and efficient. However, I found the food to be pretty average. While the place is cute, it's not somewhere I feel the urge to visit repeatedly.

Went for Saturday brunch.
Found parking close by. It can be tough to find on mission street.
The place is easy to miss as the outside is unassuming. But it was packed inside.
We put our name on the waitlist and got a seat within 10 minutes.
The service was fast
They have some instagram worthy drinks
We ordered the matcha Mango which had the perfect balance of flavors
The Chipotle Benedict came with a side of potatoes and salad. The salad dressing was Asian inspired and was tasty. The hollaindaise sauce itself could have been creamier. But the chipotle chicken was yummy.
Ordered the crème Brûlée French toast for the table and honestly it was so good! Perfect dessert!

Caught up with a friend and decided to eat here for brunch on a Sunday. We arrived around 12:30pm and put ourselves on the Yelp waitlist. It's closed on the app, so you have to sign up in person. We waited around 1-1.5 hours. We just chatted outside while waiting, but others wandered around the neighborhood to bypass the time.

Upon seating, the menu can be seen using a QR code. I enjoyed the aesthetic and variety of options on the menu, we opted for the K-Bomb Benny and Creme Brûlée French Toast to share so that we can have one sweet and one savory dish. In addition, I ordered the Mango Tango and my friend ordered a Strawberry Lemonade for our drinks.

The K-Bomb Benny was delicious! I enjoyed the savory flavors, especially the sauces they used for each component of the dish. I'm not usually a fan of Eggs Benedict, but I would definitely order this one again. The Creme Brûlée French Toast was also delicious! It was the perfect level of sweetness for me, though I wish the second toast was also torched. The Mango Tango was very refreshing to sip on after being outside, it was a good balance of mango juice and sparkling water. I was very happy with our choices of food, it made the wait worth it, including the friendly customer service! I would love to visit again and take more friends here!

Four chairs is one of my favorite brunch spots in SF! I use to get the Nova benny before they removed it from the menu, but they added the Pacific Sunrise, which is pretty similar if you substitute the tom yum hollandaise with the lemon hollandaise. The Chipotle and K-bomb chicken benny's are also really good and worth trying! The benedict plates are really filling because they come with crispy potatoes and a salad.

As for drinks, the Strawberry Matcha Latte was pretty for pictures but I wouldn't get it again because the matcha itself wasn't that good. I'd probably try their other beverages next time.

It can get busy on the weekends, so expect a wait, but it's worth it! The staff is really friendly and the food never disappoints. I would definitely recommend coming here!

One of the best brunch spots in the city! We took our friend who was visiting the Bay last week & all loved it.

Four Chairs may look a little small from the outside but the interior is actually quite spacey and very well designed / decorated. We were sat very quickly & seem to have gotten there just in time because it started filling up shortly after we arrived.

We tried the Mascarpone Pancakes, Soju Bloody Mary, By the Bay Eggs Benedict, Butterfly Lychee Cocktail, Pacific Sunrise Eggs Benedict, Okonomiyaki Fries, & Chipotle Eggs Benedict. Everything was amazing but in my opinion some standouts were the pancakes, the cocktails, & By the Bay Benedict. I think the swap to soju over standard liquor really enhanced the flavor & made the drinks more unique.

One thing to keep in mind is that there's street parking so you may have to circle for a minute but we were able to find parking just a few minutes away & walked over.

Visited on a Sunday (1/5/2025) around 10am and wow we got sat down and immediately we started ordering.

The food came so fast and we decided to family style it and try everything. The pancakes were so good and the chicken was insane!!!

Can't wait to come back and show my friends and family this amazing spot!

Came with friends for brunch! We had a reservation, so we seated pretty quickly. Note that the entire party must be present in order to be seated!

The food was delicious! I got the by the bay benedict and I really enjoyed it. It was flavorful and fresh! I also got a cocktail with soju, which tasted great as well! Definitely a vibrant color! I also liked the glass it came in, which has the four chairs logo :)

The service was great as the servers were attentive and I loved the decor! There's an aesthetic wall in the restaurant, filled with various books and kitchen supplies.

Overall, would definitely come back again for another brunch!

Came here on Christmas Day (because who doesn't crave brunch after opening presents, right?) and, wow, it was packed. Like, packed packed. Thankfully, they've got a Yelp waitlist, so you can join in on the app or in person. We hopped on the list, and luckily, the wait for two wasn't too bad. Phew!

Now, I'm not sure if it was because it was a holiday or if they were just running a little short-staffed, but the food took awhile to get to us. Not the end of the world -- just an opportunity to practice patience.
Their menu is, uh... a whole experience. It's 12 pages, which is kind of like reading a novella on your phone. I'm sure they offer paper menus, but we didn't ask for one and just scrolled through the mobile version.

Onto the food, though -- presentation is clearly their thing. Everything was Instagram-worthy, which is always a plus. I got the volcano coffee, and let me tell you, it was refreshing. A little sweet, a lot frothy -- perfect pick-me-up. The Okonomiyaki fries were crispy, saucy, and everything I didn't know I needed. Highly recommend!

For the main event, I went with the K-Bomb Benny (with scrambled eggs instead of poached because, well, pregnancy) and my bf got the Southwest Scramble with pepperjack cheese (because he's cool like that). The potatoes was crispy and the breading on the korean fried chicken was yummy. I enjoyed the side salad it came with too. A full balanced meal!
They charged a $1 extra for every substitution, which seemed fair enough, but just be aware if you're specific like us.

All in all, solid experience -- the food was tasty and the vibe was good. It's on the pricier side, well because of presentation and social media worthy pics. I'd come again and will be sure to join their Yelp waitlist via the app next time!

The line out the door accurately reflected how worthwhile it was to dine at Four Chairs! Once we put a name down on the waitlist (around noon on MLK Jr. Day) it took forty five minutes or so to be seated. Once at our table, ordering and food service was incredibly quick and efficient! And although I'm sure the employees were balancing a million tasks in the crowded restaurant, they were welcoming and polite.

The QR code on the table directed us to a colorful online menu, from which I ordered the K-bomb Chicken Benny (Korean fried chicken, cabbage, Chipotle hollandaise served on ciabatta) and the Matcha Strawberry Latte. The matcha strawberry was incredibly flavorful, probably the best one I've ever had (especially with its soft crunchy ice). And the benedict was delicious, with a side salad coated in a delectable asian-inspired dressing and incredible roasted potatoes (spiced, soft, fluffy, crispy... yum). The star of the show was the Korean fried chicken, of course, which was lightly battered and fried, then flavorfully glazed in a sticky sweet sauce. Fantastic. I wanted to order two more in a to-go box to save for later, but felt like that'd be overkill. Next time...
The banana waffle was amazing! The banana had the perfect amount of sugar and was cooked nicely. Will definitely have this again!
The volcano coffee was really good! I tried the mascarpone pancakes and those were good too - could've done with a little more fruits tho. I'll definitely try their other items soon.

Korean Fried Chicken Eggs Benedict

As soon as they brought it to my table I smelt vinegar. Well it was the hollandaise sauce, they put way too much vinegar in it. Lack of balance for me to enjoy the dish. The fried chicken was good though, moist white chicken meat with a nice crunch on the outside.

With the 1+ hour wait and mediocre food, I probably won't go back

Four Chairs has been the hype of the neighborhood as the go-to brunch spot, but ultimately didn't stick out as a spot to revisit.

For 2, we shared a mascarpone pancakes and Pacific Sunrise Benedict. Both were not particularly memorable and were fairly mid compared to other brunch spots in the city like Kitchen Story or Plow that I would prefer over Four Chairs.

Appreciated the relatively simple menu and the staff were nice. If I were ever to revisit I'd want to try the drinks as they looked creative and unique.

Made a reservation for hubby's birthday a month in advance to secure a table. Upon arrival, there was a long waitlist by the sheer amount of people in front of the restaurant in the cold weather outside. Checked in on their tablet via Yelp and was seated within a couple of minutes. There's a menu QR code on the side of the table which is convenient. I love the lack of holding a physical menu.

Arnold Palmer 3/5
Butterfly Lychee 5/5
Crème Brûlée French Toast 5/5
Birthday complimentary Mascarpone Pancake 4/5
Chipotle Benedict 4/5
Loco Plato 5/5
Host/Server (same person) 5/5
Atmosphere 4.5/5
(Unisex) Restroom Cleanliness 4.5/5

Worth the wait if you don't have a reservation. Definitely want to come back and try other items on the menu!

Not really worth the price or the long wait. The food was decent, but it definitely didn't live up to all the hype. Pretty disappointing overall.
The K-bomb benny fell flat it depended entirely on the chicken for flavor, so the rest of the dish tasted bland. The crème brûlée French toast only had that rich flavor right in the center; the rest just felt like regular bread with custard poured on top instead of an actual French toast. The chicken sandwich and mushroom burger were tasty, but still not special enough to justify what they cost.
On the positive side, the staff were very friendly and the service was quick.
It feels like one of those trendy brunch spots that's more about the aesthetic than the food itself. Not terrible, but definitely not a place I'd go back to.

Tasty fusion brunch place with aesthetic plating and creative drinks.

Wait for Sunday brunch was around 40 min.

Food came out pretty quickly and the portions were generous. I like how they incorporated greens into every plate.

My only complaint were the drinks had way too much ice in them. Within a few minutes they became watered down.

This place knows what they are doing. It was a bit of a wait but worth it. Flavorful, colorful yummy foods!

Atmosphere was nice somewhat classy but still casual. The seats were comfy and the vibe was good. Service was good for sure but the food took some time. I would go back to try some other items because the flavors were on point! I recommend.

A brunch with a unique twist.

All your american breakfast classics with korean-inspired touches that take them to the next level. The food is flavorful and delicious! The volcano coffee is a must try.

I've been wanting to give this place a try for a while after hearing raving reviews and now, I understand why.

This restaurant has a welcoming modern and cozy vibe. The staff is super friendly, fast, and attentive. (It was a Wednesday lunch so I am not sure if that changes the experience during the busy weekends.) Presentation of their meals definitely brings the experience up a notch.

K-bomb chicken Benny: perfect flavor and crunch on the chicken. My husband really enjoyed the Benedict being on ciabatta.

To the bay Benny: the tom yum hollandaise gives this dish a yummy and special touch but is not overpowering at all.

Mascarpone pancakes: I did thought they were going to be bigger but nonetheless, the flavor was good. Not too sweet!

They also had good coffee.

One downside is that the tables are kind of too close together. So you have to squeeze in between to sit down and the conversation noise can be quite loud.

Overall, we really enjoyed this spot. We look forward to coming again to try other items and some of the drinks!

This was a great choice for the day. I wasn't even inSF at the time but I was in the hunt for a good sit down breakfast and I found it! This had to be the best breakfast potatoes I have had, somehow airy and delightful. My meal I ate until there was no more. Wife was fully satisfied as well! Customer service was also perfect! Restaurant and Bathroom were clean as well,

Brunch at Four Chairs, SF
Food lineup: K Bomb Chicken Benny , Chicken & Waffles , Pacific Sunrise , and the star of the show--Mascarpone Pancake (my absolute fave!). Pretty solid flavors all around.

Service? Meh, could be better ‍.
Drinks? Total eye candy --Mango Lemonade , Volcano Coffee , and Butterfly Lychee stole the spotlight.

Cute spot, worth it for the pancakes & pretty drinks!

The best part of rainy days is being able to walk into a brunch spot like Bernal Heights Four Chairs that normally has over an hour wait and immediately get a table.

With a section dedicated to Instagrammable drinks like the less sweet mango matcha latte which is right for me, but the butterfly lychee was too sweet.

Their food are pretty Instagrammable too. Went for a sweet with the fluffy Marscapone Pancake, not to be confused with the young coconut Macapuno and the savory K-Bomb Chicken Benny with Korean Fried Chicken to get the best of both worlds. The side of okonomiyaki fries is a fun twist on traditional fries. Food was good but probably not for an hour wait.

Went to Four Chairs on a Saturday with a group of friends for brunch. They open at 9am we got there around 10am. It was already packed with customers but the wait was only ten mins. Because they are in such high demand there is a 90 min limit at the table. They put two tables together to accommodate our party of six. The table is kind of limited for space with that many people but we made it work.
After reviewing the menu we ordered the creme brûlée French toast and the mascarpone pancakes for the table cause we all wanted to try it. For my entree I went with the K Bomb Benny. It comes with salad, Korean fried chicken, home fries and eggs Benedict topped with chipotle hollandaise on top of sourdough bread. I don't like eggs Benedict so I asked for my eggs to be fried over hard and they said yes. I got the butterfly lychee for my drink. It's non alcoholic and comes with lychee juice and butterfly pea water. I have absolutely no complaints. I feel like all of the food was absolutely delicious. One thing worth mentioning is that the pancakes aren't served hot. It's more on the warm side. I didn't mind it, but my table didn't like that so they said something to the server who explained that the pancakes needed to be cooled down before adding the mascarpone to make sure that it doesn't melt, which makes perfect sense. I felt like the mascarpone and the fresh fruit with the flavor of the pancake really brought everything together. I like my food hot but I didn't mind it being served warm. I'm normally one that likes to drown my pancakes in syrup and I didn't even add syrup to it and still found it to be tasty.
The staff works as a team so we interacted with about four staff members between placing the order, asking for extras, bussing the table and getting the check. The teamwork is impressive and made for a great dining experience. For 6 ppl the check came up to $273 and that includes a 20% gratuity automatically added for a large party.
Overall, good experience and I would return.
This is my second time here and I will definitely be back. Their Korean fried chicken is so delicious. Their food is perfectly seasoned. Their French toast was so fluffy and yummy!!

The crème brûlée French toast is pure magic... caramelized on the outside, luxuriously soft inside, and just the right amount of sweet. I added crisp bacon, fluffy eggs, and a strawberry lemonade that tasted like sunshine, and suddenly my morning felt like a vacation.

The staff kept things moving with quick, friendly service and genuine smiles that made the whole experience even warmer. The space itself is open and inviting, with plenty of room to breathe and a calm energy that makes you want to linger just a little longer.

Brunch here isn't just good -- it's the kind of start to the day that spoils you for anywhere else.

9:20AM Saturday is a great time to go, no wait. Street parking available, might be a few blocks from the store or just utilize public transportation. For the space, great utilization of space when it comes to meeting, simple neat interior. When you order, you order through your phone, do say expect a wait, about 25 minutes for food.

I loved my chicken apple scramble ($19): contains avocados, roasted peppers, cheese and of course the chicken apple sausage. Egg texture is more of like Gordon Ramsey style where it is more runny. Awesome touch with the micro-greens for some texture and spice.

My friend got the Kbomb Benny ($20) and had mixed feelings. Enjoyed the variety of food since it contains veggie, but the chipotle hollandaise sauce was not great, very lemony and not chipotle taste at all. The chicken had a bit of crunch with the Korean sweet and spicy sauce, a good size piece of tender chicken. Overall, I enjoy the technical components in the food with a bit of fusion.
Four chairs a Great place to enjoy a good meal in a lively atmosphere. The service was friendly, the food came out fresh, and everything was well prepared. Definitely a spot worth coming back to.

One year later and the experience is still a 10/10! I brought my friend here who was amazed at how amazing his By the Bay Benedict turned out, with his strawberry matcha latte alongside his entree. I had ordered the Crème Brûlée French toast and it was mind-blowingly delicious. I asked to order the Pinky Winky strawberry drink which inspired my five star review of this restaurant one year ago, but sadly it was phased out of their menu. Instead, our server recommended a strawberry milk which was made with a strawberry puree rather than a syrup, which i greatly appreciate as it was SO delicious. Standing applause. Thank you, Four Chairs, for another unique experience.

Thai fusion brunch
Extravagant beautiful drinks
Nice modern interior but still has standard brunch condiment caddy with Smuckers jam packets

Coffee volcano like a coffee ice cream like a melted Baskin Robbins jamoca almond fudge. Chocolate milk more straightforward

Didn't realize just from the menu photo that there's only three pancakes in the stack and there are thick indulgent layers of mascarpone inbetween. Surprisingly light

Potatoes nicely fried

Sugar bomb sweet breakfast

Kbomb chicken tasty

Very attentive service

We recently came by for brunch. Nice comfy aesthetics. The food was also plated beautifully. We tried the Matcha Coconut. It's okay, but it looks pretty. Looking back, I should have also order the Lychee Butterfly drink because I like how that looks, too. We got the mascarpone pancakes, the chicken & waffles and a side of beef bacon. We enjoyed the mascarpone pancakes tho it's not very fluffy. The chicken (just ok) & waffles (ahmazing!) We recently went to C&B and thought their chicken was slightly better in terms of taste and texture. I absolutely love the waffles here. Nice service.

Located on Mission and 29th St. in Bernal Heights.

Arrived on a Saturday at 11:45am and waited about 30 minutes on the waitlist.

By The Bay Benny - so interesting with the Tom Yum hollandaise. Very zesty flavor, a big fan of a more unique Benny

2 egg breakfast - solid meal. Really hard to get this wrong!

K Bomb Benny - the KFC is such a hit! Savory to the max!

Mascarpone Pancake - initial bite I thought was good but a bit cakey but then I realized we forgot to pour syrup on it oops and with the syrup it was a perfect bite. Perfect pancake consistency to soak it in!

I also had the matcha mango latte and thought it was ok- the mango bits ended up being a little annoying because they got stuck in the straw.

Overall a great experience and I'd definitely come again. The food was good and had some unique twists that felt fresh and new.

The employees are great and welcoming! The food was delicious, but the fried chicken & waffle were a bit dry and flavorless. Other than that, the drinks were very pretty and refreshing! The furniture was also very high quality and comfortable!

Had to wait an hour on a Saturday morning. I really enjoyed the butterfly lychee drinks, very sweet and colorful. The chicken in the kbomb benny was really flavorful and good too. Good portion size. The mascarpone pancakes were okay, nothing fantastic. I preferred the creme brûlée pancakes.

Party of 7 had a long wait of one hour on Saturday before noon.

We ordered okonomiyaki fries (fries tasted stale), chicken and waffle, shrimp scramble, k-benny, crispy chicken sandwich, strawberry and mango matcha, dalgona, and butterfly pea lemonade. Everything was very mediocre. We expected food to be good given long wait times but we wish we went somewhere else entirely. Home style fries are on the saltier side. The chicken in the chicken and waffle had no flavor, relying on the accompanied sauce. The fruit matchas lacked matcha flavor and the lemonade was surprisingly too sweet. Hollandaise sauce had an overpowering citrus note and the crispy chicken sandwich was very plain.

There are so many good brunch places in sf I'd recommend over this one.

I'm not a big morning person but this was one of the best breakfast spots that was truly delicious. The wait was about 45 mins on a Saturday. The chicken was perfectly seasoned, I loved how they had all the sauces on the table, portion size was generous. Parking can be difficult to find as we walked a few blocks to get here but it's worth it! Very clean ambiance inside.

30 minute wait around 11:30am on a Monday. This place is packed and there continued to be a small line when we left.

I got the K-bomb eggs benedict and it is a soy garlic fried chicken (dark meat) with eggs benedict (2 poached eggs on bread) with potatoes and salad. I loved that they included both potatoes and salads as the sides so I didn't have to choose.

The chicken is tender, the marinade is a bit sweeter than other soy garlic fried chicken but still pretty tasty. The potatoes have this hard fried outer layer that I did not like, it was more hard than crispy.

Volcano coffee, aka Dalgona coffee, was pretty good although not as strong as I would've liked. Also, at the end of the drink, I had all this coffee foam that I couldn't drink because it was difficult to mix it completely with the milk.

Nice portions and fun flavor fusions I'm looking forward to try, my partner and I shared the French toast and different egg breakfasts (pictured/labeled below). The drinks aren't just gorgeous but the mocha lava foam I tried was stroonggg which was a rich surprise. The menu looked so yummy it was hard to decide! Attentive service, 20 min wait to be seated but I've waited longer for places, I do think it's worth it especially if you aren't sat near the door its cozy!

Needed a place for an early brunch and found this spot close by and was excited to see a menu with a Korean influence. Came in signs 930am on a Saturday and was immediately seated.

FOOD:
K bomb chicken Benny. Such an enticing combination. The chicken itself was quite good. A nice crisp batter, with the classic sticky sweet and mildly spicy sauce. Served with a classic Benedict, though on a piece of toast which I'm not sure came together the way I had hoped. The hollandaise was nothing special, though the egg was just fine. With the chicken, it just didn't really blend, I'm not sure the hollandaise could compete with the sauce of the chicken. The side salad was good, and potatoes were fine, but the Benedict to me was just okay.

Pacific sunrise. Hollandaise a little bit stronger with the Tom yum addition, but overall I have the same comments about the Benedict as above, which is, this was just okay. Still not enough flavor, though the smoked salmon was also fine. I liked the toast option on this one a bit better though.

Overall, I wanted to like this place. The staff were nice and attentive and they have a clean wooden ambiance. Unfortunately the food was just mediocre. Maybe the sweet options are better, but I prefer a savory brunch, so it may take another friend telling me to come for me to try again.
No line at opening on a Sunday! Get there before 10-10:30 and you'll be fine. The kbomb chicken Benny is what brunch dreams are made of.

K Bomb was fire! Not big on their hollandaise sauce, a bit too sweet.
Chocolate milk was good but wasn't worth the price to be honest.
Crème brûlée wasn't for me but it's not bad!
Service was great. Very friendly and timely. Ambiance is nice with good music.
I'd come back.

The drinks were sooooo good and really pretty!! Got the BLTA and it was really filling, the fries were really crispy too, which I loved. Servers were super friendly. Def coming again the next time I'm in SF.

Loved the food here!! They had quite a few options and pictures of the food so you know what you're getting! Loved that they had a instagrammable drinks section haha and they tasted yum! The food tasted great overall and wanna try other ones as well. We got the kinder scramble and the mascarpone pancakes which are popular for a reason.

We didn't have to wait too long either. I will say the area was not too pleasant to walk in but other than that a great experience. Will be coming back!

Been eyeing this place for brunch and it did not disappoint! It was classic brunch food and was nothing special but still good. I thought they would have more Asian inspired dishes but they did have a lot of Asian inspired drinks. Went on an empty day and the food still took a bit to come out, but nothing too crazy. The restaurant is big and the vibe was clean and inviting!

I found this place on yelp after searching for a brunch spot near my hotel. There was not a long wait to be seated and the staff was very nice. The food was so good and the portions were big, I ended up getting a to go box. One thing the note is the location has limited parking , we ended up parking at a meter and having to add money since you could only add 1 hour at a time. The vibe is very modern and relaxed. The restaurant is a bit small so I would call in advanced if you have a large group.

The food were more tasty on picture then eating it. The pancake is too dry and too sweet.

Also order the French toast, just ok, nothing special.

Service is good. But hard to find parking in the area.

The food was delicious and it come quick out . My favorite was the combination of Benedict's and chicken. The drinks are boom!! The macha is delicious too. The service is fast and people are nice. The place is small and cute . I went around 12 pm and there was not waiting list . They take of us very quickly and we had a very good experience. I'll go back .

Food was amazing!!! Every plate on every table was instagramable! perfect eggs Benedict, golden crispy hash browns, lots of brunch drink options. Restaurant was nice on the inside too. Service was good and also fast.

The food, service and ambiance here is amazing. We were seated quickly after adding our name to the waitlist, and the efficient service continued throughout our meal.

The food was delicious, and the ambiance, though a bit noisy, was still quite pleasant. I personally tried the chipotle Benedict, which was decent but not extraordinary. The eggs were unfortunately overcooked, but the volcano coffee was exceptional. The pancakes and bacon were also standout dishes.

Next time I visit, I'll be sure to try something different.

is it worth the hype? i would say so! aesthetically pleasing, instagrammable brunch spot that has a variety of options to chose from! i would say if you're coming in a weekend to expect a longer wait than a weekday and to have someone put the group down on the waitlist while you look for parking, because parking is rough.

our table of 7 arrived to four chairs around 11:20 AM on a Sunday, to our surprise found parking instantly across the street and waited an hour to be seated. inside is relatively small and cramped but they gave us a big table.

i ordered the matcha latte strawberry and the pacific sunrise! i really enjoyed the it! it contains: Smoked salmon, Sauteed spinach with Tom Yum hollandaise served on Brioche toast. the tom yum hollandaise sauce pairs so nicely with the smokiness of the salmon! the egg was also cooked to perfect, it was still very runny in the middle.

i usually don't finish my food but i finished this entire dish - they give reasonable portions. my pacific sunrise benedict dish was about $23.00.

you can make reservations for a weekday but weekends are first come first serve!

This place stood out so much to us and one of the best brunch spots in San Francisco! Each drink and dish was so delicious and unique it left us wanting to come back soon to try everything. We definitely recommend going early if you can to avoid lines because it can get pretty packed and for good reason the vibes are also so nice. Only thing is parking but that's a given with it being in the city.

- -- -- -
Pina Coco
Volcano Coffee
Butterfly Lychee
Mascarpone Pancakes
Creme BrûléeBrulee French Toast
K-Bomb Chicken Sandwich w/ Okonomiyaki Fries
Chicken Apple Scramble

I thought everything was great! It was very busy the morning we went and only had to wait about 20 minutes. We ordered the volcano coffees and they were just as good as they looked! All of our food was as quickly made and very tasty. It's a bit small inside to accommodate a lot of people but that's just SF in general.

We stopped by on a weekend and this place was packed. The line took wayyy too long, it felt like we were standing for a while. We were seated at a shared table, which was fine but not expected.

I tried the K Bomb sandwich and volcano coffee. The coffee was great!! I wish it wasn't advertised as so gimmicky and Instagrammable, but I guess it is. The coffee was nice and sweet with a strong taste as well. Cute presentation and fun! The sandwich was kind of overwhelming. The fried chicken was too sweet and too sticky. The marinade was a little too wet and the sandwich was kind of falling apart. I rarely leave a crispy chicken sandwich uneaten, but this one was way too rich, heavy, and messy. The fries, however, were perfection. Everyone else seemed to like their bennies, so maybe that is a better order. Even with the eggs, it doesn't seem like it was good enough to warrant the Instagram hype and massive line.

We've ordered takeout from here a few times, but I finally made it in person. If you are going on a weekend, make sure to arrive early. It can get busy.

We do love eggs Benedict and similar dishes for special occasions, and Four Chairs does not disappoint. They were able to accommodate our large party of 8 easily. I was pleased with the quick service at a place that was so busy.

I did not feel packed in or rushed, despite the fact there were a lot of people waiting.

The food here is amazingggg! The proportions are actually quite big! The service was great as well! The inside is simple and cute. Good for big groups as well! This would be my go to brunch spot if I lived in SF!

We waited about 20 mins to get a table, but it the wait went quickly for the three of us! Once we ordered it took about 20 mins to get our food and we enjoyed the ambiance & volcano coffees while we waited. The waitstaff were kind and efficient. Food was good & balanced and I see why it is such a hot spot for brunch.

Absolutely YES! This place is worth the little wait -- the food is sooo good! I had the crème brûlée French toast and the K-Bomb Chicken Benny, and when I say BOMB... I mean life-changing.

I had never tried eggs Benedict before, and this totally outdid itself. I could eat that dish over and over again -- in fact, I did! I ordered it again through DoorDash another day while in SF, and it was just as amazing.

Only thing I didn't care for was the Leche drink -- not my taste -- but honestly, everything else was bussin'. Run, don't walk!

Such a lovely spot for brunch! We visited here on Thanksgiving Sunday morning, hoping there'd be fewer people. There was already a line (they are popular!) But the service was so fast and efficient that we didn't have a wait for long at all.

The food was perfect brunch food. I can't wait to go back again.

Brunch Only Spot in SF!!

I've been having this bookmarked on my Yelp and I finally get to try it. So I almost ordered everything lol. They are all so tasty. I love the waffle by itself. It was light and airy but also tastes like a cornbread. Garlic shrimps scrambled have a lot of texture from crispy garlics which I really like. I'm picky when it comes to smoked salmon and they nailed it.
The benny = Benedict was tasty too. I
was drool all over the Creme Burlee toast!!!

I ordered:
- Chicken & Waffle
- Korean Chicken Benny
- Garlic Sheimp Scrambled Egg
- Smoked Salmon Omelette (Nova)
-Crème Burlee French Toast
- butterfly Pea & Lychee
- Coffee
- Mango Something
it was spiked with soju

I got there at 10am when they first opened on a Friday. It was almost full house by 11am. I definitely recommend making a reservation since they are only for breakfast and brunch. They closed around 2pm or 3pm. The service there was fast tho.

Please add me on Yelp if you like my vibe or IG @imjennime. TYSM

Nice place to have a brunch or lunch, but be aware of an hour wait on weekends. I liked the casual vibe of this place (people chose it for morning dates as well as for friends meetups and family brunches). Service was very fast food came pretty fast too. We tried K bomb Benny, French toast cream brûlée and volcano coffee- everything was good and presentation was excellent. Definitely will visit again

This Korean fusion brunch spot is one of the most popular ones in the city! My friends and I met up there and waited on the waitlist for about 10-15 mins which wasn't bad on a Saturday morning at 10:30am!
We were seated and served pretty quickly and ordered the popular volcano coffee which was sweet but strong, and the mango matcha was my fav with strong mango that blended with the matcha, and the strawberry was a bit too sweet/ very jamy overpowering the matcha.
The two Benedict's were amazing my fav being the Korean fried chicken with it! It was crispy, sweet and savory and paired well with the eggs! The creme brûlée French toast was delicious and crispy on the outside but soft and flavorful all around!
The interior design was nice more on the casual yet homie vibe as it was quite packed with tables being close to each other.
Highly recommend getting there a bit earlier too for parking as there are limited spots along the side streets!

Over-booked, understaffed, and extremely tight seating. The entire meal all I could focus on was not rubbing elbows with the table next to me. Loud and chaotic environment. Getting a table is a nightmare as is, I would just get rid of allowing walk-ins the line outside is so off-putting.

However, this is all fixable! Food is solid, menu has great options, and staff were kind. If all the factors mentioned previously were fixed, I would be there 3x a week! I would honestly be a regular, think about that.

Absolutely delicious! I found Four Chairs on TikTok and was dying to try this hot breakfast spot in SF! Upon arrival, we saw a line outside and new that was a sign that this place had to be good. We added ourselves to the waitlist at 10:30 AM on a Sunday and were seated within 30 minutes. We decided to try a variety of dishes and caffeinated drinks. Literally every single thing was delicious. The volcano coffee and strawberry matcha were super unique and tasty. We loved the Mascarpone pancakes - they were fluffy and sweet. The chipotle Benedict was very good but I wished the chicken was a piece of fried chicken versus more of a chicken chorizo. Finally the southwest Benedict was super flavorful. I highly recommending checking out this breakfast spot.

Definitely one of the best brunch spots in the city. Creative food and drink menu with something for everyone. The entrees are filling and delicious. We added a French toast order for something sweet and tasty. Volcano coffee was also excellent. Lines can be long but worth the wait.

Coffee volcano, YES please!
A few things I love about this place:
1. Potatoes are crisp, not soggy and oily
2. Portions are great. I hope they never skimp
3. Coffee and matcha choices are deelish

My go to:
Mascarpone pancakes
Lox omelette
Coffee volcano

we came around 1:20 on a saturday and still had to wait just over an hour to be seated. seems that people are willing to wait for this place! i also wanna acknowledge that the staff is amazing -- such a busy weekend morning & everyone was just as polite & friendly. a busy atmosphere with lots of families and friends meeting up for the weekend.

drinks:
- matcha latte was a bit disappointing, it lacks the depth of flavor that a matcha should have.
- strawberry lemonade was tasty and refreshing!

food:
- mascarpone pancakes were honestly a bit denser/flatter than i expected but flavor was on point! the fruit added a nice & refreshing cut to the sweetness flavor profile. and the warm maple syrup just tied everything together.
- by the bay: amazing blend of flavors! nothing was too strong or too salty, etc. i loved the new take of a benedict on brioche toast instead of english muffins. the side salad had a nice vinaigrette dressing that helped enhance the dish and bring it to life. the potatoes were well-seasoned but a bit lacking in crispiness that wouldve given it the extra "oomph" to perfection.
- lively omelet: pretty good, but the layer of cheese on top just seemed to slip off in one chunk. there was also a good amount of cheese in the omelet and just felt like it was a bit too much. everything else was pretty good, a standard omelet.

overall this place is worth it but i can't say i would wait another hour to eat here. i might consider ordering takeout or delivery next time though to avoid the wait.

Had a catch-up brunch with some friends here and we've been wanting to check out Four Chairs for a while, so it was a no-brainer. I got here about a half hour before my friends arrived, which ended up being perfect since that's about how long it took them to seat us (group of 4). They don't take reservations on weekends, so make sure you work in a wait time!

When we sat down, the menu is through a QR code right on the table. I ended up splitting the K bomb Benedict and the creme brulee french toast with a friend. Both were delicious. I think if I come back, I'd definitely just get the Benedict all to myself!

You can add soju to most drinks, which I did with my coffee. The servers were efficient but not pushy. The restaurant was a tad on the loud side, that's what you get when everyones having a good time.

This restaurant is nestled in the mission and I stumbled across it on a random morning!

Parking around this area is good, if you can't find anything on the street, there is a Safeway to park in need be.

the restaurant definitely has a cozy feel to it.
the service was fast and attentive

food - 4/5
1. Spicy Korean Fried Eggs Benedict - this was bomb! the chicken was well marinated and it tied in well with the eggs and potatoes
2. Creme Brûlée French Toast - if you have a sweet tooth, this is the one for you. I loved the caramelized sugar on top to give it that creme brûlée traditional feel. The toast itself was fluffy and well seasoned.
3. Pancakes - they give you a good amount it's also on the sweeter side. I would just say this was average.

We decided to try Four Chairs after seeing all the TikToks and positive reviews. We arrived at 11 a.m. on a Saturday morning, expecting a long wait, but were pleasantly surprised when it only took about 30 minutes to get seated.

As I looked over the menu, I was a bit surprised that their famous breakfast items were sold a la carte. I was also disappointed that there wasn't an option to order just one pancake instead of a full stack, but I realize that was my oversight for not asking. We ordered their well-known mascarpone pancakes.

The presentation was stunning, and the mascarpone was a perfect addition to the pancakes. However, the pancakes themselves were disappointing--they had the taste of dry pancake batter. It made me think that perhaps the mascarpone masks the actual flavor of the pancakes, or maybe I just caught them on a bad day. Honestly, I make better pancakes at home using store-bought Krusteaz mix. My husband enjoyed their chicken sandwich, but even that wasn't anything particularly special.

If I were to return, I would probably try the eggs Benedict instead.
Our absolute fave breakfast/brunch spot. The crème brûlée French toast and k-bomb chicken benny live forever in my dreams. LOVE.

Very happy to have Four Chairs in the neighborhood. Beautiful spotless place. And the service/staff... excellent The food is beautiful. The French Toast was ok. The outside was to tough to cut through or maybe it needed a steak knife. But the flavors were delicious. I had the iced whipped coffee, very good just too much ice. And the burger was surprisingly delicious. It didn't look like much but it was fresh and juicy. I think I need to revisit and explore more.

We love this place and often visit it with family and friends. There is a large selection of dishes, and I especially like the drinks here . But the last time we were here. I ordered a burger with potatoes, and the potatoes were either not fresh or overcooked. I mentioned this, and they told me that's how it's supposed to be, but it was clear from the taste that it wasn't. It wasn't a pleasant experience.

Wait time wasn't too bad for a Sunday morning. Service here is quick. The Thai iced tea (4.5/5) is very good here! For sure would get that again. I also got the chicken and waffles (3/5) and it was all right. The sweet and sour sauce (they gave very little) was good but the chicken breast was a bit dry. The waffles are too light and airy; I prefer them more on the crunchy side. I won't get waffles here again but would consider their other items.

We stopped in for breakfast and were seated fairly quickly. The food was delicious! I ordered the standard breakfast set and was delighted with everything. The customer service was excellent, despite the early hour.

Four chairs is amazing the service is great and food is amazing everything is fresh drinks are amazing and everything was presented very nicely the restaurant was also beautiful definitely would come back here again!

I stopped by for brunch and to catch up with a friend from middle school. We met up at 11 and a Saturday so it was super busy as expected. I was the first from our small group of three to arrive, and placed our name on the list.

I'm not sure what happened or if there was a miscommunication but when I received a notification saying our table was ready and went in I was informed that we were still on the waiting list ( I was no longer able to see the list on my side) which was fine. I waited outside because like I said it was busy, and got a notification that I was removed from the list, so I went back inside and was informed that I was removed because my table was ready but no one came in. We were still seated which I was thankful for but was confused.

The food itself was very good. The menu is very egg based with a few speciality items. I would like to go back and try one of their scramble options.

We decided to have brunch on a Wednesday knowing Four Chairs is a busy spot on weekends. A lot of hype from one of our friends who recommended their crème brûlée French toast! I also had my eye on their butterfly lychee drink. My bf tried the K-bomb Chicken Sandwich. We made online reservations, but we were seated immediately as there were a few open tables at 11:45 am. It's a cute, modern cafe. It's a bit dark inside, but cozy.

OUR THOUGHTS:

CRÈME BRÛLÉE FRENCH TOAST ~ if you like custard, you'll like this dish. I enjoyed it, but it's definitely dessert for brunch! I was almost tempted to order something savory then order this for dessert but I was sure I'd be too full to eat this after an entree! It was filling and sweet but not overly sweet. I like the crunchy burnt sugar on top! Though the French toast isn't saturated like your usual French toast. Lightly soaked, but had enough custard sauce on top so you can soak in the yummy custard! If you had a normal French toast that's saturated, you couldn't soak up the custard sauce! 4/5

K-BOMB CHICKEN SANDWICH ~ my bf noticed the chicken being very thin and also breast meat which makes it a bit drier but it was heavy on the sauce to counteract the dryness. I'm sure the breading also helped with moisture. He was disappointed about the size of the chicken. And it was pretty sweet though that was expected since they probably used gochujang in the sauce. 3/5

BUTTERFLY LYCHEE DRINK ~ pretty to look at and sweet tasting. Nice mocktail though nothing special, just lychee flavor. I think if it was sparkling, it would have been better. 4/5

It was a nice place to have brunch, but only if you can snag a table on a weekday without having to wait. And if I were to come again, I'd try an eggs benedict plate.

We visited Four Chairs Restaurant on a Saturday around 1 PM and had to wait about 30 minutes to be seated. The place was packed, both inside and outside, and parking was a nightmare to find.

Once seated, the food and drinks were nicely presented. I'd definitely order the K-bomb chicken and lychee drink again--they were the highlights of the meal. The pancakes tasted like any other typical pancakes, and the French toast was unfortunately soggy in the middle. Most of the drinks were overly sweet for my liking.

What really turned me off was finding a hair in either my chicken or eggs--it was hard to tell since the chicken was on top. I didn't make a big fuss since I was already halfway through and the staff was friendly, which is the only reason I let it go. I just picked around it. Still, it was disappointing.

Also, some of the dishes seemed a bit dirty, like they hadn't been properly washed from previous use. For a place that gets so much hype, the experience didn't live up to expectations.

Overall, it's an overhyped spot with a nice vibe and friendly staff, but the food, cleanliness, and experience left a lot to be desired. Would I go back? Probably not.

Mascarpone pancakes - 3 super fluffy pancakes with vanilla mascarpone sandwiched in between each one, topped with bananas, berries, and powdered sugar. Sweet but not too sweet, it was delight to look at and eat.

We came on a Friday late morning and the place was packed! We had to wait about 20 minutes before being seated.

This place is packed. Heard there is always a wait in line. I was captured by instagram and told my sister to take me here when I visited. I would just try EVERYTHING!
But let me tell you, the mist have is the K.Bomb Benny. My taste buds were dancing and saying come here more often (boo..I can't because not from SF.**tear**) If I could, I totally would!

Marscarpone pancakes. Idk why I thought the batter was supposed to have the marscapone in there but it was sandwiched between the pancakes. Still good all together but after getting down on the savory yumm yumm of that K. Benny...I wanted more of the K.Benny.

My sister had the Southwest scramble. It was picturesque. Still delicious but something I could find at any brunch place. Still good for the plain Jane's out there. Idk. Still thinking about that K. Benny.

For drinks, we had Thai ice tea and Strawberry matcha. Mmmm...drinks. but that K.Benny.

Someone fly me this K.Benny please. Just TRY IT!

The staff there was awesome. Even though it is super busy, you get great service.

I ordered the crème brûlée French toast and they were amazing. The service was quick and the waiter was extremely friendly. The ambiance of the restaurant was very warm and welcoming, and we were quick to be seated. My boyfriend and friend both got matcha and they both loved it!

Not a bad spot but it does get busy. I came here right when they opened but it seemed service was a bit lacking. They didn't ask us if we wanted any drinks, many workers walked past us and still no water even. I ordered the chicken and waffles and was confused why I received one cup of syrup and one empty cup. Turns out they forgot to give me sauce. I figured out after my friend went there and definitely had something in the second cup. The batter was good but it was lacking flavor. Perhaps because I didn't have the other sauce.
I would probably come back to try other options.
Everything was delicious and tasted amazing. Waffles were a little dry and flavorless per my 12yr old lol but the fried chicken was fire! Loved the volcano coffee.
great presentation on the foods and drinks. lots of creativity. Korean fried chicken Benny was good and my favorite! so was the butterfly pea as lychee was refreshing.

We shared the Creme Brulee French Toast. It was fantastic! We were so full and we couldn't finish everything, so we got boxes to go.
The restaurant has a nice contemporary look, airy with plants. Its a little noisy but not bad. It can get warm in there so try to sit near the window and the service was great.

Really great brunch gem! Be sure to be prepared to wait in a line, but otherwise everything else was great. Ordered their pacific sunrise $23 that's sharable between two. The hollandaise is Tom Yum inspired so definitely with a Thai twist. Comes with home fries flavored to perfection and crispy, as well as a side salad. Wanted to try their pancakes so ordered their side order $8 that's was less quantity but overall a good deal if you're looking to try it out. The inside is packed, but decorative wise modern and cozy. Overall recommend!

I'd have to say that this place lives up to the hype!! There was a huge crowd outside the restaurant on a Saturday but we were seated within 20 minutes. The k bomb chicken benny is a must try. The sweetness of the chicken goes perfectly with the salty Benedict. Only knocking off a star due to the service as it was a bit rushed and we received the bill before we were even close to finishing our meals.
I love this place! Everything we ordered was amazing, drinks were good, great survive and the place is cute too. Too bad parking is kinda limited and you have to pay for parking. It's in the street.

Delicious! I got the mascarpone pancake. It was a bit pricy, but it is San Francisco. I wish they had more vegetarian options on their menu. Even just a vegetarian omelette. They request people don't ask for substitutions, so it'd be nice to have more meatless options.
The service was fast and kind, and the atmosphere was plesant. Soft lighting with windows and it wasn't too loud when I was there even though it was starting to get busy. Popular spot, even on weekdays, but I got there shortly after they opened for the day and was able to get a table right away. I recommend getting there early or expecting a wait on weekends. The tables were clean and had everything needed already there including water pitchers. They accept card payments. They also seemed fine with me using my laptop which was nice for a breakfast spot.
Parking nearby is paid and can be tricky to find depending on the time of day.

Date of Visit: 8/2/2024

We visited the Four Chairs Restaurant for Friday brunch last Friday! Four Chairs is located in the corner of the neighborhood of Bernal Heights and Mission District. It was opened in early 2022 and has been family owned since then. They served many popular New American breakfast and brunch items, such as omelet, benedict, pancake, chicken and waffle, sandwiches etc.

We made a reservation beforehand and were sat right away.

Volcano Coffee with Oat Milk $7
My friend got the very popular Dalgona coffee. On the top is the thick foam of coffee with oat milk under it.

Butterfly Lychee $7
I got the blue and white butterfly lychee, made with butterfly pea tea and lychee juice.

K-bomb Chicken Benny $20
This one is one of the popular dishes, with a piece of Korean fried chicken on the side. The benedict was topped with chipotle hollandaise sauce and served on ciabatta, with home fries and house salad on the side.

Mascarpone Pancake $16
The other dish we got was the pancake. This is a stack of three pancakes with mascarpone in between, topped with banana, berries, orange and with maple syrup on the side.

food:
Mascarpone pancake: 5/5 The mascarone was perfectly light in sweetness but rich in creaminess, and paired well with the fluffy pancakes.

K-bomb chicken benny: 4.5/5 Not too spicy (I have a low spice tolerance, trust me) but had all the right spices and just the right amount of crunch! It was amazing with the soft, warm toast and eggs benedict. The side potatoes were alright but the salad had zero dressing so that was kinda sad and flavorless..

drinks:
mango matcha latte: 3.5/5 A little bit too much ice for my liking (which was 80% of the cup) but the matcha flavor was good, paired well with the mango puree. Presentation was pretty but probably would not get it again. There's definitely better matcha elsewhere.
strawberry matcha latte: 3.5/5 Same notes as the mango matcha latte.

ambiance + service: 4/5 We (2 people) waited nearly an hour on a busy Sunday so be prepared for that! They have a yelp waitlist machine inside. Service was relatively fast but they don't really check in on you throughout, hence the 4/5 rating. Ambiance however was amazing, on par with every other pricey brunch spot in SF.

Parking: Meter parking is free on Sundays but every other day of the week will be tougher to find open spots.

Overall: Would recommend the two dishes we got, and recommend getting there early to beat the possibly long wait!

This place was amazing. I love the ambiance and the service is much different than an American restaurant. Besides waiting 20 mins late on a reservation for seating, this was worth the wait.

Staff was attentive, and everything came out great.

The place is definitely beautiful, and the atmosphere is very nice for breakfast. However, I had a really disappointing experience with the menu. I wanted to order a grilled cheese sandwich, and the server told me it was only available on the kids' menu which honestly makes no sense.

For the price and the long wait in line, I don't think it's really worth it. It's a nice spot to visit once, but personally, I wouldn't go back.

In our first time having brunch in the city of SF we decided to choose Four Chairs as the spot to go to. We got there at around 9 am on Sunday morning and waited approximately 15 minutes for a table of two. Even though we were seated promptly, the place was packed. Once seated the service was quick and our orders were taken quickly.

We were quite impressed with the speed our food came out in. Sometimes that can be a red flag but the food was REALLY good. My wife got the chorizo Benedict and I got the Loco Plato with a side of hollandaise( best hollandaise I've had in a while) They serve a variety of drinks too which looked good but I only got water and an apple juice.

The space for seating is a little small but for some that's exactly what they like. The service could be a little better but like I said, the place is packed busy and it can be understood why they can't get to every table in a fast manner. Once we left around 10:30 am there was already a crowd to get a table, so try and get there early.

Definitely check this place out

Came here in a Sunday at 11am. Joined the wait list and it said wait time was 38-45 min. It was super accurate.

Ordered creme brulee french toast, loco plato, and k-bomb chicken benny. Had a coffee and a English breakfast tea.

Service was very good, staff was attentive and fast, with knowledgeable food recs.

Brulee french toast was good, a bit over sweet in my opinion. Loco plato had great flavor, but the eggs were a bit stiff from over cooking. The Korean fried chicken benny was interesting. Generally you'd expect Korean fried chicken to be double fried and crispy, the flavor was there but the chicken was a little mushy. The food presentation was beautiful.

Something that did bother me was the caddy on the table with Denny's like set up. Welch's single serve jams, delight creamer, and ketchup bottle. Just not what I would expect when I'm spending $80 on brunch.

All in all it was a decent experience.

Loved it all, the vibe, the food was amazingly Delicious, friendly service , and the drinks were to die for.
The Bloody Mary has so much taste to it and the Volcano Coffee was just perfectly made

- Price point: $$ ($30-$50pp)

- Cuisine: American (Brunch)

- Ambience: cute brunch place, super busy on weekends. Tables were put super close to each other, also long waiting time

- Food review:

1. Butterfly Lychee 9/10 (looked super pretty and tasted amazing)
2. Crème Brûlée French Toast- 9/10 (bit sweet but delicious )
3. K bomb chicken benny 10/10 (the best item here and highly recommended!)
4. Okonomiyaki fries 7/10 (high price for a plate of fries, although the taste was good, its basically fries with some mayo-based sauce )
5. Volcano coffee - 5/10 didnt live upto the name, coffee flavor was mild, a bit disappointed with this one

We loved this brunch place overall. Everything was presented beautifully and most of what we tried were delicious! Prices were reasonable for a brunch place. Portions were huge!!!

WE WILL BE BACK TO TRY THE OTHER ITEMS (Mascarpone pancake).

Recommend for: brunch, date/ group hangout

Came in for brunch around 12:30pm on a Monday and there was no wait for a party of two :)

Service was very quick - we were seated, our orders were taken, and our food was brought out all within 30 minutes. The menu had so many options and the mouth-watering pictures made it so much harder to decide what to order!

BY THE BAY BENEDICT 8/10
Sooooo good and very fulfilling! It wasn't my favorite benedict, but it was satisfying.

MASCARPONE PANCAKES 10/10
These were the fluffiest and airiest pancakes I've ever had. The layers of mascarpone were light and airy as well and went perfectly with the pancakes and fresh fruit combined. Must try!

SOJU BLOODY MARY W/ BACON 8.5/10
This bloody mary was amazing and full of flavor. Comes with celery, lemon, cherry tomato, olives, and pickled onion. You can add bacon for an additional $3 (pricey for a slice of bacon).

Overall a nice brunch spot. I will definitely be back to try more items off the menu!

The service for this place is kind and fast! We were quoted a 30-45 min wait but it ended up only being a 5 min wait for our party of 5 for Sunday brunch. The space is really large and tables turnover quick

I've heard good things about this place so I was a bit disappointed after trying their food. I got the Southwest scramble and the eggs were a bit too dry and crumbly. My bf got the mascarpone pancakes and the pancakes were too dense and not fluffy. I tried my friends' creme brûlée French toast and that was delicious! It wasn't too sweet and the French toast was soft.

Arrived for brunch on a Sunday and were added to the waitlist. All you need to do is give your name, phone number, and they send a text notification when the table is ready. It took about 30-45 minutes before we received the notification. As soon as you walk inside, you would see why. It is absolutely packed in there.

We ordered two of the k-bomb benny, creme brûlée french toast, and two drinks. I believe I got the mango tango and my friend got the strawberry version of it. Unfortunately I am allergic to strawberry, so I was unable to try it but I loved my mango drink, helps that it looked cute too lol. The k-bomb benny was absolutely amazing! The Korean chicken was the star of the show for me. The BBQ sauce the chicken was tossed in was savory with the perfect amount of sweetness. I am not from the Bay Area (from NJ/NYC), but I would return to try this again. The crème brûlée french toast was great as well and helped us with our sweets craving. The top of the sauce hardened and made my first bite nice and crispy.

Again, the place is full to the brim, on the Sunday I went at least. The ambiance is trendy and when looking around you can see many tables full of families. One of the downsides was the service, however. This could be due to how busy it is in the establishment. We ordered everything at once, however only received one of the benny dishes and had to wait 10-15 minutes for the other. A little odd. But other than that, I recommend and would return myself if I am ever back in the Bay Area!

Parking can be tough as most SF places are. Drinks were awesome and the food was very tasty and filling. So many options that definitely warrants a revisit. The eggs for Benedict's were poached perfectly. The hollandaise sauce had great texture and flavor. K-bomb benny with fried chicken was perfect - crunchy and juicy.

Very busy and fairly long wait on a Sunday lunch. Only indoor seating available.

We shared the Hawaiian omelette and the creme brulee French toast. Initially, we weren't planning on getting the creme brulee French toast but the people next to us got it and the presentation looked so beautiful that we had to get it.

The creme brulee French toast was pretty good! I liked how the cream wasn't overly sweet. I liked the burnt sugar part and wished the toast on the bottom also had it, but only the top piece did. The Hawaiian omelette was better than I expected! Omelette was flavorful, dense, and filling. The potatoes were room temperature and would've appreciated if they were hotter and crispier.

Food came out pretty quickly, and they were good at getting people in and out since it's so busy.

The food is super delicious. The coffee was outstanding. The service from M was amazing. He was friendly and well versed with the food that they have. The marscapone pancake was heavenly the coffee was outstanding. His smile and friendly attitude was contagious .Very good vibes, there was a lot of people having a great time with the food and the staff.

Bernal food scene once again pops off - Four Chairs lived up to the hype of delicious and balanced fusion branch!

We went in on a Sunday morning at 11 am (prime hours) without a reservation, so the wait was 45 min for two people. Would recommend checking in on the Yelp waitlist if available and you don't have a reservation (I took the time to wander and pop by the Mexican grocery store a few doors down for some Abuelita hot cocoa ).

Once we got seated, service was pretty quick! The interior is pretty spacious, loud, and buzzy - a good vibe to start the Sunday.

We ordered the iced coffee and mango matcha (not too sweet, very refreshing) to start. We split the Kinder Garden (veggie scramble) and Mascarpone pancakes. Both hit the spot - the scramble had good balance of vegetables and crispy potatoes. The pancakes were fluffy, and the mascarpone cream lightened the dish up and balance the sweetness too.

It was about $60 all in, which felt comparable in SF for brunch + drinks, but everything hit the spot. There are limited vegetarian options (savory), but what they do they do well!

we waited around 1 hours for a seat for a party of 2 at 1pm, and another 20 min for food to come out. The waiter was very polite. It's a small restaurant and really loud since there were a lot of people- not really somewhere you could easily hold conversation. Ventilation also was kind of poor because you could smell burning food.

The food itself was great! I got the nova Benedict and it met my expectations. My friend also enjoyed her chicken Benedict. She enjoyed the potatoes, but I thought it less seasoned and left a bit of a taste in your mouth.

I wouldn't mind coming back here to try more menu items, maybe at another time that isn't their busiest!

My friends and I made plans for Saturday brunch and decided to come early to avoid waiting in a long line - we arrived just before 10 and were seated immediately, but the line went out the door by about 1030, so we got there just in time! We skipped drinks because we had coffee plans after, but everything that was brought to other tables was super pretty and instagrammable.

We ordered three plates to share, and it was the perfect amount of food to feel full but not bloated. The regular menu had your typical brunch options, but the specialty dishes were super unique.
- By the bay eggs Benedict: the tom yum hollandaise caught my attention, and I was impressed that you could actually taste the tom yum flavor! The shrimp were fresh and plump, and the brioche toast was so soft. The home fries were satisfying because who doesn't love potatoes, but nothing to write home about. It was also nice that it came with a house salad for ~*health*~ instead of one or the other like most places.
- Creme brûlée French toast: WOW this was so airy and moist! Sometimes French toast can be too sweet for me, but this was so good especially with the berries. Whatever is in the cream was absolutely delicious - we used our bites of French toast to scrape up more of it lol.
- K-bomb Benny: the chicken was super flavorful and moist as well! The sweet and savory flavors were well balanced too. While I typically love ciabatta, it was a bit hard to cut into for an eggs Benedict, especially compared to the brioche (above).

Service was friendly but a bit rushed toward the end - understandable given the long line outside, but also felt like we were being hurried out with how quickly the check and busboy came out. I really enjoyed how unique the flavors were though, as brunch is pretty standard at most places these days. Overall a good experience!

Best place everrrrrrrrrrrr
Came from LA to visit fam in SF. On our last day we wanted to get something good before our drive back. Couldnt have stumbled upon a better option than this. Drinks & food are to die for

Loved my time here!

Came with some classmates. We came around 10AM, party of 6, no reservation, and our wait was pretty short. (When we left there was a lot of people waiting outside though, so get here early).

I ordered a volcano coffee and a k bomb chicken Benny. Both were sooo good. It was the first time I had whipped coffee and I loved the texture but also how concentrated it was -- even mixed with the milk, it wasn't watered down. The chicken benny was served with potatoes and salad. The chicken was crispy but also flavorful. You could taste the sauce but it didn't make it soggy. The serving size was perfect.

Had a great time here!

The food, service, and ambiance were all great! We looked up breakfast places in the city and this one popped up so we decided to try it. It's a small place on Mission street that we almost missed (had to go around the block and keep looking lol) but we found it and inside it was very cute and cozy. The staff was very friendly and all the food was amazing. We will definitely be back!

4.5 stars for brunch in the casual restaurant.

The food was delicious and unique. Particularly, the crème brûlée French toast which I would totally come back for. The chicken and waffle was good. There is a savory sauce that complements the sweet one.

Drinks are instaworthy, but you're probably better off at specialty dessert store. They tasted a bit watered down.

Service was professional and efficient. Getting on the Yelp waitlist before coming is ideal to avoid waiting.

I visited with friends and the food was tasty.
Drinks are also cool.
Environment inside was also nice and service was fast!
For dishes, we tried Pacific Sunrise, K-Bomb Benny, K-Bomb Chicken Sandwich, Chicken & Waffle, Mascarpone Pancake (delicious ) and French Toast Crème Brûlée.
Drinks that we tried: Volcano Coffee, Butterfly Lychee, Mocha Lava, Matcha Strawberry and Matcha Latte all delicious.
Definitely recommend this brunch place for a try!

Very cute brunch spot with entrees that aren't too heavy. The dishes look super filling but aren't as greasy or heavy as other brunch spots.

The mascarpone pancakes were super fluffy and topped with a lightly sweet cream. I didn't use much of the syrup since the pancakes and cream were already sweet but all together it was delish!

I tried to chicken sausage scramble and that was also easy to eat.

I ordered an oat milk matcha which was a touch too sweet for me. Delicious but will definitely opt for almond milk next time.

Went here for brunch. It's street parking only. There were a few parties ahead of us but we got seated pretty quickly. Staff were friendly but they were pretty busy so service was a little slow. I got the chicken and waffles with strawberry matcha. But all the food and drinks I got was pretty good. They had some sauce for the fried chicken which was sweet and tangy which was delicious. I'd recommend coming here, it was delicious and a good experience.
Great food, great atmosphere and great service. We had chipotle, classical cheeseburger, mascarpone pancake, volcano coffee, house coffee, beef bacon

I was excited to try this place but unfortunately I think it's overhyped. There's a section of the menu called "Instagrammable Drinks" and that tells you a lot.

Anyway, the food was good but not spectacular and certainly not worth the crazy wait. Luckily my party had a reservation but for people who were on the standby wait list, I don't think it's worth the wait. Yes the presentation of the food and drink are beautiful, yes "instagrammable". I had the chicken and waffles and unfortunately was underwhelmed. The breading on the chicken was THICK and honestly I don't mind thick breading in of itself (I actually usually love it), but it had zero seasoning and it was so thick that the innermost part touching the chicken was slightly under in some places. The mascarpone pancakes were okay, pretty fluffy. The rest of my party said their food was good too but not necessarily outstanding. Much more a feast for the eyes than anything.

This was a random pick for us on Yelp, and it did not disappoint. Their burger was delicious, flavorful, and juicy. Fries were seasoned well. Their Bloody Mary had a great mix. The staff were very attentive even though it was very busy. I recommend making a reservation through yelp, it made things really easy for us. The restaurant is very aesthetically pleasing to the eye.

Solid brunch spot. The coffee drinks are perfect. The service was great. Cool vibe inside. Parking g can be a challenge. Fried chicken was delicious as were the shrimp. Potatoes were hard and a bit cold and the chicken sausage seemed old.

Came here for brunch the other weekend and had a great time! We ordered kbomb eggs benny, crispy chicken sandwich and creme brûlée French toast to share. The chicken sandwich was well executed and the fries were perfectly crisp. The eggs benny was also great, the portions are pretty generous for SF prices and I enjoyed the spin on a classic. The reason I'm giving this place 4 instead of 5 stars is because the food wasn't very hot when it came out, I assume they make multiples of most popular dishes regardless of what orders are coming in, so maybe it's not made to order? The creme brûlée French toast was good but not great, maybe I'd try their pancakes next time!

Cute, very busy restaurant in Bernal Heights with an inventive and trendy brunch menu. Their creme brulee french toast was lovely without an overwhelming sweetness which surprised me. The Korean chicken benedict tastes exactly as you would expect. Fun to try, not something I would crave. Definitely choose a drink other than their matchas, there are plentiful options!

My new favorite brunch place! Came in on a Friday morning and it was already packed. However we came right as they were cleaning a table so they sat us down right away. Staff was kind and attentive. We got everything we ordered within 10 minutes.

For drinks we got the volcano coffee and the butterfly lychee. Coffee was basically dalgona coffee. Both drinks were the right amount of sweetness and definitely Instagram photo-worthy.

Now onto the food!
Crème brûlée French toast: very heavy on the brûlée mix which is a good thing. The burnt caramelization was perfect.

Mascarpone pancake: this was just okay. Couldn't really taste the mascarpone but then again it's a very mild flavor

K-bomb chicken benny: the star of the show. The Korean fried chicken was super crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. My fiancé usually isn't a fan of eggs benedict but this meal changed his mind.

The reason I'm giving 5 stars is for the french toast and especially the chicken eggs benedict. Will definitely come back and order these 2 entrees again.

TLDR: Despite there being extremely limited parking, as everything is in SF, this is a nice brunch spot in the city that allows you to either set up a reservation or walk in and get on the waitlist. This is definitely a spot that you need to get to early otherwise you could be waiting easily for an hour or more. My friend and I went for their brunch menu and we got there mid afternoon and had to wait ~45min. Once we looked at the menu, we were split between sweet and savory, so you know we had to get both. Everything had a nice Asian flavor to breakfast classics, which is what drew me out to this spot. Everything about this place is definitely an instagrammable because the plating and the aesthetics inside are beautiful.

Food/Drinks: 4/5
Like I mentioned above, the Asian flavors on breakfast classics was what I loved most about these dishes. I got the kbomb chicken eggs benedict which had a lemon/citrus hollandaise sauce on top. The kbomb chicken is how I expected the korean fried chicken to taste, but the hollandaise sauce was more citrusy than I was expecting for what they called their chipotle hollandaise sauce. Don't get me wrong, it was tasty, just wasn't what I had expected. The mango matcha latte isn't something I'd get again as it really didn't have a good quality matcha flavor I'm used to getting at matcha spots, but it isn't super sweet which was nice. My friend got the marscapone pancakes which she loved. They were really fluffy and had a nice creamy marscapone flavor, but they were on the sweeter side of things. She also got the volcano coffee, which she said is a good option for coffee lovers. We both agreed we'd want to go back and try the omlettes.

Service/Staff: 5/5
The staff were really kind and got us seated as soon as it was our turn. Since we had the time to wait and look over the menu, we were able to order after we sat down. The drinks came out within 5min of ordering, and the rest came out in the next 10min. We didn't feel too rushed to finish despite the line being long.

Space: 4/5
While the interior design is stunning and aesthetic, it is on the smaller side. But, at the same time, the space was maximized fairly well. Parking was pretty much nonexistent, so I would highly recommend parking nearby and taking a walk to the restaurant. If you're looking insta worthy pics, you'll definitely be able to get some here!

LOVE LOVE LOVE THIS PLACE!

Cute & aesthetic brunch place. We added ourselves to the waitlist via Yelp so we only had to wait about 5-10 mins even though the place was packed.
