Absolutely love this place!! The food is outstanding!! The service can be a little slow but that's just because they're really busy. The waitress do it all and try their best and do such a good job! the place is cute too such a vibe!! highly recommend this place they have the best chicken and waffles I've ever had! we also ordered the chipotle benedict, but that didn't make it to The photo opp. The drinks we got were super cute and super tasty. Definitely recommend those as well.

The line of people waiting to enter is always a good sign. With that said, get there early or plan ahead and reserve a spot online. After a few visits, what I have noticed is that this spot is consistent. The photos of the great looking food online are not fake. The food actually taste as good as it looks. Be prepared to enjoy plates of goodness. The drinks are also tasty and refreshing. The interior is crammed with tables and chairs to accommodate small to large parties, so it tends to be about average for noise. Prices are reasonable for the awesome food and drinks. Enjoy.

I've been here a few times, and the food and service are always great. There can sometimes be a wait, but if you have a reservation, it's quick. The food and drinks both are so yummy. Would reccomend!!

First time trying four chairs. I went on a Saturday afternoon. The wait to get in was about 30 minutes and outdoors, but my group was able to use this time to plan what to order. Once inside, we were seated to our table. The staff was quick to take our order.

We ordered three dishes, and this was plenty for the four of us. We got the southwest scramble and Okonomiyaki fries. The fries were okay, but the scramble was really good!

The City was hot the day we went, and there was not that much ventilation, so it was hot inside.

Parking is competitive and limited to street. Restroom is well kept.

This brunch spot is quickly gaining popularity for good reason. Fast and friendly service, a lovely ambiance, and delicious and visually pleasing dishes with large portions are the highlights of this up-and-coming restaurant.

Note that they take reservations through Yelp on weekdays but not on Saturday/Sunday. They're only open for breakfast/lunch and they're closed on Tuesdays.

We arrived around lunch time on a Sunday. We added ourselves to their Yelp waitlist in person on their tablet. We had about 18 parties ahead of us (estimated wait time of 30-45 minutes). If you have a long wait, I recommend looking at the menu, deciding what to eat so you can order right away, and then walking down Mission and then taking a left towards Bernal Peak for stunning city views or a left on Cortland Ave which is a nicer street/area with cute cafes and shops. You can keep an eye on your place in line through the Yelp link they text you. We were seated in about 30 minutes so the line moves quickly.

The ambiance is trendy, warm, and modern. The space is large but packed. We had to squeeze in between tables to get to ours. We were also seated next to an open storage space which was awkward. It would have been nice if they placed a large divider there or something.

The service was good. Staff are pretty friendly and very efficient. They don't waste any time here - food comes out quickly.

K-Bomb Chicken Benny - 5/5 - So good! Nice big portion size as well. The potatoes were seasoned and cooked to perfection with a slightly crispy exterior and soft interior. The chicken was covered in crispy breading and a generous amount of sauce. If you like a sweet and spicy or sweet and sour combo, you'll love the flavors of this chicken. It also paired well with the eggs benedict (eggs were perfectly runny). I didn't taste the chipotle in the hollandaise sauce, but I was fine with that. I did like how the salad had with a light and savory dressing to offset the sweet chicken.

Creme Brûlée French Toast - 2/5 - I was so excited about this but disappointed overall. Visually, the dish is Instagram-worthy, but the taste was lacking. The bread wasn't eggy enough to be "French toast" and the cream did not soak into it well, so it tasted like plain white bread with cream on top. The caramelized sugar added a delicious crunch, but it was only on the top and not on the bottom slice of bread. I accidentally got some of the rosemary garnish in my portion and it was way too overpowering and threw off the taste, so I suggest removing the garnish.

I also tried the Chipotle Benny which was packed with flavor and is a nice choice for those who prefer a more savory dish.

Overall, we were happy with the experience and would return in the future!

Four Chairs is a new American brunch restaurant with an Asian fusion-y twist. For a walk-in, we were told the wait would be 40 mins, but we only ended up waiting for 15.

I got the Chicken Apple Scramble, and I though it was the perfect combination of salty, sweet, and smoky. My friend got the K-Bomb Chicken Benny. The English muffin was crispy and dense on the outside and soft on the inside. The fried chicken was crispy and moist with a gochujang based seasoning.

Service was friendly and warm. The orders took longer than expected. Staff was apologetic, and they kindly offered water while we waited.

The interior was very contemporary and casual.
Four chairsIt is a cozy restaurant and spectacular service, exquisite food, they have their own personality and full of love in all their dishes! Excellent mango tea
The food was really good. I would highly recommend. It got busy really quick. I'd recommend going early to grab a table. But worth the wait!

The waffles and chicken were SOO GOOD! I would go back again! The tea went well with the food. I was hesitant to have it because I've never had chicken and waffles together before but it was delicious!

Amazing spot for brunch in Bernal Heights!

I came here for brunch Sunday afternoon at noon with 2 other friends. You can check in beforehand through Yelp waitlist, but we added ourselves to the waitlist after we got there and the wait was only ~5 minutes.

The brunch menu is a bit on the basic side and mostly features benedicts, omelets, scrambles, and some sweet options.

I opted for the chicken and waffle ($15) and the non-alcoholic drink Butterfly Lychee ($7). The drink was absolutely gorgeous with the purple and was the best lychee drink I've had in a while. My friend also ordered it and agreed.

For food, I absolutely loved the chicken and waffle! It comes with two pieces of fried chicken, one thigh and one drumstick, and both were fried to a perfect crisp. The waffle was a bit crispy and was delicious with some of the butter and syrup.

Another friend ordered the Lively omelet ($17) and enjoyed it as well. I tried a bite of his potatoes; they were roasted with some herbs and had a bit of a crunch to them.

All of us were very satisfied with our meal here. Would highly recommend Four Chairs for an amazing brunch!
Awesome ambiance, food and staff. I would like to come back to this place again. It's a nice go to restaurant

We were headed to another brunch place and decided to try Four Chairs when we saw that there was no waitlist.

Bufferfly lychee - 3.5/5, strong lychee flavor. I thought it was a little sweet or the flavor was artificial. I didn't really taste the tea. It reminded me of Calpico a lot lol. It's a nice drink to try for fun, but won't be getting it next time.

Chicken and waffles - 4/5, a light crispy waffle topped with two big pieces of thigh and drum meat. It came with butter, syrup, and sweet and sour sauce. The chicken was fried super crunchy and came out piping hot. Chicken was juicy and tender, not too much flavor in it so it paired nicely with the sweet and sour sauce. It also went well with the waffle, which was quite good but got a bit soggy.

K bomb benny - 4.5/5, korean fried chicken with eggs benny on a sourdough toast, potatoes and salad on the side. The chicken was tasty with a sticky sweet and slightly tangy sauce. It could be better if it had a bit of spice! The potatoes were delicious and crispy, definitely one of the best. The benny was your standard benny, only thing is the bread gets soggy since there's nothing between the bread and egg.

K bomb burger - 4.5/5, same chicken for the benny. Comes with cabbage and lots of sauce. Good burger. Fries were regular fries, just ok. Would def prefer the potatoes that come with the benny!

I came for weekend brunch with a friend and enjoyed the K-bomb benny, which was a unique twist on the typical eggs benedict. Super filling and tasty. The volcano coffee was also great, albeit very strong. Make sure to come early and put your name on the waitlist ahead of time to avoid long waits. Super glad I tried it, but not sure it's my favorite brunch spot in the city.

The food was amazing we got the Pacific Bay Benedict and the delicious lava coffee! I would recommend this to everyone, at least once. And I guarantee that you'll be back especially for the price! Love it and I can't wait to go back.

Solid brunch spot with some good unique favorites and also the classics. Fun place to go with groups, grab a mimosa and enjoy the day! Tip: join waitlist ahead of time if possible to avoid waiting in line as this place is popular.

Eggs Benedict and the chicken and waffle were big hits. Crispy chicken burger was decently sized and indeed crispy but lacked flavor, the aioli sauce was not memorable.

This place is worth the hype in my opinion. The food was soooo good. And so were the drinks! Even though the wait was kind of long I think it's worth it. The place is a bit smaller than I thought so it was a bit warmer than I would have personally liked inside, but you aren't touching shoulders with the people next to you so it's fine! The staff was super nice and accommodated my slightly bigger than average brunch group so I would recommend just because of that!

Came here for a late lunch on a Sunday afternoon and surprisingly, we were seated right away, so that's a plus!

I ordered the chipotle eggs Benedict and it was good, the poached eggs were cooked perfectly, had a nice kick from the jalapeño but wish it was just a bit spicer. The meal was beautifully plated. The potatoes were nice and crispy.

Hubby got the side of French toast with eggs, bacon and sausage, and did not complain.

We also ordered the chicken and waffle - the chicken was slightly under cooked and not crispy as we'd like. The batter had a hint of sweetness to it which was different but good. If they cooked the chicken a bit longer, it would have been a hit. The waffle was very delicious, it almost reminded me of a churro, very good.

Freshly squeezed OJ was great, but very pricey for OJ, $7!
really great food and good portions. i got the chicken and waffles and my friend got a burger; both were super filling and i think at a good price point for this kind of brunch food.
Everything was good, but the K-Bomb Benny was the winner. I'm not a huge pancake fan, but these were great.
Tried this place for the first time. The food and ambience was good. It was very busy with a wait line out the door
This place left a great impression, the service was friendly and efficient, the food was fresh and enjoyable, the atmosphere was cozy and inviting, I would love to come back again.

Amazing food and great atmosphere!
Definitely coming back!! Everything was delicious and the stuff was good!!

Went here for my friends birthday! It was such a great environment, clean space, and a great menu. We loved the drinks and we couldn't get enough of their waffles. Our waitress was the best and made her birthday extra special ! We'll definitely be back

I have been wanting to try this brunch spot for a while and half expected the line to be too long. Luckily, it wasn't too bad on a Monday around lunch time. I waited 20-25 minutes and was seated by a nice gentleman. It was really crowded but not too noisy. I have been craving fried chicken so I ordered the chicken and waffles with 2 eggs and a fruit cup on the side. The dish was good with 2 syrups and included. 1 was maple syrup and the other was like a spicy Thai style chili sauce for the chicken. The eggs were cooked perfectly over easy and the fruit cup was filled with fresh blueberries, raspberries and orange wedges. You can tell they really take their time to make sure everything looks and tastes great. The only criticism I have is the batter for the fried chicken didn't have any flavor.
Creme brulee french toast was perfectly sweet and creamy. Pacific Sunrise included runny eggs, crispy potatoes, a bright salad, and fresh smoked salmon.

Four Chairs has been a highly coveted brunch spot right in the Mission District. This spot gets so packed naturally on the weekends that they only allow reservations for large parties.

I ended up coming here on a Friday and was able to secure a reservation. We only had to wait a few minutes. I got to try their Korean fried chicken sandwich. The chicken was saucy and juicy while the fries were well seasoned and had a nice crunch to it. I didn't get a drink Four Chairs is known for their brightly-colored and creative drinks whether its a mocktail or cocktail.

The service is fairly quick for a busy restaurant. Table turnover is high and nearly all tables were occupied to full capacity.

The wait is long and if your entire party isn't there you will not be seated and lose your table. Staff is really kind and fast.

Food is delicious! I love that bill times are not long waits. Once you order you'll have your food arrive fairly quick.

The restaurant is cute and perfect for many occasions.

We ordered the Leafy Green, Lively, and Mascarpone Pancakes along with the Volcano Coffee, Bloody Mary, and the Butterfly Lychee.

2 out of the 3 dishes were great. The Leafy Green Benedict with the Meyer hollandaise was really good and cooked well. The muffin could've been toasted a bit more but otherwise was great. The Lively omelette was tasty and the potatoes were cooked well, crisp on the outside and soft in the middle.

The pancakes were really bad and we had to send it back. Strong taste of baking soda and they were rather dense and flat. I gave that feedback to the server.

The drinks were great! I think the Volcano Coffee is very large and I didn't need that much coffee. I didn't find it too sweet but my partner did. The other two drinks were really great also. Can't go wrong with lychee.

The service could have been a lot better. They were obviously so overloaded and understaffed on a Sunday. We waited quite a while for our server to take our order and our food came out at different times.

The ambiance is fine. Very basic but still nice and clean. Overall, would return but maybe on a different day.

FOOD: Portobello mushroom. Looked very tasty but wasn't. I left hungry. The mushroom tasted dirty and rotten. The mushroom it self had no flavor nor seasoning. Not what I was expecting. The breading was perfect. I ate some of the bun with my potatoes.
The strawberry lemonade was good enough to finish. Maybe switching the mushroom to lions mane or another mushroom

SERVICE: I told the server I didn't like the hamburger. I wasn't offered another meal no was it taken off my check

VEGAN: Portobello mushroom, potato's

PARKING: limited had to park around the corner on the other side of the block

ATMOSPHERE: Pleasant decoration felt more of a high end brunch/lunch location.

We went on a Friday for brunch and there was no wait! Loved that for us lol we got seated right away and everything sounded delicious. I ordered the kinder garden scramble and my gf ordered the k bomb chicken benny. Also, we shared the mascarpone pancakes. We loved everything!
It's definitely an aesthetic place with good food. There's even a section on the menu with Instagram friendly drinks .

Delivery launch. Tried the K Bomb chicken sandwich and the volcano coffee. The sandwich came with a side of FF. (this was unclear win the menu) it has a great taste. A good crispy crunch, sweet, and a little spicy. It was topped with slaw and pickle on a fresh bun. I would order this again. The volcano coffee came in the same bag, with plastic wrap around it, which it fell over en route causing it to leak out. I would recommend a better technique for delivery. The taste of the coffee was lovely, unfortunately I didnt ge. t the full effect of the drink, as it was mixed for me possibly due to delivery. The small cubes of ice in the drink are very nice.

Food:
5/5
it was soo good and flavorful. Each item had its unique twist.

Ambience:
5/5
Great lunch vibes and their drinks weren't too sweet or overpowering

Service:
5/5
They had fast service. All the employees were super friendly and helpful as well.

Overall we waited about 20 minutes for a table of 2 and the place was packed.

Traffic in the City got my friend and I turned around, looking for a different brunch spot from our intended destination. I am so glad it did! We started with the Crème Brûlée French Toast as an appetizer. It was our lazy Sunday brunch so we can start the meal however we like right? It wasn't too sweet and hit the creamy notes that was just very satisfying. Then our meals came out looking just like the pictures. I had the K Bomb Benny and my friend got the salmon Benedict. Both delicious in their own right! Oh, and the service was good too! Can't wait to come back and do brunch again!
food was good!! the chicken was coated in a flavorful sauce and it was so filling, hard to get a res so need to plan ahead of time. it was fairly crowded on a friday morning

Firstly, FOUR CHAIRS DOES NOT HAVE FOUR CHAIRS... they have about over 40 CHAIRS!!! Secondly, their food and staff were equally amazing. I've heard a lot about this place on instagram so I thought I'd check it out. I'm a SF native btw and never heard of this place. This was my first solo dining experience ever and I enjoyed every moment. I came in on a weekday a little right after opening (no line, but restaurant was half packed), ordered the nova Benny, which exceeded my expectations, salad was great and even the potatoes were good, along side with a glass of butterfly lychee, soju added. Everything was so flavorful. Definitely will be coming back!!

Excellent good especially the burger with bacon
The Benny chicken breakfast item was great as well
Dalgona coffee is good

Visited Four Chairs for brunch with my girls on a Friday afternoon, and the restaurant was empty for the most part. With high hopes from the pretty visuals on Yelp, I would say that my food was not up to par.

Chicken and waffles- waffle was way too crispy, lacking the fluffy soft dough texture. The chicken was also super crispy, but lacked flavor, making it hard to enjoy. The entire dish felt overly fried and I had to remove the chicken batter to eat the chicken.

My friends' omelette and pancakes looked pretty good, so maybe I just chose the wrong dish.

Service was wonderful, and our waitress seems super sweet. Will probably not come back, as there are comparable brunch spots in SF, but was worth a try!

This was our first stop after landing in San Francisco!! Food was amazing and service was good, the workers there are super attentive and nice. We waited about 15 minutes for our table but time went by quickly because there's places around you can walk to and just window shop. Definitely recommend!!

Had the best time at this restaurant, I arrived when it opened and so glad as the restaurant filled completely by 930am. The Korean Chicken Benedict was so tasty and the pancakes were fluffy and presented beautifully. The French Toast did not disappoint. They only serve beef bacon or turkey bacon so no pork. Delighted to try this restaurant as I've been seeing it on social media for so long. Great spot for breakfast with friends so everyone can try their creative dishes. Service was prompt and polite and the restaurant had a fun vibe!
The food was so good. The lighting was nice and warm too made for a great dining experience. A place you could take a date too. Busy though.

Just wanted to revisit this review because I came here again on a rainy day but discovered I got here an hour before opening! After a long drive to the city, paying for the sparse street parking, and getting wet under the rain... I felt so defeated :(

But the staff were so kind and let my sisters and I in the restaurant to keep us warm (I was ready to go back to my freezing car). They even took our order maybe 20-30 minutes before the opening time.

I was so grateful & was very excited to show my siblings the great food I ate here last time. Last time, my friend ordered the Lychee Butterfly drink & I really wanted to order it this time. It is such a yummy drink, and when I was paying out, the staff told me they'll void my drink since we waited so long (I should have ordered more drinks, LOL).

The staff here are so sweet & the food is very yummy. Thank you & good luck with the business!

This place is sooo good. A lot of items on the Yelp photo gallery aren't available anymore actually :(

I got the Chipotle Benedict & it was a 5/5. I went last Saturday, and every time I come across this photo I instantly crave it! Definitely try this brunch place next time you're in SF. Park near the houses!

Four Chairs was definitely popping even though we arrived relatively early for brunch. We joined the wait-list right around 10AM, and our table was ready earlier than the expected wait time. You'll need your full party to be present to be seated, so plan accordingly. It does get pretty packed here even though there's plenty of tables.

For our table of four, we decided to get a shared plate of Okonomiyaki Fries. For my entree, I got a Muchroom Salad, cheese on the side. And I got one of their Instagrammable drink, the Mango Matcha Latte. My partner got their K-bomb Chicken Benny and an Arnold Palmer.

Okonomiyaki Fries came first - and it was savory, a bit vinegary, but also tad salty and creamy with the Kewpie mayo. They were pretty generous with their bonito flake, which added a nice savory flavor to it as well. It's a nice shareable appetizer since portion is generous.

It took a while for our drinks and entree to come, but they serve everyone's entree at the same time. My Muchroom salad was better than I expected. I was actually debating between The Original Benedict or a salad, and in the end I'm glad I landed with the salad, since portion looked pretty big. My salad came with plenty of grilled mushrooms, yum! The greens were fresh and the vinaigrette wasn't too tart. I think it would be even better if they added more mushroom varieties and something creamy to the mix, like avocado, but alas, it's probably not something people normally go for at this place. My drink on the other hand, was surprisingly pretty good. I never mix my Matcha with fruits and such - usually just have a plain Matcha Latte, but it looks like they only serve Matcha with Mango or Strawberry puree. The Mango puree at the bottom was thick and sweet. So delicious. It mixes well with Matcha, and it looks amazing, but I'd still opt for a plain one if given the choice!

I also got to sample my partner's dish - the K-bomb Benny! The chicken patty was battered and fried like a Korean Sweet and Spicy fried chicken. A bit saucy, but delicious. It's interesting how they served it on ciabatta, so I'm not sure it even counts as a Benedict, but it works. Full of flavor and wasn't dry. His Arnold Palmer was refreshing and light, I almost wish I got one instead.

Service was really friendly! Just make sure to wait-list and plan accordingly if you don't want to wait for too long. Was it worth it? For a party of four and everything that we got, I thought it was. Check this place out if you're looking for something aesthetically pleasing, appetizing, and yummy.

Came in here on a Monday afternoon. We were seated immediately and it was a fairly full lobby with only a few open seats. I would advise to reserve on yelp on busier days like the weekends as this space is quaint but still very accommodating. The staff was very friendly and recommended we split a mimosa pitcher as it would be cheaper and get us more bang for our buck! We tried the creme brulee French toast, chipotle benedict & k bomb chicken sandwich. Every thing tasted fresh and delicious! There were so mony other things on the menu we wanted to try so we will definitely be back!
Foods are fantastic. Nice fusion branch. The place is packed. Line is long. You may park your car in Safeway a block a way

My friend and I came on a Saturday around noon, and we waited about an hour before we were seated. We ordered the k-bomb chicken benny, okonomiyaki fries, mascarpone pancake to share, and each had the volcano (dalgona) coffee. The fries were good, but I'm not sure if I be dying to order them again (7/10 rating). They're good if you are craving that creamy mayo, zesty eel sauce, smoked bonito flakes, and toasted nori seasoning though. The k-bomb chicken benny was great for a savory dish, and the mascarpone pancakes for sweet. I'd recommend both if you're coming with a friend to share. Chicken was moist and crisp, and Benedict style eggs were standard - I'd rate the plate maybe 7.5/10. Mascarpone pancakes were stacked, incredibly soft and fluffy; 8.5/10. And finally, we had to give the volcano coffee a chance - soooo yummy, 9/10. It definitely gave me flashbacks to the dalgona trend during TikTok, made to a sweet perfection.

The ambiance was loud and bustling with a lot of guests inside. My friend and I had to speak a bit louder to get our words across the table, but I guess that's brunch time for you. The presentation of the food was gorgeous, and definitely Instagrammable. Solid brunch place if you want standard good brunch food, photos for your food blog, and if you don't mind waiting a while to get seated.

We joined the waitlist and waited....waited....waited...-along with several other groups!! Checked in the kiosk and our waitlist/phone # wasn't found!! Along with the other 2 groups!! Crazy. I have the text showing we were on the waitlist!!

Servers inside had no clue. Took 3 people coming over to ask what the problem was. DISASTER!!

Can only imagine the food and service inside!

$8 for a single, 6" pancake. Unreal!!

I was supposed to take my MIL for brunch at Glen Park Cafe on Monday but didn't realize they were closed so I found this spot. Thank goodness for Yelp wait list, I added myself then drove over and found myself a nice parking spot across the street. By the time I arrived, I was ready to be seated so I love the efficiency of it. The neighborhood was unassuming and we didn't expect to find such a gorgeously decorated brunch spot! My MIL and I both got the lychee drink and it was very delicious - I love lychee anything and this had very good flavor without tasting like heaps of lychee syrup. I got the creme brulee french toast and it came with 2 slices of French toast, mhmmm. It was expecting this to be overly sweet but it was a nice surprise that it wasn't. The only thing I would say is to add creme brulee topping on both toast pieces. It's only on the top slice...

Anyways, a very solid brunch spot with a great wait list system. Staff is friendly and they turn the tables quickly!

Wow! What an incredible brunch spot! Came here at 9AM on a Sunday morning and my friend and I had a wonderful meal here (there was no wait because we went right at opening). They have some cool drinks and nova benedict that I had was superb as well. Street parking was pretty easy since we went early, but it might be more complicated later in the day. I would highly recommend you try this place if you're a big fan of brunch!

My friend and I stopped by on a rainy Saturday morning after working out at the gym. There was no wait and we were seated right away. We shared two plates:

Grilled Chicken Avocado (Grilled chicken breast, mixed greens, avocado, cherry tomato, red onion, cucumber with ranch)

Lively Omelete (Spinach, avocado, green bell pepper, red onion, scallion, cheddar)

The food was delicious! It looks like their fried chicken and waffles is very popular since I saw a few tables around us order this dish. Their volcano coffee also looks amazing and I will definitely order this the next time I'm there. The vibes in the restaurant are laid back and inviting. We could totally hear the tables conversation next to us but it didn't bother me. I will definitely be back here.

Great vibes

The food was standard brunch food and to be honestly, felt like it was a bit over priced. I got the crème brule french toast and a matcha drink which I enjoyed
Amazing foo. This is my fav restaurant ever. The chicken is elite and the food is so pretty. Service is great too.

Amazing food. All of the plates we ordered were delicious, definitely worth the wait. We were taking pics of the food and a waiter came with the drinks and told us to wait so we could take a picture with the drinks as well and it was the cutest thing ever. Ordered the korean eggs benedict and the Korean fried chicken was amazing.

Four Chairs is a hidden gem located in the more quiet neighborhood of Bernal Heights.

HIGHLY recommend getting there early or making a reservation since its always crazy busy.

The service is great. Servers are always smiling and are attentive. Their food is amazing. Been here several times and you MUST order the Mascarpone Pancakes. So fluffy and light, but flavorful and filling. My go to order is the K-Bomb Benny. 10/10. Their house coffee is solid too. Four Chairs provides excellent food that's plated and presented nicely for pictures. The interior of the restaurant is clean and modern, providing a nice aesthetic.

Whether you're visiting or a local, I recommend checking this place out. Hands down my favorite brunch place in the city.

Still trying to figure out this restaurant. Service is great and restaurant is very stylish. I can see people loving taking pictures of food and restaurant.
For me, coffee was ok, I notice a lot of people didn't finish their coffee. More for the picture reason...
I did enjoy the pancakes, less of chicken.
We tried three different drinks and mango drinks were good and Matcha drink was ok.

We tried twice and I don't think I will be back for a while. But I think it will be fun to try at once, just watch out the waiting line if you don't like it :)

Went for Saturday brunch around 11am and had to wait around 45 mins for a table of 2. There is. Yelp waitlist you can join beforehand so would recommend doing that.

My friend and I got the volcano coffees which reminded us of dalgona coffees. And then got a vegetarian egg scramble and the crème brûlée French toast. Both were pretty good and decent portion sizes. Never seen a crème brûlée French toast before so that was a unique dish to try.

Service was pretty fast for how packed it was inside, but overall had a good experience here.

Four Chairs is a lovely breakfast/brunch place. Personable and attentive staff, and they're all so beautiful too. We arrived w/o a resie but signed in and waited about 5-10 mins on a brunch-ish Sunday.
It's busy and kinda loud, inside lots of seatings and one communal table for bigger groups. Our servers worked together, one who took orders, one who tended the tables, and one who bussed'em were fast and efficient! Food & drinks were delicious! My daughter killed their Okonomiyaki fries w/ the shaved bonito flakes were umami-licious ! She also ordered the mascarpone pancakes that were heavenly! Nova Benny, Southwest Scramble, BLTA sammie were also very good and filling! Huge portions equally priced entrees...great restu! We shall be back!
made a reservation for 1:30 pm, however had to a wait a little bit which is no problem. mimosa pitcher for $25 with choice of orange or cranberry i believe?

This place is so delicious. It's influenced by Korean, Mexican and traditional American cuisine and let me tell you it's sooo freaking good!
I took my bestie and mom to this place and we all had a great time. Perfect brunch spot and vibes.
The service was wonderful too. The staff was courteous and someone went around constantly refilling cup of coffees and table water. I didn't have to ask for refills. It was great.

There's street parking
One can get in- line via Yelp for faster service.
And you can also order to-go if you don't feel like dinning in.
This is def a spot to try.
Enjoy!

Came here for the first time for brunch around 11am on a Saturday, and it was bustling! We got lucky and didn't have to wait too long for a table, but there was constantly a line out the door as we were eating. The interior was super cute and aesthetic too! There is a QR code at the table to scan for the menu, but it was super blurry and we ended up using photos on yelp to help us decide what to get. We got:

- Four Chairs Benny - the bacon was the star of the show! The perfect mix of sweet and savory, not to mention a huge portion of it! The potatoes were also really good, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. Would definitely order this again.
- French Toast - super aesthetic and nicely plated, but unfortunately it looked better than it tasted in my opinion. I thought it could've definitely used more flavor. No major complaints but also nothing special at all, taste wise. Probably wouldn't get this again.
- Sangria pitcher - solid in terms of taste, but the pitcher was smaller than I expected. Each person only got about half a glass (5 people), so not sure it was worth the price.
- Butterfly lychee - seems to be their most common drink! I tried my friend's and it was really good! Think a light, sweet, butterfly-pea lychee blend. Non-alcoholic and super aesthetic for the photos.

Overall, I would come back for the Four Chairs Benny OR to try something new, but not sure if I would wait more than 10-15 minutes for a table. Super aesthetic interior and plating, but I'd personally want to try other brunch spots in SF before coming back again.

The place is reallyyyy cute, very chill vibes, definitely casual breakfast/brunch place. When we walked in we added our names to the list but there was no one there to greet you at the door. Nevertheless we were seated after a few minutes. But unfortunately no one greeted us at the table, we actually had to wave someone down after about 10 minutes because no one said anything.

Once we got drinks it went UPHILL! The coffee they use is absolutely DELICIOUS, and their honey is flavored and tea is very unique! The drinks were lovely!

The food was pretty good too! It came out well seasoned, hot, and tasty!
Favorite fusion brunch in SF. The drinks are so fun (mocktails). Wait time is a little long but so worth it!

There was surprisingly no wait so we got seated immediately. I never know what to expect with restaurants in SF since they are a huge hit or miss, and the last time I was in the city, it was a bit of a miss every time. but four chairs did not disappoint! 
- chipotle benedict - slight flavoring but not overpowering, still recommend k-bomb benny over chipotle benedict though
- k-bomb benny (benedict) - AMAZING. highly recommend this dish! packed with so much flavor and great portion size
- chicken & waffles
- okonomiyaki fries - pretty big portion even for a side, couldn't finish it
- thai iced tea
- matcha mango latte with almond milk - was better towards the end
- volcano coffee

Food, vibes, drinks, and service were all amazing! One of my fave brunch spots in SF

We got the kbomb benny which indeed tasted bomb the only thing I'd change would be the bread, it needed more flavor and it's not toasted enough so it just gets soggy with the egg. The French toast was good but wish they'd bring it out later so it would be more warm and fresh! The chipotle Benedict was also really good but again the soggy bread problem. The volcano coffee was strong which I liked but wished it was a bit sweeter. The butterfly lychee was sooo good I loved it, super refreshing and just the right amount of sweetness!

Overall would recommend trying this spot out if you're in the Bay Area!

We went ~12 pm on Friday and had to wait 20 minutes for a table for two. The waiter was friendly. We ordered the loco plate scramble, which was my favorite -- it was so delicious. The Hawaiian omelette was pretty good too. Would come back again for the loco plate.

Four chairs is all the hype in the last few months.

Ordered
k-bomb Benny - chicken has a great taste not too sweet just a perfect balance INMO.
The original Benny w/ avocado( I added) which I like that it was spread at bottom of the muffin or bread because the it's a thick piece of bread then your typical english muffin. This was good not over the top
Start of the show was the Crème Brûlée French toast. Will definitely be coming back for that.

We were seated in the middle which is not my fave since it can get tight in there once it's busy.

It was my first time there on Wednesday around 11am and is was busy with only 2 servers. Which as much hype this place has they need at least 4. They were both friendly but seemed a bit overwhelmed as when we were leaving there was a line full of folks to be seated and the place was full.

A group of friends and I came here for brunch on a Saturday morning around 10:30am and got seated by the window fairly quickly (shout out my bf for joining the waitlist beforehand).

As a group we ordered a few different items and thought they were all fairly good. I ordered the Four Chair Benny and really liked that it came with a side salad and the citrus in the hollandaise sauce because the bacon was very succulent. The bacon itself was thick cut and had a nice sweetness to it, but I do wish it had a better seat or some crispness. The homie home fries (potatoes) were also super yummy and crispy!

I would definitely come back to try the French Toast/pancakes because they also looked so yummy!

Our overall rating for Four Chairs is 3.5 stars, but we round up in our house :)

Perfect brunch! I love Asian fusion brunch spots and this place did well. We were a party of four which is perfect for family style brunch. We ordered:

-Chicken and waffle: 5 stars. I loved the fried chicken seasoning. Very flavorful. And the waffle was crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.
-Citrus French toast: 4 stars. Beautiful presentation and overall delicious. I wouldn't say mind blowing though - would have loved a slightly crispier exterior.
-K chicken benny: 5 stars. This is such a decadent dish. The eggs were perfect, the chicken was flavorful. And I appreciated the small side salad to cut through the heaviness.
-Grilled chicken avocado salad. 5 stars. A great complement to the otherwise decadent dishes. Fresh ingredients and good seasoning.

Only con of this place is that it's really loud on weekends. So, not the most conducive for conversations but maybe worth it for the delicious meal.
The drinks here are so fun! The food was also amazing, I don't think you could go wrong with anything.

I've been waiting to go to this restaurant for years. It was just on my list of foodie places I wanted to try and it did not disappoint the wait was long but totally worth it. I'd wait in that line again me and my friends split our plates so we could try a little bit of everything and it was so good. Definitely worth the hour and a half trip out

We ordered the k-bomb chicken benny and it was so yummy. The chicken wasn't dry and was seasoned very well. The potato's and salad were also a nice balance with the egg and chicken. The bread was a bit soggy though. We also ordered the citrus french toast. The flavor was okay. It threw me off that the fruit was room temperature. It didn't taste as fresh. We also ordered the lychee and mango drink. Both were very sweet. The lychee tasted better than the mango tango because I could taste the lychee flavor more.

I came here yesterday with my boyfriend and there was a lot of people waiting to get in. We arrived around 1 and waited about 25 minutes to be seated. Sadly they don't take reservations on the weekends. The restaurant was quite spacious. We ordered the chicken waffle, mascarpone pancake and K-bomb chicken Benedict. For drinks we got the butterfly lychee and mango tango. I really loved the lychee drink! It was so refreshing! I liked the waffles for the chicken waffle the best. The butter on it was really tasty too. It was so light and crispy. It's probably one of the best waffles I've had. The K-bomb chicken was also really good. I wasn't a fan of the Benedict. The mascarpone pancake is on the sweeter side for sure.

This place is definitely hyped up. If you're coming here or looking it up- you've heard. If you can stomach the wait and begin in a frenzy to get a table: this place rocks. The menu is perfect size, the chicken is chefs kiss, the drinks are delicious. Go to brunch here you will not be dissapointed. They have a lot of customers and no time to wait for nonsense. So come in with your game face and be ready to wait. It will be worth it!
The food was satisfactory overall. The service left a lot of room for improvement. It felt unorganized and inattentive.

It gets really crowded pretty quickly so make a reservation ahead of time! Service can be slow because of the rush. The food was good - nothing outstanding from brunch food but it was good. The drinks were amazing! Overall ambience was nice but the atmosphere is lively w the crowd

we waited about 30 minutes for a table, and the place was super packed for brunch so go early!

k-bomb chicken benny - i'm not going to lie, it was nothing special. the bay area has a lot of great fusion brunch places, and this one was just ok.

i can see this place being great for a friend hangout brunch day, but there's nothing particularly special about it.

The food was amazing had the crambule French toast and Marscapone Pancakes. They where just amazing! And let's not forget the Volcano coffee was strong but delicious. Will defenetly come back if I'm ever back in SF
The place was good. Not my favorite, great for pictures if that's something you are looking for. But quality wise it was just regular nothing special. Would come back though.

Food was great! The chicken was super crispy and moist. The waffle was light and fluffy.

My friend ordered the chipotle eggs Benedict that came with Korean fried chicken. I could do without the sauce on the chicken next time. It was very sweet and didn't compliment the eggs.


Wait time is long more than an hour so don't expect to be seated when you arrive.

You must try the whipped coffee !

Loved the vibe, the food and great fast service, we ordered a lot as everything looked so tempting! Plain French toast was so good, pancakes so pretty but maybe a little too sweet for my personal taste with the cream but fresh fruit topping yummy. Delish chicken w waffle & k-bomb Bennie's really good - we really enjoyed checking the place out and will definitely return again! Would recommend as a great place to bring out of towners if you live in Bernal or mission - we walked easily from home & didn't have to deal with any parking issues. Walked off some of the calories on the return!
The Food is amazing !! Service is 10/10. Only 30 minute wait on a very busy Saturday.

Yes! FOUR CHAIRS is definitely my new favorite brunch spot in San Francisco. Not only is the food delicious, it's beautiful and affordable too.

Everything we ordered was so pretty and so tasty including the drinks!! The Mascarpone Pancake is a must-order, so good you don't wanna share! The Berries Shrimp Harvest Salad was so light, refreshing and delicious- it was perfect with the Crispy Chicken & Waffle. The Chipotle Benedict was so creamy!

We can't wait to try the burgers!
It looks amazing!

Service was really good and friendly. I ordered the Chipotle Benny and shared the Mascarpone Pancakes with friends. The chipotle Benny was really good and the potatoes that came with it were good and crispy. The Mascarpone Pancakes were definitely the star of the show. Overall really nice experience

Had a random lunch date in San Francisco, and found this place. The wait wasn't too long, so we decided to try it. The food was okay, nothing stood out to me honestly. The service was good. The price was very affordable. Food just wasn't good enough for me to want to go back.

Location 7/10
Food 6/10
Service 8/10
Price 8/10

Great breakfast spot, they have all of your standard breakfast options but spruced up a bit and with some novelty choices as well. I decided to get the Hawaiian omelet when I came here and it was delicious. It was filled with pineapples and gooey pepperjack cheese and paired with a side of fresh, crunchy ciabatta toast. The potatoes weren't bad, nicely fried but a little on the bland side. I also was really feeling in the mood for a Bloody Mary to have with my meal but they were out, and it was only 11 am =(

Street parking wasn't too bad. We came pretty early so we were able to find a spot fairly quickly.

Place is cozy and since the food is so delicious it can get crowded fairly quickly.

Food so delicious we went back twice to try more options. There is no wrong order on the menu. Everything is delicious.

Worth the hype. Completely recommend.

I love this place -- definitely worth the wait! It's one of my favorite spots in San Francisco. I do wish the menu had a bit more variety, but everything they offer is consistently good. Always a great experience overall!
Everything I have tried from here is delicious from food to drinks. 100% recommended for brunch. Service has been great every time I have been there.

Lovely space, beautifully plated dishes, the fresh flowers are a nice touch. However, we were disappointed in the quality of our food.

RESERVATIONS
Made by phone about an hour in advance for Friday lunch. We didn't need it, there was plenty of walk-in space.

THE COST
$54.03 including tax/tip for lunch for two.

THE FOOD
* Coffee - 1 stars
I didn't have this, but my partner called this airplane quality coffee. You do get free refills.

* Four Chairs Benny ($22) - 3 stars
The thick bacon, runny eggs, and sauce were tasty, 4 stars for these. But the potatoes were dry and the salad overly simplistic (the ingredients similar in quality to what you might find in a buffet style salad bar).

* Crispy Chicken Burger ($16) - 3 stars
Breading was thick, the spicy aioli good. Otherwise, this was lackluster. The bun and chicken were mushy, the toppings boring, and usually fried chicken burgers do better with a zesty sauce.

Three out of the for people enjoy their meal the one who didn't enjoy their meal said the chicken wasn't that good but the other three thought their food was delicious.

Really nice service they came to the table a couple of times asking if everything was OK food delivery was good timing as well.
Ambience was nice. I didn't take a picture though.
The food is so good. The wait time is a little slow. The wait time is fast. I would go there again. love it. I felt happy to go here. There was no music, I would want music there.
Came here for the mascarpone pancakes and volcano coffee, did not disappoint. A little slow even before it got busy but presentation and the pancake to cream ratio made up for the wait

Worth the hype! I live pretty close, but I've never been there because it gets craaaazy I'm the weekends and I've been intimidated by the line. This morning we finally got there early and it was definitely worth while! I had the k-bomb chicken Benedict my friend had the Bay Benedict with salmon and Tom yum hollandaise. So good! The Tom Yum hollandaise in particular was phenomenal. I'm definitely getting that next time I go and there will be a next time I swear it! Service was great refills of my coffee were frequent and generously offered.

The place gets pretty busy so either come early or make a reservation. I got here as soon as it opened so I was seated right away.

I was looking for bottomless mimosas yesterday and this place popped up! They DON'T have bottomless mimosas but they do have single mimosas and a pitcher of champagne that comes with a small side of orange juice which was $35. (They also have the option to order a cranberry flavored mimosa as well).

The food was pretty good. I ordered home fries breakfast potatoes and French Toast which came with an assortment of fresh fruit. My partner ordered the Okonomiyaki Fries. Definitely worth $10!

Definitely recommend, I just wish they had more food options on the menu.
Excellent food! Must try! I had the chicken and waffle breakfast. Chicken was crispy and waffles were so soft and sweet.

Surprisingly no wait on a Sunday morning for brunch. Interior is very spacious for an SF restaurant and modern with lots of wood pieces.

Came with brunch in mind and they did not disappoint. Can't go wrong with a Benedict and the chipotle one was good. It wasn't spicy at all, maybe a mild spice. The egg was nice and runny. My favorite thing was probably the potatoes! Thick chunks super crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. The French toast was yummy as well and I enjoyed that all of the fruits on the plate were sweet and ripe. The mango tango drink was super refreshing it felt like a mix of a mango purée and sparkling soda.

Definitely will be back to try their dinner menu!

We came to Four Chairs without a reservation on Sunday during peak brunch hours and it took us about 20 minutes to get seated.

My bf ordered the Four Chairs Omelet, which was kind of bland aside from the bacon. I ordered the Nova Benny that had a perfect lemon hollandaise on top but the potatoes were again bland - it tasted like they didn't season it with any salt or oil. No biggie, I doused them with ketchup because I love sauce anyway. The arugula salad had a citrusy dressing and was quite refreshing.

All in all, this satisfied my brunch craving but I recommend getting their benedicts or something else other than their omelets. While the food isn't astounding, the wait time and prices are reasonable for SF.
The food was amazing my daughter had a great experience ! The food and service were great. Nothing but pleasure and quick service

We were really disappointed with our experience here. The service was good but the food not so much. Our food took about 30min to come out but nothing tasted fresh. I got the burger with fries and the fries tasted stale and overly salty. Thought about asking for the homes fries instead but then tasted my wife's and they also tasted terrible. My burger was cooked well but it had an overwhelming amount of aioli on it that really took away from the burger. My wife got the k-bomb chicken Benedict and the chicken was good but everything else on her plate was lack luster. Ordered a pancake as a side and it also seemed old. Soon after we left, my wife developed stomach pain and has been on the toilet ever since. Two star for the service and volcano coffee, which was good. overall will not be revisiting this restaurant.

I wonder what the four chairs refer to. I only take up one chair, at least on a good day, so what happens to the other three? Are they going to seat me with strangers they pull off Mission? Apparently not as I was allowed to sit at a table by myself. It was also past 2PM, so the lunch hour was coming to a close anyway. This was a trendy-looking ramen house (RakiRaki) in its previous life, but I never tried it. Now the space is more of a new American brunch spot. It looked a bit too stylish to be referred to as a diner, though their menu veered in that direction.

I decided to try the $16 Truffle Omelet, which was tasty and nicely presented with the mushrooms and spinach visible through the eggs which also featured truffle garlic and black pepper. It came with a fresh fruit cup as a substitute for toast (my preference for an extra $2) and "homie home fries" which were indeed homestyle and slightly overcooked- though I cannot attest as to whether 'homies' made them (photo: https://bit.ly/3f0zO8N). No matter as it was all satisfying - perhaps enough for me to find three people to fill the other chairs. Sheesh, too much trouble for this curmudgeon.

FOOD - 4 stars...diner fare but done with a bit more upturned style
AMBIANCE - 4 stars...more contemporary than you'd think and reasonably spacious
SERVICE - 4 stars...polite and efficient
TOTAL - 4 stars...I guess I didn't need the three other chairs

RELATED - Exploring the Outer Mission? Here's a collection of places I've visited and reviewed: http://bit.ly/37B1acE

The restaurant is nicely decorated, minimalist style. We walked in and there and there want a host to greet us. You put your name and party in a tablet and it gives you a wait time. After we were seated, no one came to take our order. We flagged a server down when we were ready to order.
The food was good, I ordered the crème brûlée French toast and beef bacon. The sauce on the toast was delicious. I wish I would've gotten at least three pieces of bacon since the side order was $7. I also ordered the strawberry matcha latte and that was tasty. Their regular coffee is really good. The food was delivered quickly and correctly. I would return to this restaurant.

We decided to check this place out because it was pretty popular and the food and everything looked great. We enjoyed it for sure but I think my wife and I both ordered the wrong thing because neither one of us liked it too much. But two positive things to note is that the service was so good. I mean some of the fastest we've ever had and there were a lot of other items on the menu that looked great. So even though we struck out, this place will most likely have something you enjoy!

Well in town for the weekend I found with restaurant on TikTok. I got the K-bomb benny. It was good but took a little bit for the flavor to blend for me. I also got the recommended volcano coffee. The was a tad bitter until I was able to Stirr in the cream. All the all it was a great experience. I got there before the rush so it was peaceful. It was a cute venue and the service was good.

Got seated within 10 minutes on Sunday around noon, service was quick and attentive. The mascarpone pancakes are delicious but nothing special, could be slightly fluffier. The k chicken benny was solid, the chicken is tender and flavorful. The baguette however was soaked in hollandaise sauce and wasn't too pleasant to eat. The strawberry matcha latte wasn't terrible but was weak in matcha flavor. Overall no dealbreakers and you get tasty instagrammable food for reasonable prices. Would definitely come back if I'm in the area!

Came on a Saturday and we just had to wait a few minutes to be seated. We were lucky to find street parking just across the street. Environment is lively and bustling, so indoor noise level was a bit high.

Food is absolutely delicious! I got the chipotle benedict. The hollandaise was just so flavorful and with a tinge of spice. Definitely my favorite part along with the added bacon we got. Their bacon is sweet and so flavorful as well. The french toast was very soft and fluffy-- probably the best I've had. We also got the butterfly lychee and mango tango drink. There was quite a bit of ice in the butterfly lychee drink, so it gets watered down quickly if you do not drink it fast. I am not a fan of the canned lychee they use; it tasted very tart. Overall, I would definitely come back! We were very attracted to their dinner menu as well!

This place is incredible. Easy check in, fast service, excellent food, and reasonably priced.

The chicken sandwiches and fries are absolutely fantastic.
Came back and was on point!!! Potatoes were better and service was great . Highly recommend good vibe!!

Started off with some Amazing drinks, then an off the chart omelette (Hawaiian) potatoes could use a little seasoning. Service was right on time no long wait , and vibe was really nice!! Place was clean and everything was on point . I do wish the glasses were bigger because the drinks were so good!!

This place was so cute for a date and brunch! The aesthetics here are great - very Instagrammable.

Good:
- Good service! Everyone is super nice and checks in a lot
- I liked the coffee here - they even had oat milk for us
- Good portion sizes - I was stuffed by the time that I was done eating - I loved the Nova Benedict - a huge fan of smoked salmon and cream cheese combo and there were a lot of sides there too so it felt like it was super worth the price. The salad had a great dressing too!

Bad:
- Longer wait times for the food - super hungry by the time it arrived but worth the wait

Overall I loved the place and would come back!

Four Chairs is a brunch spot in SF that has been very popular recently, with a huge social media presence. We came here on a Saturday for brunch - they unfortunately do not take reservations on the weekends - and waited 30-40 mins for a table of 4. It was incredibly busy and the space was rather tight, with very little wiggle room between the tables.

Their positioning is very similar to that of Kitchen Story, Son & Garden, Surisan, Sweet Maple, etc, with a heavy emphasis on things looking aesthetic and photo-ready (which can sometimes be a bad sign, as it comes at the price of taste). Their menu literally has a section called "Instagrammable drinks".

A lot of their dishes are typical brunch items with a twist of Asian-inspired flavors (e.g. Korean fried chicken eggs benedict). The chicken & waffle was pretty standard, however, other than the fact that it came with a sweet & sour sauce. The fried chicken was incredibly juicy, and was honestly my favorite part of the meal. The waffle, on the other hand, was a little burnt. I had to put a lot of syrup on it to cover up the taste of burnt, because otherwise that's all I could taste.

I personally thought the chicken & waffle tasted better than the chipotle benedict, which just felt like it was missing something (like a kick to it).

Service was not great because they seemed understaffed. We waited a pretty long time (~30-45 mins) for our food and they messed up one of our orders.

I would rate this place above Kitchen Story but there are definitely more interesting brunch places in the city.

Solid asian fusion brunch spot. Wait times can be 30-60 min during peak hours. We tried the chicken and waffles, as well as the k-bomb benny. The waffles were magical, perfectly crunchy yet soft at the same time! Chicken was good, and both had good syrups/sauces. The k-bomb was really crunchy, it looks super spicy but it wasn't spicy at all. I would try the sandwich next time.

Went to Four Chairs for brunch on my birthday. Here are the items we ordered:

1) Butterfly Lychee - Beautiful drink with a very strong lychee flavor. It was very sweet. Love the aesthetics but probably won't be getting this one again.
2) Salmon Benedict w/ Salad and Potatoes - Everything was cooked very well. The Benedict's had just the right amount of Hollandaise and had the perfect egg yolk run. Would order this again.
3) Citrus French Toast - The french toast was a little underwhelming. Plating was great but there wasn't a whole lot of cinnamon flavor and it didn't seem like the bread was soaked. It was just kind of just like regular bread with sugar. Definitely needed to add maple syrup.

Overall Four Chairs is still a nice place to dine at and I would come back!

Came here for a second time on Saturday around 12pm. The service was still really great, but we were a little disappointed by the omelets. xD

It was pretty warm in the restaurant, so I was low key sweating balls while we sat there.

- Truffle omelet: pretty good but didn't have any truffle taste at all

- Hawaiian omelet: this was decent, but there were only two small pieces of pineapple in this lolz. I also didn't taste the red onion and cilantro at all

- Pancakes: decent normal pancakes

Really liked Four Chairs! We got there around 1:30pm, and there were a few open tables. We were seated right away, and the interior was pretty spacious with all of the tables spread out. It was pretty quiet inside.

Our server was super nice, and our water cups were constantly refilled throughout our time there. We ordered the volcano coffee, Four Chairs Benedict, and chipotle Benedict. The coffee was like dalgona coffee and pretty sweet.

The French toast came out first and a lot quicker than the other food, which wasn't ideal since it was cold by the time we ate it. It was pretty average French toast but had a kind of citrusy taste. We liked both Benedict's. The jalapeños on the chipotle Benedict were really spicy even though the seeds were taken out. I usually like crispy bacon, but I really liked the thick cut bacon on the Four Chairs Benedict.

I was happy we tried this place and will definitely come back!
Food service and colorful food presentation. This place was pretty busy for a weekday and the space was inviting and Instagram photo worthy. A nice find in the Mission without the long lines.
This was a nice and unexpected find in the Mission for brunch. Service was attentive and the food was nicely presented. The food and drink are so colorful and Instagram worthy for pictures.

Was really surprised by how everything tasted! First off the two drinks

Volcano coffee was basically a dalgona coffee, but it was much lighter. For people who don't like super strong taste of coffee ( my partner) this is definitely good! If you like stronger tasting coffee this might not suit you as good.

The butterfly lychee was really good! It was like a lychee soda. Very light and a nice compliment to the foods we ordered.

Chicken and waffles were great. Loved the little cup aesthetic to poor the syrup over. Waffles were good, light and not too thick. Chicken was alright, not the greatest but still really good!

The truffle omelette did not have as much truffle aroma as i wished it did, but overall was a solid dish.

This place is great, definitely worth a try!

Came here on a Saturday morning and the wait was just about over an hour. Not too bad buuuut it was worth it!!! From the drinks, the food, the ambiance, the service, to how fast the food came out!!
It was delicious and one of the best brunch places I've been to in the Bay Area.

The pancakes were so fluffy and delicious and the chipotle Benedict's were so flavorful and just the best I've had. I left my plate clean

I visited Four Chains on a Sunday afternoon, it was a very pleasant experience!
Pro tip: if you are not coming alone, have someone hop off to put your name down before finding a place to park; this worked out perfect for us as parking is not easy here, so once we found a spot and walked in we were sat within minutes!

We tried a few things here, for the volcano coffee I was able to substitute with almond milk which was perfect for me, it was pretty good id give it a 4/5 as I like my coffee pretty strong.
The mascarpone pancakes on the other hand were definitely not bad, but for me personally when I order pancakes I like them SWEET, and these were just a hint of sweet, so for me 3/5. But my friend who prefers not super sweet pancakes LOVED them.
The other dish the K-bomb chicken Benny was DELICIOUS, I would say 5/5 and I would actually go back just for this dish.

The vibes were nice as well, everyone was close but not too close to each other, luckily we were sat in a corner too so that helped.

It was busy, but we were seated fairly quickly. The waiters were great and cleaning up and turning over to all waiting customers. Instagramable good/drinks were delicious and were happy to say we arw leaving satisfied. All foods were cooked to perfection, all flavors came through, and we look forward to coming back on our next visit to San Francisco! It was a bit crowded and super loud, but I understand because this place is so popular
I really like the food here! It can get a bit busy and loud, but it's kind of nice to have a place like this closer to home and not have to drive so far from the excelsior district. Metered parking.

I discovered Four Chairs through social media. This is such great lowkey brunch spot in SF! Decent prices, yummy and aesthetic food, a clean space, attentive service... What more can you ask for?!

Food / Drink: To my surprise, everything tasted just as good as it looked! When I've had butterfly pea drinks in the past, the taste is usually kind of bland. But with their Butterfly Lychee drink, it was sweet and delicious! The bacon in the Four Chairs Benny was reminiscent of millionaire's bacon.

Price: Considering this is a brunch restaurant in SF, everything seemed to be reasonably priced.

Aesthetic / Space: I love the aesthetic of the restaurant.

Service: Our server was very attentive and kindly clarified the many questions we asked.

Parking: Metered street parking around the area.

The food here was really good and overall the staff seemed friendly, but I had an experience that left me a bit disappointed. When I ordered, the waiter seemed impatient. I was the last to order at my table, and as soon as I said what I wanted, he quickly said "okay" and left before I could add any adjustments. For example, I wanted to order a matcha latte with almond milk, but he walked away before I could say the rest of my order. I had to wait until he came back around to clarify. The same thing happened with my food order, which made me feel rushed and not able to enjoy my meal the way I had hoped. It seemed a bit busy and I understand it, but that part of the service rubbed me the wrong way.
Very kind staff, delicious food and a cozy setting! Great spot for a date, solo, or a couple of pals!

Cute and trendy brunch spot with yummy drinks like the volcano coffee. Service was friendly and efficient and we were seated on a Saturday around noon with a short wait after we put ourselves down on the Yelp waitlist since they don't take reservations on weekends. The food is pretty average for a brunch spot, the eggs were over cooked for the benedict :(
Very good food great service!! The k bomb was really good it's a line for a reason we got seated fast

Cam and I took the kids and his mom for brunch for a late Mother's Day brunch , so this review is for May , sorry ! I am a little behind finally have some off time so yay . We arrived around 12:00 pm and had no reservations , the wait time was 1 hour so we put ourselves on the wait list and hung out outside with the other families waiting to be sat. It was very busy when we went it could have been how they look every day or it could of been due to everyone graduating . Cam and i always like to decided on 2 dishes and we go halfsies to experience the flavor of something that caught both of our eyes . The decor is simple but it works for this establishment. The seats are close next to other parties . When we finally got sat they put 2 tables together and the tables were different height so that was a little annoying as they would wobble. For the instagramable drinks they offer the kids got strawberry matcha and the mango tango . We also ordered a mango tango to share, the mango tango was okay it was lacking mango flavor . Our kiddo liked their strawberry matcha. The chicken and waffles and crème brûlée French toast is what cam and I ordered. One of our kiddos ordered a chicken sandwich and the other one had a kids meal , his mom also had chicken and waffles which she enjoyed. The chicken sandwich according to our kiddo was "cool" so use your teenager translation to that one . For the kids meal she said the bacon was good but her pancake was dry. Cam and I thought the chicken was missing flavor it had a really basic taste , maybe frying the chicken in some herbs with garlic would give it that flavor its missing , that's usually how we cook our fried chicken. The waffle was soggy maybe the chicken was applied as soon as it came out and the condensation is what caused it . For the crème brûlée French toast , we were expecting a flavorful experience but it did not taste like crème brûlée at all , it tasted more like a simple custard lacking some flavor as well. Would we go back here ? Hmmm i said yes we would give them another shot to try some of their different plates they offer which we might feel different about but this is how we honestly felt about it the first Time trying brunch items. The bill was about $160 with tip for a party of 5.

If you don't want to go into the city for brunch, Four Chairs is a good alternative. I love their volcano coffee which essentially is the viral dalgona coffee from pandemic times. I tried multiple dishes here and they do everything well from classic omelettes to fusion Korean fried chicken egg benedicts. They can accommodate large parties which most spots have trouble doing on a weekend - I had a group of 10 and they were super efficient!

Solid brunch place in the city! Food does not just look good, but also tastes delicious, which is not always the case.

Our party of 4 didn't have to wait long for a table on a recent Saturday and I was surprised by how many tables were inside actually. The space can serve a decent amount of people. Service is prompt - not too attentive, but just enough. Things we ordered:

* K-bomb chicken benny - Chicken was perfectly fried with the perfect amount of sauce. Not too spicy, just enough heat that I can handle.
* Mascarpone pancake - Pancakes were smaller in size than what we expected, but the taste and lightness of it made up for it. The mascarpone cream is placed in between the pancakes and not whipped in the pancake batter btw
* Chicken and waffles - Again, chicken was nicely fried. By itself, it didn't have much flavor so accompanying sauce was much needed. The main star for us though were the waffles. They were so light and the edges had this perfect, soft crisp to them. I'm never impressed by waffles, but this was an exception.
*Loco Plato - I only got to try a small bite of this, but would say this was probably the least impressive item we ordered. It was still good though.
*Butterfly Lychee - Billed as one of their "instagrammable drinks," which it certainly was. I didn't taste it but was told it was too sweet and could've used more lychee.

This place has been on my list of places to try and I am so glad that I got to stop by for brunch. If you are driving to the restaurant, just know that it is only street parking and parking can be very difficult to find.
We came on a Friday and we got seated immediately, the restaurant itself is nice and modern. There was plenty of seating inside and I saw tables for larger groups.

We ordered a side of fries, bacon, the original benedict, K-bomb chicken benny, and chicken and waffle. The food came out quickly and it was very delicious.

Overall, I would recommend this place for brunch!

Stumbled across this place on Yelp! Decided to give this place a try on New Year's Day. Since we did come on New Year's Day, there was a wait. But it is DEFINITELY worth the wait.

We got to try the Nova Omelet, K-bomb Chicken Benny Benedict, Mascarpone Pancake, Okonomiyaki Fries, Butterfly Lychee and Volcano Coffee! I must say that everything that we ordered was delicious! It definitely didn't disappoint. What I really appreciated the most was the freshness of the ingredients because to be honest, the quality of a lot of brunch places in the bay area has gone downhill.

So if you love breakfast and brunch, you must give them a try ! Also, great ambience, attentive staff and fantastic service ! Will definitely come back again !
Amazing food! Service was great! Loved the brunch vibes. Would definitely be going back soon

Went here for NYE brunch. Food and service were just ok but the place and the ambiance were good. Overall I'll try it again. Discovered the place from watching some IG Reels for their colorful and "instagramable" selections.

Food: we tried quite a few of the popular dishes here

1. Okonomiyaki Fries: Crispy, flavorful and came with lots of bonito floss. (Not the usual shaved bonito) it looked like shredded cheese at a glance - this is the highlight of the meal

2. Marscapone Pancakes: best part of this was the marscapone, pancakes were dry and not fluffy at all. My friend even mentioned that it probably came from a Kellogg's box

3. French Toast: to be honest, I don't even remember it for me to comment on it

4. Chicken and waffles: The chicken were cooked, flavorful, but if there's a bad thing for a fried chicken, it's that the breading was wet. Waffles were forgettable too

5. Korean Benny: Basically Korean fried chicken over eggs Benedict. Another wet mess. They put 2 poached eggs over an UNtoasted baguette next to a salad with a good portion of Korean fried chicken. Imagine all the liquids in there seeping through the untoasted baguette and chicken. Flavors were all good though and it seems the bang for your buck.

Drinks:
Mango, Mango & matcha, Strawberry & Matcha, Butterfly lychee and Coffee. All were very pretty to look at, and for $7 each is a steal. Next time however, I'll probably just stick to water.

Overall I like how the food taste but I wish they pay attention more on the textures.

I came during a weekday lunch hour so there wasn't a wait to grab a seat. My eyes immediately locked on the K-Bomb chicken sandwich when I was walking by this place one day so that's what I got here along with a side of fries. It's basically a fried chicken sandwich except the pieces of chicken were Korean fried chicken. It wasn't too spicy and the chicken was tender and juicy. Fries were your standard thin fries. Not soggy or overly crispy. It's basically self water over here since they put a water jug at your table but they still checked in on me.

Oh. My. Gosh. I could probably say that 2 more times. But it would add nothing of value for a person who hasn't been here before.
Ok, so EVERYTHING here is instagrammable: the beverages, the food and even some of the other customers. Everybody's feeling pretty hip and excited just to be seated and in the mix.
Our new LLC needed a kick-off Meet Up. So why not here, at Four Chairs on Mission St? It's Sunday, 9:00am. They're open! We beat the crowds! We secure a 4-top, *window table* spread out our notebooks and legal pads. We're the first ones in the place! Waiting for a menu. Waiting for a menu. Such a pleasant vibe inside, didn't want to prod the waitress casually walking the dining room. Finally looked over at the condiment/cutlery holder on the table. Oh, there's a QR code labeled "Menu", inconspicuously placed near the ketchup & hot sauce. Connecting to that gets you these amazing photos of what you will be eating and drinking. Menu listings give names, ingredients, prices.
You know how all these great food photos on restaurant menus hype their dishes and never measure up. Not here! Every dish - just like the photo. And tastes like - well, that's something we have no tech yet to create virtually. It's all great. Chef approved, I might add. I've been a chef - for over 40 years. And I approve it. I even had some of my wife's Benedict leftovers from her 'girls' brunch-out. Didn't even bother reheating anything. Full of flavor, straight from the to-go container. It would be hard to imagine anyone eating here and NOT finding something to love, and not being fully happy with it. I mean not *absolutely impossible*. But, honestly. da*n close. Elina had Chicken n waffles: not a spec of grease, crispy delicious looking waffles. My pancakes and fresh fruit were beautifully assembled - almost imitating a Japanese soufflé-type stack. But NOT soufflé pancakes! To see how it's done, order it for yourself.
My bud had scrambled eggs, country fries, nice looking sausage (he'd never had that before. All excellently prepared. My little Cranberry Mimosa had two blueberries floating inside and the glass rim was beautifully adorned with pink sugar crystals.
Oh. Reality check.
One minor criticism. And so easily corrected! coffee.
Our biz partner Elina is French. I mean veeerrry French. And we all enjoy good, sturdy *real* Java. In all its many variations. Ive been at this too long to hold my comments. And the place is just so good. I would be a shame not to say something. I let the (obviously the) owner - a tall, very gracious host know of our experience in his wonderful eatery: Excellent food? Sure. I don't think 5+ stars would be out of line. Classy fun beverages? Check Pleasant ambiance Check .
Real coffee? Espresso machine? Nuanced javas?? Mmmmm. Psst (hint, hint)Chicken and Waffle
It was okay I got the pancakes was expecting more flavor on it but it was good I tired the French toast those I'd recommend ! Service was good

We came here on a Sunday (during Outside Lands Weekend) and were able to join the waitlist through the Yelp app. For a table of three, it only took about 25 to 30 minutes to get seated. There were lots of seating options for small and larger groups.

Chicken and Waffle: 4 out of 5 stars
A single order of the chicken and waffle came with two large pieces of chicken. It was crispy and easily came off the bone. The waffle was also tasty but could be crisper.

Mascarpone Pancakes: 4 out of 5 stars
The pancakes were very light and just the right amount of sweetness for my friend. The mascarpone was too overpowering, but still a good light breakfast option.

Just recently my girlfriend and I got to experience this amazing brunch spot! We got to try the K-Bomb Chicken Benny as well as the Chipotle Arnold Egg Benedict. Both meals were super filling since it came with a side of salad and wedges!

For desert we got to try the Citrus French Toast with different fruits! Although this looked good on the menu, but I personally was not a fan of it. Still delicious though!

And as for the drinks we got to try the Butterfly lychee with soju and the Volcano coffee! Personally I'm wouldn't get coffee at a restaurant which is why I decided to get the most favorited drink! Very refreshing and 10/10 would recommend!

We also really loved the ambience! This spot was a perfect spot for a Sunday brunch in the city! It does get crowded around lunch as per usual, but wait time was not that long!

There are also plenty of small shops around to check out while waiting! Feel free to check this location out! Great for family and friends!

Four chairs has great food. Our first time there and I was pleasantly surprised. The menu is eye catching and all items sound delicious.
My dish was flavorful and hearty.
I didn't order coffee or drinks but they did look very IG worthy.
The space is very big but I did feel the table space for our party was quite tight. Although, we were not rushed which is always a plus.
Food, service, the atmosphere was 10/10. Everything we got was very good and flavorful. Forgot to take a picture of the crème French toast but that was the best!

Fast service for brunch, large portions, korean chicken better than MANY MANY places. Place has had several owners (Raki Raki ramens!!) but food remains very good. Sides are very well done as well (not an after thought).
Overall, great brunch place, simple decor but good food.

Stopped by here for brunch with some coworkers! I love how Four Chairs is an Asian fusion restaurant. It looks like they serve more fusion style dishes during the evening.

We were a big group of 8 and were comfortably seated within 20 minutes on a Thursday morning. We all ordered the fried chicken and waffles and it was amaaazing. The waffles were crispy on the outside and the chicken was crunchy and juicy and very well seasoned. It tasted so delicious in the hot maple syrup that it was served with. I also ordered a butterfly lychee drink and although it was very beautiful, it was a bit underwhelming. I wish it had more of a lychee flavor.
